name: Devils Fork State Park Campground
note: Many waterfront RV sites on Lake Jocassee.  To reserve a single night, call the campground directly within one week of arrival.  --AWH

booking.note: Booked on South Carolina State Parks' own reservation site or 1-866-345-7275, up to 13 months ahead. 'Camping reservations must be made for a minimum of two nights'; per the --AWH note, a single night can be booked by calling the park within a week of arrival. Maximum 14 nights; in peak season high-volume parks may cap the cumulative stay at 14 consecutive days. Same-day reservations go through the park (864-944-2639). Check-in 2 pm, check-out noon; arrivals after 5 pm get late-arrival instructions by email.

fees.note: $38-62 a night for a standard campsite. The price changes by site and night, higher on weekends and busy dates. No reservation fee and no out-of-state rate. Every bookable night on the park's reservation calendar for two weeks from 2026-10-13 and from 2027-06-15, read 2026-10-12.

DNR: 'Some sites can accommodate motorhomes'.

name: SH001 Town Hill
note: Buchanan State Forest motorized roadside site SH001 Town Hill (Sideling Hill area), beside Spade Road (T 402) at the top of Town Hill: a secluded grass parking lot with road noise from I-70. From the south, Rice Road becomes Spade Road at the forest line and climbs about 120 m in 1.2 km to the site: about 10% on average, with the last 450 m near 14% and short pitches steeper still. The road is fine for a small AWD motorhome on a dry day; avoid it when the road is wet, muddy or icy. The approach from the north is also doable in dry weather, but it has a couple of small brook crossings that could be difficult when wet or muddy, and small tree branches encroaching on the road make it a tight fit. The road is unpaved from either direction. No toilets or trash service (carry in, carry out). --Claude

name: Little River Dispersed Camping
note:
15 numbered sites along the Little River, suitable for tents and small to medium RVs.  The narrow gravel road may be tricky for larger rigs.  Very remote with no cell service.  Sites fill up on weekends.  --AWH
Reviews (2020-23, all 5*): about half the ~16 numbered sites on FR 17 take a trailer, and a side loop of 5 gravel-pad sites (turnoff between sites 6 and 7) is the trailer pick. It's often empty even on weekends, while the riverside sites fill. Largest rig reported is a 36-ft fifth wheel, but the road is narrow, potholed and muddy after rain, with tight turns onto one-lane bridges. Sites 9 and 13 are called the prettiest, with small pools and a gravel beach ~50 yd below 9, and wildflowers, ferns and grassy spots at the water. Fire rings and a few tables; no trash service. Daytime helicopter and low-level military jet noise is a recurring complaint. An aggressive black bear was reported in 2023, so keep food locked in the vehicle. --Claude

sites.note: Six camping areas; 368 campsites on the booking site besides 6 equestrian sites, cabins, cottages and glamping: Lower Lake Campground's Beechwood (101 electric), Northwoods (28 electric, 18 full-hookup), Rhododendron (15 electric, 45 non-electric); Pickerel Point (23 electric, 12 full-hookup, 38 walk-to tent sites); Deerfield (32 rustic non-electric) and Pines (56 rustic non-electric). note: Several sites are waterfront or just on the other side of the drive from the water.  Pretty much all sites have a water view.  --AWH

Pets $5.38 each per stay, three at most; two parking passes included, more $5 each. All payments are final, and a cancellation costs one night with tax. RVs at most 30 days in any 45. Booked online (the city's WebTrac), by phone (904-255-4255, weekdays) or in person. The page gives no year. Read 2026-10-13.

facilities.note: Heated showers; year-round dump and fill station; campground store (740) 385-6842. Outdoor pool Memorial Day - Labor Day. Off-peak (November 1 - April 1) Shower House 1, the dump station and the store stay open; water only at Shower House 1.

season.note: Off-peak November 1 - April 1 with reduced facilities. ReserveOhio sells sites 1-93 (71 electric and full-hookup) for a January night; sites 94-172 are not sold then.

booking.note: 'Reservations for full hookup, electric, or non-electric sites may be made up to six months in advance, online or by calling (866) 644-6727.' 14-night maximum on ReserveOhio.

Cedar's 8 tent-only sites $43 (2027) and the 10 Jackpine hike-in tent sites $20 are left out. A Recreation Passport is required for vehicle entry to all state park campgrounds.

Senior/Access pass halves the basic site fee, not the electric fee.

season.note: USFS: 'Campground open early April through late October.' Day use April 1 through December. (recreation.gov's 2026 rate season runs April 1 - October 30.)

sites.note: 65 sites: 31 electric in Meadow (C) and River Bend (B) loops, 'suitable for larger camping units and RV's' (catalog lengths to 40 ft, back-in), and 34 non-electric in White Oak Loop (A), restricted to units under 20 ft by the access road. Unlevel mountain ground.

facilities.note: Showers, flush toilets and drinking-water hydrants (not threaded) in each loop; a signed RV fill station with threaded hose and a trailer dump station. No firewood or ice for sale; mandatory food storage lockers (bears). Lakes allow electric motors and hand-carried boats only.

name: Cherry Springs State Park Rustic Campground
note: Cherry Springs State Park is nearly as remote and wild today as it was two centuries ago. Its dark skies make it a haven for astronomers. fees.note: $33 a night, or $37 on a Friday, a Saturday or the night before a holiday, for New York residents; non-residents pay double ($66 / $74). Nothing is added on top: all 176 sites are plain campsites with no hookups, and the booking site charges every one the same. The $33 already contains New York's $3 flagship-campground charge, and it matches the state's fee table only with the $10 oceanfront charge included too. $7.25 reservation fee. Read 2026-10-12.

booking.note: ReserveAmerica, up to 9 months ahead, same day included. Peak season (mid-June to mid-September; 2027: June 18 - September 11, by area) takes 7-night reservations only, starting on the loop's own Friday, Saturday or Sunday, and only ONE 7-night reservation per name, address, email or phone. Non-peak minimum 2 nights, maximum 14 continuous nights then 48 hours away. Where less than the minimum stay is open, those nights go to walk-ins, first come first served. Register by 9 pm. Permit holder must be 21+ and present; reservations are non-transferable.

sites.note: ReserveAmerica lists 176 campsites (the park description says a 190-site campground); listed equipment lengths 20-40 ft (118 at 30 ft, 15 at 40 ft), every driveway back-in. The J Loop is tent-only, key-card entry, no generators.

Camping-only park (no day use): registered campers get a PIN for the security gate, and should arrive during office hours. --Claude

name: McClintic Point Primitive Campground
note: Small campground on Lake Moomaw near Bolar Mountain Recreation Area.  All sites claim to accommodate 21 feet RVs but will probably handle a few feet more.  A couple sites appear to be waterfront.  Route 603 NW of the campground is a narrow one-lane gravel road with steep drop-offs not suitable for RVs.  Campground should be accessed from route 600 instead.  --AWH

sites.note: 21 single sites plus two group sites (20-35 people); every site is listed at 21 ft, back-in.

booking.note: The 21 single sites are first-come, first-served; only the two group sites book on recreation.gov (4 months ahead; reservations carry a 2-night weekend / 3-night holiday minimum). 14 nights a month. Limit 3 camping units and 2 vehicles per site; all equipment must fit on the site. No cell reception.

name: Mower Tract Dispersed Camping
note:
Often described in reviews as the best dispersed camping in WV.  Approximately 20 high-elevation campsites with breathtaking mountain views, dark skies, and significant distance between sites.  Sites range from tent-only spots to big group sites.  Sites 12, 14 and 16 are particularly sought-after for their views and privacy.  Extremely remote and not likely to be crowded.  The gravel road is maintained but may be steep and rough in places.  Reviews indicate no problems for 22-25 ft trailers and a 39-ft converted school bus.  Limited cell signal may be available near site 1.  --AWH and Claude

name: Abes Run dispersed camping
note:
Dispersed creekside sites at the confluence of Abes Run and the East Fork of the Greenbrier River.  Sites on far side of the river may not be accessible when water is high.  --AWH
There are 4 distinct sites off Abes Run Rd (FR 51), all with fire rings and a view of the river; one has a picnic table. The East Fork Trail runs right through them. name: Beckys Creek Wildlife Management Area
note:
Dispersed camping sites along Becky Creek. Camp in designated sites only. --AWH
CAVEAT (2026-09-23): not visited. WVDNR says camping is allowed "in designated areas only" but never says where. Its official map (Dec 2021) marks no campsites, only two Hunter Access Parking lots, so expect overnight parking for hunters rather than developed campsites. The WMA is 1,930 acres of WV Dept. of Agriculture land leased to WVDNR, not national forest. Access is CR 43 (Becky Creek Rd) off US 219, ~9 mi south of Huttonsville. The county road ends at the WMA boundary; beyond it the map draws the route along the creek to the inner lot as an unimproved hunter access trail, and several stream fords can cut off access in high water. Whether a 23-ft rig can get in is unknown, so scout on foot first. Satellite shows unbroken hardwood canopy at this pin. It is steep second-growth hardwood managed for hunting (bear, deer, turkey, grouse), so expect hunters in season. No facilities and no reviews found anywhere. --Claude

name: Jekyll Island Campground
note: Campground in a wooded setting surrounded by live oaks, about a half mile walk to driftwood beach. --AWH

booking.note: NOT in the Georgia State Parks reservation system, despite Jekyll Island calling itself a state park: booking is Campspot or 912.635.3021, not gastateparks.reserveamerica.com, so the state:GA booking window and 4pm cutoff do not apply here. Three-night minimum on Memorial Day, July 4th and Labor Day, with holiday rates; no general minimum. 'We only offer daily rates, with the maximum stay allowed being 14 nights.' Check-in from 2pm, check-out by noon. Boats and utility trailers must go into storage rather than on the site.

fees.note: THE ISLAND ENTRY FEE IS THE TRAP, and the campground says so itself: 'the parking fee collected at the entrance gate is separate from the campsite reservation fee, and must be paid for each day on the island.' It is mandatory for every vehicle entering Jekyll - $10 per day, '$15 for vehicles exceeding 8' ' (which is most RVs), plus $5 more on designated special-event days (Independence Day, Shrimp & Grits Festival, Holly Jolly Jekyll). Annual is $100, or $150 oversized. per is vehicle_DAY, unlike the Georgia state parks ParkPass, which an overnight guest pays once for the whole stay - a week here is 7 gate days on top of the site. A GEORGIA PARKPASS IS NOT VALID and earns no discount: the Authority's own discount list names CCGA students, state-government vehicles, public school buses and disabled veterans (free annual pass, service-connected VIC/VHIC, redeemed in person) and explicitly not GA State Parks pass holders. Jekyll 'does not receive operational dollars from the State of Georgia like other State Parks', which is why it gates its own fee. Rates are 'from' figures: the cheapest site a 23-ft motorhome fits is the full-hookup back-in from $51 (primitive tent sites from $36 take only small self-contained rigs 'depending on size'), pull-through from $54, yurts from $125; the hookup premium is not published as a separate surcharge so none is recorded. One-time $4 pet fee per pet (tent/RV sites). Cancelling 7+ days out costs $25; inside 7 days it is higher, and an early departure is also $25.

An Acadia entrance pass is required while staying in the campground: $35 per vehicle. Non-US residents 16 and older also pay a $100 nonresident fee unless admitted with an Annual or America the Beautiful pass.

booking.note: All sites by reservation on recreation.gov; none at the office or in person. 90% of sites are released six months ahead on the first of each month at 10 am Eastern, the other 10% at 10 am 14 days ahead of arrival, rolling; same-day reservations if sites are open. Combined limit of 14 nights in Acadia campgrounds between the Friday of Memorial Day weekend and Columbus Day, 30 nights per calendar year. Check-in after noon, check-out before 10 am.

season.note: 'open seasonally, typically from the Wednesday before Memorial Day to Columbus Day'. NPS's page still gives the 2025 dates, May 21 through Oct 13; recreation.gov's 2026 rate season ran May 20 to Oct 11.

sites.note: Of 202 sites only Loop C's 30 RV sites list 30 or 35 ft; Loop A's 20 RV-permitted sites and C15, C33 list 20 ft. The rest are walk-to or tent-only. NPS gives a 20-ft maximum, explaining it by the tight turn of the A-Loop road. One vehicle per site, all equipment on the pad. Generators only in Loop C, 8-10 am and 4-7 pm.

facilities.note: No showers in the campground (portable showers prohibited); private pay showers less than a mile away. Cell coverage is poor.

booking.note: Reservable online up to 365 days ahead and for the same day ('Reservations can be made for today'), or at 1-888-432-2267 (Mon-Fri 9-5); DNR: 'Reservations are Recommended'. Check-in between 3 p.m. and 9:30 p.m.; campsite check-out 1 p.m. Pets only in the Choptank, Elk, Miles, North East, Susquehanna and Wye loops.

sites.note: DNR: 'The park has 250 campsites' (the booking site lists 218: 167 non-electric, 23 electric, 28 full-hookup). Most RV-capable sites are back-ins of 25-30 ft, some 35-40; six North East Loop full-hookup sites are pull-throughs (20-25 ft). All of Sassafras Loop and parts of Bohemia, Choptank, Susquehanna and Wye are tent sites.

facilities.note: Each camping loop has a central bathhouse with hot showers; five bathhouses are being renovated during the 2026 season. The park store is staffed on weekends Memorial Day to Labor Day; firewood ($5) and ice ($2.50) are sold by honor box, cash or check.

Must be 21 to reserve.

name: Wind Creek State Park
note: On Lake Martin, one of the largest state-operated campgrounds in the US.  157 of 586 sites are waterfront, situated on peninsulas jutting into the lake.  --AWH

name: Edisto Beach State Park
note: 75 sites just behind the dune line on the Atlantic Ocean.  To book a single night, call the campground directly within one week of arrival.  --AWH

sites.note: 112 water/electric sites in two campgrounds, one ocean-side behind the dunes and one inland near the salt marsh (Live Oak), plus five walk-in rustic tent sites in Live Oak. Several sites take RVs up to 40 ft.

booking.note: Booked on South Carolina State Parks' own reservation site or 1-866-345-7275, up to 13 months ahead. 'Camping reservations must be made for a minimum of two nights'; per the --AWH note, a single night can be booked by calling the park within a week of arrival. Maximum 14 nights per site (cumulative up to 42 of 49). Same-day reservations go through the park. Check-in 2 pm, check-out noon.

name: Hillman Ferry Campground
note:
USFS campground in Land Between the Lakes National Recreation Area on Kentucky Lake.  Many sites are lakefront on peninsulas.  --AWH
Five areas (A, B, C, D, T) on wooded ridges and peninsulas, with a swimming beach, two boat ramps reserved for campers, a fishing dock, an archery range and bike trails. About 100 sites go to the seasonal lottery. Water at the sites can be shut off in spring and fall. Some sites take only rigs up to 15-20 ft. --Claude

fees.note: Basic $12-16; 30A electric $26, 50A $28; electric/water $34-36; full hookup $40-42.

sites.note: The county gives 86 campsites on a 15-acre peninsula; ReserveAmerica sells 56 (30 'Standard Waterfront', 26 'Standard') plus 11 'Tent Only Waterfront'. Up to one camper/RV and one tent, or two tents, per site; six people.

hookups.source: https://experienceoconee.com/parks/south-cove-park ('86 campsites with water and electricity on each site'), captured 2026-10-14

The county's reservations page instead says 'Camping rates are $25/night for standard sites and $30/night waterfront sites all taxes included', residents $5 off.

hookups.note: Every campsite has water and electricity; the county does not state the amperage.

facilities.note: Two bath houses serve the campground.

booking.note: Reserve on ReserveAmerica up to 11 months ahead; county residents up to 12 months in person, and must call the PRT office (864-888-1488) once to set up the resident rate. Waterfront sites need a 2-night minimum; Memorial Day, July 4th and Labor Day need 3 nights at every site. Maximum 30 days March-October, 60 days November-February. Gate closed 10 pm-5 am.

booking.note: Not reservable: first-come, first-served, paid on site with recreation.gov Scan & Pay. No more than 14 days in any 30 at Sutton Lake; one site per primary occupant. Check-in 6 p.m., check-out 5 p.m. per the site record.

note: USACE campground below Tionesta Dam along Tionesta Creek (Pittsburgh District). Reservation required, on recreation.gov only. 124 full-hookup sites (63 with 50-amp). A few sites (e.g. 46, 48) back up above the creek; not step-to-water lakefront. --Claude

name: Loleta Recreation Area
note: Allegheny NF campground along East Branch Millstone Creek with a pond and small beach. Reservable online; Lower Loop has 30-amp electric and fits larger RVs (Upper Loop not recommended for big rigs). Per the official FS site map the numbered RV sites sit across Loleta Road from the creek, and the pond/beach by the bath house isn't adjacent to the RV loop either, so not waterfront for RVs. --Claude

Group sites must be reserved.

name: Dingmans Campground
note: NPS concessionaire campground on federal land within Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area, on Route 209 at Dingmans Ferry. Book direct through the campground's own Campspot link, not Recreation.gov. Riverfront sites on the Delaware are tent-only (no vehicles); the 35 RV sites are in the forest, set back, with 20/30/50-amp electric and water (no sewer; dump stations at the two bathhouses). Dry campground, no generators, no cell service. Senior/Access passes 50% off up to 2 nights, 10% military. --Claude

booking.note: Online booking on Campspot ('Camping Reservations for Holiday weekends require a two-night minimum stay'). Cancel 7+ days out for a refund less $10; none after.

name: Denton Hill State Park (Nine Mile Loop)
note: DCNR state park campground (Nine Mile Loop) along Nine Mile Run, operated by the Denton Go concession under DCNR. RV sites with electric; flush toilets and warm showers in the Adventure Center. One of PA's highest parks. --Claude

sites.note: Denton Go says there are currently 10 RV sites, all rustic back-in gravel pads along Nine Mile Run; DCNR describes the Nine Mile Loop as 11 sites. Site-specific RV size limits are only shown in the Firefly booking engine.

facilities.note: Restrooms and warm showers are in the Adventure Center, not in the camping loop.

booking.note: Run by the Denton Go concession, not on the state parks' ReserveAmerica system (DCNR: 'Currently, this park has no reservable facilities'). RV sites book through Denton Go's Firefly Reservations page; phone (814) 754-9013.

Sites P1 and P2 are on a small loop near the lake's west end, beside SR 159 behind a board fence; P3-P5 are along the campground road to the east, back from the water. The agency gives no length. A 2021 Dyrt reviewer in a travel trailer found P1-P3 unlevel and the highway noisy. --Claude

facilities.note: Pit toilets; drinking water is seasonal. Table, fire ring and grill at each site. The forest's dump station is here.

sites.note: Lower campground (Rally Field 13-46, Riverside 104-115, The Island / Water's Edge 66-93): open grassy sites, no gravel pads, water & electric, no sewer. Upper campground (Hill Top 1-23, Oak Ridge 24-53): wooded gravel pads, 27 of them full hookup; 'Campers or RVs over 32 feet are NOT recommended' there. No dry-camping sites.

booking.note: 'Reservations are accepted by phone only. Campers may also inquire about availability upon arrival.' Call 540-261-7321. Tent camping limited to 2 weeks.

AT hikers $5/night, Passport America members $20/night, seniors 62+ $1 off. 'Taxes and fees not included.'

facilities.note: Bath house serving the lower campground areas and one each for Hill Top and Oak Ridge; high water pressure (regulator recommended).

name: Lake A. Willis Robertson Campground
note: Rockbridge County recreation area near 26-acre Lake Robertson (a DWR fishing lake). ~53 sites, all electric+water, 7 pull-thrus, RVs to ~33-40 ft. Reservable, open Apr-Oct. The campground sits on hillside loops set apart from the lake (reached by a separate road); RV sites do not front or overlook the water. --Claude

sites.note: 'Sites are available to accommodate most all sizes of recreational vehicles or tents (some are pull-through).' No length is published; the 40 ft came from note prose with no operator source.

season.note: Approximate: Open April to October.

booking.note: 'Regular season reservations are accepted with deposit beginning April 1. Guests will need to register at the park headquarters.' Cash, money orders or checks only; no credit cards. Campers must be set up by 9 p.m. Superintendent's Office 540-463-4164.

name: Leeman Field Campground
note: Town of Pennington Gap RV park at the Leeman Field fairgrounds, beside the historic Leeman Field park (a seasonal pool, and a greenway with trout-stocked fishing access) and near the Stone Mountain ATV trailhead.  The RV pads sit in the open fairground lot, 150-250 m from the North Fork of the Powell River and out of sight of it; tent camping is along the river.  The fairgrounds hold ATV drag races, riding competitions, a rodeo and the Lee County Fair on some summer weekends. --Claude

booking.note: Reserve online on Campspot; long-term stays and on-site tent camping by phone, (276) 298-5177. No refunds or cancellations less than 7 days before check-in.

name: Natural Chimneys Park and Campground
note: Augusta County park on the North River. 165 sites (96 30-amp, 12 50-amp, 36 both, water+electric; dump station) plus a riverside tent section. Reservations encouraged, walk-ups welcome. Only the primitive tent (T) sites run along the river (behind the River's Edge Trail); the electric RV loops are set back in woods/field with no river view (the North River can run dry mid-summer). --Claude

sites.note: 165-site campground (144 with electric and water, a limited number also with sewer) plus a separate tents-only section near the river. 'While we don't have paved pull-through sites, a lot of our sites are easy to maneuver into.' One axled camping unit per RV site.

booking.note: Reserve on Augusta County's WebTrac site, in person or at 540-245-5753; paid in full when booked; reservations cannot be cancelled online. 'Advanced reservations are encouraged but walk-ups are welcomed if space is available.' 14 consecutive nights on RV sites (5 on tent sites), and 21 nights in any 30 days per household. Check-in 2 p.m., check-out noon; late arrivals see the camp hosts on site F1.

name: Northwest River Park Campground
note: City of Chesapeake park (Parks, Recreation & Tourism) on the 763-acre Northwest River park. 72 family sites (20/30/50-amp electric and non-electric, some pull-throughs for rigs 25 ft and longer) plus six group sites, 2 cabins and an equestrian area; hot showers, laundry, fresh water, RV pump-out, camp store. Open March 1 - November 30; reservations online (Firefly) or at the Welcome Center. Wooded inland sites; river access via trail (sites not on the water). --Claude

sites.note: 72 family campsites plus six group sites, 2 cabins and an equestrian area. 'Pull-through campsites are limited to trailers/RVs 25 feet or longer.' One trailer/RV and one tent per site.

booking.note: Reserve online through Firefly or in person at the Welcome Center, paid in full; no phone card payments. 'Reservations for campsites start January 1 for the following camping season.' 14 nights in any 30-day period. A specific site is assigned at check-in (2 p.m.); check-out noon; late check-in by prior arrangement for the gate code. The park map marks campground rentals 'Reservable; then First Come, First Served'.

name: Rural Retreat Lake Campground
note: Wythe County campground on 90-acre Rural Retreat Lake, in the woods and set back from the water, which is reached by a trail or the boat launch; no RV site fronts or overlooks the lake.  There is a boat ramp, shoreline fishing (a Virginia license or access permit is needed from age 17), a trout pond, hiking trails, a playground and picnic shelters, and a swimming pool, closed for the 2026 season; swimming in the lake isn't allowed.  A site holds 6 people at most, alcohol isn't allowed, and quiet hours run from 11 p.m. to 7 a.m.  The campground's own phone is answered May to September; from October to April call 276-223-4517. --Claude

name: Sugar Hollow Park Campground
note: City of Bristol park (~400 acres) along Beaver Creek. 75 electric (30/50-amp) sites, no cabins. Pay at entrance booth. Creekside trail; the mapped 'Beaver Creek Lake' is a TVA dry flood basin, not a standing lake. --Claude

sites.note: 75 sites, 'most will accommodate all types of recreational vehicles'; each has a picnic table, charcoal grill and fire pit. Most have electric and cable TV hookups with access to water. No tent camping except Rhythm and Roots weekend.

booking.note: Stays limited to 5 days, with a possible 5-day extension on approval. Check-in 3-8 p.m. weekdays, 10 a.m.-7:30 p.m. weekends; the registering party must show a photo driver's license with proof of current residence.

name: Washington County Park
note: Washington County Park Authority park on South Holston Lake (lake is TVA, park is county-run). About 140 full-hookup (30/50-amp) RV sites, plus tent sites, 7 shelters, swimming beach, 2 boat launches. The campground fills a narrow lake peninsula - outer-loop full-hookup RV sites back directly onto the lake (some with docks); inner sites have lake views. --Claude

sites.note: 'Size limit of campers are 10' x 42'' (2026 rules). RVs of all sizes up to that limit, from pop-ups to motor coaches; one camping vehicle and two vehicles per RV site; tents only in the separate tent area. Seasonal rates are published for site numbers 1-140.

booking.note: Book online on the Park Authority's Firefly reservation page (credit card required for all rentals) or through the front booth, 276-628-9677. 'Temporary (overnight) camping has a maximum stay of 21 days in any thirty-day period.' Check-in 3-9 p.m., check-out by noon. Seasonal sites are assigned from a waiting list.

name: Little Bennett Campground
note: Montgomery County / M-NCPPC (Little Bennett Regional Park), Clarksburg MD - the county's only public campground. Full hookups are in Loop D; the other loops are tent sites, besides canvas tents, yurts and cabins. Campground loops sit on wooded uplands, not on the water. --Claude

sites.note: 91 campsites: 22 full-hookup sites in Loop D and 63 tent sites, plus 3 canvas tent sites, 3 cabins and 3 yurts. Loop D's two-vehicle gravel parking pads run 40-74 ft; four (D49, D51, D54, D55) are pull-through, and the operator marks most as a best option for Class A or fifth-wheel rigs. No maximum rig length is published.

booking.note: Reservations through ActiveMontgomery. After 14 nights a camper must leave for at least seven nights. Cancellations must be emailed; one made 3-13 days out is refunded less $25. Check-in 1 p.m., check-out 11 a.m.

name: Watkins Glen State Park

booking.note: Suffolk County's online reservation system, with a Green Key login; on 2026-10-21 the county's Reservations page said a new reservation system is 'coming soon' and some services are temporarily unavailable. Reservations 1 to 180 days ahead (no same-day). From May 15 to Oct 15 a reservation must be at least 4 nights if it takes in Thursday-Sunday and 2 nights if Monday-Wednesday only; 2 nights the rest of the season. A reservation made with the $50 Non-Resident Reservation Green Key must be at least 4 nights at any time ('Non-Resident green key card holders may reserve throughout the season for one week maximum, except the following holiday weeks: Memorial Day ... Fourth of July ... Labor Day'). Sites not reserved go to walk-ups from 8 am, paid in full at check-in, at non-resident rates without a Green Key; the rig must be with you. Generators two hours a day, 9 am-6 pm. --Claude

name: Bee Rock Campground
note: USFS Daniel Boone NF, Bee Rock Recreation Area (off KY 192, ~18 mi W of London), along the Rockcastle River; renovated 2022. 25 wooded first-come sites, no hookups, vault toilets, water spigots. North loop is the RV-friendly side; best for compact rigs - a 23-ft motorhome fits, but call the London Ranger District before bringing anything bigger (access road has narrow/bumpy stretches near the river). Pulaski-side loop ~mid-Apr-mid-Oct, Laurel-side year-round. RV Life lists it under 'state' but it is USFS. --Claude

name: Loud Thunder Forest Preserve
note: Rock Island County Forest Preserve District's largest preserve, near Illinois City, on 167-acre Lake George (summer boat rentals) with a 12-mile trail loop. RV camping is in White Oak (back-in sites) and Deer Haven (concrete pull-throughs), both in the woods west of the lake, not on the water. Equestrians must camp in the separate Horse Corral campground. --Claude

hookups.note: Deer Haven has water and sewer at every site; White Oak's water is a hydrant shared through a valve, so bring at least 50 ft of hose.

booking.note: Reserving (WebTrac) is optional and needs two nights; sites not reserved go first-come, and every camper checks in at the park office for a permit. No refunds or site switches.

name: Johnson's Shut-Ins State Park
note: Wooded campground in five loops north of the shut-ins day-use area. The shut-ins parking lot normally fills by 10 a.m. Memorial Day to Labor Day. --Claude

booking.note: Missouri State Parks' reservation site or 877-422-6766, up to 12 months ahead. 'The campground is fully reservable'; 'Reservable sites may be available on a walk-up registration basis if the site is not reserved.' The booking system here sets a 2-night minimum for Friday and Saturday arrivals in every season checked (January, April, June and October 2027; Sunday-Thursday arrivals 1 night) - not on the agency's list of seven two-night-weekend parks. Camping is limited to any 15 days within a 30-consecutive-day period.

The river runs along the park's south edge behind a wooded strip, about 45-60 m from the nearest sites. Campers must keep a vehicle on hand for flood evacuation. --Claude

name: St. Joe State Park
note: Campground 1 at St. Joe State Park near Park Hills, the campground beside the park's off-road-vehicle riding area and the one ORV riders must use; campers without ORVs or horses may use it too. Shaded asphalt pads among oaks; four lakes, two beaches and paved bike trails elsewhere in the park. Generators are not allowed. After-hours entry by the gate code on the reservation confirmation. --Claude

name: Stockton State Park
note: Two wooded campgrounds on adjoining peninsulas of Stockton Lake near the park marina (West and East), set back in the trees from the shore. Boat and ATV trailers may park off the pad on the grass. The park closes to the public each November for a managed deer hunt. --Claude

Drive-in pads 47-62 ft; every drive-in site fits 23 ft.

name: Thousand Hills State Park
note: Two wooded campgrounds above Forest Lake near Kirksville. Campground 1 has the paved electric and family sites plus a basic loop at its east end; Campground 2's nine gravel electric sites stay open through winter. Sites sit 100 m or more back from the water through woods, though the photo of basic site 33 shows the lake through the trees. Boat and ATV trailers may park on the grass. --Claude

booking.note: Campground 1 takes reservations April 1-October 31; Campground 2 year-round.

name: Bucksaw
note: Large USACE campground on a peninsula in the Grand River arm of Truman Lake, south of Highway 7 near Clinton. Loops A and B sit in scattered shade on the peninsula's east side, loop C on the west shore. A few sites see the lake through the shoreline trees, such as A062 and the nonelectric C105 and C108, which sit about 20 m above a rocky bank. Day-use swimming beach, boat ramp, and a marina next door. --Claude

name: Sparrowfoot
note: Corps of Engineers campground on the Grand River arm of Truman Lake south of Clinton, in two wooded loops on a point: Loop A (56 sites with electric and water) and Loop B (27 electric-only sites) 400 m south. A few Loop A pads look down an open slope to a cove about 70 m off. Boat ramp, playground and laundry. --Claude

season.note: Showers and flush toilets are seasonal within that; vault toilets otherwise.

booking.note: Check-in and check-out are both 6 pm. One wheeled camper per pad, and all equipment must fit on the pad.

booking.note: One wheeled camper per pad, and all equipment must fit on the pad. A camping permit from the park booth is required before setting up.

name: Cedar Ridge
note: USACE campground on Stockton Lake near Bona. Site A07 sits about 40 m above the riprap shore with the lake in view through scattered oaks; the other shoreline sites (A10, A15, A18, A20, A22) are 50-70 m back in the woods with only glimpses of the water. --Claude

sites.note: 45 RV/trailer sites and 12 walk-to tent sites (T01-T12). A loop: 21 sites with 30-amp, 15 non-electric, listed lengths 30-60 ft (A36 20 ft). B loop: 9 sites with 50-amp, but B1-B7 are listed at 20 ft; only B8 and B9 (40 ft) take a longer rig. One wheeled unit and two tents, or three tents, per site.

season.note: The recreation.gov description says open year round. Reservations run Mar 15 - Nov 30 only; call the project office (417-276-3113) in the off season.

booking.note: Overnight camping only, with no day use. Check-in and check-out 4 p.m. 14 nights in any 30 days.

name: Crabtree Cove
note: USACE campground on a point in Stockton Lake east of Stockton. Sites A31-A34 at the tip of the point open straight onto the shore; the rest sit in oak woods, the B loop inside a road loop. --Claude

booking.note: Overnight camping only, with no day use. Check-in and check-out 4 p.m. 14 nights in any 30 days.

name: Hawker Point
note: USACE campground at Hawker Point on Stockton Lake, on a wooded point with two loops on the north and east shores. The shore-side sites of loop A (A03, A07, A09, A11) and of loop B's knob (B02, B04, B05, B06) back onto the open riprap shoreline. --Claude

sites.note: recreation.gov lists 45 sites (the description says 62): loop A 14 electric, loop B 16 electric and 7 non-electric, and loop C, 8 non-electric sites on a separate point about 2 km south. 40 of the 45 take an RV of 23 ft or more; B19 and B20 are tent/trailer only and C12, C17 and C18 are capped at 20 ft. B18 is the one pull-through.

booking.note: 14 nights in any rolling 30. Check-in and check-out 4 p.m. The park does not take reservations by phone. Day use is not allowed in the campground.

name: Orleans Trail
note: Stockton Lake Corps campground in two parts a cove apart. North holds the electric sites: the B loop on a wooded point with the lake on three sides, and the A loop around an open field by the swim beach. South (C and D loops) is non-electric. No site has a water hookup. The lake shows through the hardwoods from the point sites, across the loop road; no site is on the shore. --Claude

booking.note: Check in at the attendant booth. The non-electric South loops (C and D) were closed on the calendar in early November 2026 while the North loops stayed open.

name: Ruark Bluff East
note: Corps of Engineers campground on two wooded points of Stockton Lake. 29 of the 67 RV sites have electric, all in the B loop: 50 amp at B25-B34, 30 amp at the rest. The A sites are basic. Only some sites are on the water: A02 to A10, A12, A14, A16 and A17 on the open shore of the north point, and B06 to B13 and B37, all 10 to 35 m from the lake across mown grass; the rest are back in the woods. Water is a shared fill-up, not at the site, and is off outside Apr 16 to Sep 30. Reservations run Mar 15 to Nov 30. Boat ramp and beach just outside the entrance. --Claude

booking.note: Not on the reservation calendar Dec 1 to Mar 14; the campground stays open then, with no water.

name: Ruark Bluff West
note: Corps of Engineers campground on an open-wooded point of Stockton Lake. Sites 7-46 have electric; sites 1-6 and 47-66 are basic. Only the sites around the rim of the point are on the water: 10, 13, 15, 17, 19 and 21 (electric) and 57, 59, 61 and 63 (basic), 17 to 35 m from the lake across open grass; the rest are inland. Drinking water and electric are on only from Apr 16 to Sep 29; in the shoulder seasons (Mar 15 to Apr 15, Oct 1 to Nov 30) amenities are reduced. Camping only, no day use. Boat ramp and beach just outside the entrance. --Claude

Outer-side pads on the west loop and the south point back onto the shore across mown grass under scattered trees. Swim beach, boat ramp, playground and a separate group camp. Sites 71, 73, 75 and 87 have a second pedestal sold only when the campground is full. --Claude

name: Bluff View

Listed max vehicle length runs 33 ft (A06) to 100+ ft, most 54-90 ft. One wheeled unit and one tent per site, 10 people maximum.

name: Highway K

Five sites sit on the open flat by the ramp and beach; the rest climb a wooded hillside on paved spurs, many of them steep, and the Corps warns that access is steep and means backing a camping unit uphill. --Claude

name: Piedmont Park
note: Corps campground on a wooded hillside at the north end of Clearwater Dam, three loops stepping down to the lake with the marina, boat ramp and swim beach along the shore below. Loop C's sites 13 and 14 sit on the open bank outside the loop road and 10-12 look over it to the water; loop A's sites 14-16 are just above the swim beach; most of the rest are in timber up the slope. Two camping units and 10 people per site. --Claude

name: River Road Park
note: Corps of Engineers campground below Clearwater Dam, on both banks of the Black River's wide tailwater pool: three paved loops on a lawn under big scattered trees on the north bank, with the boat ramp, shelters and playground, and a small wooded loop on the south bank reached separately. A few sites at the east end of loop A and the south-bank loop are closest to the water. One wheeled unit per site. Trailhead of the Black River hike and bike trail. --Claude

name: Loggers Lake
note: Forest Service campground on the south-east shore of 22-acre, spring-fed Logger's Lake (electric motors only), in Shannon County south-west of Bunker; small swim beach, boat ramps and a fishing pier. Reached by 6 miles of Dent County Road 565 and 1 mile of FR 2193: the Forest Service says 4WD is not required but the last part of the road is rough and a high-clearance vehicle is highly recommended. Sites must be booked at least 5 days ahead; April and October nights are first come, first served. --Claude

sites.note: Paved back-in sites; the Forest Service recommends 30 ft at most (recreation.gov lists 40 ft on its 10 bookable sites).

name: Sutton Bluff Recreation Area
note: Forest Service campground in a bend of the West Fork of the Black River north-west of Centerville: paved spurs on a wooded bottom, the outer sites backing onto the timbered river bank with a gravel-bar beach below. It serves the Sutton Bluff ATV and motorcycle trail system, so machines ride through to the trailhead (road surfaces only) and it is busy on riding weekends. Sites 29, 32 and 33 have short spurs. In the old lead-mining district; the Forest Service capped affected campsites with clean fill in 2015 and rates the exposure risk low. The last 3 miles are on County Road 849. --Claude

booking.note: Reservations close 4 days before arrival, so a short-notice stay means one of the 8 first-come sites (3 electric); the weekend minimum may be relaxed close in. Check-in 3 pm, check-out 2 pm. No more than 8 people at a single site.

name: Council Bluff Recreation Area
note: Mark Twain National Forest campground (Wild Boar Ridge) on a wooded ridge above 440-acre Council Bluff Lake near Belgrade; the lake, Chapel Hill Beach and boat ramps are about a mile's walk or a short drive away. Sites are screened by trees and brush. --Claude

sites.note: 39 single and 7 double sites on one loop, 9 walk-in tent sites and 4 group sites (up to 50 people). RVs up to 40 ft fit at most sites; recreation.gov lists the loop sites at 30-40 ft. Two vehicles per site; 8 people per single site, 16 per double.

note: Forest Service campground near Davisville, rebuilt in 2023 on high ground above the Huzzah Creek floodplain: paved roads and spurs in the Ridge Top and Creek loops, both with 30/50A pedestals, plus a group loop and the small non-electric Pines Overlook loop. The creek, with its gravel bars and red bluffs, is a walk down from the Creek Loop; no site is on it. Flash flooding is possible along the creek. One-mile Red Bluff Trail. --Claude

note: Forest Service campground on Marble Creek off Highway E between Fredericktown and Arcadia, beside the old grist-mill dam and the Marble Creek trailhead of the Ozark Trail; remote, with no cell service. Shaded sites along the road down the hill to the loop; the six downhill-side sites at the bottom sit on a wooded slope above the creek with paths down to it. Creek access and the 4-ft mill pond are at the day-use area about 1/4 mile past the campground. --Claude

name: Silver Mines Recreation Area
note: Forest Service campground in four wooded loops above the St. Francis River, Missouri's whitewater river, at an old silver mine. Riverside, the only loop with electric, is beside the Highway D bridge with the river 50 to 75 m away through the trees; Prospect and Summit on the hilltop and Spring Branch farther north have no river views. Busiest during spring kayaking; a trail follows both banks. In the old lead-mining district: campsite soils were capped in 2015. --Claude

booking.note: Riverside (electric), Prospect and Summit sites are reservable; the Spring Branch loop (sites 57-75) is first come, first served. Check-in 3 pm, check-out 2 pm.

name: McCormack Lake Recreation Area
note: Primitive Forest Service campground at 15-acre McCormack Lake, a non-motorized lake (electric trolling motors only) south of Winona, reached by Forest Road 3155, which the Forest Service calls drivable in any vehicle. Sites are in woods along the road on the lake's west side; tables, fire rings and lantern posts, with the vault toilet at the picnic area. Pack in, pack out. A trail from the day-use area joins the Ozark Trail's Eleven Point River section. The lake has been drawn down for repairs since September 2025; short closures are possible while heavy equipment works. --Claude

sites.note: Campsite parking for two vehicles per site; no length published.

Recreation.gov takes reservations for the electric Birch loop from May 1 to Labor Day; the three primitive loops are first come, first served, in woods along the river. Eagle Bluff Trail, a 1.5-mile loop, follows the river. --Claude

name: Cobb Ridge Recreation Area
note: Forest Service campground on a ridge top in the middle of the Chadwick motorcycle and ATV trail system, about 80 miles of trails for vehicles 50 inches wide or less; most visitors come to ride, so expect engine noise and trail traffic, and it fills on fine-weather weekends. A host lives on site year-round; check in on arrival. Riding needs a separate Chadwick permit. --Claude

sites.note: 38 RV or tent sites (26 electric, 12 non-electric), 5 tent-only sites and 2 electric group sites; back-in and pull-through, asphalt pads. Some single sites take two vehicles and a towed trailer.

booking.note: 22 standard sites take reservations March through November, at least 5 days ahead; the other 16 RV sites are always first-come, and from December through February every site is first-come. Group sites book 12 months ahead. Unreserved sites pay at the fee tube (cash or check) after checking in with the host.

name: Round Spring Campground
note: National Park Service campground in the Ozark National Scenic Riverways, in woods above the Current River off Highway 19. 46 sites take an RV; only the six E sites have hookups (50-amp electric and water), the rest are basic. Posted lengths run from 20 ft (sites 12-14) to 60 ft. Eight more sites are tent-only, six of them walk-in along the spring branch. Reservation only, same-day included. In winter (Oct 16 to Apr 14) the water is off except the heated shower house. No cell signal. --Claude

name: Pulltite Campground
note: National Park Service campground strung along the Current River at the end of Highway EE south of Salem: paved road and spurs, with roughly half the sites on the river side of the road under open hardwoods. About 11 of those that fit a 23-ft rig, the even numbers from 22 to 40 chiefly, are within 30 m of the water; the others are farther back or across the road. One RV and one tent per site, six people. Seasonal camp store with ice and firewood; no dump station; no cell service. Canoe and tube outfitter at the landing. --Claude

name: Two Rivers Campground
note: Small National Park Service campground at the Jacks Fork / Current River confluence at the end of Highway V east of Eminence, inside Ozark National Scenic Riverways. The drive-in loop is set back from the river behind the park road, a lawn and the walk-in tent sites on the bank. Gravel spurs are short: one site is posted for a 28-ft RV and the rest for 20 ft or less, so a 23-ft rig has a single site to book. No dump station. Cell service is unreliable. --Claude

season.note: Flush toilets, showers and drinking water run April 15 to October 15; a vault toilet by the boat launch stays open all year.

name: Powder Mill Campground
note: National Park Service campground in an open grass field beside the Current River at the Highway 106 bridge east of Eminence: eight gravel back-in spurs off one gravel drive, four backing toward the river bank. The park calls it a backcountry campground, meaning few amenities; the approach is paved. No drinking water, no trash service. On recreation.gov it is booked under Jacks Fork / Middle Current Backcountry Campsites. Six people per site. Trails lead to Blue Spring and Owls Bend. --Claude

name: Whetstone Creek Conservation Area
note: MDC area north of Williamsburg, managed for quail and field trials. Camping is on two gravel lots at the north end of the area's main gravel road, just north of Big Lake: a larger lot at the end of a 100 m spur and a small one at the road bend, with a privy nearby; no pads, tables or water. Big Lake is about 130 m off through timber and not in view, and is under renovation (closed to boats in 2026). A second designated spot, 4 km east, is the parking lot of the rifle and pistol range. The whole area closes to all public use during managed firearms deer hunts (in 2026: October 16-18, November 19-23, December 4-6). --Claude

name: Deer Ridge Conservation Area
note: Large forested area along the North Fabius River north of Lewistown, with 48-acre Deer Ridge Lake, about 20 miles of hiking, biking and horse trails, wetland pools and a shooting range. The area map marks primitive camping at about eight spots; this entry is the lake camp, a gravel shoulder above the boat-ramp lot on the east side of Deer Ridge Lake, with other spots and a horse camp with tie-ups in the main tract. The three camps along the county roads in the north tract are their own entry. No hookups or water; quiet hours 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. Spot length is not published. --Claude

name: Lead Mine Conservation Area
note: Large Ozark upland area along the Niangua River and Jakes Creek, five miles east of Tunas. The main campground (with the only privy) is a gravel loop with back-in spurs plus sites along a spur road, in upland oak forest off the area road from the southwest entrance (Route YY), well away from the water. Four smaller primitive camping spots elsewhere, two of them at boat ramps on the Niangua; the east side (Bluff Trail entrance) has no road link to the west side. Multi-use trails are open to horses, and an unstaffed shooting range sits on the southeast side (closed Mondays). --Claude

It has a playground, a covered pavilion, propane and firewood, and a clubhouse with games, a pool table, a large TV and air conditioning; pets and children are welcome.  Monthly stays are booked by phone, not online. --Claude

name: Pheasant Acres RV Park
note: Small wooded park of gravel back-ins on Highway 8 near St. James, two miles from Maramec Spring Park. RVs must be self-contained; the shower building is for tent, pop-up, truck and van campers. Strict site rules (working RV components, nothing stored outside, photo ID and vehicle registration at check-in). --Claude

booking.note: By phone, text or email (314-303-5504), with a $10 card prepayment. 3-night minimum on 3-day holiday weekends (two nights allowed for an extra $15); 2-night minimum on Maramec Spring Park special-event weekends (one night for an extra $15). Check-in 3 pm, check-out 11 am; arrival after 11 pm $10.

name: Cedar Bluff State Park (Bluffton Area)
note: Main north-shore area of Cedar Bluff Reservoir (Bureau of Reclamation lake run by KDWP as a state park): utility loops Arapaho, Butterfield, Overland, Wagon Rut, Hoonii and Despatch, the Broken Spur group camp, open primitive areas, five cabins, two boat ramps and a swim beach. The reservoir runs low: the nearest utility sites are ~100 m from the water across the ramp lot and a wide sand apron. --Claude

min_stay.season: Memorial Day, Independence Day and Labor Day weekends (2027 rule)

booking.note: Reserved on Kansas's ReserveAmerica site (campitks.gov). 2027 holiday minimum: 3 nights over Memorial Day, July 4th and Labor Day weekends (Friday-Sunday or Saturday-Monday). Up to 14 consecutive nights in one campground, then move to another campground in the park; a 14-day extension needs the park manager's written permission, and a five-day absence is required before camping again. The Broken Spur group camp books through the park office only; several sites are held as long-term or monthly seasonal sites and are first-come when not let. Off-season the grid shows every site as walk-up.

sites.note: 119 designated utility sites in the Bluffton Area: Arapaho 20, Butterfield 16, Overland 30, Wagon Rut 30, Hoonii 5, Despatch 6 and the 12-site Broken Spur group camp. Plus open undesignated primitive camping (KDWP counts 250) and designated primitive sites 281-288. 23 utility sites are pull-through; listed lengths run 50-180 ft (Wagon Rut 158 at 180 ft). Camp hosts in 101, 102 and 201; monthly seasonal sites 103-106; long-term sites 051-052, 156, 163 and 301-305.

season.note: Open year round; off-season the sites are walk-up.

name: Eisenhower State Park
note: KDWP park on the north shore of Melvern Lake, in tallgrass prairie and woods: five utility campgrounds (WestPoint has 15 equestrian sites with corrals for the 20-mile Crooked Knee Horse Trail), primitive areas, cabins and yurts, swim beach, boat ramps and dock, disc golf, archery trail, Ike's General Store at Doud. Free WiFi at the park office. --Claude

Other sites first come, first served. Up to 14 consecutive nights in one campground. 2027 holiday minimum 3 nights.

name: Perry State Park
note: KDWP state park on the southwest shore of Perry Reservoir, 4 mi north of US-24 on K-237. The reservable hookup loops are Lakeview (pinned: 50 A, mostly pull-through, beside the swim-beach lot and cabins) with Cougar Pass and Cottonwood Bridge just south and Eagle Landing about 1 km north; Hobie Cove primitive, more first-come sites, and the horse-only Wild Horse equestrian campground are elsewhere in the park. The Hobie Cove shower house is permanently closed. --Claude

name: Webster State Park
note: Campgrounds along the north and west shores of Webster Reservoir west of Stockton: Eagle Landing (long pull-throughs on a peninsula), Old Marina and Hill Top in the west cluster, plus Lake View on its own spur off the shore drive; two modern cabins, swim beaches, and non-reservable primitive areas. Rock Point (by the east entry) and Goose Flat (south shore, by the dam) are their own entries. Irrigation reservoir often sits well below conservation pool, so the walk to the water is long at low levels. --Claude

name: Barber State Fishing Lake
note: KDWP state fishing lake at the north edge of Medicine Lodge in the Gyp Hills. KDWP allows camping throughout the area with no marked sites: campers use the gravel shore roads, turnarounds and points (a 2019 camper found most spots better for smaller units, with a couple of big ones on the loop across the lake). Group picnic shelter, two boat ramps (boats for fishing only) and a fishing dock; the northern 80 acres are open to hunting. --Claude

booking.note: Free, first come; no reservations at Kansas state fishing lakes. Seven consecutive days at a state fishing lake, then five days away (K.A.R. 115-8-9(c), amended 2023); a longer stay needs a written KDWP permit.

name: Fall River State Park (Fredonia Bay)
note: West side of Fall River SP on the 2,450-acre reservoir, between Cross Timbers woods and Flint Hills prairie: the Fredonia Bay and Casner Creek campgrounds, Gobbler's Knob cabins, swim beach and trails. No staffed office on site (managed from Cross Timbers). --Claude

name: Prairie Dog State Park
note: On Keith Sebelius Reservoir near Norton. --Claude

name: Elk City State Park
note: KDWP park on the east shore of 4,500-acre Elk City Reservoir near Independence, in oak-hickory woods and prairie (RV Life mislabels it a city park). Four campgrounds along one park road: Sunset Point on the shore (sites 312-313 at the water's edge), Comfort Cove, Prairie Meadow (long pull-throughs on open grass) and Timber Road. Swim beach, boat ramps, trails. --Claude

hookups.note: 11 full-hookup sites (Comfort Cove 201-211), 75 water and electric, 1 electric only; all but Sunset Point 312-313 (30 A) have 50-A service.

min_stay.season: Memorial Day, Independence Day and Labor Day weekends (2027 rule)

booking.note: Reserved site-specific on Kansas's ReserveAmerica site (campitks.gov). 2027 holiday minimum: 3 nights over Memorial Day, July 4th and Labor Day weekends (Friday-Sunday or Saturday-Monday). Up to 14 consecutive nights in one campground, then move to another campground in the park; a 14-day extension needs the park manager's written permission, and a five-day absence is required before camping again. Check-out 2 pm; call ahead if arriving after the office closes at 4 pm. Prairie Meadow 119-128 and Timber Road 401 are long-term sites.

name: Geary State Fishing Lake
note: KDWP state fishing lake and wildlife area 10 mi south of Junction City off US 77; primitive camping in designated areas by the 99-acre lake, with picnic shelters (several with fire-ring grills) through the camping area, a boat ramp at the southeast corner and a double vault toilet. Gravel drive-in access. Busy in summer (a June 2026 camper found every site full). --Claude

booking.note: Seven consecutive nights at a state fishing lake, then five days away; one extension of up to seven more nights by written permit from KDWP if sites are vacant (K.A.R. 115-8-9(c), amended 2023).

name: Crawford State Park
note: KDWP park on a 150-acre CCC-built lake at the Ozark edge: campgrounds on Oak Point peninsula and the Rocky Cove shore, shoreline primitive pads, five lakefront cabins, swim beach, two boat ramps, trails, marina restaurant (weekends). Through summer 2027, reach it from the south via Girard (K-7 north of the park is closed). --Claude

hookups.note: About half the electric sites have 50-A service with water (Rocky Cove's odd numbers, Oak Point 140-169); the rest are 30-A electric only. No sewer hookups; one dump station.

name: Glen Elder State Park
note: KDWP park on the north shore of 12,500-acre Waconda Lake (Glen Elder Reservoir). Reservable water/electric sites, mostly 50-amp, in four campgrounds: Kanza (66, the largest, by the marina cove), Kiowa (20, just north of Kanza), Cheyenne (36, 0.8 km east) and Kaw (18, 1 km west), on concrete, asphalt or gravel pads; primitive camping in Kanza and Cheyenne and in several unreserved areas (Osage, Sioux, Pawnee). Shower houses at Kanza, Cheyenne and Kaw; full-service marina; two rental cabins. --Claude

min_stay.season: Memorial Day, Independence Day and Labor Day weekends (2027 rule)

booking.note: The 140 water/electric sites in Kanza, Kiowa, Cheyenne and Kaw reserve site-specific on Kansas's ReserveAmerica site (campitks.gov); unreserved sites allow self-registration on arrival, and the primitive areas (Osage, Sioux, Pawnee and others) take no reservations. In winter only the Kanza and Cheyenne concrete sites are open, first come first served. 2027 holiday minimum: 3 nights over Memorial Day, July 4th and Labor Day weekends. Up to 14 consecutive nights in one campground, then move to another campground in the park.

name: Meade State Park
note: KDWP park on 80-acre Meade State Lake (no-wake, fishing boats only) in the southwest Kansas high plains: 42 water/electric sites in four loops (Lakeview on the north shore, Cedar, Cottonwood, Sagebrush - the last 8 are long-term sites) plus primitive areas around the lake, shower house, swim beach, tornado shelters. Open year round; reserve on campitks.gov or self-register. A May 2026 wildfire closed some primitive areas and the trails; the park reopened May 21, 2026 with the only entrance from Highway 23 - check with the office. --Claude

The 8 Sagebrush sites are long-term sites. 2027 holiday minimum: 3 nights over Memorial Day, July 4th and Labor Day weekends. Up to 14 consecutive nights in one campground, then move to another campground in the park.

name: Milford State Park
note: On the southeast shore of Milford Reservoir, Kansas's largest lake. The campgrounds sit in two clusters about 2 km apart on the park road: Woodland Hills (the pin), Hickory Hollow, Walnut Grove and Cedar Point (a marina peninsula whose west-row sites sit just above the water) to the north; Eagle Ridge, Prairie View (on a cove), Sunset Ridge and Rusty Windmill to the south. Cabins and equestrian camping too. --Claude

hookups.note: Full hookups at Eagle Ridge (21), Hickory Hollow (29), Rusty Windmill (2) and one site each at Woodland Hills and Sunset Ridge; water and electric at Cedar Point (34), Woodland Hills (29) and Prairie View (20); all 50/30/20 A. KDWP counts 60 three-utility and 91 two-utility sites.

Up to 14 consecutive nights in one campground, then move to another campground in the park. 31 sites are marked long-term.

Swim beach and showers nearby. --Claude

name: Atchison State Fishing Lake
note: KDWP state fishing lake (66 acres) in the Independence Creek valley, 2.5 miles of hilly gravel off K-7 that can be slick when wet. Primitive camping on the south and east sides, first come, no hookups; restrooms and picnic areas, rural water at the SE entrance. Seven-day limit. --Claude

sites.note: Undesignated primitive spots on the south and east shores; KDWP posts no rig limit. The access is 2.5 miles of hilly gravel road from K-7 that can be slick when wet.

booking.note: Free, first come; no reservations at Kansas state fishing lakes (only the KDWP cabin books). Seven consecutive days, then five days away (K.A.R. 115-8-9(c), amended 2023); a longer stay needs a written KDWP permit.

name: McPherson State Fishing Lake
note: KDWP state fishing lake 6 miles north and 2 miles west of Canton, managed with the adjoining Maxwell Wildlife Refuge (bison and elk). The camping is the wooded campground along the gravel shore road on the west side of the lake, with gravel pull-offs, fire rings and vault toilets near the fishing piers and the west boat ramp. The open field with the herringbone pull-ins west of that road is Battlehill RV Park, a private park, not the state lake. Fishing boats only; no alcohol or firearms; trash to the dumpster by the west toilet. --Claude

name: Anthony City Lake
note: City of Anthony's 153-acre lake 1 mi NW of town. Four RV camping areas: A (33 sites) and B (22, on the peninsula) on the east side by the stage, restrooms, showerhouse and boat ramp; C (18) on the west shore by the golf course; D (1 site, no water) 0.75 mi north. Every site is 30 A or 30/50 A with shared water hookups; no sewer; dump station south of the dam. Tent camping in the unimproved areas. Showerhouse replacement planned for 2027. --Claude

booking.note: Book on Campspot or at the City office (not for holidays); walk-ups pay before pulling into a vacant site (online or with the camp host). May 1-September 30: 14 nights at most in A, B and D and 28 in C, then 5 days away; no limit October 1-April 30. Check-in and check-out 2 pm. Reservations are non-refundable.

name: Boyd Lake State Park (Cottonwood)
note: CPW park on the west shore of Boyd Lake at the NE edge of Loveland; Cottonwood Campground sits ~100 yd back from the shore behind a treeline and the paved lake-loop path, with open reservoir views from the perimeter sites. Marina and swim beach are separate areas north of the campground. Boating is closed for the rest of 2026 for low water (hand-launched craft and swimming still allowed). --Claude

hookups.note: All sites have 20/30/50-amp electric; 44 sites in loop A are full hookup (water and sewer).

sites.note: Cottonwood Campground, loops A-F. CPW's booking site lists 200 campsites (152 electric + 4 electric ADA, 42 full hookup + 2 full-hookup ADA; 124 pull-through, 74 back-in); the park's camping page still says '140 paved pull-through sites, equipped for vehicles up to 40 feet'. Per-site lengths on the booking site: 60 ft (loops B-F pull-throughs), 40 and 55 ft (loop A). Two sleeping units (one hard-sided) and six people per site; all vehicles and trailers must stay on the asphalt. Entry gate clearance 14 ft 2 in.

facilities.note: Three restroom buildings with showers; only the A/B loop restroom is open in winter. Laundry in the camper services building except in winter. Playgrounds, horseshoe pits.

season.note: Winter camping November 1 to March 31: loop A only open restroom (A/B), no laundry.

booking.note: A reservation is required: cpwshop.com or 1-800-244-5613, up to six months ahead. Display a vehicle pass. Check-in 1 p.m., check-out noon. An unoccupied first night is a no-show unless you call the park; the site may be resold.

name: St. Vrain State Park
note: CPW park off I-25 at Longmont, built around a chain of ponds, with views of Longs Peak; sites on level concrete pads. Oct 2026: a paving project closed the south campground access road, so full-hookup sites 42-87 are unavailable (CPW: trails closed through November, possibly into December). --Claude

hookups.note: Every site has 50-amp electric; the 44 full-hookup sites (Bald Eagle Point, Coot Pond, Kestrel, Red Tail Pond, Tail Feathers) add water and sewer, the 37 in Mallard, Pelican and Sandpiper are electric only.

facilities.note: Flush toilets and showers in the three electric loops; vault toilets in Kettle Creek. Camper registration buildings in the campground.

entrance.name: State Wildlife Area pass
entrance.waived_by: an annual Colorado fishing, small-game, big-game or turkey license

fees.note: Two people, one night: $40. There is no camping fee; the cost is Colorado Parks and Wildlife's State Wildlife Area pass, which everyone 16 or older needs on the property. 2 people x 2 one-day passes x $10 = $40: a one-day pass is valid only on the date printed on it, and a night spans the arrival and departure dates. Nobody holding an annual Colorado fishing, small-game, big-game or turkey license needs the pass, and neither do under-16s. An annual SWA pass is $43.87 (March 1 to March 31 of the next year; youth/senior $11.96). The pass is per person, not per vehicle; buy it online or in the My CPW app, up to 60 days ahead. (AWH 2026-10-11: price as two people, one night.)

fees.note: Two people, one night: $40. There is no camping fee; the cost is Colorado Parks and Wildlife's State Wildlife Area pass, which everyone 16 or older needs on the property. 2 people x 2 one-day passes x $10 = $40: a one-day pass is valid only on the date printed on it, and a night spans the arrival and departure dates. Nobody holding an annual Colorado fishing, small-game, big-game or turkey license needs the pass, and neither do under-16s. An annual SWA pass is $43.87 (March 1 to March 31 of the next year; youth/senior $11.96). The pass is per person, not per vehicle; buy it online or in the My CPW app, up to 60 days ahead. (AWH 2026-10-11: price as two people, one night.)

name: Stagecoach State Park (Pinnacle)
note: Largest of Stagecoach State Park's four campgrounds, on the north shore of Stagecoach Reservoir near the marina, south of Steamboat Springs. The only loop open in winter. --Claude

sites.note: 36 electric sites (one ADA) plus a group site; 32 pull-throughs to 40 ft, 5 back-ins to 30 ft.

facilities.note: Park amenities: water, coin-operated showers and the dump station are summer only; flush toilets, showers, dump and drinking water are shut October 31 to May 15, leaving vault toilets.

season.note: Winter camping is limited to 4-6 Pinnacle sites with electric and vault toilets, by reservation.

booking.note: A reservation is required: cpwshop.com or 1-800-244-5613, up to six months ahead. 14 days within a 28-day period; six people per site; one hard-sided RV, trailer or van and one tent, or two tents. Check-in 1 p.m., check-out noon. Display a vehicle pass. Reservations are taken May 15 to September 30 park-wide; in winter only Pinnacle takes them (4-6 sites).

name: Pearl Lake State Park
note: Quiet wakeless lake near Clark. The lower loop runs along the shoreline, the upper loop sits on a ridge with lake and mountain views. Two drive-up yurts with electric heat, reservable all year with a 2-night minimum; winter camping is at Steamboat Lake SP's marina lot. --Claude

sites.note: CPW says 36 campsites plus two yurts; cpwshop lists 34 basic sites (15 lower loop, 19 upper loop) and the two yurts. Site lengths 16-30 ft: 10 sites take 30 ft, 13 more take 24-28 ft; a few pull-throughs. Gravel, level parking areas. One accessible site.

season.note: Summer camping from the Friday before Memorial Day (May 28 in 2027) to September 30, fall camping October 1 - November 1; closed to camping in winter (the two yurts stay open all year).

booking.note: Reservation required, on cpwshop.com or 1-800-244-5613, up to six months ahead for summer (Friday before Memorial Day - September 30). October 1 - November 1 it is still reservation-only but bookable only on the day of arrival (cpwshop, the Steamboat Lake visitor center, or by phone). 14 days in any 28; one camping unit, two vehicles and six people per site. A no-show site may be resold after 24 hours.

name: Rifle Gap State Park
note: Five loops around Rifle Gap Reservoir off one park road from the main entrance, at most ~0.9 km apart: Lakeview (full hookups, atop the north mesa with an open overlook of the reservoir, plus walk-in tent sites), Cottonwood (east end by the main entrance and the dump station, flat on the shoreline apron, the park's most natural shade), Cedar (on a rise to the west), Sage (no hookups, central, near the boat ramp and swim beach; the only loop where ATVs/OHVs may ride out onto BLM land) and Pinon (five secluded no-hookup sites among pinyon and juniper, with hammock stands). A 1.5-mile trail links Lakeview to Cottonwood. Merged from three per-loop entries 2026-10-26 (AWH). --Claude

sites.note: cpwshop sells 82 sites: Lakeview 32 full-hookup (2 ADA pull-throughs, 55-95 ft) + 10 walk-in tent; Cottonwood 7 (6 electric with water + 1 full-hookup ADA, 50-60 ft); Cedar 14 electric (28-85 ft); Sage 14 no-hookup (60-115 ft, pull-throughs); Pinon 5 no-hookup (20-30 ft). The 2024 brochure says 46, 8, 15, 15 and 5. Most hookup sites are back-ins.

facilities.note: Flush toilets and coin-operated showers in Lakeview, Cottonwood and Cedar; Sage and Pinon have restrooms only, with drinking water in the middle of Sage. The dump station is near Cottonwood. Ask the park office which amenities stay open in winter.

season.note: CPW: camping year-round at Rifle Gap. Only Cottonwood takes bookings all winter (see booking.note).

booking.note: A reservation is required to camp: cpwshop.com or 1-800-244-5613, up to six months ahead. Booking seasons by loop (cpwshop, 2026-27): Cottonwood all year; Cedar, Sage and Pinon April 1 - November 30; Lakeview April 15 - November 6. 14 days in any 28-day period; six people per site.

name: Sylvan Lake State Park
note: Colorado Parks and Wildlife, Sylvan Lake State Park, 16 mi south of Eagle by Brush Creek Road. Two loops off the one park entrance, nearest sites ~70 m apart: Elk Run on West Brush Creek below the dam, and Fisherman's Paradise on the north shore of the 42-acre lake east of the dam. No cell service. Merged from two per-loop entries 2026-10-28 (AWH). --Claude

sites.note: 42 sites in two loops. Elk Run: 32 sites (001-034, no 011 or 017; 016 is ADA), maximum vehicle lengths 20-120 ft, only 001 under 25 ft. Fisherman's Paradise: 10 sites (035-044; 042 is ADA), every one 40 ft, driveways 35-55 ft. Pull-throughs in both loops. Plus a group site for up to 60, mid-May through September. Gravel driveways.

facilities.note: Summer only: flush toilets and coin showers. Winter (Nov 1 - May 14): vault toilets and dump station only. Late 2026 drought notice: spigots, showers and flush toilets shut off, limited potable water at the visitor center; fill tanks before arriving.

season.note: Open year-round; winter camping Nov 1 - May 14 is first come, first served. CPW does not say which loop stays open in winter.

booking.note: Reservation required: cpwshop.com or 1-800-244-5613, up to six months ahead; display a vehicle pass. Winter camping (Nov 1 - May 14) is first come, first served, paid at the self-serve station at the park entrance. 14 days in any 28; up to 6 people, 2 vehicles and one camping unit per site. Check-in 1 p.m., check-out noon.

name: Moraine Park Campground
note: Rocky Mountain NP campground in Moraine Park, the Big Thompson River meadow below the high peaks. About 236 sites in five loops, many not level. Solar shower stalls (bring your own bag). Rangers may enforce keeping RV windows closed due to bears. --Claude

sites.note: 236 bookable sites in the recreation.gov catalog (46 electric) plus 22 management sites. Vehicles over 40 ft, including tow vehicle and hitch, are not permitted; many sites are for tents or vans only, so check each site's length.

facilities.note: Two solar shower stalls: campers bring their own solar shower bag, no water in the stalls. Dump station and fresh water fill near the ranger station, open in winter too. Firewood sold in summer.

booking.note: Summer season: reservation only on recreation.gov (no in-person booking), some sites up to 6 months ahead and some on short-term release; the reservation includes the Timed Entry + Bear Lake Road permit from 1 p.m. on arrival day. Winter season: first come, first served, paid by Scan & Pay or at an entrance station. Summer limit is 7 nights in total across all RMNP campgrounds.

name: Glacier Basin Campground
note: Rocky Mountain NP campground on Bear Lake Road, with peak views; fir and pine with open meadows. A free park shuttle stop in the campground serves the Bear Lake Road trailheads. Generators allowed 7:30-10 a.m. and 4-8:30 p.m. in Loops A, B, D and part of C (not Loop C sites 76-104 or the group sites). --Claude

sites.note: 150 campsites: 13 group sites (no RVs or trailers in the group loop) and 73 tent-only, leaving about 65 standard sites that take RVs. Catalog lengths on those run 15-35 ft; about 48 take 25 ft or more. Parallel, back-in and pull-through spurs.

facilities.note: One solar shower stall; bring your own solar shower bag. Food storage lockers; firewood sold in the campground 5-8 p.m. (one rec.gov notice says it is not sold - the two notices conflict).

booking.note: Reservation only (recreation.gov or 1-877-444-6777); no same-day sales and no booking in person at the park. Some sites open 6 months ahead on a rolling window, some only 2 weeks or 1 week ahead; group sites 1 year ahead. From May 1 to October 15 the 7-night limit is 7 nights in total across all RMNP campgrounds.

name: Aspenglen Campground
note: Rocky Mountain NP, just inside the Fall River Entrance west of Estes Park on US-34; pine and fir forest with meadows, paved loops, a few walk-to tent sites. --Claude

facilities.note: Flush toilets and drinking water in season only; no RV fresh-water fill or dump (use Moraine Park or Glacier Basin). Generators only in Loop C, 7:30-10 a.m. and 4-8:30 p.m. No wifi; cell service unreliable.

booking.note: Reservation only. Some sites open 6 months ahead on a rolling window, others only 2 weeks or 1 week ahead. The campground reservation includes the park's timed-entry (Timed Entry + Bear Lake Road) reservation: enter from 1 p.m. on the first day and show the confirmation at the entrance station. Seven nights a year maximum.

name: Timber Creek Campground
note: Rocky Mountain NP's only west-side campground, along the Colorado River 8 mi north of the Grand Lake Entrance on Trail Ridge Road. Generators 7:30-10 a.m. and 4-8:30 p.m.; food in the lockers. --Claude

booking.note: Reservation only (recreation.gov, its app, or 877-444-6777); no same-day sales and no booking at the campground. Some sites open 6 months ahead on a rolling window, others 2 weeks or 1 week ahead. The reservation includes a timed-entry permit (not Bear Lake Road); the park entrance fee is separate. 7 nights total park-wide May 1 - Oct 15. Check-in 1 p.m., check-out noon.

name: Pinon Flats Campground
note: Great Sand Dunes NP & Preserve campground among piñon pines and sagebrush a mile north of the visitor center, with views of the dunefield and the Sangre de Cristo peaks. Paved, historic-design loops. Generators only 8-10 a.m., noon-2 p.m. and 5-7 p.m. Medano Creek at the foot of the dunes runs in late spring and summer. --Claude

sites.note: 88 sites in Loops 1 and 2 (52 RV, 34 tent-only) plus 3 tent-only group sites. RV, or vehicle plus trailer, limited to 35 ft combined; the NPS says 'RVs or trailers up to 33 feet may fit in a few sites'. Most sites are small and unlevel: per-site lengths on recreation.gov run 15-35 ft, 28 of the 54 RV-usable sites at 25 ft or more. Mostly back-in or parallel, 2 pull-throughs. If the rig is longer than the site booked there is no alternative site.

facilities.note: All seasonal. Restrooms with sinks and a dishwashing basin; bear boxes; firewood and ice sold in summer. Limited cell signal; nearest wifi in Alamosa.

booking.note: Reservation required for every site, on recreation.gov or 877-444-6777, up to 3 months ahead (shortened from 6 months for 2026 while the campground is improved); no first-come camping, no waiting list. Reservable 'Peak Season' 2027: April 1 - October 30. Pick a site that fits the rig - there is no alternative site if it doesn't. 8 people, 2 vehicles per site (a trailer counts).

name: Morefield Campground
note: Mesa Verde NP campground in Morefield Canyon, 4.5 mi inside the park entrance, among Gambel oaks; deer and wild turkeys. Trailers/towed vehicles not permitted beyond the campground. Concessioner-run (Aramark). --Claude

name: South Rim Campground
note: Black Canyon of the Gunnison NP campground on the South Rim, a mile from the South Rim Visitor Center; sites fairly close together, partly shaded by tall scrub oak. Loop B is the electric loop. After the 2025 South Rim Fire only limited non-electric sites are open in 2026, electric hookups are unavailable and some areas are closed (NPS, 2026-10-27). No generators; no firewood collection or sales. --Claude

sites.note: 88 sites in Loops A, B and C; 23 with electric (Loop B). Loop B takes RVs or car-plus-trailer up to 55 ft combined, most Loop B sites about 30 ft; Loops A and C typically fit a 23-ft RV. recreation.gov's catalog: Loop A sites 16-65 ft (most 27 ft or more, several pull-throughs), Loop B 16-50 ft, Loop C mostly 21 ft.

facilities.note: Drinking water seasonal (about mid-May to mid-September/October); no water for RV tanks. Bear boxes, amphitheater, seasonal host.

booking.note: Reserve on recreation.gov. The NPS record counts 74 reservable and 14 first-come sites but also says all sites in all loops must be reserved; recreation.gov says the campground is first-come in winter, while its rate table now sells 'Peak Season' through March 31, 2027. 14 consecutive nights, 30 days a year; 8 people and 2 vehicles per site; 2 sites per booking.

name: Elk Creek Campground
note: Curecanti NRA's largest campground, on the north shore of Blue Mesa Reservoir off US-50; paved, very few trees. Marina and visitor center nearby. --Claude

sites.note: NPS: 155 sites (14 tent-only, 35 electric in Loops C and D); RVs to 55 ft, trailers to 35 ft. The recreation.gov catalog lists 150 (16 tent-only, 38 'Standard Electric', 11 pull-throughs) with lengths to 62 ft. Blue Mesa Adventure Pods in Loop C are booked only through the concessioner (Elk Creek Marina LLC).

facilities.note: Flush toilets, potable water and the dump station are seasonal; vault toilets year-round. Paved campground with very few trees; seasonal amphitheater programs and host.

booking.note: 'All sites can be reserved on Recreation.gov and can be made the same day of arrival. Dates are released on a 6-month rolling basis.' NPS lists 111 sites reservable and 49 first-come; cell service is unreliable, so book before arriving. Up to 14 nights in a rolling 30 days; at most 2 sites held.

name: Lake Fork Campground
note: Curecanti NRA (National Park Service) campground on Blue Mesa Reservoir near the dam, on CO 92 just off US 50 about 27 mi west of Gunnison. Set up for RVs: paved loops, little room for tents outside the walk-in sites. Lake Fork boat ramp with mussel inspection nearby. --Claude

sites.note: recreation.gov lists 83 sites: 78 RV/trailer sites (paved spurs 20-52 ft, 16 of them 50-ft pull-throughs) and walk-in tent sites 46-50 (RVs may not use their parking). NPS gives 90 sites in all and 'Small to large trailers can be accommodated'.

facilities.note: Flush toilets, water and the dump station are seasonal (summer). Fish-cleaning station. Cell reception unreliable.

booking.note: Reserve on recreation.gov ('Dates are released on a 6-month rolling basis'); same-day booking allowed. NPS recommends reserving because cell service is poor and first-come sites may be unavailable. The NPS pages disagree on walk-ups (see flags), so fcfs is not recorded. 14 consecutive nights.

name: Stevens Creek Campground
note: Curecanti NRA campground on the north shore of Blue Mesa Reservoir off US-50, 12 mi west of Gunnison; open sage with no shade. The Stevens Creek boat ramp and its inspection station are closed (2026); the nearest ramps are Elk Creek and Lake Fork. --Claude
