booking.note: First-come, first-served: no site can be reserved. Register and pay on site with the Recreation.gov app's Scan & Pay (download it before arriving). Loop A: 14 nights in a 30-day period; other loops 30 consecutive days. Up to 8 people and two camping units per site. Check-in and check-out 1 p.m.

name: Ponderosa Campground
note: Curecanti NRA campground at the northwest end of the Soap Creek arm of Blue Mesa Reservoir, with wide views and solitude. Access is 7 miles of gravel Soap Creek Road (CR 721): passable to trailers and RVs when dry, impassable when wet. --Claude

facilities.note: No water. Trash/recycling and food-storage lockers in season; horse corral in the upper loop; boat ramp (hand-launch only when no inspection is offered).

name: Cimarron Campground
note: Curecanti NRA campground on US-50 between mile markers 112 and 113, ~20 mi east of Montrose, at the old narrow-gauge railroad town of Cimarron beside the Cimarron River; the Cimarron Canyon rail exhibit is next door and Crystal Reservoir at Morrow Point Dam is ~1.5 mi away. Rarely fills. No cell service; an emergency 911 phone is by the visitor center door. --Claude

sites.note: Tents to medium-sized RVs; NPS gives no length. Paved parking pads, mostly back-in, a few parallel.

facilities.note: Potable water is seasonal and may be off when nights stay below freezing.

name: Dry Gulch Campground

name: Saddlehorn Campground
note: Colorado National Monument's only campground, by the Saddlehorn Visitor Center on the canyon-rim mesa, 4 mi from the Fruita (west) entrance and 19 mi from Grand Junction (east). Rim Rock Drive's tunnels lie either side: clearance 10'6" at the curb edge to 16' at the centerline, and a vehicle must stay in its lane. No wood fires; generators banned in Loop C. --Claude

sites.note: 79 sites in three loops: A (19), B (31), C (29). 40 ft maximum in Loops A and B, tow vehicle and trailer combined; Loop C is 19 ft maximum with no trailers (sites 52-80). Some pull-throughs.

facilities.note: No dump station in the monument: the Fruita Welcome Center (I-70 exit 19) has a free dump and water refill year-round. Do not fill RV tanks at the campground faucets. Pay phone and free wifi at the visitor center.

booking.note: Every site, same-day ones included, must be reserved on recreation.gov (app, website or 1-877-444-6777); sites open at 8 a.m. Mountain. Three windows: 6 months ahead (Loop B outer sites), 2 weeks ahead (B inner sites, C 70-80) and same day (Loop A this summer for maintenance, C 52-69). 14 nights per calendar year in total. Groups of 15+ through the park (970-858-3617 ext. 332, colm_campground@nps.gov). Checkout 11 a.m.; a reservation is held until checkout the day after arrival.

name: Gates of Lodore Campground
note: Dinosaur NM campground at the Green River's Gates of Lodore boat ramp at the head of Lodore Canyon (Colorado side), popular with rafters the night before launching; some sites shaded. Remote: 106 mi from the Canyon Visitor Center. Access is CO-318 from Maybell, then about 6 mi of unpaved Moffat CR 34N/34 (NPS: 'All vehicles OK in good weather'); avoid when wet. --Claude

sites.note: 'All sites are pull-throughs and can easily accommodate a 25 foot (8 m) RV. Some sites can accommodate larger RVs. All sites are level.' NPS gives no maximum. Compacted gravel or dirt; 8 people and 2 vehicles per site.

facilities.note: Drinking-water spigots in the summer season only; no RV tank filling anywhere in the monument. Food-storage lockers; seasonal host. No trash collection, no cell service from some carriers.

Book at least 4 days ahead; a reserved site must be occupied within 26 hours of its start or it is let first-come. Max 8 people per site.

name: Echo Lake Campground
note: Clear Creek RD (Arapaho-Roosevelt NF), in the trees at the Hwy 103 / Mount Blue Sky Road junction; Echo Lake is about 500 m west across the road. Several trails leave from the campground. --Claude

sites.note: 17 sites: 10 suitable for RVs and 7 tent-only (FS; recreation.gov says 11 and 7). Parking spurs run 20 to 55 ft (FS and recreation.gov). Per the catalog, nine RV sites take 25 ft or more (006, 007, 009-014, 018; 014 to 55 ft, 011 a 35-ft pull-through); 005 is 20 ft and 015-017 15 ft. The forest's status table gives a 20-ft maximum spur.

booking.note: Reservable on recreation.gov for the 2026 season June 5 - Sept 12 (2027: June 4 - Sept 11), closing 4 days before arrival; 'Limited sites available on a first-come, first-served basis.' 2-night weekend and 3-night holiday-weekend minimums (not marked soft); 14 nights in a rolling 60 days. A reserved site must be occupied within 26 hours or it goes first-come; no site swapping. Check-in 2 p.m., check-out noon; up to eight people a site.

name: Mountain Park Campground
note: Canyon Lakes RD, Arapaho-Roosevelt NF: in ponderosa pine on the banks of the Cache la Poudre (a National Wild and Scenic River) beside CO-14, 40 mi northwest of Fort Collins (mile marker 98.8). Rafting and trout fishing; playground, volleyball and basketball courts, horseshoe pits. --Claude

sites.note: Sites 1-32 have 50/30-amp electric and are reservable; 33-54 have no hookups and are first-come; plus a group site for up to 75. Parking spurs 35-45 ft per the FS page and recreation.gov, but the catalog's electric spurs run 20-45 ft (most 30-35), and the forest's status table gives a 50-ft Max Spur. A few pull-throughs (2, 31, 32).

No minimum stay; 14 nights in a rolling 60 days. A reserved site must be occupied within 26 hours.

name: Narrows Campground
note: USFS (Arapaho-Roosevelt NF, Canyon Lakes Ranger District) campground in Poudre Canyon on CO-14, ~32 mi northwest of Fort Collins, in ponderosa pine and aspen on the Cache la Poudre, Colorado's first National Wild and Scenic River. Rafting, trout fishing and nearby trails (Mt. McConnel, Kreutzer, Young Gulch). Only Upper Narrows takes RVs; Lower Narrows is walk-in tent sites on a slope that drops steeply to the river. --Claude

sites.note: Two sections. Upper Narrows has 7 drive-in sites with back-in parking spurs of 30 to 50 ft (vehicles must fit on the spur; no parking off the road). Lower Narrows is 8 walk-in tent sites reached on foot paths from separate parking. Up to 8 people a site.

booking.note: Reserve on recreation.gov up to four days ahead; a reserved site not occupied within 26 hours goes first-come. Sites may be first-come before and after the reservation season (2026: May 15 - Sept 19; 2027: May 14 - Sept 18).

name: Pawnee Campground
note: Boulder RD, Arapaho-Roosevelt NF: in spruce-fir forest on the east side of Brainard Lake in the Brainard Lake Recreation Area, at the foot of the Continental Divide beside the Indian Peaks Wilderness; about 4.5 mi up Brainard Lake Road from CO-72 at Ward. Parking is limited to the campground during a stay; trailhead lots need a separate timed ticket. Expect cold, wet weather at any time. --Claude

sites.note: 47 sites, eight of them tent-only in the catalog. Catalogued RV spurs mostly 48 ft; a few pull-throughs at 45-100 ft; one reservable site 20 ft. Book a site that fits: you may not move to another (but snow drifts can force a move until mid-July).

booking.note: Recreation.gov for the 2026 season June 26 - Sept 12 (2027: June 25 - Sept 11), closing 1 day before arrival; 2-night weekend and 3-night holiday-weekend minimums. A few sites are first-come, admitted only from 2 p.m. and not guaranteed. Do not arrive before 2 p.m.: there is nowhere to wait or turn around. A reserved site not occupied within 26 hours goes first-come.

name: Stillwater Campground
note: Arapaho NF (Sulphur RD) in the Arapaho National Recreation Area, on a peninsula on Lake Granby's north shore, 8 mi north of Granby off US-34. The sites along the peninsula's south and east shore sit at the water. --Claude

sites.note: Spurs range from 25 to 40 ft; the FS page gives 46 ft as the maximum vehicle length at 3 sites. Single and double sites, plus walk-to tent sites. RVs and extra vehicles must fit on the spur; no off-road parking. The catalog lists 105 of the 129 sites, with 6 pull-throughs in Loops B and C.

booking.note: Most sites reservable on recreation.gov up to 4 days before arrival; the rest first come, first served. Up to 7 consecutive nights per reservation; no site-swapping. A reserved site not occupied within 26 hours goes first come. 2026 reservation season May 15 - Oct 10. Check-in 2 p.m., check-out noon.

Online photos show at least a few sites that can take a class-B or small class-C, but reviews say the sites are short and unlevel: have a backup plan. --AWH

name: Willow Creek Campground
note: In the Arapaho National Recreation Area on the south shore of Willow Creek Reservoir (no-wake), three miles west of US-34 on County Road 40, north of Granby. Lodgepole loop on a point beside the boat ramp; sites sit back in the trees from the shore. Narrow single-lane dam access. --Claude

The forest's Campground Status table gives a 25-ft maximum spur against the page's 40 ft. Vehicles must fit the parking spur; no driving or parking off road.

facilities.note: Drinking water, but availability varies, especially early and late in the season: bring your own. Trash service, boat ramp; some sites have a bear locker.

booking.note: Individual sites are first come, first served; only the group site is reservable (recreation.gov 'Willow Creek Group').

name: South Fork Campground
note: Arapaho NF (Sulphur RD) campground in the Williams Fork Valley: from US-40 two miles before Parshall take County Road 3 ~18 mi, then County Road 30 south 12 mi through a large culvert; the campground is a half-mile on. Next to South Fork Creek, in thinned lodgepole (beetle-kill removal has reduced shade). FS and recreation.gov give a 23-ft maximum vehicle length, so a 23-ft rig fits with no margin (the district status table says 50 ft). --Claude

sites.note: 21 non-electric single sites for tents, trailers and RVs, plus one reservable group site for up to 25. Rigs must fit on the parking spur. The forest's campground-status table lists Max Spur 50'.

facilities.note: A small corral for one or two horses (no water troughs); the Sulphur RD's only campground designated for horse camping. South Fork Trail starts at the campground.

booking.note: Single sites are first come, first served; only the group site books on recreation.gov (facility 234211).

OHVs may drive in and out of the campground only. --Claude

name: Difficult Campground
note: Near the Roaring Fork River 5 mi southeast of Aspen on Hwy 82 (Aspen-Sopris RD, White River NF); shaded mixed forest. Bears visit daily: food lockers, strict storage rules. Day-use area and trailhead on site. --Claude

sites.note: 47 single sites plus a group site (20 people, 10 vehicles). The FS says the sites 'have limited spurs to accommodate trailers up to 40''; the catalog's per-site lengths (20-60 ft) were not used. Five pull-throughs. Vehicles over 35 ft may not cross Independence Pass and must come in from Aspen.

booking.note: Reservable on recreation.gov for the 2026 season May 13 - Sept 26 (same dates in 2027), closing 2 days before arrival; every single site is reservable in the catalog. Five-day stay limit (5 nights in any 30). The site must be occupied the first night; campers may be away up to 24 hours. Concession-run (American Land and Leisure).

note: Trailhead campground in a conifer-and-aspen grove at the East Marvine and Marvine trailheads into the Flat Tops Wilderness, 35 mi east of Meeker via Rio Blanco CR 8 and CR 12 (Blanco RD, White River NF). The creek is about 400 yards away. Cattle may graze in the area. --Claude

sites.note: 7 family sites (30-ft back-ins in the catalog) plus 3 pull-through stock sites with corrals, outside the main campground and for stock users only. The trailhead parking areas have plenty of room for trailers.

booking.note: The Forest Service lists the 7 family sites as non-reservable, and recreation.gov's 2027 table is a first-come season only (May 13 - Oct 31, 2027). The one exception seen: in the 2026 fall hunting season (Sept 29 - Nov 1) recreation.gov took bookings for site 1 and the three stock sites. A site must be occupied the first night.

name: Elliott Creek Campground
note: On the northwest side of Green Mountain Reservoir just past the dam and the town of Heeney, on Heeney Road (CR 30) off Hwy 9 (Dillon RD, White River NF). Site access is difficult when the road is wet (recreation.gov). The Green Mountain Reservoir boat ramp was closed for the 2026 season for low water (FS alert). --Claude

name: Heaton Bay Campground

sites.note: 66 RV/tent sites (14 with electric) and 18 tent-only sites; mostly back-in, 4 pull-throughs. Driveways run 18-80 ft (one 128 ft).

booking.note: Run by the concessionaire American Land & Leisure (801-226-3564). Reservations close 2 days before arrival; the site must be occupied the first night and is held until 11 a.m. the next day. One RV per single site; an extra vehicle pays a nightly fee at the campground.

name: Lowry Campground
note: Dillon Ranger District campground (White River NF) off Swan Mountain Road between Summit Cove and Breckenridge, near Dillon Reservoir (body contact with the reservoir prohibited; boat ramps at the Frisco and Dillon marinas). Little or no shade since beetle-killed trees were removed. --Claude

Occupy the site the first night. Two vehicles per site, extra vehicles charged nightly. Run by a concessionaire (American Land & Leisure, 801-226-3564).

name: Marvine Campground
note: Blanco RD, White River NF: in conifer and aspen on Marvine Creek, 35 mi east of Meeker (the last 6 mi on Rio Blanco CR 12). Marvine and East Marvine trails into the Flat Tops Wilderness start beside it, toward Marvine Lakes. The horse sites sit in their own loop. --Claude

sites.note: 17 standard sites in loops 1-2 (max vehicle 20-40 ft; 6 pull-throughs, three of them 40 ft) and 5 equestrian sites with corrals in their own loop 3, for campers with stock only (the FS page says six). Several standard spurs take only 20 ft.

booking.note: Every site is reservable on recreation.gov; 2026 season May 13 - Nov 1 (2027: May 13 - Oct 31), closing 2 days before arrival. No minimum stay (weekend minimums set to 0). 14 nights at most, and 14 a month. A site must be occupied the first night; reserved sites are held until 11 am the next day. Run for the Forest Service by American Land & Leisure.

name: North Fork Campground
note: Blanco RD (White River NF) campground, 32 mi up County Road 8 from Meeker, in an aspen grove on a bench above the North Fork of the White River (across the road). Fly fishing on the river; OHV routes and Flat Tops trailheads nearby. Livestock may graze in the area. --Claude

Group site currently closed.

name: Peak One Campground
note: Dillon Ranger District campground (White River NF) on the Frisco Peninsula of Dillon Reservoir, off Highway 9 south of Frisco; the entrance is one-eighth mile south of the Frisco Peninsula area. Body contact with the reservoir prohibited. Little or no shade since beetle-killed trees were removed. --Claude

The forest's table gives a 50-ft maximum site length; catalog lengths run 17-45 ft (39 sites at 30, 9 at 45; site 43 is 17 ft, site 9 24 ft) with four 99-ft placeholders.

booking.note: Reserve on recreation.gov at least two days ahead; 14 nights a month at most. Occupy the site the first night (a reservation is held until 11 a.m. the next day). One RV with tow per site; an extra vehicle is charged nightly at the campground. Run by a concessionaire (American Land & Leisure, 801-226-3564).

name: Prospector Campground
note: Dillon RD (White River NF), in the Swan Mountain Recreation Area on Dillon Reservoir between Frisco and Keystone, a mile of dirt road off Swan Mountain Road. Open sites with little or no shade since the beetle-kill clearing, looking out over the reservoir to the Gore and Tenmile ranges. No swimming or body contact with the reservoir. --Claude

booking.note: All sites reservable (the host has one more); booking closes 2 days before arrival and no reservations are taken after October 1. A site must be occupied by 11 a.m. the day after arrival or it is released. 14 nights a month.

name: Redstone Campground

sites.note: 37 sites plus 2 host sites (20 and 39). 40-ft maximum RV length including the tow vehicle. Gravel spurs, a few pull-throughs in Osgood and Mechau.

booking.note: Reserve on recreation.gov at least two days ahead; 14 consecutive nights, 14 nights a month at most. Occupy the site the first night (held until 11 a.m. the next day). One RV per single site, two per double; an extra vehicle is charged nightly at the campground. Run by a concessionaire (American Land & Leisure, 801-226-3564).

name: Shepherds Rim Campground
note: Last campground on the right up the hill above the Trappers Lake outlet bridge, beside the Flat Tops Wilderness (Blanco RD, White River NF); trails to Trappers Lake and the wilderness. 50 mi from Meeker on Rio Blanco CR 8 and Trappers Lake Road (FSR 205). --Claude

A reserved site must be occupied by 11 a.m. the day after arrival or it is released. 14 nights in a row, 14 in a month.

name: Silver Queen Campground
note: White River NF (Aspen-Sopris RD) campground in the Maroon Bells Scenic Area, 6.5 mi southwest of Aspen on Maroon Creek Rd, in aspen a short walk from Maroon Creek, with views of Pyramid Peak. Campers drive in on a vehicle pass bought at the Maroon Bells Welcome Station. --Claude

Reservations must check in at the Maroon Bells Welcome Station (7 a.m.-7 p.m.) within 24 hours or the site is forfeited. 2026 reservation season May 22 - Sept 30 (2027: May 28 - Sept 30). Check-out 11 a.m. (recreation.gov) or 2 p.m. (FS).

name: Willows Campground
note: On the north arm of Green Mountain Reservoir, off Heeney Road (County Road 30) just west of CO-9, between Silverthorne and Kremmling. Sites line the shore along a dirt loop; the reservoir is drawn down through late summer. Recreation.gov: site access is difficult when the road is wet. Motorboats launch only from Heeney Marina after an Aquatic Nuisance Species inspection. Length (2026-10-28): the forest's 2026 table gives a 20-ft maximum site, but recreation.gov's catalog shows roadside pull-outs of 30-93 ft. Have a backup plan. --Claude

name: Dearhamer Campground
note: Aspen-Sopris RD (White River NF), ~22 mi up Frying Pan Rd from Basalt: a small loop under cottonwoods at the head of Ruedi Reservoir where the Fryingpan River enters. --Claude

sites.note: FS and recreation.gov say 13 sites; the catalog lists 12 bookable sites plus site 006, a management (host) site. All back-in gravel spurs; the catalog's per-site lengths (30-69 ft) run past the FS's 35-ft RV maximum.

Bear-proof food lockers at each site. The Ruedi Marina dump station is closed (nearest Silt or Edwards).

booking.note: Concessionaire-run (American Land & Leisure). Reserved sites must be occupied the first night (held until 11 am the next day). One RV with tow per site; most sites take one extra vehicle at a nightly fee paid at the campground. Up to 14 nights a month.

name: Little Maud Campground
note: White River NF campground on the slope above the north end of Ruedi Reservoir, off Frying Pan Road (CR 104) about 16 mi east of Basalt, sharing the Ruedi complex entrance with Little Mattie and Mollie B; boat ramp and picnic ground below, walk down to the water. --Claude FS, read 2026-10-28: 'Due to lack of water the campground is now closed for the 2026 season.' --Claude 2026-10-28

sites.note: 21 sites plus a host site. FS: '40-foot maximum RV length'. Catalogued driveways run 17-83 ft; 02 (20 ft) and 06 (17 ft) are short; 03, 13 and 20 are pull-throughs. One RV with tow per site.

facilities.note: Two flush toilets. Bear-proof food locker at each site; trash collection. Water may not be on before Memorial Day weekend or after September 30.

name: Pine Cove Campground
note: White River NF (Dillon Ranger District) campground in the Peninsula Recreation Area on Dillon Reservoir near Frisco, off Hwy 9: paved parking-lot-style sites in two rows along a central lane, the west row facing the open shore. Motorboats must launch from the Dillon Marina after an aquatic nuisance species inspection; swimming and other water contact are prohibited. Dillon Reservoir ran low in 2026 (Denver Water: down 20 ft by late July, a near-record low projected for April 2027), which widens the beach in front of the sites. --Claude

facilities.note: White River NF asks RV campers to fill tanks before arriving and not to fill RV tanks at campground spigots (drought); filling small jugs is fine.

booking.note: First-come, first-served; not on recreation.gov. 14 days in a 30-day period on the White River NF unless posted otherwise.

name: Yeoman Park Campground
note: On the edge of a wetland meadow beside East Brush Creek, partly in mature spruce, with views of Craig Peak; beaver colony in the meadow. From Eagle (I-70 exit 147): Sylvan Lake Road, then about 9 miles up Brush Creek Road to the fork and 6 miles up East Brush Creek Road (FR 415). Trailheads nearby for the Lake Charles Trail into the Holy Cross Wilderness and Fulford Cave (permit; closed Oct 15 - Apr 15); the old mining town of Fulford is a few miles up FR 418. --Claude

sites.note: Loops A and B. Eighteen sites take RVs 15-30 ft and 6 have room for vehicles over 30 ft; 11 sites have tent platforms. 15 sites in spruce forest, 9 in the open.

facilities.note: Three vault toilets. Accessible sites in Loop A; fishing platform on Brush Creek near the entrance. Food must be stored in bear-resistant containers; pack out trash.

booking.note: Loop A (14 sites) reservable on recreation.gov; Loop B (9 sites) first come, first served. A reserved site is forfeited if not occupied by 11 am the day after arrival. 2027 reservation season May 27 - Oct 1. Check-in 2 pm, check-out 11 am.

note: Three adjoining loops (Bucks, Cutthroat, Trapline) beside the Flat Tops Wilderness boundary near the Trappers Lake Outlet trailhead (Blanco RD, White River NF). From Meeker: CO 13 east 1 mi, Rio Blanco CR 8 39 mi, then Trappers Lake Road (FSR 205) 10 mi. Trappers Lake is in the wilderness: no motorized boats or wheeled boat carts. The reservable Shepherds Rim loop is a separate entry. --Claude

booking.note: All three loops are first come, first served; none is on recreation.gov.

name: Deep Lake Campground
note: Eagle-Holy Cross RD, Flat Tops (White River NF); spruce/fir and meadow loops on the east side of 37-acre Deep Lake, ~29 mi up gravel Coffee Pot Rd (FSR 600) from the Dotsero exit - the last 30 mi unpaved. recreation.gov: FSR 600 is passable to passenger 2WD vehicles but has slow rocky sections, and when wet parts of it may be impassable even to 4WD. --Claude

booking.note: No reservations: pay on site with the fee envelopes at the entrance or by Scan & Pay in the recreation.gov app.

name: Sweetwater Lake Campground
note: White River NF (Eagle-Holy Cross RD) at the south end of Sweetwater Lake, among scrub oak and willow under limestone cliffs; reached from Dotsero by the Colorado River Road and Sweetwater Creek Road. Ute, Cross Creek and Sweetwater Nature trails start at the campground; horse traffic is heavy, so dogs on leash. The lake is the site of the proposed Sweetwater Lake State Park. --Claude

name: Purgatoire Campground
note: San Carlos RD, Pike-San Isabel NF: in aspen and spruce near the headwaters of the Purgatoire (North Fork) in the Culebra Range, 25 mi south of La Veta off CO-12 and 4 mi of rough gravel up County Road 34. North Fork Trail #1309 trailhead at the north end. Remote: no real-time information. --Claude

sites.note: Two loops: a wooded loop of 14 standard/RV sites (spurs 18-35 ft; six at 25, four at 35) and a grassy meadow loop of 6 equestrian sites for horse campers (spurs to 45 ft). Grass-and-gravel aprons, all back-in. One RV per site.

booking.note: Recreation.gov or 877-444-6777 at least four days ahead, for the 2026 season May 15 - Sept 19 (2027: May 14 - Sept 18); some sites are first-come and must be occupied the first night. Reservations need Friday and Saturday nights on weekends and three nights on holiday weekends; walk-ups are exempt. 14 consecutive nights at most.

A 2022 windstorm blew down many trees (cleared 2024), so the campground is more open and can be very windy. --Claude

name: Southside Campground
note: San Isabel NF (San Carlos RD) campground in the Lake Isabel Recreation Area in the Wet Mountains: from I-25 exit 74 take CO-165 west 18 mi to the south entrance, then 1/2 mi. A small RV campground on the wooded slope above Lake Isabel's south shore, in aspen and ponderosa; non-motorized boating and fishing on the lake, Cisneros, St. Charles and Snowslide trails nearby. --Claude

sites.note: Seven RV/trailer sites (30 ft) and one tent site (008), all pull-through on paved roads; tight turns keep out vehicles over 30 ft. Built for RVs without large slide-outs.

Check-in 2 p.m.; check-out noon (FS).

name: La Vista Campground
note: San Carlos RD (Pike-San Isabel NF): meadow above the west side of 40-acre Lake Isabel, a CCC-built lake for non-motorized boating and fishing, in the Wet Mountains off CO 165. Bear closure order in place. --Claude

sites.note: 15 electric sites for RVs or tents (lengths 25-45 ft, mostly back-in, one pull-through) and 10 tent-only sites (1-10), most of them walk-in 15-50 yards from the parking spurs. One RV, or two tents and two vehicles, per site.

booking.note: Reserve at least four days ahead (877-444-6777 or recreation.gov); a few sites are first-come, and the whole campground is first-come for a week either side of the reservation season. Two nights on weekends, three on holiday weekends; 'Walk-ups are exempt from the nightly minimum.' First-come sites must be occupied the first night; self-service fee tube. Run by the concessionaire ExplorUS.

name: Alvarado Campground
note: Sangre de Cristo foothills above Westcliffe (San Carlos RD, Pike-San Isabel NF), at the edge of the Sangre de Cristo Wilderness; lower level for tents and RVs, walk-in tent sites up top, equestrian sites in the middle; some sites beside Alvarado Creek. Last ~2 miles on dirt/gravel (CR 141). Concession-run (ExplorUS). --Claude

sites.note: Catalog: 42 standard/RV sites (27 reservable, 15 first-come), 5 walk-to tent sites on the upper level, 3 equestrian sites (no corrals). Max vehicle lengths 18-45 ft, about half 30 ft or more; two pull-throughs. Dirt and gravel aprons; one RV or two vehicles per site.

booking.note: Reservable on recreation.gov for the 2026 peak season May 15 - Sept 19; the weeks either side are first-come, and 15 standard sites are always first-come (must be occupied the first night). recreation.gov closes booking 4 days before arrival. 2-night weekend and 3-night holiday-weekend minimums (not marked soft). 14 nights in any 30.

name: Ohaver Lake Campground

Walk-ups are exempt from the weekend and holiday minimums and must be occupied the night paid for. Usually full from Friday (sometimes Thursday); no phone service at the campground.

note: Chalk Creek Canyon about 9.5 miles up CR 162 from US-285, past Mount Princeton Hot Springs and just after Cascade Falls (Salida RD, Pike-San Isabel NF); dense Douglas fir and aspen, Chalk Creek across the road, Chalk Lake a mile east. Camping in the canyon is allowed only in its four developed campgrounds. --Claude

Reserved weekends need Friday and Saturday nights, holiday weekends three; 'Walk-ups are exempt from the nightly minimum.' 14 consecutive nights at most. Normally full from Friday, sometimes Thursday.

note: Primitive campground on Horseshoe Creek at the base of Sheep Mountain, 8 mi west of Fairplay via CR 18 (South Park RD, Pike-San Isabel NF); trees give good privacy between sites; Limber Grove Trail nearby. A bear closure order is in place: store attractants in hard-sided vehicles or bear boxes. --Claude

sites.note: The FS says 19 sites with parking spurs 25-40 ft and a 25-ft RV/trailer maximum; the catalog lists 18 public sites (12 for RVs, 6 tent-only) plus the host's, and rates the RV sites at only 14-20 ft. One pull-through.

The FS page also states a 3-night holiday-weekend minimum that recreation.gov's rules do not carry. 14-night limit.

name: May Queen Campground
note: Pike-San Isabel NF, at the far western end of Turquoise Lake near the Boustead Tunnel outlet, in lodgepole pine beside a day-use and picnic area. The Turquoise Lake Trail runs 6.4 mi along the shore to the dam; the Timberline Lake / Colorado Trail trailhead is 1/2 mi up the road. Busy on weekends. --Claude

Every vehicle must fit on the spur, no parking on the grass. Up to 8 people; one RV and two tents, or three tents, per site.

booking.note: 13 sites on recreation.gov (or 877-444-6777) at least 4 days ahead; 6 hillside sites first-come, which must be occupied the first night. Friday and Saturday together on weekends, 3 nights on holiday weekends; walk-ups are exempt from the minimums. 14 consecutive nights at most. 2027 reservation season May 21 - Sept 5 (2026 ran through Sept 19).

note: South Park Ranger District, Pike-San Isabel NF: 12.5 mi south of Fairplay off US 285, 1 mi up Forest Road 431 (unpaved campground roads); widely spaced sites in aspen and mixed conifer on a hillside, near the Buffalo Peaks Wilderness. --Claude

name: Collegiate Peaks Campground

Usually full from Friday, sometimes Thursday.

name: Spruce Grove Campground
note: Beside large rock outcroppings on Tarryall Creek, with little shade among spruce and aspen; about 13 mi up Tarryall Road (CR 77) from Lake George, the entrance set back from the road (South Park RD, Pike-San Isabel NF). Trails into the Lost Creek Wilderness start across the creek bridge; Tarryall Reservoir is 11 mi away. --Claude

name: Riverside Campground
note: South Park RD (Pike-San Isabel NF), concessionaire-run: near the entrance of Eleven Mile Canyon, 2 mi southwest of Lake George on CR 96, across the road from the South Platte River; large open sites, the walk-in tent sites in the pines. The 1-mile Hard Rock Interpretive Trail starts at the campground. Bear closure order in effect: store food hard-sided. --Claude

Up to 8 people, two tents and two vehicles or one RV a site.

booking.note: Reservable on recreation.gov until 5 days before arrival; sites not reserved by then become first-come and must be occupied the same night. recreation.gov marks the 2-night weekend minimum soft, so it may be relaxed for a same-day booking. 14 consecutive nights at most. 2026 reservation season May 15 - Oct 11 (2027: May 14 - Oct 10). Check-in 2 p.m., check-out noon.

name: Springer Gulch Campground

name: Lone Rock Campground
note: South Platte RD (Pike-San Isabel NF), on the South Platte River's gold-medal water beside Jefferson County Road 126 about a mile west of Deckers; the only campground on that stretch of river that takes RVs. Private land lines the river nearby: mind the fences. --Claude

sites.note: 16 RV/tent sites and one tent-only; 10 pull-throughs. Spurs catalogued 20-40 ft, most 25 ft (sites 006 and 007 are 20 ft).

booking.note: Every site is reservable in the reservation season (closes 4 days before arrival) and the campground fills fast: the two designated walk-up sites are usually taken by the hosts. Outside the reservation season (2026: Jan 1-May 21, Sept 7-Dec 31) all sites are first-come.

name: Spillway Campground
note: Last campground up Eleven Mile Canyon, on the South Platte River below the Eleven Mile Reservoir dam; trailhead for the Overlook Trail. Concessionaire-run (recreation.gov contact (661) 702-1420). Bear closure order: store attractants hard-sided. --Claude

The 2027 reservation season runs May 28 to September 5, then first-come until October 10 (in 2026 reservations ran May 15 to October 11). Weekend minimum 2 nights, holiday weekends 3; recreation.gov marks the weekend minimum soft, so it may be relaxed for a same-day booking, and walk-ups are exempt.

name: Painted Rocks Campground
note: Pikes Peak Ranger District (Pike NF) campground on the edge of a grassy meadow, 7 miles north of Woodland Park off CO-67, then 1/2 mile up gravel Painted Rocks Road; named for streaked sandstone outcrops. The paved Centennial Bike Trail, half a mile away, runs to Colorado and South Meadows campgrounds and Manitou Lake. --Claude

sites.note: 14 RV/trailer sites and 4 tent-only (8, 11, 12, 13) on two loops; the west loop is mostly shaded by ponderosa pine, the east loop more open. The Forest Service gives parking spurs up to 30 ft and says the narrow road and spurs are not recommended for large motorhomes or trailers; recreation.gov says rigs over 36 ft will have a very tough time on the tight corners. One RV per site; every vehicle must fit on the gravel spur.

booking.note: Limited sites reservable on recreation.gov or 877-444-6777 up to six months and at least four days ahead; 6 sites are first-come (must be occupied the same night). Two-night weekend and three-night holiday-weekend minimums; 14 nights in a rolling 60 days. Reservation season 2026 May 22 - Sept 6 (2027: June 5 - Sept 6). Check in with the host.

name: Colorado Campground
note: Pikes Peak RD (Pike-San Isabel NF), concessionaire-run, in ponderosa pine on CO-67 about 7 miles north of Woodland Park; a short trail and the paved Centennial Trail lead to Manitou Lake. --Claude

sites.note: The FS page says 80 sites 'with parking areas up to 30 feet long'; recreation.gov warns that RVs or trailers over 36 ft 'will have a very tough time making it through the campground because of tight corners and trees'. The catalog's lengths (41 sites at 30 ft, 19 at 40, a few 45-80, one 100) run longer than either. Rigs must fit the spur; no overflow parking.

booking.note: 49 of the 79 sites are reservable, up to four days before arrival; the rest are first-come and must be occupied the same night. Up to 14 days in a 30-day period. Concessionaire-run; check in with the host.

name: Parry Peak Campground
note: Leadville Ranger District campground in aspen and lodgepole along Lake Creek, on CO-82 west of Twin Lakes Reservoir and Twin Lakes Village (from Leadville, 15 mi south on US-24 then west on CO-82), with a view of Parry Peak; the Continental Divide Trail is just down the road. Two loops: a ring north of the highway entrance and a spur road south along the creek. --Claude

facilities.note: Vault toilets in each loop; no water - bring enough to drink and to put out your fire. Firewood sold at the host site ($10 a bundle).

booking.note: Strictly first-come: you must be at the campground to claim and pay for a site, and must occupy it the first night. recreation.gov Scan and Pay may work on site (download the app beforehand; cell service is limited).

name: Matterhorn Campground
note: Uncompahgre NF beside CO-145 (San Juan Skyway, paved) ~7 mi south of Telluride. Outer-loop sites are wooded, inner-loop sites open; the walk-to tent sites have panoramic mountain views. The Galloping Goose Trail leaves from the campground; Lizard Head Wilderness is ~3 mi. --Claude

sites.note: 28 sites: 25 for RVs (4 full-hookup) and 3 walk-to tent sites (012-014). Forest Service: maximum spur 45 ft; recreation.gov rates the sites 30-40 ft (the hookup sites 30). Four pull-throughs. One camping unit per standard site.

facilities.note: Showers are open to day users too ($8 for non-registered guests). Firewood $10 a bundle.

season.note: Forest Service: 'Late Spring to Early Fall - weather dependent'. Dates are recreation.gov's 2026 fee seasons (first-come May 17 - June 4, reserved June 5 - Sept 12, first-come Sept 13-30); 2027 so far lists May 28 - Sept 30.

booking.note: 14 sites reservable (incl. all 4 hookup sites), the rest first-come; outside the peak season every site is walk-in. Book at least 4 days ahead; weekend 2-night minimum; up to 7 consecutive nights per reservation. First-come sites are claimed in person only ('DO NOT call to determine availability'). A reserved site is held 24 hours after check-in time. 2027 reservation season May 28 - Sept 12 (2026: June 5 - Sept 12).

name: Sunshine Campground
note: Uncompahgre NF (Norwood RD) on CO-145 about 8 mi southwest of Telluride, in dense aspen with a small pond and views of Sunshine Peak. --Claude

facilities.note: No water (the FS page: 'No water available for 2025 season'). Showers at Matterhorn Campground for $8; firewood $10 a bundle.

booking.note: First come, first served; claim a site in person and pay on site, by Scan & Pay in the recreation.gov app where available (download it first, cell service is limited).

name: Rosy Lane Campground
note: Gunnison NF campground in Taylor River Canyon, 17 mi from Gunnison (CO 135 north to Almont, then 7 mi up paved Taylor Canyon Rd/CR 742), on the bank of the Taylor River among lodgepole pine and aspen; sites are set back from the water, which a trail reaches (Gold Medal fishing; calm stretch for rafting). No ATVs in the campground. --Claude

sites.note: FS counts 20 campsites; recreation.gov lists 15 (11 reservable, 4 first-come), driveways 25-50 ft with 10 of the 15 at 45-50 ft and 8 pull-throughs. Site 004 is accessible.

facilities.note: Nearest dump station is 16 miles north of the campground.

booking.note: Four sites (006, 008, 013, 019) are first-come and must be taken in person, and the whole campground is first-come outside the June 12 - Sept 12 reservation season. The weekend two-night minimum may be relaxed for a same-day booking. A reservation is held 24 hours past check-in before it counts as a no-show.

name: Lake Irwin Campground
note: GMUG campground at the end of FR 826 (Lake Irwin Road), 2 mi off Kebler Pass Road (CR 12) and about 9 mi from Crested Butte, on the west shore of Lake Irwin below the Ruby Range; most sites shaded by spruce and fir. Non-motorized boating. The last 2 miles are dusty and washboarded; campers report 27-34 ft rigs fitting. --Claude

facilities.note: No water: bring your own. Firewood $10 a bundle.

season.note: Weather permitting.

booking.note: A mix of reservable and first-come sites; the whole campground is first-come from opening to mid-July and for the last weeks of September (2026: Jun 15 - Jul 16 and Sep 13-27). First-come sites are booked in person only. Booking closes 4 days before arrival; two nights on weekends (not marked soft). A late reservation is held 24 hours. Extra vehicles paid to the host on arrival.

name: Amphitheater Campground
note: USFS campground on a steep hillside above Ouray off US-550, among Gambel oak and mixed conifers, overlooking the town and the Amphitheater cliffs; the Upper Cascade Falls trail starts here. The FS calls it best suited to tents and smaller trailers/RVs: the access road and loops are steep with tight turns, and RVs follow the 'trailer' signs (second right). --Claude

sites.note: 35 sites: 17 take RVs, 18 are tent-only. The FS caps total RV length at 35 ft, but most RV sites are catalogued at 15-20 ft; only six take 23 ft or more: 004 (30 ft), 006 (25), 016 (26, pull-through) and 024 (25), reservable, and 030 (35) and 032 (30, pull-through), first-come. 017 is a 20-ft pull-through.

facilities.note: Trash collection; picnic table and fire ring at each site.

booking.note: Reservable sites book on recreation.gov for the peak season (2026: May 31 - Sep 12; 2027: May 28 - Sep 12); the shoulder weeks (2026: May 17-30 and Sep 13-30) are first-come only. First-come sites must be claimed in person ('DO NOT call to determine availability'). recreation.gov closes booking 3 days before arrival (reservationCutOff 3). 7 consecutive nights maximum; 2-night weekend minimum on reservations. One camping unit per site; extra vehicles are paid to the host on arrival. Run by a concessionaire (contact 928-537-8888).

name: Woods Lake Campground
note: In aspen forest next to Woods Lake, below the Lizard Head Wilderness, between Placerville and Telluride: from CO-145 2.4 miles east of Placerville, 7.4 miles up Fall Creek Road (FR 618), then about 2 miles on FR 621. Sites are set back in the trees; the lake (fishing) is a short walk. Trailheads for the Woods Lake and Lone Cone trails into the wilderness; Wilson Mesa Trail half a mile away. --Claude

sites.note: Three loops. The main loop has a group site, 4 double sites and pull-throughs; the horse loop (sites 32-36) has paddocks, hay racks, watering troughs, pull-throughs and a large trailer parking lot.

season.note: Late spring to early fall, weather dependent. In 2026 the main campground closed September 30; the horse loop stays open free (no water) until November 3.

booking.note: First come, first served; pay on site, by recreation.gov Scan & Pay where available (download the app beforehand; little cell service).

name: Dinner Station Campground
note: Gunnison RD (GMUG): in the upper Taylor River valley, 3.75 mi above Taylor Park Reservoir and ~35 mi up Taylor Canyon Rd from Almont (improved dirt past the Cottonwood Pass turnoff). Ponderosa loop beside the Taylor River plus an open sage loop with the pull-throughs; popular with OHV riders, Collegiate Peaks Wilderness 4 mi east. --Claude

name: Cobbett Lake Campground
note: Grand Valley RD, Grand Mesa NF (GMUG), along the Grand Mesa Scenic Byway within walking distance of the visitor center; dense spruce grove beside Cobbett Lake (non-motorized boats). --Claude

sites.note: All but 2 sites shaded. recreation.gov's catalog lists site lengths 15-45 ft: 16 of the 20 take 25 ft or more (sites 8, 10, 11 are 20 ft; 13 and 17 are 15 ft); three are pull-throughs (9, 15, 18).

name: Silver Jack Campground
note: Uncompahgre NF (Ouray RD) campground ~18 mi up Cimarron Rd (CR 858) from US-50, just north of (below) the Silver Jack Reservoir dam; three loops heavily wooded with aspen and a few spruce over tall grass and wildflowers. Trails around the Cimarron Ridge and OHV trails nearby. --Claude

name: Buckeye Recreation Area (Pioneer Campground)
note: Manti-La Sal NF (Moab RD) recreation area in Colorado at Buckeye Reservoir, among ponderosa pine on the east side of the La Sal Mountains. About 13 mi of winding gravel (FR 0371) from Paradox; follow the FS route, since GPS apps send drivers onto 4WD roads or to locked private gates, and the Upper Two Mile Road alternative is very muddy or impassable when wet. Pioneer Campground is on the reservoir's north side. The reservoir is irrigation storage and can be drained completely in low-water years. --Claude

sites.note: Pioneer Campground: 30 single-family sites with graveled parking spurs, concrete picnic tables, fire rings and a utility table, plus one group site. Recreation.gov per-site lengths run 33-74 ft (most 40-55 ft); 3 pull-throughs (sites 02, 08, 14 at 73, 74 and 66 ft), the rest back-in. The 18 less-developed dispersed sites around the reservoir are separate.

facilities.note: No water at the campground. Boat ramp (5 hp limit, wakeless), day-use picnic area.

season.note: Typically open mid-May to September.

booking.note: Pioneer sites and the group site reservable on recreation.gov through the end of September, up to 5 days before arrival. 14 nights in any 30 days.

name: Mavreeso Campground
note: San Juan NF, along the West Dolores River off West Dolores Road (FR 535, gravel) about 6 mi from CO-145 and ~19 mi NE of Dolores, under spruce, pine and fir. Fishermen's parking nearby; private land along parts of the river. The last 6 mi of FR 535 north toward Rico are steep, narrow and not recommended for trailers, so come in from the south end. Generators no more than an hour at a time. --Claude

sites.note: 18 family sites in loops A and B plus one group site (tents only, no RVs or trailers). Forest Service: 'Max RV size = 35 ft'; every wheeled vehicle must fit on the spur and there is no overflow parking. Most sites level, many pull-throughs. Up to 8 people per site.

facilities.note: Water in season only (none during the late-2026 extension).

season.note: Forest Service: 'May through September'; dates are recreation.gov's fee season (the same May 8 - Sept 26 every year 2026-2028). In 2026 it stayed open from the end of September to Nov 22 with limited services and no water.

booking.note: 12 sites reservable (incl. the group site and four electric sites), 7 first-come (11-15, B08, B09). Book at least 4 days ahead. 14 nights in any rolling 30 days. If a site is empty, campers may come in before check-in time.

name: West Fork Campground
note: Wooded USFS campground (mixed conifer, sun and shade) near the West Fork of the San Juan River, 1.5 mi up FR 648 off US-160 between Pagosa Springs and Wolf Creek Pass. The river can be heard but not seen from the sites, and since the October 2025 flood it runs farther from them. --Claude

sites.note: 28 sites per the Forest Service (recreation.gov's catalog has 27: 15 reservable, 12 first-come). Catalog lengths 26-40 ft, most 30; the Forest Service gives 35 ft and says most sites suit large RVs. Vehicles must fit the parking spur, no overflow parking.

season.note: Mid-May through September per the Forest Service; specific dates on recreation.gov.

name: Target Tree Campground
note: USFS campground on a south-facing ponderosa/Gambel oak hillside overlooking Thompson Park, about 7 mi east of Mancos off US-160; a short trail leads to a Ute-scarred 'target tree'. Drinking water is trucked in (no RV fill). Well-maintained access road suitable for a 23-ft RV. --Claude

sites.note: 28 sites: 24 in Loop A (15 reservable, 9 first-come) and 4 in Loop B (sites 25-28, pull-throughs; 25-26 equestrian with corrals). 17 barrier-free. Catalog lengths 25-45 ft in Loop A (most 32-40), 50-60 ft for the Loop B pull-throughs; the Forest Service gives 45 ft. Most large and pull-through sites need levelling.

facilities.note: The Forest Service lists three accessible composting toilets; recreation.gov calls them vault toilets. No firewood sold.

season.note: May through September per the Forest Service; specific dates on recreation.gov.

booking.note: 19 sites reservable on recreation.gov up to 4 days ahead; 9 Loop A sites (001, 004, 005, 008, 011, 012, 020, 021, 023) are first come, first served. 2-night weekend and 3-night holiday-weekend minimums. 2026 reservation season May 8 - Sept 26; recreation.gov's 2027 table starts June 5. Livestock only at sites 25 and 26.

name: Williams Creek Campground
note: USFS campground among ponderosa, aspen and juniper on Williams Creek, about 23 mi N of Pagosa Springs via Piedra Rd (CR 600 / FR 631) and FR 640, ~1 mi below Williams Creek Reservoir. Some sites on the east loop sit on the creek bank; many have mountain views. Dispersed camping is closed along upper FR 640. Washboard forest-road access. --Claude

sites.note: 61 sites per the Forest Service, including double sites and a group site; recreation.gov's catalog has 60 (one a host site, 54). Catalog lengths 20-45 ft: 36 sites (one the host site) list RVs, mostly 30-45 ft; 21 sites are listed for tents and trailers only (most 20-25 ft) and 3 are tent-only. A few level pull-through and back-in sites suit larger RVs (pull-throughs include 03, 28, 30).

facilities.note: No dump station: the nearest is in Pagosa Springs. Firewood sold by the camp host.

season.note: May through September per the Forest Service; specific dates on recreation.gov.

booking.note: 32 sites reservable on recreation.gov (the catalog marks 36) up to 4 days ahead; the rest first come, first served, claimed in person. Often full on summer weekends. 2026 reservation season May 8 - Sept 26; the 2027 table runs May 2 - Sept 27. Check-in 2 pm, check-out noon.

name: Ute Campground
note: On a gentle south-facing slope under ponderosa pine just north of US-160, ~15 mi W of Pagosa Springs, facing Chimney Rock National Monument (summer guided tours; entrance 4 mi away on CO-151); gets very warm in summer. Hiking on Haystack Mountain. Length (2026-10-28): the Forest Service gives a 35-ft maximum RV and the site catalog lists 28-62-ft driveways, but a recreation.gov notice says the gravel spurs fit about a 20-ft extended-cab pickup. Have a backup plan. --Claude

sites.note: Recreation.gov lists 21 sites including one group site (the Forest Service page says 26). Forest Service: max RV 35 ft; everything with wheels must fit the parking spur, no overflow parking. Catalog driveways run 28-62 ft (vehicle maximums 30-40 ft where given), though a recreation.gov notice calls the gravel spurs about 20 ft.

facilities.note: Two pairs of vault toilets and one pressurized water station; trash collection, host, firewood for sale. No dump station.

season.note: May through September; recreation.gov has the exact dates (2026 season May 8 - Sep 26).

booking.note: Sites 08-12, 17, 21, 22 and the group site are reservable on recreation.gov; the rest are first come, first served. Stay limit 28 nights at first-come sites, 12 on reserved ones. Reservation season varies by year (May 8 - Sep 26 in 2026, Jun 5 - Sep 26 in 2027).

sites.note: Only a few sites suit larger RVs; vehicles must fit the parking spur, no overflow parking.

name: West Dolores Campground
note: USFS campground on the West Dolores River, ~21 mi north of Dolores via Hwy 145 and gravel FR 535, a mile past Mavreeso. The steep, narrow stretch of FR 535 that the Forest Service says is not recommended for trailers is its last 6 miles toward Rico, well beyond the campground. Mostly shady, level sites under spruce and fir; site 4E sits on the riverbank. --Claude

facilities.note: The Forest Service lists one composting toilet; recreation.gov lists vault toilets and a water spigot. Two picnic areas.

name: Golden Horn Designated Camping Area
note: Designated dispersed camping area on South Mineral Creek, 2.6 mi up FR 585 (South Mineral Rd / CR 7) from US 550, 2 mi north of Silverton. A large open dirt area with pockets into the trees and vault toilets; no numbered sites. The good gravel road is 2WD as far as the Ice Lakes trailhead (4.4 mi). Camping only in the designated areas along FR 585 and at least 100 ft from the creek; extremely busy in July-August. Status (2026-10-28): the Forest Service names Anvil, Bear and Sultan as FR 585's designated camping areas, not Golden Horn; only the San Juan Mountains Association lists it. Have a backup plan. --Claude

note: San Juan NF campground under ponderosa pine midway up the east shore of Vallecito Reservoir, ~14 miles north of Bayfield via County Road 501 and then Forest Road 603 (CR 501A). No gas on the east side of the reservoir. --Claude

name: Bradfield Campground
note: BLM (Tres Rios Field Office) site in the Dolores River canyon below McPhee Dam, ~30 mi NW of Dolores: US-491 north, then a rough but passable gravel road (FR 505 / CR S) down into the canyon past the Bradfield Bridge. Large, open, flat gravel loops with shade shelters beside the brushy riverbank. Busiest during the lower Dolores boatable release (BLM: generally mid-April to mid-June). --Claude

Also a separate, more dispersed equestrian camping loop. No length stated.

facilities.note: Two double-vault toilets. Potable water from hand pumps, seasonal (BLM: generally April 1 - Sept 30; its accessibility survey says March through Sept 30); the FS page says September-May brings limited or no services (water, trash, restrooms). Boat ramp and trailer parking; day-use area with shade shelters. No cell coverage.

booking.note: First come, first served; pay at the kiosk's fee tube.

Reached on West Dolores Rd (FR 535, gravel) from Hwy 145 about 13 mi north of Dolores; the Forest Service says the road's last 6 miles, rejoining Hwy 145 north of Rico, are steep, narrow and not recommended for trailers, so come in from the Dolores end. --Claude

season.note: Forest Service: 'Memorial Day weekend through the second Monday of September' (its Current Conditions line says 'through Labor Day'); recreation.gov's 2026 season ran May 22 - Sept 7.

booking.note: Most sites reservable on recreation.gov (or 1-877-444-6777) at least 4 days ahead; the rest first-come, not guaranteed. A reserved site not occupied by check-out time the day after arrival goes to first-come campers. 14 nights in any 30 days. 2027 reservation season May 28 - Sept 6.

sites.note: 18 sites: 15 dead-end spurs and 3 pull-throughs, with ample turn-around and trailer parking. 'Maximum spur length is 45 feet. Not all sites will fit vehicles of this length.'

facilities.note: Hand-pump drinking water and trash service only in the summer season (Memorial Day weekend to Labor Day weekend); off-season no water, pack out trash.

booking.note: Pay at the fee box by the entrance, cash or check.

name: Highway Springs Campground
note: Rio Grande NF campground just off US 160, 4.1 mi southwest of South Fork toward Wolf Creek Pass. The upper loop circles a knoll above the highway under mature ponderosa; access down to the South Fork of the Rio Grande for fishing. --Claude

sites.note: 13 sites in two loops (3 pull-through); all tent sites are in the lower loop. The FS describes adequate turnaround and parking for RVs but posts no length limit.

facilities.note: No drinking water or firewood provided.

season.note: Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day (2026 concessionaire season began May 22).

booking.note: Pay by envelope at the collection box near the entrance (cash or check).

name: Bristol Head Campground
note: Rio Grande NF (Divide RD), run by a concessionaire; ~21.6 mi from Creede on Hwy 149 (toward Lake City), then 0.3 mi of gravel FR 510. In a meadow on a bench above South Clear Creek with spruce and aspen for some shade; every site faces Bristol Head peak. A short trail leads to an overlook of the Clear Creek canyons and a waterfall. Moose often seen. --Claude

sites.note: 15 sites, 11 pull-through, the rest dead-end spurs, strung 0.6 mile along a bench above South Clear Creek. The FS page gives site lengths of 35-55 ft in its description and a 50-ft maximum spur under Parking ('Not all sites will fit vehicles of this length').

facilities.note: Trash service by the concessionaire Memorial Day to Labor Day.

season.note: Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day weekend; concessionaire operations for 2026 began May 22.

booking.note: All sites first come, first served; pay cash or check with the fee envelopes at the collection box near the entrance. Check-in after 2 p.m., check-out before 11 a.m.

sites.note: 19 large, well-spaced sites in one loop, 4 of them pull-through. Maximum trailer length 30 ft; two vehicles per site.

season.note: 2026 season scheduled May 19 - November 18 ('Dates may change'); seasons of use mid-May to mid-November.

name: North Crestone Creek Campground
note: Rio Grande NF (Saguache Ranger District) rustic campground strung up the canyon along North Crestone Creek, 1.3 mi north of Crestone on Alder Street; quiet, widely spaced sites. Camping is not allowed at the North Crestone Trailhead. --Claude

sites.note: Sites spaced far apart along 0.7 mile of North Crestone Creek among aspen, juniper and fir; one is a pull-through. No length limit is posted.

facilities.note: Bear-resistant food locker at every site (food only, not trash).

season.note: 2026 season May 15 (the conditions line says May 11) to November 18. The forest road beyond (FR 950) is closed Nov 25 - May 1.

booking.note: Best chance at a site is a weekday (Monday-Friday) morning.

name: Big Creek Lakes Campground
note: Routt NF (Parks RD) campground beside 343-acre Big Creek Lake near the Mount Zirkel Wilderness, about an hour (35 mi) NW of Walden via CO-125, CR 6W and gravel FR 600. Mostly large gravel pull-throughs in lodgepole and fir; pine-beetle thinning has opened some sites to sun. Moose often seen. No potable water at present: bring your own. --Claude

sites.note: 54 sites: 24 reservable, 30 first-come. The FS page gives no length; the recreation.gov catalog for the 24 reservable sites lists 20 ft (5 sites), 30 (9), 40 (4) and 50 (6), 15 of them pull-through. Two vehicles per site.

facilities.note: 'Currently there is no potable water, campers should come prepared with their own water. No date has been determined as to when it will have potable water again.' Two boat ramps; a horse corral near site 17 (first come).

season.note: Early June to mid/late October, weather dependent.

booking.note: 24 sites reservable on recreation.gov (up to 7 days before arrival); the other 30 are first-come. The FS page says first-come sites take exact cash or check, with payment instructions at the kiosk. Campground host mid-June to mid-September.

note: Routt NF campground beside 160-acre Hahns Peak Lake, 2 mi west of CR 129 on FR 486, in spruce/pine/fir. The Lake Loop sits on a peninsula with the lake on two sides; the Woods Loop is ~200 m west, away from the water. Lake is non-motorized/electric-motor boats only; the West Side Lake Trail follows the shore. --Claude

name: Dry Lake Campground
note: Hahns Peak/Bears Ears RD (Routt NF): aspen and spruce-fir campground on lower Buffalo Pass Rd (CR 38), about 8 mi NE of Steamboat Springs near Strawberry Park Hot Springs, beside the busy Dry Lake Trailhead. Rebuilt and expanded in 2024 from 8 sites; reopened 2025. The road is good to the campground (the rough stretch is beyond it toward Buffalo Pass). 'Dry Lake' is an 8-inch-deep pond that dries up by early summer. --Claude

booking.note: Sites open for booking two weeks ahead; five sites are first-come, and from Sept 15 the whole campground is first-come (2026). Pay at the kiosk by exact cash or check for walk-up sites.

name: Freeman Reservoir Campground
note: Medicine Bow-Routt NF campground beside Freeman Reservoir (non-motorized boats only), 21 mi north of Craig: Hwy 13 north 12 mi, then 8.5 mi of graded gravel on Moffat CR 11 - don't follow GPS routes via CR 40, which campers report gated on private land. Open meadow at the reservoir's southeast end; site 17 has the best lake view. Horse riding, motorbike and hiking trails; California Park nearby (closed to vehicles May 15 - July 1 for sandhill cranes). Formerly run by Moffat County; the FS said it would resume management in June 2026. --Claude

sites.note: The FS page gives no site count or length limit. Aggregators list 17 or 18 sites, pull-through and back-in, with a 25-ft or 32-ft maximum; a 26-ft Class B+ fitted in 2022, but campers call the sites small.

facilities.note: The FS says there is no potable water; a 2022 camper reported a hand-pumped well west of site 1. Bring water.

name: Hidden Lakes Campground
note: Routt NF campground beside a small mountain lake, 32 mi southwest of Walden, near several small lakes and a reservoir (trout; no motorized boats). Access: CO 14 to Hebron, County Road 24 west (becomes Forest Road 60 at the forest boundary), then Forest Road 20 south ~6 mi; the FS gives no high-clearance warning. --Claude

sites.note: 9 single sites, each with a picnic table and fire grate. Most mature pines were removed after the beetle kill, so there is little shade.

facilities.note: No trash service: pack out all trash.

booking.note: Pay at the kiosk, exact cash or check only.

name: Kenosha Pass Campground
note: Small Pike NF campground at the summit of Kenosha Pass on US-285, in lodgepole and aspen; the Colorado Trail runs through it, and the Kenosha Pass Interpretive Area (wetlands, old South Park railroad) is across the highway. Dirt and gravel parking aprons. --Claude

note: Pike NF campground in the Jefferson Lake Recreation Area, strung along a forested ridge above the Jefferson Creek valley, a mile below Jefferson Lake; Colorado Trail access. Bear country (bear-resistant storage order). Access via unpaved CR-37, not plowed in winter. --Claude

name: Lodgepole Campground (Jefferson)
note: Largest of the Jefferson Lake Recreation Area campgrounds, in aspen and mixed conifer in the Jefferson Creek valley, 4 miles north of Jefferson off CR 35 and CR 37, 3 miles below Jefferson Lake. Colorado Trail access. Campers report CR 37 as graded dirt, bumpy but passable for cars and RVs, and tight maneuvering for larger rigs. --Claude

name: Timberline Campground (Kenosha)

Reservations need Friday and Saturday nights on weekends and 3 nights on holiday weekends; walk-ups are exempt. After Labor Day the whole campground is first come through December.

note: South Park RD, Pike NF: about 4 miles NW of Jefferson off CR 35 and CR 54; campground roads unpaved. Bears are common and a bear closure order applies: keep attractants in hard-sided vehicles or bear boxes. --Claude

facilities.note: No trash service: pack it in, pack it out. Services may be reduced early and late in the season.

season.note: Forest Service: 'open mid-May to mid-October, weather dependent'. Dates are recreation.gov's 2026 first-come fee season (2027: May 14 - Oct 10).

booking.note: Strictly first-come; a site must be occupied the same night. Pay at the self-service fee tube (cash, check, money order) or with recreation.gov Scan & Pay.

name: Aspen Campground (Jefferson)
note: USFS (Pike-San Isabel NF, South Park Ranger District), concessionaire-run, in the Jefferson Lake Recreation Area: a single loop under aspen and spruce near Jefferson Creek, a few miles below Jefferson Lake. From Jefferson on US-285, County Road 35 about 2 miles then County Road 37 about 2.5 miles (gravel). Colorado Trail access nearby. --Claude

sites.note: 11 sites in one loop, gravel aprons; 7 are catalogued tent-only. The FS caps trailers at 25 ft; only two sites take 23 ft or more: 001 (30 ft, pull-through) and 009 (26 ft, back-in). 004 takes 22 ft; the rest 14-22 ft.

facilities.note: Drinking water from a hand pump; picnic table, fire ring or grate and pedestal grill at each site; firewood sold at the host site.

season.note: Open mid-May to mid-October, weather permitting; the recreation-area gate is open 24 hours in season. Roads are not plowed in winter.

booking.note: recreation.gov season 2026: May 15 - Oct 11 (2027: May 14 - Oct 10). Booking closes 5 days before arrival; sites not reserved by then become first-come walk-ups, which must be occupied the same night (pay at the self-service fee tube: cash, check or money order). 14 consecutive nights maximum; 2-night weekend minimum on reservations. Check-in 2 p.m., check-out noon; up to eight people, two tents and two vehicles or one RV per site.

name: Devil's Head Campground
note: South Platte RD (Pike NF), concessionaire-run: two loops on the Rampart Range, at the base of Devil's Head and its fire-lookout trail (#611), ~10 mi south on gravel Rampart Range Rd from CO 67. The lower loop near Jackson Creek is closed until sediment is cleared (FS, 2026); the upper loop is a dry forested ridge. --Claude

facilities.note: Onsite host and trash in the peak season (Memorial Day - Labor Day); reduced services after.

season.note: Typically Memorial Day week to late September, weather dependent; full service ends after Labor Day weekend. Rampart Range Road closes by Dec 1 each year and reopens (target April 1) when conditions allow.

booking.note: Claim a site in person; pay by cash, check or money order, or Scan & Pay in the recreation.gov app. Two vehicles or one RV per site.

name: Coffee Pot Spring Campground
note: Small Forest Service campground on a south-facing aspen/spruce slope, roughly 16 miles up Coffee Pot Road (FDR 600) from the Dotsero exit off I-70, a long, narrow one-lane gravel road. Not on the White River NF's campground list or its 2026 operating-dates sheet (checked 2026-10-28), and Campendium now lists it as dispersed camping; the loop still shows on imagery. Confirm with the Eagle-Holy Cross Ranger District before going. --Claude

name: Homestake Valley Campground
note: Designated-site Forest Service campground (formerly the informal Blodgett/Homestake established-dispersed sites) spread along the lower gravel of Homestake Road (FSR 703) and Missouri Creek Road southwest of Red Cliff, overlooking Homestake Creek. Some sites take RVs and others only personal vehicles, and turnarounds are limited, so pick an RV-capable site. No restrooms: solid human waste must be packed out (a self-contained RV qualifies); fire rings and tables. The graded lower road is passable for most vehicles (the rough 4WD pitch is the last mile to the reservoir, well past the campground). --Claude

name: Marshall Park Campground
note: Rio Grande NF, ~7 mi SW of Creede off Hwy 149 (FR 523), the closest forest campground to Creede: an open meadow between the highway and the Rio Grande, with views of Bristol Head; highway traffic is visible and audible. Paved loop, passenger-car access; ADA fishing access with a boat launch. --Claude

sites.note: FS: 16 sites in one large loop (7 paved pull-throughs, 9 gravel dead-end spurs), the host usually in site 16. recreation.gov lists 15: 14 RV sites (8 reservable, 6 first-come) and tent-only site 007. FS: 'Maximum trailer length is 40 feet'; 'Maximum spur length is 40 feet. Not all sites will fit vehicles of this length.' Up to 8 people and 2 vehicles per site; open meadow with little shade or screening from CO-149.

facilities.note: No drinking water (bring your own); a sink-water disposal facility; trash Memorial Day-Labor Day; firewood from the host.

Weekend 2-night and holiday-weekend 3-night minimums on recreation.gov. A reserved site is held until check-out time the day after arrival. 2026 reservation season May 22-Sep 7 (2027: May 28-Sep 6). Tends to be full mid-June through August.

name: River Hill Campground
note: Rio Grande NF double-loop campground in a willow meadow on the Rio Grande just below Rio Grande Reservoir (2.3 mi to its lower end): from Creede 20.1 mi southwest on CO 149, then 9.5 mi west on gravel FR 520 (Rio Grande Reservoir Rd). Many sites well screened by trees. Popular; usually full mid-June through August. Weminuche Creek and Grizzly Creek trails into the Weminuche Wilderness nearby. --Claude

sites.note: FS: 20 sites, 'Maximum spur length is 55 feet. Not all sites will fit vehicles of this length.' recreation.gov's catalog lists 18 (001-018), lengths 25-125 ft (site 005 25 ft; 45 ft at 003, 006, 007, 017; 125 ft at 011 and 013 is a placeholder); pull-throughs 002, 005, 011, 012, 013, 014.

facilities.note: Two lit vault toilets; drinking water from two well hand pumps (trailers may not fill at the hydrants). Trash service Memorial Day to Labor Day.

Two-night weekend and three-night holiday-weekend minimums (recreation.gov rules). 14 nights in any 30. A reserved site not occupied by check-out time the day after arrival goes to first-come. 2026 reservation season May 22 - Sept 7 (2027: May 28 - Sept 6). Check-in after 2 p.m., check-out before 11 a.m.

name: Thirty Mile Campground
note: Rio Grande NF, ~11 mi west on FR 520 off Hwy 149, ~1 mi below Rio Grande Reservoir in a wooded meadow between the Rio Grande and Grizzly Creek. Trailheads to the Weminuche Wilderness (Grizzly Creek #814, Weminuche Creek #818); no horse trailers in the campground (stock unloading area 3/4 mi east on FR 520). Concessionaire-run. --Claude

season.note: Open year-round but may be inaccessible from snow or spring road closures. Full service (water, trash, host, higher fee) Memorial Day weekend - Labor Day weekend; the 2026 concessionaire season began May 22.

name: Road Canyon Campground
note: Rio Grande NF, ~6 mi west on FR 520 (Rio Grande Reservoir Rd) off Hwy 149 (~20 mi SW of Creede), in an open treeless meadow at the head of Road Canyon Reservoir, not screened from the road (sites not at the shoreline). Fishing access and a primitive boat launch on the reservoir (no wakes, trolling motors OK). Usually has vacancy when the upriver campgrounds are full. --Claude

name: Rock Creek Campground
note: Rio Grande NF (Divide RD) campground and picnic area beside fast-moving Rock Creek in a stand of mature aspen, in a narrow valley, close to Monte Vista: CO 15 south 2.4 mi, right 2.5 mi to a T, then left 10 mi on CR 28 (dirt after 3.1 mi and single-lane in places, but passable by passenger vehicle). FS says some sites are next to the creek, but no per-site map or legible imagery shows a pad at the waterline. No horses in campsites. --Claude

facilities.note: No trash service or receptacles; pack out all garbage.

Reached by FSR 250, either 23 mi up the Conejos from CO-17 or over Stunner Pass from the Alamosa River side. Access point for the South San Juan Wilderness. --Claude Oct 2026: the Rio Grande NF conditions page says 'FSR 250 between Stunner to Highway 17 has damage - 4WD is recommended' after the October storm; check road status before going. --Claude 2026-10-28

note: Rio Grande NF (Saguache Ranger District) campground on a spruce-and-aspen hillside above the South Fork of Carnero Creek. From US 285 take County Road 41G west 6 miles (paved), then gravel Carnero Creek Road (FR 690) 10 miles and FR 675 west 1.5 miles; the road becomes dirt and single-lane with turnouts inside the forest. No horses or pack animals in the campground. Group picnic area and the rentable Carnero Guard Station cabin nearby. --Claude

name: Spectacle Lake Campground
note: Rio Grande NF (Conejos Peak RD) in the Conejos River canyon, on a bench inside a bend of the river; most sites look up at the canyon's cliff walls. Small Spectacle Lake (entering the lake is prohibited by forest order) is across FR 250 from the campground; fishing access to the river and the lake. Access via CO-17 then 6.3 mi on dirt FR 250. October 2026: flood damage on FR 250 between Stunner and CO-17, where the Forest Service recommends 4WD until repaired. --Claude

name: Big Meadows Campground
note: Rio Grande NF (Divide RD), run by a concessionaire; ~11 mi W of South Fork, 1.8 mi off US-160 on FR 410 (passenger-car access), in 3 loops up the lightly wooded hillside above Big Meadows Reservoir, not on the shore. Boat ramp and accessible fishing pier on the reservoir's north shore. --Claude

The recreation.gov catalog lists 20-60 ft (most 40-50 ft; one 20-ft site) with 12 pull-throughs. Single sites hold 6 people and 1 vehicle (up to 8 and 2 for $10/night each extra).

facilities.note: Drinking water in the peak season only; trailers may not fill at the hydrants. Nearest dump station 13 miles away at the Rainbow Grocery in South Fork. Trash service Memorial Day to Labor Day only.

booking.note: 23 sites reservable on recreation.gov or 877-444-6777, at least 4 days ahead and up to 6 months out (12 months for the group area); 19 first-come. A reservation not occupied by check-out time the day after arrival is released to first-come campers. 14-night limit in any 30 days. Check-in after 2 p.m., check-out before 11 a.m.

name: Park Creek Campground
note: Rio Grande NF campground strung along the South Fork of the Rio Grande just off US-160, 7.8 miles west of South Fork and 9.5 miles below Wolf Creek Pass; shady and secluded with heavy understory, but highway noise carries day and night. A handy overnight stop on US-160. --Claude

sites.note: 13 gravel sites, maximum spur 35 ft but not every site takes that length; some sites are wider for larger RVs, and there is turnaround and parking space for trailers. Many sites sit beside the river under mature spruce and cottonwood.

facilities.note: Two vault toilets, hand-pump drinking water in season, central refuse bin (trash service Memorial Day - Labor Day); table and steel fire ring at each site, no firewood provided. Bear country.

The two stocked Tucker Ponds (~10 acres each) are across the road from the entrance, not in the campground. --Claude

name: Aspen Glade Campground
note: USFS (Rio Grande NF, Conejos Peak Ranger District), concessionaire-run (PMC), on the Conejos River off CO-17 about 15 miles west of Antonito. Three loops: A and B lightly wooded with ponderosa pine, C heavily wooded with spruce, aspen and fir along the river. Gold Medal fly-fishing-only water starts 1/4 mile upstream; Sheep Creek Trail nearby. --Claude

sites.note: 32 sites in three loops, 7 of them pull-throughs, including two host sites (018 and 019 in loop B). Catalogued lengths run 20-90 ft and nearly every site takes 23 ft or more (only 009, 20 ft, does not); the FS caps RVs at 45 ft.

facilities.note: Water spigots (no trailer filling at the hydrants); picnic table and fire ring at each site; bear-proof trash containers.

booking.note: Reservable on recreation.gov or 1-877-444-6777 (2026 season May 23 - Aug 31; 2027 May 28 - Sep 6); booking closes 4 days before arrival. Ten public sites are catalogued not reservable, so first-come sites may be available but are not guaranteed. A reserved site is held until check-out time the day after arrival, then released as a no-show to first-come campers. 14 nights in any 30 consecutive days, strictly enforced. Six people and one vehicle included per single site; up to 8 people and 2 vehicles at $10 a night each extra.

name: Lakeview Campground (Taylor Park)
note: GMUG campground on a pine-and-spruce slope above Taylor Park Reservoir, south of CR 742 (Taylor Canyon Road) across from the marina; most sites look out over the reservoir to the Sawatch Range. Boat ramp just below; fishing and pontoon boat rentals at the marina. Dump station nearby. Largest of the Taylor Park campgrounds. --Claude

Extra vehicles $13-23 a night, paid to the host.

name: Island Lake Campground
note: Grand Mesa NF campground, one of the few on the Mesa not on a lake: Island Lake (boat ramp, fishing pier) is 0.1 mi east. Most sites sit in thick mature spruce; a few have panoramic views over the Grand Valley and the lakes below. Mosquitoes are plentiful. Access via paved CO-65 then 1.4 mi of gravel FR-116. --Claude

name: Big Creek Campground
note: Grand Mesa NF (Grand Valley RD) campground on the south shore of Big Creek Reservoir; the loop runs along the shore behind a fringe of conifers and most sites are shady. Hand-pump water. Reached by a long gravel road: FR 121 from CO-65 north of Cedaredge, or CR 58/59 then FR 521 from Collbran. Reservoir is drawn down in summer and recent reviews call the grounds run-down but operating. --Claude

No motorboats on the slough. Campers report FR 706 as narrow dirt with tight turns, passable for cars and RVs to about 28-30 ft, with larger trailers discouraged. --Claude

note: San Juan NF campground in ponderosa pine beside Haviland Lake, ~18 mi north of Durango off US 550, reached across the dam on FR 671. The lake is a CPW State Wildlife Area (wakeless: electric trolling motors or hand-powered boats only); using it needs a SWA pass or a fishing/hunting license. --Claude

name: Sig Creek Campground
note: San Juan NF (Columbine RD) campground ~6 mi west of Purgatory Ski Resort on Hermosa Park Rd (FR 578): a small loop beside Sig Creek, ~200 m from the East Fork of Hermosa Creek. The FS says FR 578 to the campground is accessible by 2WD; the upper section over Bolam Pass is 4WD only. Hermosa Creek Trailhead is 2 mi past the campground. --Claude

name: Transfer Park Campground
note: Former mining-era ore transfer station on 11 acres above the Florida River, ~1 mi past Florida Campground: from Durango ~13 mi on Florida Road (CR 240), then CR 243 / FR 596 ~8.5 mi, passing through Florida Campground. Burnt Timber Trail parking (Weminuche Wilderness) is near the campground. --Claude

booking.note: First come, first served only; claim a site in person and pay on site (recreation.gov Scan & Pay).

note: One of the largest campgrounds on the San Juan NF, on Vallecito Creek beside the Weminuche Wilderness, ~3 mi up County Road 500 from the Vallecito community (Vallecito Reservoir 4 mi). Sites near the creek fill first. Vallecito Creek Trail (hiking/horse) starts at the entrance, with hitching posts and a livestock dock but no horse camping; fly and lure fishing only; seven fee picnic sites along the creek. Concessionaire-run. --Claude

sites.note: Four loops (B, C, D, W); most sites large and fairly level, shaded by ponderosa, aspen and oak. Everything with wheels must fit the parking spur; no overflow parking. Catalog vehicle maximums run 28-50 ft (one site 20 ft).

season.note: May through September (recreation.gov has exact dates). In 2026 it stays partly open, with no water and limited services, from the end of September to November 15.

name: Bridge Campground
note: San Juan NF (Pagosa RD) campground in a flat, open meadow beside Williams Creek, ~18 mi NW of Pagosa Springs via Piedra Road (FR 631, gravel, open year-round and suitable for most vehicles). Large sites with views of the high peaks to the north. No horses in the campground. --Claude

Check-in 2 p.m., check-out noon (any time if the site is empty). Generators no more than an hour at a time; quiet 10 p.m. - 6 a.m.

name: Cayton Campground
note: San Juan NF (Dolores RD) campground in a meadow ringed by fir and aspen beside the Dolores River: 6 mi NE of Rico on Hwy 145 (San Juan Skyway, paved), then 0.5 mi on Barlow Creek Rd (FR 578). The electric sites are in Loop A on the river side, behind a band of conifers; non-electric Loop B is set back up the slope. Barlow Creek Rd beyond the campground over Bolam Pass is often limited to 4WD. --Claude

sites.note: 27 sites in two loops plus 3 day-use picnic sites. The FS page states 'Max RV size = 50 ft'; recreation.gov's catalog lists 30-70 ft, 10 of them pull-throughs (9 in Loop A). Rigs must fit in the parking spur (no overflow parking).

facilities.note: Dump station costs $15 to use.

name: Ophir Creek Campground
note: San Carlos Ranger District campground strung along Ophir Creek in a narrow canyon on FSR 361, just off CO-165 north of Lake Isabel (west of Wetmore), past a private campground at the turnoff. Sites 1-19 take trailers/RVs; 20-31 are walk-up tent sites. A trail behind site 22 leads a mile to a small waterfall; Bishop's Castle is 4 miles away. --Claude

sites.note: Sites 1-19 are drive-in; 20-31 are tent-only, up a hill from the road (car or motorcycle parking only, no trailers or rooftop tents). The catalog gives RV lengths only for sites 3 (40 ft), 5, 18 and 19 (32 ft); site 1 is listed at 15 ft. One RV, or two tents and two vehicles, and 8 people a site.

facilities.note: Four accessible outhouses; hand-pump water (seasonal). Picnic table, fire ring and pedestal grill at each site. Firewood sold at the host site ($10 a bundle). Bear country: store attractants hard-sided.

season.note: Early May to late September, weather dependent; services may be missing early and late in the season.

booking.note: Reserve on recreation.gov or 877-444-6777 at least four days ahead; some sites are first-come and must be occupied the first night. The Forest Service page says Friday+Saturday is required on weekends and three nights on holiday weekends (walk-ups exempt), but recreation.gov's rules set no minimum. Reservation season 2026 May 15 - Sept 19 (2027: May 14 - Sept 18), with first-come weeks either side.

name: Rancho Del Rio
note: Private rafting outpost on the Upper Colorado River at State Bridge, ~20 acres of riverside camping with standard and premium RV sites, car-camping, walk-in and group sites, and cabins. Boat ramp/raft put-in, vehicle shuttles and gear rental. Access via Trough Road (Grand County Rd 1, the Colorado River Headwaters Scenic Byway), a maintained gravel road -- passable by 2WD when dry (rutted/slick after heavy rain). No cell service (Wi-Fi calls work; landline at the store). --Claude

facilities.note: Potable water only for filling small jugs, not RV tanks; the nearest dump station is in Edwards, about 20 minutes away. Convenience store, restaurant and liquor store on site. Wi-Fi across the property including the campground, for browsing and calls only.
