name: The Campers Hub
note: Newer RV park on the Montrose outskirts (~20 km from Black Canyon of the Gunnison NP), still being built out, with mountain views, a pond (no swimming) and a dog park; a bike path runs into town. Built for recreational campers rather than long-term housing (monthly stays by application). --Claude

hookups.note: Full hookups (50 amp, water, sewer) on the pull-through sites; the cheaper back-in sites have 20/30 amp only or 50 amp and sewer without water.

sites.note: Back-in sites are straight, single-vehicle spurs for rigs under 30 ft; the full-hookup pull-throughs are 70 ft.

facilities.note: Two restrooms with 24/7 showers in the outbuilding, two more in the main building during coworking hours; laundry $10 a load; free Wi-Fi and a fiber-internet coworking space (9 am - 6 pm) in a renovated 1945 schoolhouse. No dump station: guests can dump and fill free at a vacant pull-through (ask the office); passers-through pay $5-$20.

booking.note: Booked online through Firefly Reservations (nightly, with a Motorhome Class C equipment type). Cancellation: full refund 30+ days out, 50% at 14-30 days, none inside 14 days; the $3.50 service fee is not refunded. Tent stays are limited to 3 nights.

name: Carter Lake - Eagle Campground
note: Larimer County campground at the north end of Carter Lake, west of Loveland; the loop runs from a hill above the lake (E01-E22, with lake views) down into a meadow below the dam (E23-E49, no view). --Claude

sites.note: 47 50-amp electric sites (E02-E49 without E34), 43 of them pull-through, listed for vehicles 32-80 ft (most 40-50). E01-E22 sit on a hill overlooking the lake; E23-E49 are in a meadow below the dam with no lake view.

facilities.note: Token-operated shower house with flush toilets next to the overflow lot; vault toilets around the loop. Water spigots are shut off September-April except the frost-free ones.

booking.note: A reservation and a park entrance permit are required before setting up at any site; a no-show unannounced within 24 hours may lose the site (call 970-619-4570). Check-in noon, check-out 11 am. One wheeled camping unit per site.

name: Chief Hosa Campground

booking.note: Reservation required, online only (no in-person or phone payments); a season's bookings open on one February morning (February 11 at 8 am for 2026). Same-day bookings online until 8 pm, on your own device or the office terminal. 14 days in any 28. $5 cancellation charge, one night's rate within 7 days.

name: Clear Creek RV Park
note: City of Golden municipal RV park on the banks of Clear Creek at 1401 10th St, a half-mile walk along the creek path to downtown Golden; the Golden Community Center (pools, gym) is across the street. --Claude

sites.note: Creek-side full-hookup sites, full hookups in the "Island", and electric-and-water sites; all with 20/30/50 amp. Sites are "rated true to size" on the booking engine: pick one your rig fits. One RV per site; no cargo or flatbed trailers in tow, no car camping, converted buses or tiny houses; RVs must meet ANSI/RVIA standards. Tent sites April-October only, booked in person or by phone.

booking.note: Reservation-only: book online or at the office (303-278-1437, 9 am-4 pm daily); sites open 60 days ahead at midnight Mountain time. Daily stays are capped at 14 nights in any 30. name: Molas Lake Park & Campground
note: Town-of-Silverton-run park on US-550 (Million Dollar Hwy) at a stocked 25-acre lake. Generators only in the Ultra RV and Rock Cliff RV sites, 8 AM-8 PM; no swimming. --Claude

facilities.note: Hot showers by $5 token, not guaranteed after September 15. A water pump by the office; RVs may take up to 30 gallons. Nearest dump station in Silverton, 10 minutes away. No internet and limited cell service.

name: Pinewood Reservoir Campground
note: Larimer County campground on the northeast end of Pinewood Reservoir west of Carter Lake, part of the Colorado-Big Thompson Project. The county warns the only access is a narrow 4-mile paved road with 8-10% grades and that most sites are small, not recommended for larger RVs and motorhomes. Drinking water runs April-August only; the nearest frost-free spigot is at Flatiron Campground, 4 miles east. Boat ramp closed: hand-launched craft only, no swimming. --Claude

sites.note: 16 drive-in electric sites (P01-P16) and 11 walk-in tent sites (P17-P27) on the booking site; the county's description says 15 electric and 12 walk-in. Max vehicle length by site: 55 (P05, P07, P16), 45 (P09), 40 (P01), 30-35 for most, 15 (P08). Pull-throughs P01-P04, P06, P08, P10-P15. One wheeled camping unit per site.

booking.note: Larimer County's ReserveAmerica site (larimercamping.com) or 1-800-397-7795, same day up to 180 days ahead. March-October, sites not reserved become first-come that day for people at the park (same-day reservations at the visitor centers); November-February a reservation and a park entrance permit must be bought online before setting up. 14 nights in any 30 across the county system. Check-in noon, check-out 11 a.m.; a no-show unannounced within 24 hours may lose the site (970-619-4570).

name: Standley Lake Regional Park
note: City of Westminster regional park on Standley Lake reservoir; no-alcohol park, no glass. The southern 'waterfront loop' (e.g. site 28) overlooks Standley Lake from a low bench set back behind an open grassy/drawdown apron - open lake view, no pads on the shore; interior loops have no water view. --Claude

sites.note: 66 campsites (plus six bell tents); only sites 52 (20-30 A), 53 (30 A) and ADA site 16 (20 A, not recommended for trailers) have electric. One camping unit and one tent, or two tents, per site; one vehicle included.

facilities.note: Two permanent restroom buildings with free open-air showers and drinking water; self-serve water-fill spigots. No dump station in the park; the city's station is at the Big Dry Creek Wastewater Treatment Facility, 13150 Huron Street, for a fee.

booking.note: Reservation only, through the City of Westminster's WebTrac site; booking opens in January each year. Same-day sites are first-come, booked in person before 8 pm. 14 consecutive days, then 24 hours out of the park. Full refund with 72 hours' notice. Gates close at 10 pm; call the gatehouse (303-425-1097) if arriving later.

name: Telluride Town Park Campground
note: Town of Telluride municipal campground between the San Miguel River and Bear Creek, walkable to downtown. A 23-ft rig needs a 25- or 30-ft site. Dump before arriving (the town's wastewater plant takes RV waste by arrangement only). Generators 3-6 p.m. only; charcoal grills, no wood fires; no idling over 30 seconds in town. --Claude

sites.note: 28 vehicle sites (14 Premium on the perimeter or river, 14 Standard in the interior) plus 5 walk-in tent sites. No unit may exceed 30 ft, bumper to bumper or tongue to bumper; sites come in 30, 25 and 20 ft lengths and each has its own limit, which the town does not list per site. Slide-outs not recommended at every site.

season.note: 2026 season May 15 - October 4. During festivals (Bluegrass mid-June, Jazz early August, Blues and Brews mid-September and others) the campground is run by the festival and open only to festival pass holders.

booking.note: Online only, in four booking windows opening at 9 a.m. MT (2026: April 21, May 19, July 7, August 18), each for a block of arrival dates; peak dates sell out within minutes. 7 nights in any 30-day period and 14 nights a season per person; one site per person per day, no group bookings. Give the true vehicle length when booking: the system may move you to another site of the same type and length class. Online pre-check-in required, then check in on site 3-9 p.m.; check-out 2 p.m.

Designated sites in an East and a West campground around the reservoir, each with a fire ring and picnic table; at the East Campground many RV sites sit on the open, treeless shoreline, though not all are on the water. Motorboats barred in 2026 for low water (cartop boats from the west ramp). --Claude

name: Wupperman Campground
note: Hinsdale County campground on the east shore of Lake San Cristobal south of Lake City, on gravel County Road 33. The county's map marks a steep, narrow stretch of CR33 at the overlook between the main sites and the north loop. Sites on the lakeshore and on the cliffs above; public fishing access. --Claude

sites.note: 31 sites of various lengths for RVs, tents and ADA campers, on the lakeshore or on the cliffs above; a few tent-only sites; the north loop (26-31) has no water. No maximum length published.

facilities.note: Water spigots at the toilets; RV tanks may be filled. Bear lockers.

booking.note: First-come, first-served; no reservations. 14-night limit per site.

name: Alexandria State Recreation Area
note: NGPC state rec area on two sandpit lakes (about 18 and 30 acres) 4 mi E of Alexandria. The camping loops wind through shade trees north of the east lake, set back 70-100 m from the water behind a marshy edge. Modern restrooms, playground; camp host Apr-Oct. Self-pay at the Iron Ranger (cash/check). --Claude

name: Bassway Strip State Wildlife Management Area
note: Platte River WMA adjacent to I-80 SE of Kearney. Reservoir levels can run very low in drought. --Claude

note: Nebraska Game and Parks SRA on 20 sandpit lakes (~300 water acres) just west of Fremont off US-30. name: Grove Lake Wildlife Management Area
note: NGPC wildlife management area on 50-acre Grove Lake, 2 mi north of Royal (86502 Grove Lake Rd), with a trout hatchery. Primitive camping is allowed in three areas off the gravel road along the west side of the lake; no hookups. A 2023 camper found almost no amenities (one outhouse, two boat docks) and tight turnarounds for a large motorhome. Directories list tables, fire pits, hydrants and vault toilets. Little or no cell service. --Claude

Two RV campgrounds about 450 m apart off the same park road: Ash Grove (51 Electric Plus, 36 Electric) and Hackberry Hollow (32 Electric Plus, 15 Electric), plus tent, basic, Adirondack-shelter and equestrian camping. The river is far below; no site is near the water. --Claude

note: State park on the bluffs at the Niobrara-Missouri confluence, NE Nebraska. The modern campground is one paved loop with an inner row, east of the park road below the bluffs; the east row backs onto a thick tree belt along a river backwater, with no water view. Carpets on the asphalt pads only. Tent camping on a separate hilly one-way loop. --Claude

Primitive camping only, no pads, at the gravel turnaround in the trees; backwater ponds and the river lie south behind the trees. Pit toilet, picnic tables, grills, playground; no water. --Claude

name: Pressey State Wildlife Area
note: NGPC wildlife management area on the South Loup River north of Oconto. The campground (Google's 'Pressey Park') sits in a bend of the river west of NE 21, reached by about 1 km of gravel from the highway north of the bridge: a few designated electric sites at the entrance turnaround by the picnic shelter, then primitive spots with tables and fire rings strung along the river road through the trees. Vault toilets, playground. A shooting range on the WMA can be noisy (camper reports). State park entry permit required. --Claude

Primitive restrooms; swimming beach. Pay at the iron ranger. Lake levels were low after a 2022 aquatic-habitat renovation plus drought. --Claude

name: Weigand Campground - Lewis and Clark State Recreation Area
note: Weigand camping area of Lewis and Clark SRA (the park headquarters) on the 16-mile Lewis and Clark Lake (Missouri River reservoir) north of Crofton. Paved pads, many shaded; the lakefront row on the lake side of the loop backs onto the shore through a patchy treeline. Coin showers and a playground; the Burbach campground is a separate loop 1.6 km west. Weigand Marina slips and boat ramp closed for marina construction from September 10, 2025 through 2026 (camping not affected). --Claude

booking.note: Reservations must be made at least one day ahead; November nights showed first-come availability only.

name: Wildcat Hills State Recreation Area
note: Pine-ridge SRA on a rocky escarpment ~10 mi S of Gering on NE-71, with a nature center (park HQ), hiking trails and a shooting range. Primitive sites along the interior park roads; NGPC: the summit access road's turnaround is extremely sharp and not for large RVs or long trailers. Most sites are small and no source gives site lengths (NGPC's 2022 map labels the camping 'Basic Nonreservable Tent Camping'), so fit for a 23-ft rig is unconfirmed - ring the park (2026-11-05). Three primitive restrooms; drinking water near the Nature Center. Nearest dump station in Gering. --Claude

booking.note: NGPC says half the sites can be reserved and the other half are first-come; register at the Nature Center, or after hours at the self-pay station (cash or check only). Online bookings must be made at least a day ahead.

name: Bessey Recreation Complex
note: Nebraska National Forest (Bessey Ranger District) campground at Halsey, in the historic hand-planted Bessey forest. Loops of pine-shaded pads, most with electric; a group site and tent-only sites besides. The Middle Loup River (tubing, canoeing) and a 7-acre stocked pond are nearby, but the loops sit back in the trees, not on the water. ATVs may ride from the sites to the trailhead. --Claude

Corps office 308-799-2105. --Claude

Paved main road, gravel loops. Playground, volleyball court, boat ramp and fish-cleaning station; two marinas on the east end. Attendant on duty May-September; all campers check in on arrival. --Claude

name: Methodist Cove
note: USACE park on the west side of 13,000-acre Harlan County Lake, 2.5 mi east of Alma. Mostly shaded; paved main road, gravel back-in spurs. The west non-electric loop sits on open lawn at the shore; the electric loops are behind the shore road. Attendant on duty May-Sept; boat ramp, fish-cleaning station by the entrance, two marinas on the lake's east end. --Claude

Every camper checks in on arrival; one camping unit and six people per site.

note: USACE campground on the south (Nebraska) bank of the Missouri just below Gavins Point Dam, between Hwy 121 and the river: one long row of back-in sites under trees, facing the river across the campground road and the riprap bank. Pine Ridge Trail via the Outrider and Strong Canyon trailheads. Heavy US-385 truck noise. --Claude

name: Soldier Creek Campground (Nebraska NF)
note: Nebraska NF Pine Ridge unit adjacent to Soldier Creek Wilderness and Fort Robinson SP. From Crawford, US-20 to Fort Robinson then ~6 mi north on Soldier Creek Rd (gravel, with a paved creek crossing that can be dicey after heavy rain). Open grassland sites along the corral spur; general campground that also serves horse users (15-paddock corral, round pen, wilderness trailheads). Not inside the state park, so no state park permit is needed. A Forest Service alert (2026-11) posts intermittent closures of FS Road 7055; check it before going. --Claude

booking.note: Walk-in only: pay on site (recreation.gov Scan & Pay). The 14-night limit is the forest-wide order: no more than 14 days in a ranger district within any 30-day period.

name: Toadstool Geological Park Campground
note: Oglala National Grassland (Nebraska NF & Grasslands), NW of Crawford in the badlands; trailhead for the one-mile interpretive loop, the Bison Trail to Hudson-Meng (3 mi) and the Great Plains Trail; replica 1929 sod house. Gravel spurs off a gravel loop with picnic tables, fire rings and grills; no water, bring your own. Reached by Toadstool Road (11.4 mi of gravel from NE Hwy 2, 4.2 mi N of Crawford) and FS Road 902 (1.4 mi): the Forest Service says the roads are very difficult when wet and to wait until they are dry. The Forest Service gives no site length; a camper reported a 25-ft trailer fit, just barely (undated). --Claude

name: Arnold Lake Recreation Area
note: Village of Arnold municipal recreation area half a mile south of town on Hwy 40: 10 acres around a 22-acre lake stocked by Nebraska Game & Parks, mature shade trees. On the village map sites 10, 11 and 13-15 sit along the shore; the $10 primitive sites are the three tent-only ones (7, 8, 12). Open drive-in grassy loop fits a 23-ft rig. RV dump north of the park entrance on the west side of Hwy 40. NGPC only stocks the lake -- not a state rec area despite some directory labels. --Claude

name: Bader Memorial Park
note: Merrick County park run by the nonprofit Platte PEER Group, three miles south of Chapman between the Platte and Wood Rivers. The Prairie campground is an open gravel loop on the prairie (sites 15-40); the 30-amp Cottonwood campground (sites 1-13) sits in the trees by the office. Coin showers (50 cents for three minutes), dump station, convenience items in the office; seven fishing ponds, a swim beach and six miles of trails. Booked online through Firefly. --Claude

name: Bassett City Park
note: RV camping spread through the Rock County Fairgrounds and Bassett City Park south of US-20: fairground sites (donations to the Rock County Ag Society) and the city's pads west of the fishing ponds, 2 of them accessible (donations to the City of Bassett). Water from hydrants around the grounds, not at the sites. Spaces are very limited during the Sandhills Ranch Expo in June, the Rock County Fair at the end of August and the High School Rodeo the weekend after; call City Hall to check dates. A September 2025 camper found the fairground 30/50-amp hookups not turned on. --Claude

note: City-run 55-acre municipal park & arboretum (ball fields, pool, playground) on the south edge of Battle Creek. ~18 RV sites with electric (20/30/50 amp) and water. Pay on site. Caveat (2026-11-05): the city's parks page doesn't mention camping and one trail guide lists only two campsites, so call City Hall (402-675-2165) before counting on a site. --Claude

note: Little Blue NRD's Bruning Dam & Wildlife Management Area: a 250-acre reservoir with 123 acres of public land, 2 mi E, 1 mi N and 1 mi E of Bruning. name: Cody Park
note: City of North Platte campground in Cody Park on the North Platte River; large day-use park (lake, mini-zoo, rides, pool). The pads are for small campers or tents; campers report the bigger ones on the river side of the loop, and site 1 is the only pull-through. Quiet generators allowed. The pads sit inside the loop road, with the road and a grass strip between them and the river. Pads run 18-28 ft: a 22.5-ft motorhome fit with no room to spare (9/2025), and pull-through site 1 took a 39-ft rig - aim for site 1 or a river-side pad. --Claude

booking.note: Limited to 7 days in a one-month period.

name: Crawford City Park
note: City of Crawford municipal park along the White River (a narrow stream here). Four electric pads in the park proper, which campers say back onto the river, plus three non-pad electric sites near the White River Wacipi arbor and dry camping throughout the park complex. Restroom seasonal, no showers. The bridge at the main entrance is posted 5 tons, under a loaded 23-ft motorhome's weight: campers (2024, April 2026) come in instead by the dirt road around the outside of the park to the back entrance. Firsthand reviews report 29-34 ft RVs (incl. a 32-ft Class C) at the electric sites. Frequent BNSF trains sound their horns day and night. Camping at the rodeo grounds goes through the Old West Trail Rodeo Board. --Claude

note: City of Deshler campground in Washington Park (Park St east of 4th St) by the municipal pool and ballfields; ~10-12 sites along the lot. Paved walking path, horseshoes, sand volleyball. CAMPER-REPORTED RATE: first night free, then $15 (July 2025). --Claude

note: Nemaha NRD recreation area on 160-acre Kirkman's Cove Lake, 2.5 mi W and 0.5 mi N of Humboldt. Two camping areas with separate entrances: the Beach Entrance loop off 715 Road on the east shore (all the electric pads, a few non-electric pads, tent camping and the sand swimming beach), and the non-electric pads off the Main Entrance from Hwy 4 on the southwest shore, by the playground and the boat ramp. name: Riverside Campground (Scottsbluff)
note: City of Scottsbluff campground in Riverside Park, with views of Scotts Bluff National Monument; 43 RV sites and 20 tent sites, each with a fire ring and picnic table. The park has playgrounds, disc golf, a dog park, fishing ponds and the Riverside Discovery Center zoo. Golf carts and UTVs aren't allowed. The pads sit well back from the North Platte River, behind a ditch, the park road and a treeline. --Claude

No refunds; a booking can be moved to another date in the same calendar year. Site assignments may change. Tents 7 days, RVs 14.

note: City of Crete Parks & Rec campground in the 96-acre Tuxedo Park, west of the Big Blue River (the Saline County fairgrounds buildings are in the park, but the camping is city-run, not event-only). Two areas: 10 sites by the baseball field along Old Settlers Rd (20/30-amp) and 11 along the river on Cottonwood Rd (20/30/50-amp). The city page says the main entrance crosses a 3-ton bridge (a new concrete bridge opened in 2021, so the posting may be old); a motorhome is over that, so come in by the back entrance off Idaho Road (2026-11-05). --Claude

name: Valentine City Park
note: City of Valentine 40-acre park on North Main Street, just outside town, along Minnechaduza Creek. Primitive camping on undesignated gravel pull-offs beside the park road; low oak branches (a 32-ft Class C got through in 2023). Water spigots around the park; water and restrooms typically shut off in the off-season. No dump station noted. Mill Pond across the road is stocked. CAMPER-REPORTED RATE: $5 (9/2024) and $10 (4/2024) a night, self-pay drop box (RV Life reviews); no city page posts a rate. --Claude

name: Verdigre City Park Camp
note: Village of Verdigre campground in the trees at the south end of Wildwood Acres Park, on the southeast edge of town; oak-shaded, with three primitive sites and two sleeping cabins besides the camper pads. Communal water spigots (no per-site water). Playground, swimming pool (closed for the 2026 season for repairs). Pads are small (a 4/2022 RV Life reviewer called most of them too small, with a handful of larger pads; 9/2017: 'Not for large rigs', 27-ft trailer) - pick a larger pad. Dump station uncertain. --Claude

booking.note: Camping (primitive and pads) is first come, first served; only the two cabins are reserved, through the Village Clerk at 402-668-2621.

name: Wisner River Park
note: City of Wisner river park along the Elkhorn River (south side of town, 1111 Ave E). Concrete camper pads under the trees between the ball fields and the park's gravel river road, plus a row near the rodeo arena by the East Parking Lot; electric at some pads (the city page gives no count or amperage). Kids' fishing pond, boat dock on the Elkhorn. The park hosts the Wisner Lions Club Rodeo, a livestock show and the Thunder by the River truck and tractor pull. --Claude

name: Maskenthine Lake Recreation Area
note: Lower Elkhorn NRD recreation area around a 100-acre flood-control lake, 10 mi east of Norfolk near Stanton; fishing, no-wake boating, swim beach, disc golf, mountain-bike trails, arboretum. The 33 electric camper pads sit on a loop near the swimming beach, 70-100 m from the shore across a mowed lawn and a tree line. Tent area first-come. --Claude

facilities.note: Shower house water is on from about May 1 to October 1, weather permitting.

booking.note: Camper pads book on the NRD's Firefly page up to 60 days ahead; some pads stay first-come, and the tent area is first-come. The portal takes reservations from May 1 on; before that the campground is first-come only ('Campground is open through April 30th on a first-come first-served basis'). Weekends need Friday and Saturday; Memorial Day weekend needs Friday, Saturday and Sunday (the only holiday the portal names).

name: Clear Lake State Park (IA)
note: On the southeast shore of Clear Lake at the edge of the town of Clear Lake. The loops sit in open oak woods about 120 m east of the shore, behind South Shore Drive and a wooded strip; the 900-ft sand beach and the day-use lodge are nearby. The South Loop is closed for the rest of the 2026 season for fire-ring pad installation (sites 1-108 stay open until December 1; ReserveAmerica notice of 2026-11-02). --Claude

name: Pine Lake State Park
note: Iowa DNR park on Upper and Lower Pine Lake and the Iowa River near Eldora. One campground in open-grown trees west of the lake, with 22 long pull-throughs; the east loop's outer sites look toward the lake past the loop road and a shoreline tree belt. Boat ramps, fishing jetties and an unsupervised beach; CCC lodge and four stone cabins. Modern restrooms and showers close for the season in mid-October; hydrants and dump stay on. No daily Iowa park-entry fee. --Claude

name: Red Haw State Park
note:
Iowa state park on high cliff overlooking 72-acre Red Haw Lake.  Some sites wooded, some full sun; threaded potable spigot at dump station; roads and facilities are somewhat poorly maintained.  No daily park-entry fee in Iowa, camping fee only.  --AWH
51 public campsites since the campground reopened. --Claude

sites.note: ReserveAmerica lists 52 campsites: 41 electric RV sites, 1 non-electric RV site, 9 tent-only sites, plus the host site and 3 shelters. Listed equipment lengths for RV sites 20-70 ft (most 55-60 ft); all listed driveways back-in.

season.note: ReserveAmerica: reservations April 1 - November 30 ('Open through Mon Nov 30 2026'). The DNR page says the campground 'accepts reservation April - October and is closed November - March', so the two official pages disagree about November.

booking.note: ReserveAmerica, campsites up to 3 months ahead. The booking site says the campground 'is 100 percent reservable and accepts reservations April 1 - November 30 until 10:00 pm CST the day of arrival'; the DNR page says 'The campground is 100% reservable and a reservation is required.' Iowa's rule for a 100%-reservable campground: a Saturday alone (or Saturday/Sunday on a holiday weekend) can be booked once the cutoff for the Friday arrival has passed unreserved; a Friday night alone cannot.

Memorial Day and Labor Day weekends; July 4th when it falls on a Monday

The campground fills a peninsula on the lake's east shore: electric loops to the north, a non-electric loop to the south, and back-in rows on both loops facing the water. Marina concession (mid-April to mid-October) rents pontoons, fishing boats, canoes and kayaks; swim beach, boat ramps, jetties and 8+ miles of multi-use trails. --Claude

name: Springbrook State Park
note: Iowa DNR state park ~9 mi N of Guthrie Center, 930 acres of timber and prairie with CCC-era structures. The campground lies in the woods south of the 17-acre lake's dam, across the park road and a day-use strip (playground, courts) from it; the swim beach, fishing jetties and docks are on the lake (electric trolling motors only), and a boat ramp at the south end reaches the Middle Raccoon River. The four-bedroom Sherburne House rents as a group cabin. 12 miles of trails. --Claude

name: Stone State Park
note: Iowa DNR park in the Loess Hills on the north-west edge of Sioux City. One small wooded campground: 8 electric and 4 non-electric back-in sites of 30-42 ft for RVs, the rest tent-only, plus a youth-group site and three camping cabins; modern restroom and shower building, water hydrants, no dump station. CCC-built lodge and shelters; 15 miles of hiking, mountain-bike and multi-use trails; the Dorothy Pecaut Nature Center (Woodbury County) is next door. No daily Iowa park-entry fee. --Claude

The modern campground runs along a wooded valley road; a separate, more primitive equestrian campground sits to the north-east. Trails for hiking, mountain biking and horses; 7-acre Lake Virginia (electric motors only); eight cabins. --Claude

name: Wilson Island State Recreation Area
note: Iowa DNR recreation area of 544 acres of cottonwood woods in the Missouri River bottoms west of I-29 exit 72, next to DeSoto National Wildlife Refuge. One large, well-shaded campground of long back-in sites (45-70 ft), set back in the woods about 200 m from the river. Showers, flush toilets, dump station, playground; three youth-group areas. Missouri River boat ramp and dock; about five miles of trails; the area outside the campground is open to hunting in season. --Claude

name: Yellow River State Forest - Little Paint Campground
note: Primitive drive-in campground in the Paint Creek Unit of Yellow River State Forest, strung for about a kilometre along Little Paint Creek (a stocked trout stream); grassy sites with tables and fire rings. --Claude

name: Bob Shetler Recreation Area (Saylorville Lake)

name: Willow Lake Recreation Area
note: Harrison County Conservation Board park and headquarters, 6 miles northwest of Woodbine on F20L, on a 27-acre fishing lake (electric motors only). The campground wraps the lake's narrow north arm; sites 1-6 on the south loop and the pads at the peninsula's tip sit a few steps from the shore. Electric sites with water hydrants nearby, two shower houses, swimming beach, boat ramp, fishing jetties and pier, nature center, 6 miles of trails. No dump station (use the city parks in Woodbine or Pisgah). Up to 1 RV and 1 tent per site. --Claude

season.note: Park gates are closed to vehicles November 1 to April 1; walk-in campers are still welcome then. Shower houses open April 1 - October 31, weather dependent.

name: Pammel Park Campground
note: Madison County Conservation Board park (one of Iowa's first state parks, county-run since 1989), 4 miles southwest of Winterset on the Middle River. The main (north) entrance goes through the Harmon Tunnel, 12 ft 6 in clearance with a fairly tight turn at its east end; the county's alternate route from US 169 via Carver Trail and Pammel Park Trail enters by the south gates and avoids it. --Claude

sites.note: South Campground: 47 numbered water/electric sites (24 reservable online, 23 walk-in; gravel pads 45-71 ft) plus a tent area; the host uses 39-40. North Campground: 15 numbered full-hookup sites (50-64; 15 x 40 ft pads), all walk-in.

North seasonal sites are drawn by lottery in March; sites left over are first come. Check-in after 4 pm, check-out by 3 pm.

note: State-owned park run by the Appanoose County Conservation Board, which has its offices and nature center here, on the wooded bluffs above the Chariton River east of Centerville. name: Coffins Grove Park
note: Delaware County Conservation Board park (22 acres of bur oak woods) 4 mi NW of Manchester on Early Stagecoach Rd. One gravel loop: the water/electric sites in a row along the east edge, electric-only sites inside the loop, primitive sites at its north end. Coffins Grove Creek runs through the woods north of the loop (stream fishing); the county warns it can flood into the park. Two picnic shelters, ball diamond, playground. --Claude

name: Snively Access Campground
note: Louisa County Conservation campground on the shore of Lake Odessa (the Odessa Wildlife Management Complex, a Mississippi backwater), 3 mi from Wapello off the Great River Road, with a paddle launch for the Odessa Water Trail. The gravel road down from the bluff is winding and steep: doable, but go slow. Subject to river flooding; call ahead in flood season. --Claude

booking.note: Book a site on mycountyparks.com or with the QR code at the campground; all sales are final, though a flood closure is refunded.

name: Turtle Creek Park
note: Delaware County Conservation park 3.5 miles southwest of Delhi on the Lake Delhi impoundment of the Maquoketa River, home to the lake's two main public boat ramps. The camping loop sits in woods south of 267th Street, set back from the lake behind the road and the boat-ramp area. --Claude

name: Swede Point Park

No site lengths are published and campers call the sites 'a little close'; check fit before booking. --Claude

name: Boulder Lake Campground
note: Chequamegon-Nicolet NF (Lakewood-Laona District) around the south end of 362-acre Boulder Lake, the forest's largest campground. Sites 17-35 run along the shore behind a band of pines; the rest sit back in young hardwoods around a bog, with puddles and damp spots common. Swim beach, amphitheater and boardwalk trail. ATVs and UTVs are barred in the campground. --Claude

name: Chippewa Campground
note: On the east shore of the 2,714-acre Chequamegon Waters Flowage, a shallow, stumpy flowage used for fishing and paddling. Electric is at sites 31-49 in the Bass loop. Sites numbered with a P are premium, with lake access or a paved pad. Beaver, Bass and Hardwoods loops have flush toilets and showers; the Rustic loop (61-78) has vault toilets only, and ATVs and UTVs may ride from those sites to the Perkinstown Motorized Trail (prohibited in the other loops). Two sand beaches, a fish-cleaning station and a very shallow boat landing. --Claude

booking.note: 41 sites are reservable on recreation.gov, closing 4 days before arrival; the Beaver loop (1-21) and most Rustic sites (61-69, 76-78) are first-come.

name: Spearhead Point Campground
note: Rustic Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest campground (Medford-Park Falls district) on the 411-acre Mondeaux Flowage, with a campers-only boat landing. Premium P sites each have a small dock; the sites are wooded and set back from the shore. Coin showers and a concession stand are at the nearby Mondeaux picnic area. --Claude

Only sites 28 and 30 are on the water: they back onto an open lawn that runs to the riprapped shore; the rest are shaded and set back. Self-service: a ranger or volunteer checks campers in at the site. --Claude

name: Liberty Harbor RV Park
note: SPECIAL CASE (--AWH): an urban paved RV lot at the Liberty Harbor Marina / Morris Canal Basin in Jersey City - included for its unmatched NYC access (PATH/ferry/light-rail to Manhattan minutes away, plus Statue of Liberty & Liberty State Park), not as a traditional campground. It is a tightly-packed angled-stall parking lot, not a scenic campground. 24/7 self check-in. Front-row sites overlook the marina basin with open Manhattan-skyline views across the water. The operator warns to check your own route for height, weight and propane restrictions. --Claude

season.note: Winter stays are possible; site water is shut off whenever it freezes and stays off until spring.

booking.note: Booked on CampLife or by phone, (201) 516-7500; 50% of the stay is a non-refundable deposit. Office Monday-Friday 9-5 until April 1, 2027, then daily 9-5.

name: Central Wisconsin State Fair
note: City of Marshfield fairgrounds at 513 E 17th St; the Central Wisconsin State Fair Association runs the campground on open grass fields north of the horse arenas. Over 100 water/electric sites and 500+ primitive spaces. Showers and restrooms in the Lang 4-H building, by key from the Fair Office on weekdays; WiFi codes sold there. Generators not allowed. Dump station by the Round Barn ($5). No long-term camping. --Claude

season.note: Water, and with it the campground, may shut earlier in a cold fall (Oct 8 in 2025).

booking.note: Reserve by mailing the camping form with full payment at least two weeks ahead, or at the Fair Office (Mon-Fri 9 am-4 pm); call first to confirm the grounds are open to the public on those dates. Closed to the public during the August fair and some other events (2026: July 15-19 and Aug 19 - Sep 2).

name: Wildwood Haven Resort and Campground
note: On 111-acre, spring-fed Long Lake south of Mellen. Lakeside sites 1-5 back onto the lake behind a thin line of trees, with a footpath down to the docks; site 1, a pull-through beside the boat landing, has the most open view. North Loop sites are in the woods a short walk from the lake. Swim beach, boat launch, docks, cabins and glamping. The dump station is kept locked: arrange and pay for it in advance, before 11 am checkout. --Claude

name: The Backyard on Amnicon Lake
note: Campground with a bar and grill on Tri Lakes Road at Amnicon Lake, south of Superior. The sites climb the hill north of the road; the swim beach and boat slips are across the road by the bar. Mostly seasonal: about 10 of its 97 RV sites are sold by the night online; a small mobile home park adjoins. The operator warns that GPS routing uses back gravel roads not suited to towing: from the south, follow WI 35 to County B, County A south, then Tri Lakes Road. --Claude

booking.note: Booked online on ParkWith.us (same-day allowed, 1-night minimum); stays over 21 nights are arranged by phone. Monday and Tuesday arrivals go straight to the site, as the bar is closed. Check-in 1 pm, check-out noon.

name: Grangers Campground
note: In-town Tomah RV park (Grangers LLC), 566 N Oakwood St. 45 total spaces - 27 grass transient/pull-thru sites (30x80 ft) + 18 seasonal; ~half full hookup, rest E+W, 30A; level grass, big-rig friendly. Free hot showers, restrooms, laundry, dump + mobile sewer, cable, WiFi, playground. Adjacent to the Omaha/La Crosse River State Trail. Open Apr 1-Nov 1. Reservable online or phone. --Claude

name: Pine View Campground (Fort McCoy)
note: Fort McCoy Army MWR campground on Suukjak Sep Lake beside the La Crosse River, open to the public: its entrance is off Hwy 21 about 1.6 miles west of the Fort McCoy main gate, with no base gate to pass. Any firearm brought in must be registered with the Fort McCoy Police, and bugle calls sound through the day. Cabins, yurts and rental campers too; swimming beach, accessible fishing dock, paddle-boat and canoe rentals, mini golf and a disc golf course. --Claude

Ten full-hookup and electric-only sites are held each week for active-duty military; any not reserved for the weekend open first-come to anyone each Friday. Paid in full at booking; the renter must be 18+ with ID. Check-in 12 PM, check-out 11 AM.

name: Lake Emily Park
note: Portage County park on 96-acre Lake Emily west of Amherst Junction, in two campgrounds: North, a large loop of sites in pine woods north of Park Drive, and South, a small wooded loop on the lake's south shore off Lake Drive beside the Tomorrow River State Trail. name: Petenwell County Park
note: Adams County park on Lake Petenwell with a swim beach, boat launch, a harbor of refuge with transient slips, a game room, and an ATV/UTV camping area with direct trail access. Mostly seasonal: about 142 of its 322 sites are sold by the night or week; the rest are seasonal or yearly. The nightly sites on open grass about 30-45 m from the shore are 1 and 4-8 at the beach end of the main loop; the other nightly 'lakefront' sites (11-17 at the west end of that loop, and the West Expansion's lakeside row) mostly face the lake through a band of shoreline trees. --Claude

name: Bay City Campground
note: Village of Bay City campground on a sand point at the head of Lake Pepin (Mississippi River), 7 mi from Red Wing, MN; sand beach, public boat launch, fish-cleaning area, pavilion. Mostly seasonal: only 10 of the 44 hookup sites take daily, weekly or monthly campers (the village page lists 21-23, 34-38, 43-44; its 2025 map marks 19, 20, 23, 34-38, 43, 44). The Lake Pepin row (35-44) sits about 35-40 m from the water across a riprap line and the beach. Seasonal flooding may delay the opening. --Claude

booking.note: By phone only. Daily and weekly reservations open March 1, monthly February 1, for the 10 non-seasonal sites; holidays fill fast.

Sand swim beach, boat ramp and harbor docks; tent sites 40-47 are the lakeside ones. Electric pedestals are shared between two sites. --Claude

name: Dalrymple Park and Campground
note: City of Bayfield campground 1 mi north of downtown, in heavy woods on the slope above Lake Superior facing Madeline Island. A walkway runs from the campground road toward the lake, and there are lookout points over the Apostle Islands. Nearest dump station is the wastewater plant south of town, by appointment on weekdays; showers at the Bayfield Recreation Center for a fee. --Claude

Sites 25-35 line the Big Birch Lake shore and 1-22 the Little Birch Lake shore; sites 1-7, 16-18, 20-22 and 25-35 may tie up a private dock. name: Wazee Lake Recreation Area
note: Jackson County campground on the wooded bluff above Wazee Lake, a 146-acre former iron-mine pit and the clearest, deepest inland lake in Wisconsin (popular for scuba diving). The lake is non-motorized; sandy beach with flush toilets and a concession stand, boat launch, fishing pier and hiking and paved bike trails. Generators need the park manager's approval. ATVs must stay trailered. --Claude

Seven sites on the upper loop by the entrance road, five on the lower loop south of the picnic area. Only sites 1, 9, 10 and 12 are 24 ft long or more (1 and 12 are 40 ft); the rest are 12-20 ft. --Claude

booking.note: Marinette County's own booking site or the parks office (715-732-7530, weekdays 8-4), 184 days ahead. No more than 14 days on one site in any 21. Check-in 3 pm, check-out noon.

name: Sheboygan Broughton Marsh Park & Campground
note: Sheboygan County park on the Sheboygan Marsh near Elkhart Lake; the campground is run by the Marsh Lodge restaurant and bar on site. Electric posts can be up to about 90 ft and water spigots up to 200 ft from a site, and no extra hose or cord is lent: the operator's chart lists each site. Launch ramp, fishing piers and the state's tallest wooden observation tower. --Claude

name: Fond Du Lac County Fairgrounds
note: Fond du Lac County Fairgrounds RV park, a row of sites north of the grandstand. Rents ordinary nights all season except fair week (mid-July); a few outdoor music events at the fairgrounds can run all day. No tents; dirt bikes, snowmobiles and ATVs are not allowed. --Claude

name: Waubedonia County Park
note: Ozaukee County's only camping park, on the east bank of the Milwaukee River in Fredonia (W1155 Fredonia Ave). RVs may use the six water and electric sites and basic site 14; sites 6-9 and 14 take long rigs, while 10 and 15 are harder backing for 25 ft at most. The other basic sites are tent only, and 16-17 are walk-in. Sites 1-9 sit in a row above the river, across the park road and a mowed bank. Free boat and canoe launch. --Claude

booking.note: Book online (Planyo) and pay in full before setting up; same-day reservations allowed. No more than 18 nights a season. Nobody on site to check campers in. Check-in 1 pm, check-out 11 am.

note: Lincoln County Forestry, Land & Parks campground at the north end of 34-acre Otter Lake in the Harrison Hills near Gleason. The camper sites sit back in the woods; sites 12-19 are walk-in tent sites on the shore. No motors on the lake; swim beach and day-use area at the south end, and a nature trail around the lake. --Claude

name: Glen Hills County Park
note: St. Croix County park: 700 wooded acres around 78-acre Glen Lake near Glenwood City. Peninsula Campground's wooded loops fill a peninsula in the lake, with the two camper cabins at its tip; Vista Prairie is an open loop on the prairie 0.9 km north, beside the Whispering Oaks extended-stay campground; Picnic Point takes tents and truck campers only. Swim beach, non-motorized boat landing, fishing pier, disc golf; adjacent public golf course. --Claude

name: James N. McNally Campground West

note: Town of Clover campground on Lake Superior's south shore at Herbster, off Bark Point Road. The water-and-electric RV sites sit in an open block across the road from the beach, the front row (22-27) looking over the lake; the electric-only sites by the pavilion take only small rigs, and the rustic tent sites are on the beach side or in the woods. Playground. Charging an electric vehicle at the sites is prohibited. --Claude

name: Blackhawk Lake Recreation Area
note: Recreation area on 220-acre Blackhawk Lake between Highland and Cobb.  The Wisconsin DNR owns the land, Iowa County holds an operating easement and the Cobb-Highland Recreation Commission runs it on no state or county tax money; it is not a state park, and state park passes don't work.  Over 150 open and wooded sites for campers, tents and groups, with a beach, a boat launch on a no-wake lake, a nature center and hiking trails.  No generators for now, and no ATVs or UTVs. --Claude

season.note: Online booking runs April 15 to October 31; outside it the park may close for weather.

name: Calumet County Park
note: Calumet County park on the east shore of Lake Winnebago, NW of Stockbridge. Its sites sit in four areas along about 2 km of the park road: the North End loop (N sites, N14-N18 on the lakeshore), the West End along the lakeshore (W sites, W9-W14 rated only 20 ft and W11-W14 grassy and uneven), the South End above the harbor (S sites) and the wooded Upper Park (U sites). A band of shoreline trees stands between the lakeshore sites and the water. Modern boat launch and harbor, two camping cabins. Construction blocks parts of the campground from late October 2026 to May 26, 2027 (N1-N24 and W1-W16; W11-W14 to June 16, 2027). --Claude

sites.note: The booking site lists 81 sites plus group site G1: North End N1-N3, N5-N24; South End S1-S28; West End W1-W16; Upper Park U1-U13; double site M1. Most pads are rated 40 ft; N1, N3, S21, U1, U2, U5 and U8-U13 25 ft; W9-W14, U3 and U4 20 ft. The county's own pages give 82 and 86 sites including 2 cabins.

season.note: Main season April 1-October 31; winter camping (December 1-April 1) up to 14 nights, call ahead about a plowed pad. Fresh-water fill and dump station typically closed November 1-March 31.

booking.note: Reservations are a 2-night minimum, 21 nights max April-December (14 in winter); Memorial Day and Labor Day weekends Friday-Sunday. Holiday weekends open on set dates (2027 Memorial Day sites from June 2, 2026). Late arrivals before Memorial Day and after Labor Day use the self-registration station. Check-in 3 pm, check-out 2 pm.

name: Pine Point County Park
note: Chippewa County campground on a wooded peninsula in Lake Holcombe (Holcombe Flowage). Fifteen shoreline sites have their own boat dock; sites 1-5 sit apart along the entry road. Beach, swim area, playground, pavilion and boat launch. --Claude

name: Camp New Wood County Park
note: Lincoln County park on the Wisconsin River about 10 miles northwest of Merrill on Highway 107. The campground sits on a wooded strip above the river, joined by a footbridge over Ripley Creek to the day-use area, which has pavilions and a gravel boat landing with a kayak launch. The Ice Age Trail runs through the campground. Firewood is provided; don't bring your own. No ATV/UTV trail access. --Claude

name: Russell Memorial Park and Campground
note: On the Arnold Creek arm of Lake Arbutus, near the Levis Mound mountain-bike and hiking trails. Sites 31-39 are closed for construction from October 5, 2026. Designated ATV/UTV sites connect to the county trail system; ATVs may not use the park's blacktop. Generators are generally not permitted. Shoreline docking is first come, first served and open to the public. Business office 715-743-5140. --Claude

Rock outcroppings, 2.5 miles of hiking trails and an overlook. After October 15 the water tower closes, and an early freeze any time after October 1 can shut the water system, shower building and dump station for the season. --Claude

name: Solberg Lake County Park
note: Price County park on a 35-acre peninsula in Solberg Lake. The 40-site addition (61-100) sits in an open field across West Solberg Lake Road, its facilities across the road in the main park; it also sells 1-month and 4-month stays. The county calls 20+ sites lakeside; the shore sites sit under trees behind a marsh fringe. Sand beach, paved boat ramp, two fishing piers; ATVs/UTVs may ride from every site to the Flambeau trail system. --Claude

facilities.note: Showers are 25 cents for 2 minutes; the dump takes quarters. Wi-Fi only in the addition, while the water is on.

season.note: Roads are not plowed in winter. Showers, flush toilets, pressure water and the dump run about early/mid May to early/mid October; potable water at the pumphouse until about November 30.

booking.note: Sites 1-9, 43-60 and the 61-100 addition book online at least 8 days ahead; sites 10-42 are first come, first served, and any unreserved site may be self-registered at the pay station for up to 7 days or until the next reservation. Monthly and 4-month stays in the addition must be booked online. The 2-night minimum covers Thursday-Saturday on reservable sites; 3 nights on Memorial Day, July 4th and Labor Day weekends.

sites.note: 21 drive-in electric sites (2-6, 8-22 and an accessible site booked by phone) and 3 walk-in canoe sites by the river.

booking.note: Reservations close 7 days before arrival; inside that, open sites are taken by registering in person at the campground on the day. Reserved stays run 2 to 14 nights, 3 on the Memorial Day, July 4 and Labor Day weekends; from June 1 to Labor Day no more than 14 days in any four weeks.

Part of the campground is let by the season, and units may be stored over winter on sites 22-42. --Claude

name: Sidie Hollow County Park, Main and Upper Ridge Campgrounds
note: Vernon County park near Viroqua around a 38-acre flood-control lake, with trout streams, fishing piers, a boat launch and about 10 miles of hiking and mountain-bike trails. This entry covers two of its three campgrounds: the Main area on County Road XX, where electric sites 214-218 sit on open grass beside Coe Hollow Creek, and Upper Ridge on a wooded ridge west of the lake, which is reached by its own road, Campsite Road, off Sidie Hollow Road rather than from the Main area. name: Waterloo Recreation Area - Portage Lake Campground
note: Modern campground of Waterloo Recreation Area (Michigan DNR) on Big Portage Lake, off Seymour Road (11500 Seymour Road, Grass Lake, per the DNR directions), in three loops (north, central, south) on gently rolling ground under a tree canopy; paved pads with grass. The designated swim area, beach house and playground are down a paved path in the day-use area, with an 18-hole disc golf course. Camper cabin and two tiny houses. Recycling available. --Claude

sites.note: 134 campsites on the booking maps (the DNR page's 136 includes the two tiny houses): North 29, Central 64, South 41. Allowed equipment is 25-45 ft at 106 sites and 20 ft or unlisted at 28; pull-throughs at sites 31, 109 and 111.

facilities.note: Sanitation station with potable water and two lanes. Modern toilet and shower buildings April 1 - Nov 30 (a portable toilet in the off season). JR's Concessions store is at the beach house in the Portage Lake day-use area.

season.note: From Dec. 1 to April 1 the campground is open for overnight stays Thursday through Saturday only.

booking.note: Reserve online on MiDNRReservations or at 800-447-2757; reservations are taken year-round (Thursday-Saturday nights only from Dec. 1 to April 1).

name: Bewabic State Park
note: Shady, wooded modern campground on three loops (A, B, C) on spring-fed Fortune Lake, part of the Fortune Lakes Chain; CCC-era park with a swim beach, the chain's only public boat launch and a 2-mile nature trail. One of the few state parks that let ORVs ride between the campground and nearby trails (entering and leaving only). Sites #71-122 were renumbered after a new toilet/shower building and repaved roads, so check site numbers. --Claude

hookups.note: Only 3 of the 130 sites have water and sewer (50-amp full hookup); every other electric site is electric only.

sites.note: Booking site classes: 56 50-amp, 67 20/30-amp, 3 non-electric (RVs up to 20 ft only) and 4 walk-in tent sites (mapped as C-Loop 104-107; the DNR page still numbers the walk-ins #107-110, which require a walk of up to 125 yards from the parking lot). The largest equipment class offered is 'Trailer or RV up to 40''.

facilities.note: Two-lane sanitation station in the modern campground, registered campers only, with potable water. Kayak, paddleboard and canoe rentals Memorial Day through September.

booking.note: Reserve online at MiDNRReservations.com or call 800-447-2757.

sites.note: Three loops; most sites moderate in size and shaded by maple and cedar. The 11 50-amp sites are the pull-throughs and take trailers/RVs to 50 ft; the other 50 sites range from 20 to 40 ft (two tent-only).

name: Wilson State Park Campground
note: Modern campground of Wilson State Park (Michigan DNR) at the north end of Budd Lake in Harrison (910 N. First Street), on the site of the 1800s Wilson Brothers sawmill; north and south loops, most sites generous in size and shaded by oaks, maples and pines, near the swim beach and picnic area. The Leota ORV Trailhead is nearby. --Claude

name: Holly Recreation Area - McGinnis Lake Modern Campground
note: Modern campground of Holly Recreation Area (8,000+ acres, northern Oakland County); the campground entrance is at 5300 McGinnis Road (8100 Grange Road is park headquarters). Often compared to campgrounds 'up north': the East Campground (Maple, Oak and Aspen loops) mixes trees and grass, the West Campground (Trillium and Hickory loops) is densely forested, with large sites throughout. Two mini cabins sit in the campground. --Claude

facilities.note: Two-lane sanitation station with potable water in the modern campground. Golf discs sold at the campground office.

note: Single modern campground along Sand Lake in the SE corner of the park, near Big Seven Lake, opened 1992; moderate-size sites, paved roads, a designated swimming beach and playscape. --Claude

note: Modern campground of Ionia Recreation Area (4,500 acres between Grand Rapids and Lansing), on a hilltop just east of Sessions Lake; two mini cabins sit in the campground. facilities.note: Two-lane sanitation station with potable water near the campground entrance. Playground, swings, sandbox and horseshoe pits in the campground.

name: Sleepy Hollow State Park Campground
note: Modern campground in two loops, each site on its own asphalt or concrete pad screened by shrubs. The park surrounds 410-acre Lake Ovid, but the campground is set back inland with a footpath/short drive to the swim beach; one fishing pier is near the campground. 12+ miles of equestrian trails with a staging area just past the campground entrance. --Claude

sites.note: 180 modern sites in a north loop (99) and a south loop (81), each on its own asphalt or concrete pad. Allowed trailer/RV length is 45 ft at 48 sites, 40 ft at 61, 35 ft at 49, 30 ft at 19, 25 ft at 3; 11 pull-throughs. Also six walk-in rustic sites and a 20-site auxiliary overflow area.

booking.note: Reserve online on MiDNRReservations or at 800-447-2757; the DNR rates table gives a reservation season of April 15 to October 31 for the campground and the walk-in sites (the cabins book year-round).

name: Rifle River Recreation Area - Grousehaven Modern Campground
note: Modern campground of Rifle River Recreation Area near Lupton: wooded sites on two loops, the Upper Loop overlooking Grousehaven Lake and the Lower Loop level with the lake; designated swim beach and easy access to the park's 14-mile multiuse trail. --Claude

name: Muskegon State Park - Channel Campground
note: Modern campground in two loops by the Muskegon Lake navigation channel walkway: the first loop is adjacent to the channel, the second has larger sites near the big dune and Muskegon Lake. The channel walkway and its parking lot are closed for a U.S. Army Corps of Engineers project through Nov. 14, 2026 (DNR park page, read 2026-10-25). --Claude

sites.note: 139 campsites: 93 in the first loop (sites 1-92, beside the navigation channel) and 46 in the second (101-147, larger sites near the dune and Muskegon Lake), every one with electric. Allowed rigs run up to 20-50 ft: the first loop is mostly 30-ft sites (67), the second mostly 45-50 ft; 33 sites take 50 ft. Ten pull-throughs (first loop 5, 8, 9, 18, 48, 53; second loop 131, 144, 146, 147).

name: P.J. Hoffmaster State Park Campground
note: Modern campground on the north side of the park off Lake Harbor Rd, shaded by oaks, maples, beech and pine and next to Little Black Creek and the dune trails. It sits behind a wooded foredune ridge; the closest sites (25-60) are under a quarter-mile walk to the Lake Michigan beach and a buoyed swim area. --Claude

sites.note: 297 sites in three loops, most generous and shaded; the booking site allows trailers/RVs up to 20-50 ft by site (about 210 take 30 ft or more). Pull-throughs: 136, 140, 195, 197, 199, 233, 235, 237. Concrete sites 87, 180, 213, 221; ADA sites 5, 13, 70, 131, 145, 232, 241, 248, 259, 261.

name: Newaygo State Park Campground
note: Rustic campground in two loops atop 20-ft embankments overlooking Hardy Dam Pond, a 6-mile flooding of the Muskegon River; large private sites. Boat launch between the loops with a few mooring spots for registered campers, buoyed swim area in the Poplar loop, kayak rentals at the office early June to mid-September, 18-hole disc golf; borders the Manistee National Forest. Spongy moth larvae can surge in summer. --Claude

sites.note: 99 rustic campsites in two loops, Oak (#1-48) and Poplar (#49-99), with 20- to 30-ft forested buffers between them. Allowed rig lengths on the booking site run 25-50 ft; all but 3 take 30 ft or more. No pull-throughs listed.

facilities.note: Drinking water and trailer fill at the one-lane sanitation station near the campground office.

booking.note: Reserve online on MiDNRReservations or at 800-447-2757.

name: Leelanau State Park Campground
note: Rustic campground at the very tip of the Leelanau Peninsula beside the Grand Traverse Lighthouse (15310 N. Lighthouse Point Rd, Northport): rocky beach and big trees, about half the sites right on Lake Michigan and the rest tucked into the woods with lake views. Known for small sites: choose one the booking site rates for your rig. Three mini cabins in the campground; the park's Cathead Bay trails and sandy beach are on a separate unit 4 mi south. --Claude

sites.note: 51 rustic campsites, about half right on the water. Small sites: on the booking site 22 take trailers/RVs of 25 ft or more (12 to 25 ft, 5 to 30, 4 to 35, site 1 to 40), 12 only to 20 ft, and the rest are tent-only. One pull-through. Two vehicles per site.

facilities.note: Drinking water and a place to fill trailers with potable water, but no dump station. Lighthouse gift shop sells some camping supplies.

booking.note: Reserve online on MiDNRReservations or at 800-447-2757.

name: Onaway State Park Campground
note: Modern campground on the southeast shore of Black Lake (Michigan's seventh-largest), with a cobblestone shoreline and rock outcroppings; the lower loop has sites on the lake, the upper loop sits on a bluff in white pines. Ocqueoc Falls is 10 mi east. --Claude

sites.note: 82 electric campsites in a lower loop among cedars, with sites on the lake, and an upper loop in white pines (lake views from its east side), plus a camper cabin. Allowed rig lengths run 20-40 ft: 13 sites take only 20 ft, 18 take 35-40 ft. The shower building is a short walk from the lower loop.

name: W.J. Hayes State Park Campground
note: Modern MI DNR campground on no-wake Round Lake in the Irish Hills, in two loops (west and east) with a mix of sunny and shady sites on asphalt pads; the Red and Blue trails run between the loops. Two mini cabins and two tiny houses. The day-use area, buoyed swim beach and general store are on all-sports Wamplers Lake across the street; the Round Lake boating access site is reserved for campers on weekends in the camping season, beside an accessible fishing pier. The DNR says the campground has lots of midweek availability. --Claude

sites.note: 176 campsites on the booking maps (the DNR page's 180 includes the two mini cabins and two tiny houses): East Loop 89, West Loop 87. Allowed equipment is 25-40 ft at every site (40 ft at 74, 35 at 64, 30 at 36, 25 at 2). A 20-site auxiliary overflow area is mapped separately.

booking.note: Reserve online on MiDNRReservations or at 800-447-2757; the DNR rates table gives a reservation season of April 22 to October 21 for the East and West Loops.

Old Baldy Dune and Portage trails in the park; the Little Traverse Wheelway passes the entrance. --Claude

name: North Higgins Lake State Park Campground
note: Modern campground in East and West loops along the north shore of Higgins Lake (Michigan's 10th-largest), at the former site of the world's largest seedling nursery; the Higgins Lake Nursery and CCC Museum, a day-use swim beach, boat launch and the Iron Belle Trail are in the park. Roscommon and Grayling are each about 15 minutes away. --Claude

Most sites are generous and shaded by oaks, maples and pines.

note: Single-loop modern campground of grass drive-in sites on the west shore of Lake Roland, about 26 miles from Houghton, near the designated swimming beach, boat launch and picnic area. Use the entrance at 32650 N. Hwy M-26, Toivola: some online resources give an address on Poyhonen Road, a logging road where turning a camper around is very difficult. ORVs may ride between the campground and the nearby trails (entering and exiting only). A base for the Porcupine Mountains and the Keweenaw. --Claude

name: Thunder Bay River State Forest Campground
note: Rustic MI DNR state forest campground on the banks of the Thunder Bay River, 9 mi SW of Alpena via M-32 and Indian Reserve Rd; the last stretch is a narrow gravel and dirt road. Undeveloped carry-in launch on the north side; pike, bass, walleye and panfish; also reachable by canoe. The 1.5-mile Wah-Wah-Tas-See Pathway starts here, and an ORV/snowmobile trailhead to the Devil's Loop trail adjoins the campground. --Claude

sites.note: Ten sites 'for tent and small trailer use' (no length posted) at the end of a narrow gravel and dirt road; water access at every site. One camping unit and six people per site.

season.note: The DNR amenity table gives seasonal closure dates of Dec 1 to May 1.

name: Portage Bay State Forest Campground
note: Remote rustic state forest campground on Big Bay de Noc (Lake Michigan), ~10 mi S of Garden via County Road 483 and Portage Bay Road; many sites have Lake Michigan views. Ninga Aki Pathway (2.7 mi) hiking; an unimproved boat ramp for very small boats south of the campground. --Claude

name: Trout Lake State Forest Campground
note: Rustic MI DNR state forest campground in the Gladwin Field Trial Area, 17 mi N of Gladwin via M-18 N and Adams Road; neighbour to House Lake State Forest Campground, with direct access to the 2.8-mile Trout Lake Pathway. 10 of the sites accommodate up to 40-ft vehicles/trailers. Trout Lake has significantly receded since the DNR began an emergency drawdown of the Trout Lake Dam in April 2025 (to prevent a structural failure); the DNR points campers to nearby House and Hoister lakes. --Claude Update: the drawdown finished 2025-07-11; the outlet pipe needs repair before any refill, and the DNR's 2026 fishery report recommends removing the dam, which would leave wetland and stream. --Claude 2026-10-26

name: Lake Margrethe State Forest Campground
note: Rustic state forest campground in heavy woods on Lake Margrethe, 6.6 mi W of Grayling via M-72, McIntyres Landing Rd, Regimental Way and Euclid Ave (Crawford County); managed by Hartwick Pines State Park. Most sites have direct lake access; the Manistee and Au Sable rivers are close by for canoeing and fishing. DNR advisory (2026): MDHHS fish-consumption guidelines for PFOS and a warning not to swallow foam on Lake Margrethe, as high PFAS levels may be present. --Claude

facilities.note: Drinking water from a hand-pump well. Developed boat launch at the south side of the campground; lakefront picnic area with four tables at the north end; carry-in access straight from some sites.

booking.note: First-come only, but registration is now by phone or online (using the number or website posted at the campground), no earlier than 8 a.m. on the day of arrival; the site must then be set up and occupied. No advance payments or reservations.

note: Rustic state forest campground on the Muskegon River at the Reedsburg Dam impoundment, 5 mi NW of Houghton Lake via M-55 and County Road 300. Boat launch and carry-in access in the campground. --Claude

name: Lake Dubonnet State Forest Campground
note: Rustic state forest campground among soaring pines on Lake Dubonnet, 4.2 mi NW of Interlochen via US-31 South and Gonder Road (Grand Traverse County); managed by Interlochen State Park. The Lost Lake Pathway (hiking, ungroomed skiing, snowshoeing) runs through the campground; ORVs may be ridden from the campsite to local ORV routes. The separate Lake Dubonnet Trail Camp is not part of this entry. --Claude

booking.note: First-come only, but registration is now by phone or online (using the number or website posted at the campground), no earlier than 8 a.m. on the day of arrival; the site must then be set up and occupied. No advance payments or reservations.

note: Rustic campground on Ross Lake in the UP near Melstrand, 22 miles northeast of Shingleton via H-15, H-58 and Russ Lake Road (the last ~3 miles a well-maintained dirt road), fewer than 10 miles from Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore. name: Tomahawk Lake State Forest Campground
note: Rustic state forest campground on the shore of 40-acre Tomahawk Lake, 13 miles southeast of Onaway via M-33 South and Tomahawk Lake Highway; sandy shoreline with picnic tables in the middle of the campground. Gravel and concrete-plank boat launch on the east side of the lake, about a quarter mile away (no-wake lake); bass, panfish and crappie. The High Country Pathway passes through the campground, and ORVs and snowmobiles may ride from it to the Atlanta Trail system. --Claude

name: Tomahawk Creek Flooding State Forest Campground
note: Rustic state forest campground on the Tomahawk Creek Flooding, 12.5 miles southeast of Onaway via M-33 South and Tomahawk Lake Highway, in two units (east, sites 1-24; west, sites 25-47), both on the flooding. Boat launch at the west unit and an undeveloped carry-in launch at the east unit; known for fishing among submerged timber (panfish, bass, pike, crappie). The High Country Pathway is just down the road; ORVs and snowmobiles may ride between the campground and nearby trails, including the Atlanta Trail. --Claude

name: Van Etten Lake State Forest Campground
note: Rustic MI DNR state forest campground overlooking 1,320-acre Van Etten Lake near the former Wurtsmith Air Force Base, 4.5 mi NW of Oscoda via US-23 and F-41. A walking path lines the water's edge; boating access site on the south side of the campground (perch, walleye, pike, bass). The Iron Belle Trail is reached south of the campground via F-41 and River Road; ORVs and snowmobiles are prohibited in the campground (Old State House ORV trailhead 5.5 mi SW). Advisory: MDHHS fish-consumption guidelines (elevated PFOS) and advice to avoid swallowing foam on Van Etten Lake, as high levels of PFAS may be present. --Claude

name: Ossineke State Forest Campground
note: Rustic state forest campground in a cedar forest on the shore of Lake Huron's Thunder Bay, 1 mi east of Ossineke via US-23 S and Ossineke Road; campground host all season. About half the sites have direct access to a sandy beach; day-use area with picnic tables and grills and a boardwalk out to the lake. Carry-in paddling access from the day-use area or beach sites; Devils River boat launch under a mile north. --Claude

name: East Branch of Fox River State Forest Campground
note: Rustic state forest campground on the East Branch of the Fox River (a designated natural river known for wild brook trout) and King's Pond, eight miles north of Seney National Wildlife Refuge via M-77 North, Schoolcraft County. A working fish hatchery 1936-1980; concrete release slabs and storage areas remain. The one-mile Steeb Pathway circles King's Pond. ORV and snowmobile riding allowed between the campground and nearby trails (Danaher Plains trailhead 4.5 miles south). --Claude

name: Kingston Lake State Forest Campground
note: Rustic state forest campground almost entirely surrounded by Kingston Lake, on the northern edge of the Kingston Plains, 18.8 mi SW of Grand Marais via H-58 (Alger County); managed by Indian Lake State Park. The closest state forest campground to Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore; the Fox River Pathway runs four miles to Lake Superior, and ORVs and snowmobiles may run to the trails (ORV Trail 8 is adjacent). Sites are tight: some fit a 23-ft rig but larger rigs struggle (a reviewer's 18-ft fit fine). --Claude

facilities.note: Drinking water from a hand-pump well. Boat launch on Kingston Lake (no-wake rules); carry-in access about 10 yards from the parking area or straight from some sites; picnic area with two tables on the south side.

name: Weber Lake State Forest Campground

The lake is reached by a stairway on the south side of the campground, with carry-in access between sites 4 and 5 (panfish, paddling, swimming). The 4.67-mile Lost Tamarack Pathway runs through the campground; the Tomahawk Trail is half a mile away and the Indian River Route about a mile, and ORVs may ride between the campground and the trails. A camper review reports a 22-ft toy hauler fit at site 18; sites are large and spread out, some unlevel. --Claude

name: Bowman Bridge Campground
note: Manistee NF campground up the hill from Bowman Bridge Boat Landing on the Pere Marquette National Scenic River, ~5 mi west of Baldwin via W 52nd Street; concession-run (American Land & Leisure). Popular canoe and trout/steelhead fishing access; connector trail to the North Country Trail. --Claude

sites.note: One loop of 16 paved family sites, plus 4 walk-in family sites and 4 tent-only group sites (up to 20 people each). The catalog lists 13 RV-capable family sites (7 reservable, 6 first-come), all back-in, max vehicle length 50 ft. Two vehicles or one RV per site, two camping units with only one wheeled; all tires must fit on the spur. Thinner shade than neighbouring campgrounds since a 2005 tornado.

facilities.note: Camp host, self-pay station, trash collection. Connector trail to the North Country National Scenic Trail; Bowman Bridge Boat Landing down the hill.

booking.note: Reserve on recreation.gov up to 4 days before arrival; 6 of the 13 family sites are first-come. Weekend reservations 2 nights. recreation.gov's stay rule is 16 consecutive nights. Check-in 2 p.m., check-out 11 a.m. A watercraft permit is needed to float the Pere Marquette Memorial Day weekend - Labor Day weekend.

name: Pine Lake Campground
note: Manistee NF rustic campground on the shore of Pine Lake (Manistee Co.); the east side of the lake is mostly private cabins, the federal west side swampy and long used by bald eagles. Shallow, gravel-bottomed swimming beach off the picnic area; boat access. Near the Big M cross-country ski / mountain-bike trails, the Pine National Scenic River and the Bear Track / North Country Trail area. --Claude

name: Peterson Bridge Campground
note: Manistee NF campground, the only Forest Service campground on the Pine National Scenic River, on M-37 at the Pine River bridge 1.5 mi S of M-55 (21 mi N of Baldwin). Many RV sites are shaded and secluded; the riverbank tent sites can also be reached from the river. Canoe/boat launch across the river at Peterson Bridge North; a watercraft permit is required on the Pine from Memorial Day weekend to Labor Day. --Claude

booking.note: Reserve on recreation.gov up to 3 days before arrival; 21 of the 31 catalog sites are first-come. Weekend stays need 2 nights, holiday weekends 3; no more than 16 nights in a rolling 30 days. Check-in 2 p.m., check-out 11 a.m. Run by a concessionaire (American Land & Leisure).

name: Pines Point Campground
note: Manistee NF campground on the banks of the White River near Hesperia, quiet and secluded under towering white pines, several sites overlooking the river. Walk-in canoe landing (a 30-60 minute float around the point) and a day-use area. Reached via 168th Ave / FR 5637. --Claude

sites.note: 27 first-come family sites along the river, several overlooking it, plus a reservable loop of 5 group sites (20 guests each) southwest of the main campground. Site capacity 2 vehicles and 2 camping units, only one of them wheeled; all tires must fit on the spur. recreation.gov's catalog lists only the 5 group-loop sites (back-in, 80 ft), so it says nothing about the family sites' length.

name: Sand Lake Recreation Area Campground
note: Manistee NF campground near Dublin and Wellston (Manistee Co.) on ~50-acre Sand Lake, mostly ringed by private land (the recreation area is the only public access): sandy swimming beach (the bottom turns mucky further out), boat ramp and picnic area. Wooded sites, some heavily shaded, on paved pads in two loops (sites 1-30 main loop, 30+ secondary loop); about 15 minutes from the Pine National Scenic River. This is the Sand Lake near Irons, not the one near Nottawa. --Claude

sites.note: 41 standard/RV sites (24 reservable, 17 first-come) taking 34-40 ft (28 take 40), all back-in, plus 2 tent-only sites and a group tent area. Site capacity is 2 vehicles and 2 camping units, only one of them wheeled; all tires must fit on the spur.

facilities.note: Coin-operated showers.

booking.note: 24 of the 41 RV-usable sites are reservable on recreation.gov; the other 17 are first-come. Reservations need 2 nights (3 on holiday weekends). Concession-run (American Land & Leisure): customer service 801-226-3564, Help.Huron.Manistee@AmericanLL.com. Check-in 2 pm, check-out 11 am. The site reserved is the site kept (no moving).

name: Seaton Creek Campground
note: Rustic Manistee NF campground adjoining Seaton Creek at the upper end of the Hodenpyl Dam backwater of the Big Manistee River, in mostly pine forest near a picnic area. Connector trail to the Manistee River Trail; the North Country Trail is across the suspension bridge over the Manistee. Kayakers can come up the very shallow Seaton Creek. Reached from M-37 by 26 Road, O'Rourke Drive and Forest Road 5993. --Claude

sites.note: 17 family sites (13 pull-through, 4 back-in; no lengths posted) and 2 group tent-only sites. Two vehicles and two camping units per site, only one of them wheeled; all tires must fit on the spur.

booking.note: The 17 family sites are first-come, first-served; only the two group sites book on recreation.gov (cutoff 3 days before arrival).

note: Manistee NF campground on the Little Manistee River (a National Scenic Study River, known for steelhead and trout) in Lake County; about 16-20 sites with fire pits and picnic tables, plus walk-in riverside sites, and parking for 20 vehicles. Drive-in via FR 5202. A 1.5-mile trail connects the campground to the North Country National Scenic Trail. --Claude

name: Lake Michigan Recreation Area Campground
note: Manistee NF campground on the Lake Michigan shore 15 mi south of Manistee (between Manistee and Ludington), along Porter Creek beside the Nordhouse Dunes Wilderness. Boardwalk/stairs to a sandy beach, overlook deck, amphitheater with peak-season programs, playground; the Arrowhead Trail loops between the campground and the beach and a Nordhouse Dunes trailhead is in the recreation area. 8 mi in from US-31 on Forest Trail Road (FS 5629). --Claude

sites.note: 99 single family sites in four loops plus 3 group sites (tent camping only, up to 50 guests each). The 48 RV sites in the recreation.gov catalog are all back-in, listed maximum vehicle lengths 28-54 ft (most 34-44 ft); the rest of the single sites are not in the catalog.

booking.note: Run by a concessionaire (American Land & Leisure; customer service 801-226-3564). Only about half the 99 single sites are on recreation.gov (46 bookable standard sites + 2 tent sites in the catalog); the campground also has first-come sites. A reserved site is yours: you may not move to another. Check-in 2 p.m., check-out 11 a.m.

name: Monument Campground
note: Huron NF campground established in 1909, on the River Road National Scenic Byway above the AuSable River and beside the Lumberman's Monument Visitor Center; secluded, shaded sites in a red pine plantation, fully accessible. The Highbanks Trail starts at the campground. 15 mi W of Oscoda. --Claude

sites.note: 19 sites in a red pine plantation, 9 reservable and 10 first-come; every site lists a 50-ft maximum vehicle length, all back-in.

facilities.note: Pressurized drinking water, vault toilets, trash collection and grills; a camp host is on site.

booking.note: 9 of the 19 sites book on recreation.gov; the other 10 are first-come. 14 nights in any 30. Occupy the site within 24 hours of the reservation start or it may be forfeited; late arrivals and early departures through Lumberman's Monument, 989-362-8961.

name: Mack Lake ORV Campground
note: Huron NF, largest campground on the Mio Ranger District, in two loops (Warbler 1-21, Beaver 22-42) on 175-acre Mack Lake amid rolling jack pine plains; the lake is part private. Sunfish, perch and walleye. The Forest Service says the campground 'is primarily used by ORV trail riders': the Mack Lake Trail System starts here, though ORVs may not be driven within the campground, and it is not restricted to ORV users. --Claude

sites.note: The catalog lists 41 family sites numbered 1-42 (no site 12), all back-in, plus a management site. Max vehicle lengths 30-90 ft, most 50-75; site 1 (30 ft) is for tents, vans and pop-ups only, and sites 1, 5-7, 10, 13, 38 and 40 do not list trailers.

facilities.note: Drinking water from hand-pump wells; trash collection. The day-use area inside the Beaver Loop has picnic tables, grills, a buoyed swimming area and carry-in boat access.

booking.note: 24 of the 41 family sites book on recreation.gov; 17 are first-come. recreation.gov's reservable rate seasons run May 15 - Sept 30 (2026, 2027); October 1 - November 30 is a first-come season. A reservation must be occupied within 24 hours of its start or the site may be forfeited. Run by the Forest Service (Mio Ranger District), not a concession.

name: Gabions Campground
note: Huron NF campground on the National Scenic stretch of the Au Sable River, a short walk from the river (a small spring at the river's edge by the gabions, rock-filled erosion baskets); sites shaded by hardwoods, red and jack pine, each with picnic table, fire ring and lantern post. Off Brodie Road north of Au Sable River Road. The Shore-to-Shore Trail passes through, but horse camping is not permitted. OHV trail access at the campground road. --Claude

sites.note: 8 sites: 5 reservable standard, 2 first-come standard, 1 reservable tent-only. Back-in RV sites list 40-45 ft; one site lists 75 ft and the two first-come sites 99 ft (placeholder values, left out). Site 6 is a 30-ft parallel spur for vans/pickup campers, not RVs.

facilities.note: Trash collection provided.

booking.note: Run by the Forest Service (Mio Ranger District; unstaffed). Reserve on recreation.gov; sites 1 and 7 are first-come only, and the rate table runs a first-come, first-served season Oct. 1 - Nov. 30. Occupy a reserved site within 24 hours of its start or it may be forfeited.

name: Rollways Campground
note: Huron NF near Hale, built in 1909 as one of the first Huron campgrounds, on a high bluff overlooking Loud Dam Pond on the AuSable River just off the River Road National Scenic Byway. Adjacent day-use area with a log shelter; an accessible trail runs to Westgate Scenic Overlook and passes a stairway down to the river. --Claude
