name: Round Lake Campground
note: Huron NF in the village of Sand Lake near National City: a rustic, wooded campground in two loops on 91-acre Round Lake, which is mostly ringed by private land (the campground is the only public access). About a quarter of the sites have water access; sandy beach and a gravel boat ramp; garbage service. Groceries and fuel nearby. --Claude

name: Kneff Lake Campground
note: Huron NF campground on the far west side of the Mio Ranger District, east of Grayling, around 20-acre Kneff Lake (designated trout lake stocked with rainbow trout in spring; carry-in non-motorized boats only; buoyed swim beach at the day-use area). Site 9 is tent-only. Reached from M-72 via Stephan Bridge Rd and FR 4003; campground host on site in season. --Claude

facilities.note: Drinking water from hand-pump wells; trash collection; day-use area with picnic tables, grills and a buoyed, ramp-accessible swim beach.

booking.note: 16 of the 27 sites are reservable on recreation.gov (15 standard + the tent site), 11 first-come. Occupy a reserved site within 24 hours of the reservation start or it may be forfeited.

name: Wagner Lake Campground
note: Huron NF campground (Mio Ranger District) on shallow, sandy-bottomed Wagner Lake in mixed hardwood forest, 1 mile west of M-33 on Wagner Lake Road: beach play and swimming, carry-in canoes and kayaks, good bass and panfish fishing. Reportedly a dirt access road and a narrow, hilly interior loop with tight curves - a 23-ft rig fits, bigger rigs struggle. --Claude

sites.note: 12 back-in sites on paved parking pads; the recreation.gov catalog lists driveways of 40-70 ft (60-65 ft at most).

booking.note: Seven of the 12 sites are reservable on recreation.gov and five are first-come; recreation.gov's rate table runs a 'First-come, First-served Season' from October 1 to November 30. Occupy the site within 24 hours of the reservation's start or it may be forfeited. Run by the Forest Service (Mio Ranger District), not a concessionaire.

note: Huron NF campground on 58-acre Island Lake, a short drive north of Rose City on M-33 (Mio Ranger District): the lake is cold and clear, 25 ft deep, with a buoyed swimming beach and non-motorized boating from the day-use area; several sites see the lake through the trees. 1.25-mile loop trail with a spur to Loon Lake Day Use Area; the M-33 trailhead nearby reaches the Mack Lake ORV trails (no ORVs in the campground). --Claude

name: Bay Furnace Campground
note: Rustic Hiawatha NF campground on the south shore of Lake Superior at Christmas, about 3 miles west of Munising across M-28 from the Kewadin Casino, looking out toward Grand Island. Amid hardwoods; some sites overlook the lake, others sit near Furnace Creek. No lake access from the campground: boat ramps in Munising and at AuTrain. --Claude

name: Little Bay de Noc Campground
note: Hiawatha NF campground on the shore of Little Bay de Noc at the north end of Lake Michigan, 8 mi from Rapid River via CR 513; the group area is screened from the other sites by oak, hemlock and hardwoods. Day-use picnic area beside the swimming beach and boat ramp; the bay is a noted walleye fishery, and the Hunter's Point paved ramp is under a mile from the entrance. --Claude

facilities.note: Accessible vault toilets and drinking water. Day-use picnic area and open grassy area beside the swimming beach and boat ramp.

booking.note: 20 single sites and both group sites are reservable on recreation.gov; 16 single sites are first-come, and the 2026 rate table opens with a first-come week (May 15-21) before the reservable peak season. No switching sites on arrival; a reserved site is held until noon the day after arrival. Check-in 2 p.m., check-out noon (rec.gov) or 11 a.m. (FS page).

name: Monocle Lake Campground
note: Hiawatha NF campground around the south end of 172-acre Monocle Lake, off Lake Shore Drive (Whitefish Bay Scenic Byway) via FR 3699 near Bay Mills, under 2 mi from Point Iroquois Lighthouse; heavily shaded sites in mixed hardwoods. Day-use picnic area with a swimming beach, and the Monocle Lake Trail with an accessible boardwalk. Concession-run. Repaving is scheduled for autumn 2026 and spring 2027, during the seasonal closure (FS alert, October 2026). --Claude

sites.note: 42 sites in the catalog: 26 reservable and 15 first-come standard sites plus one tent-only site. Maximum vehicle lengths run 30-80 ft (14 sites 30 ft, 10 at 50 ft, 9 at 45, 3 at 75-80); 7 pull-throughs.

facilities.note: Accessible pressurized water and vault toilets spaced through the campground; day-use area with a swimming beach and a paved boat launch.

booking.note: 26 standard sites book on recreation.gov (or 877-444-6777) up to 4 days before arrival; 15 are first-come, and the rate table runs first-come weeks in mid-May. Weekend reservations 2 nights, holiday weekends 3. A reservation is forfeited if you have not arrived by check-out time the day after your arrival date; walk-up sites cannot be traded for reservations. Check-in 2 pm, check-out noon; self-pay station, no office.

name: Carp River Campground
note: Rustic Hiawatha NF campground of wooded sites beside the Carp Wild and Scenic River, about 8 mi from St. Ignace via Mackinac Trail (H-63) and a quarter mile on FR 3445; brook, brown and rainbow trout from stair sets down the riverbank, plus canoeing and kayaking. Concession-run. --Claude

sites.note: 20 wooded sites, each with a table and fire ring. Max vehicle length 25-45 ft (35 ft on most); 4 pull-throughs. Maximum 8 people per site.

facilities.note: Water pumps and vault toilets spaced through the campground. Stairs down the riverbank to the Carp River. Self-pay station; no office on site.

booking.note: Reserve on recreation.gov or (877) 444-6777 up to 4 days before arrival; 8 of the 20 sites are first-come, and the rate table runs a first-come week before the peak season (2026: May 15-21). Weekend reservations 2 nights, holiday weekends 3 (recreation.gov rules; they may be relaxed for a same-day booking). A reservation is forfeited if you have not arrived by checkout time the day after arrival; you must occupy the site the first night.

name: Bay View Campground
note: Rustic Hiawatha NF campground on Lake Superior's Whitefish Bay, off the Whitefish Bay Scenic Byway (Lakeshore Drive) about 8 miles west of Brimley. Heavily shaded sites beneath pine, oak, maple and birch, a few steps from a sandy beach. Camp host lives on site in season. --Claude

sites.note: The Forest Service says 25 sites; recreation.gov lists 24: 23 drive-in (16 reservable, 6 first-come, one held by management) and a walk-to site. RV lengths 20-50 ft: sites 01, 02, 07-10 and 14 are 20 ft, the rest 30-50; 13 is a pull-through.

facilities.note: Vault toilets and hand-pumped drinking water at several points in the campground. No office on site: self-pay station.

booking.note: Run by a concessionaire ((906) 767-1111). 16 sites reservable on recreation.gov (or 1-877-444-6777) up to 4 days before arrival; the rest first-come, and the first week of the season is first-come. Occupy a reserved site the first night; it is forfeited if you have not arrived by check-out time the next day. Up to 14 consecutive days.

name: Camp 7 Lake Campground
note: Hiawatha NF campground on 60-acre Camp Seven Lake, Rapid River/Manistique district, reached from FH 13 and 7.8 mi east on CR 442; shaded, private sites, some right on the lake. Swimming beach, boating and fishing (smallmouth, bluegill, perch); the 2-mile Van Winkle Lake loop trail leads to a paper birch stand. --Claude

sites.note: 38 single/double family sites (11 electric) and electric group site 32. Max vehicle length 50-60 ft; 4 pull-throughs. One RV with tow vehicle per single site.

facilities.note: Accessible vault toilets and drinking water. Swimming beach with a paved walking trail; group picnic area for up to 25.

booking.note: Reserve on recreation.gov up to 4 days before arrival; 16 of the 39 sites are first-come, and the rate table runs a first-come week before the reservable peak season (2026: May 15-21). No minimum stay. A reserved site is held until checkout time (noon) the day after arrival. Check-in 2 pm.

name: Chicago Lake Campsites
note: Primitive Hiawatha NF campsites clustered at the north end of 188-acre Chicago Lake, beside an improved gravel boat ramp; a busy lake, but loons still call. Sites 2 and 4 are the ones for a trailer or motorhome. Pike and bluegill, some bass and perch; best swimming at sites 3 and 4. Reached via FH-13, CR 442, CR N-3 and 0.25 mi of FR 2422; access road is decent gravel. --Claude

sites.note: Site 2 (55x45 ft, open) and site 4 (55x50 ft, semi-open) each take two families and trailers; site 3 (60x50 ft, under tall pines near the shore) has difficult trailer access for lack of turning room. Catalog lengths: sites 2 and 3 24 ft, site 4 32 ft. Site 1 (a small tent site on a poor road the FS says needs 4WD) is decommissioned. Up to 16 people per site.

facilities.note: Primitive (pit) toilets at site 2 and between sites 3 and 4. Pack in, pack out. Improved gravel boat ramp beside site 4.

booking.note: Reservation only from May 15 to Columbus Day ('Walk ins are not allowed'); no reservations or fees from Columbus Day to May 15. Run by the Forest Service (Rapid River/Manistique Ranger District), not a concessionaire. The site must be occupied the first night and not left unattended over 24 hours.

name: Widewaters Campground
note: Hiawatha NF campground (Munising Ranger District) in mature hardwoods between Irwin Lake and the Indian River, about 16 miles from Munising via M-28, Forest Highway 13 and Forest Road 2262. Sites range from heavily wooded and private to open; boat ramp at the campground (and at Fish Lake), an access point for the Indian River Canoe Trail; brook trout. The 9-mile Bruno's Run Trail passes through the campground. --Claude

sites.note: 32 back-in single sites in the recreation.gov catalog, driveways 18-58 ft (53-58 ft at 11, 43-50 at 9, 28-38 at 11, one of 18). A few waterfront sites have river access.

booking.note: 17 of the 32 sites are reservable on recreation.gov (or 1-877-444-6777) and 15 are first-come; recreation.gov sells the opening week (May 14-20 in 2027) as a first-come season. A reservation is held until noon the day after arrival. Recreation.gov's notices refer to a campground concessionaire and manager (facility line 906-767-1111).

name: Colwell Lake Campground
note: Hiawatha NF campground on the eastern shore of 145-acre Colwell Lake, 25 mi north of Manistique via M-94 and FR 2246, in mixed hardwood and conifer forest. Sandy swimming beach with a picnic area, and a 2-mile hiking and snowshoe trail. Bass, pike, crappie, perch and bluegill. --Claude

facilities.note: Water hydrants through the campground. Boat ramp and launching pier near the entrance with trailer turn-around, accessible fishing pier, swimming beach (no lifeguard).

booking.note: 17 family sites and the group site are reservable; the other family sites are not reservable in the catalog, and the season's first week (about May 15-21) is a first-come season on recreation.gov. Run by a concessionaire (recreation.gov refers to 'the campground concessionaire', unnamed). A reserved site is held until noon the day after arrival.

name: Flowing Well Campground
note: Small Hiawatha NF campground on the west bank of the Sturgeon River, 2.8 miles north of US-2 on Forest Highway 13 (east of Rapid River). Spacious sites, some along the bank overlooking the slow-moving river; group picnic area. The Sturgeon River Canoe Trail runs through the campground. --Claude

sites.note: The recreation.gov catalog lists 6 standard sites (4 reservable, 2 first-come), each for an RV, trailer or tent to 25 ft; 4 are pull-throughs. The pages call it 'less than a dozen spacious sites'.

facilities.note: Well water with heavy iron and sulfur content ('an acquired taste, but is safe to consume'). The Forest Service page currently reports a temporary water outage (bring all water, including drinking water). recreation.gov lists accessible vault toilets; the Forest Service page says 'Restrooms are not available at this site.'

booking.note: Reserve on recreation.gov or (877) 444-6777; 2 of the 6 sites are first-come only, and the rate table opens each season with a first-come week in mid-May (2027: May 14-20). Reservations close 4 days before arrival. A reserved site is held until noon the day after arrival. Check-in 2 pm.

note: Small Hiawatha NF campground on a bluff overlooking the Indian River, 19.8 mi N of Manistique on M-94 (14.2 mi S of Shingleton); a short trail leads down to the river. Large, wooded, private sites. Near the halfway point of the Indian River Canoe Trail, a convenient overnight stop for canoeists. --Claude

facilities.note: The FS page lists a pit toilet.

booking.note: Check-in 2 pm, check-out 11 am.

name: Petes Lake Campground
note: Hiawatha NF campground on 190-acre Pete's Lake, about 10 mi south of Munising via H-13 and FR 2173. Spacious, private forested sites, a few overlooking the lake, on blacktop roads. Shaded day-use picnic area on the shore with a swimming beach (no lifeguard), accessible fishing pier and boat ramp; the 9-mile Bruno's Run Trail passes through the campground. --Claude

sites.note: 48 sites on recreation.gov: 41 single and 5 group standard sites, all back-in on gravel spurs, 40-75 ft by the catalog (most 45-60), plus 2 tent-only sites. One RV with tow vehicle per single site; most take one extra vehicle, which must fit on the spur.

booking.note: Reserve on recreation.gov or at 1-877-444-6777, up to 4 days before arrival; 23 of the 48 catalog sites are first-come, and recreation.gov runs the first week of the season (mid-May) as first-come. A reserved site is held until noon the day after arrival. Check-in 2 p.m. Run by a concessionaire.

name: Soldier Lake Campground
note: Hiawatha NF campground of shaded sites in pine, aspen and maple surrounding 15-acre Soldier Lake, a mile south of M-28 on FR 3138 near Raco/Strongs, away from highway noise. Two sandy beaches; non-motorized boating; large day-use picnic areas with a CCC-built 1930s shelter; North Country Trail access from the parking area. --Claude

sites.note: 44 single-family back-in sites for tents and RVs. Max vehicle length 30 ft at 23 sites, 35-50 ft at 12, 55-75 ft at 9. One RV with tow vehicle per site; most sites take one extra vehicle on the spur.

name: Corner Lake Campground
note: Rustic Hiawatha NF campground on the south end of 100-acre Corner Lake, 18.7 mi north of US-2 on Forest Highway 13 then 1.1 mi east on CR 440. Large wooded sites with room for RVs; primitive - no drinking water, bring your own. Boat ramp with parking, a small sandy beach suited to young children, and nearby access to the Pine Marten Run Trail; OHV camping. --Claude

sites.note: Nine wooded campsites, each with a picnic table and fire ring.

booking.note: First-come, first-served; no recreation.gov listing. Run by the Forest Service (Rapid River/Manistique Ranger District).

name: Island Lake Campground
note: Small, quiet Hiawatha NF campground in a classic pine forest on 32.5-acre Island Lake, about 12 mi south of Munising via Forest Highway 13 and FR 2268/2254/2557; lighter use than most, with a boat slip for small carry-in boats and canoes and shore fishing. Off-road vehicles may ride in and out of the campground (in and out only), with ATV trails nearby; the campground road is narrow and one-way. --Claude

name: Black River Harbor Campground
note: Ottawa NF campground beside the Black River Harbor Recreation Area at the river's mouth on Lake Superior, at the end of Black River Road (CR-513) about 15 miles north of Bessemer. Wooded, partly shaded sites bordered by vegetation. A footbridge crosses the river to the Lake Superior sand beaches; trails follow the river past a series of waterfalls (platforms and trails under major repair from May 2026, with temporary closures). CCC pavilion and harbor with charter fishing next door. --Claude

sites.note: The Forest Service gives 39 paved camping spurs; recreation.gov says 38 available campsites and its catalog lists 37 (26 reservable, 11 first-come) plus 3 management sites. Every site is back-in; posted driveway lengths run 22-74 ft, most 40 ft or more. Seven sites overlook Lake Superior.

facilities.note: Pressurized water system, not potable; recreation.gov: 'No water available at campground for entire 2026 season'. Flush toilets in the CCC pavilion in the adjoining day-use area; boat ramp in the harbor.

booking.note: 26 sites reservable on recreation.gov, 11 first-come (self-pay). name: Marion Lake Campground
note: Ottawa NF campground on 317-acre Marion Lake, 4 mi E of Watersmeet via US 2, FR 3980 and FR 3985 (Watersmeet/Iron River RD); three loops with sites screened by natural vegetation. Adjacent sandy beach and day-use area (picnic tables, grills, play area); free concrete boat ramps east of loop 2 and west of loop 1. Walleye, smallmouth bass, northern pike and perch. A group site for up to 100 sits beside the loops. --Claude

booking.note: Single sites are first come, first served with self-pay; campers must occupy the site the first night. Only the group site (up to 100 people, $100) books on recreation.gov. Run by a concessionaire, Camp Host, LLC.

name: Sylvania (Clark Lake) Campground
note: Drive-in Clark Lake Campground in the Sylvania Recreation Area, Ottawa NF, 7 mi SW of Watersmeet off CR 535 (distinct from the Sylvania Wilderness backcountry, which it adjoins). Paved access; sites screened by natural vegetation. Adjacent day-use swimming beach and canoe landings on Clark Lake. --Claude

sites.note: 48 drive-in sites in four loops for 'tents, trailers and motor homes' (one is a management/host site in the catalog); 10 electric. All back-in; catalog vehicle lengths 31-88 ft, most 40 ft or more. Eight people, two vehicles, and one RV or trailer plus two tents per site.

facilities.note: Water faucets in loops 2, 3 and 4; two flush toilet buildings and one accessible vault toilet; an RV water and dump station beside the campground. Day-use area with picnic area, swimming beach, canoe landings and trailheads adjacent.

booking.note: 38 of 48 sites bookable on recreation.gov (cutoff 4 days before arrival); the rest are first-come, and 'typically there is always a site available'. Run by Camp Host, LLC under a special use permit; self-pay. A Sylvania permit (from the entrance station) is required of all day and overnight users. The site must be occupied the first night.

name: Bobcat Lake Campground
note: Ottawa NF campground on Bobcat Lake, ~3 mi SE of Marenisco on FR 8500 off M-64, Bessemer RD; run by concessionaire Camp Host, LLC. Swimming beach and day-use area half a mile east. --Claude

name: Moosehead Lake Campground
note: Ottawa NF campground beside Moosehead Lake on the Wisconsin border, 10 mi SE of Marenisco (Bessemer RD); reached from M-64 by FR 8220, FR 6860 and FR 6862. A free concrete boat ramp next to the campground; a channel lets boats pass to Little Presque Isle Lake in Wisconsin. Northern pike, bass, muskellunge, crappie and bluegill. --Claude

facilities.note: Two vault toilets in the loop and a centrally located pressurized faucet (no water after the September 30 service cutoff).

booking.note: First-come only: claim a site in person and self-pay, or pay by scanning the QR code with the recreation.gov app (Scan and Pay). Campers must occupy the site the first night.

name: Norway Lake Campground
note: Ottawa NF two-loop campground among towering red pines beside Norway Lake, 8 mi SE of Sidnaw (Sidnaw Road south 5.5 mi, then 2 mi east on FR 2400), Kenton Ranger District. Sites are naturally screened by vegetation, each with a tent pad, table, fire ring and lantern post. A boat landing, change house and picnic area are adjacent. --Claude

sites.note: 27 drive-in sites in two loops that 'can accommodate tents, trailers and motor homes' (no length posted). Up to eight people and two motorized vehicles per site, with at most one RV or camper trailer. No accessible sites.

facilities.note: Three sets of double vault toilets and hand pumps for drinking water in the loops; picnic shelter.

booking.note: First-come only; campers must occupy the site the first night. After 14 days, move to another campground or dispersed site for at least 24 hours. Run by a concessionaire (Camp Host, LLC).

name: Perch Lake Campground
note: Ottawa NF campground on 994-acre Perch Lake, Kenton Ranger District, 10 mi SE of Sidnaw via Sidnaw Road (paved about 6.5 mi, then gravel). One loop of spacious sites, many with lake access. Concrete boat ramp and trailer parking adjacent; popular for canoeing, kayaking and deep-woods fishing; Hannah-Web and Winslow lakes a few minutes west. --Claude

sites.note: 20 drive-in sites in one loop for tents, trailers and motor homes (18 back-in, 2 pull-through); no lengths in the catalog. Eight people and 2 motorized vehicles per site, at most one RV or trailer.

booking.note: 12 of the 20 sites are reservable on recreation.gov, up to 4 days before arrival; the other 8 are first-come. Reservations run through September 30; October 1-15 every site is first-come self-registration. recreation.gov marks a 4-night minimum as 'soft': it may be relaxed for a same-day booking. 14-day limit, then move at least 24 hours; the site must be occupied the first night. Run by a concessionaire (Camp Host, LLC).

note: Small rustic Ottawa NF campground along the Sturgeon River beside the Sturgeon River Gorge Wilderness, 5 mi N of Sidnaw via FR 2200 (Kenton RD). Brown trout and steelhead; the river is floatable from here in high water (mid-April to June) but rocky with Class III-IV rapids. Sidnaw Creek Trail and the North Country Trail nearby. Site lengths not published. --Claude

name: Bob Lake Campground
note: Ottawa NF campground on 133-acre Bob Lake, ~18 mi SE of Ontonagon, Ontonagon RD; run by concessionaire Camp Host, LLC. Many sites near the lake; adjacent day-use picnic area, boat landing and the 1.2-mile Beaver Lodge Interpretive Trail. Shallow lake (3-17 ft) with walleye, smallmouth bass and perch. Reached via FH 16, FR 1640 (Pori Road), FR 1470 and FR 1478. --Claude

sites.note: Single loop of drive-in sites, screened by vegetation, that 'can accommodate tents, trailers or motor homes'; each has a picnic table, fire ring, lantern post and parking spur. No length limit posted. Eight people, two motor vehicles and at most one RV or camper trailer per site.

facilities.note: Three vault toilets in the loop (one accessible); drinking water from a hand pump near the entrance. Adjacent day-use picnic area and boat landing with a concrete ramp (no launch charge).

booking.note: Campers must occupy the site the first night. After 14 days, move to another campground or dispersed site for at least 24 hours.

note: Ottawa NF campground on 111-acre, no-wake Imp Lake (trout, panfish), 6 mi SE of Watersmeet via US 2 and FR 3978, Watersmeet Ranger District. Two loops of screened drive-in sites: lakeside sites look onto a small island with nesting loons, off-lake sites sit beside towering hemlocks. Free concrete boat ramp and picnic area beside the campground, and the 1-mile wheelchair-accessible Imp Lake Interpretive Trail across the road. Run by the concessionaire Camp Host, LLC. --Claude

note: Ottawa NF campground on 151-acre Lake Ste. Kathryn (25 ft deep), 8 mi south of Sidnaw on Sidnaw Road (Kenton Ranger District, Iron County). About 1 mile from Stony Lake and 2 miles from Lake Michigan public access; no on-site swimming/lake frontage. --Claude

In the peak season (late June to late August) a weekly program for families runs: horsemanship, target and adventure sports, crafts and the waterfront. --Claude

name: Bond Falls West Campground
note: Upper Peninsula Power Company campground in the pines on the Bond Falls Flowage's southwest peninsula, about 1.5 km south of the dam. From Paulding take Bond Falls Rd about 3 miles and follow the brown-and-yellow signs for the West Shore boat access and campsites on a packed-sand road; a 2024 reviewer warns not to follow Google or RV Life for the last mile. Pick an open site; a host comes round about 11am with the required permit. Site sizes vary. UPPCO posts no length limit: a reviewer fit a 34-ft fifth wheel in Oct 2023, calling the loop a little tight, while another found tight turns and scraping branches at site 10 with a travel trailer in Sep 2023. --Claude

sites.note: UPPCO: 48 rustic sites across West and East, no split published. The posted board runs W-1 onward with W-24 and W-25 walk-in and W-26 marked camps; reviewers and signs give the drive-in loop as 1-22 or 1-23. Pull-through: W5, 21 (reviewers). Each has a picnic table and fire ring.

facilities.note: Hand-pump water at points around the campground, not at each site. Its own public boat launch.

booking.note: UPPCO: 'Reservations: None. All campsites are available on a first-come, first-served basis.' Maximum stay is 14 nights PER YEAR. Holiday weekends often reach capacity. Free permit required; valid ID.

name: Sebewaing County Park
note: Huron County park at 759 Union St, on the Sebewaing River at the end of Union St (drains to Saginaw Bay/Lake Huron), on 40 acres with a fishing dock and three nature trails; no boat launch at the park (the marina is a few miles away). Operated by Huron County Parks -- a DISTINCT campground from the private Sebewaing River Campground (id3849) at 541 Union St. --Claude

sites.note: 54 full-hookup sites (1-54) and 10 sites in a separate tent-camping circle (55-64), per the park map (rev. 1/24). Tents are allowed on any site, one camping unit per site.

booking.note: Booked online through Huron County Parks' Checkfront page ('Book a Site') or by phone. The next season opens to the public around December 1 (2026 season: Dec 1, 2025, noon). Refunds only 30+ days out and not for holidays or special events. Seasonal sites are limited and sell out each year.

name: Haymarsh Lake Campground (Haymarsh State Game Area)
note: Rustic Mecosta County Parks campground on Haymarsh Lake (375 acres, a 1949 flooding that joined six small lakes) within the DNR's 6,737-acre Haymarsh Lake State Game Area, ~7 mi E of Paris; public hunting land access. facilities.note: Hand water pump, two boat launches, fish cleaning station, trash dumpster.

name: Wagener County Park
note: Huron County park on Lake Huron, 5 mi S of Harbor Beach (2671 S Lakeshore Rd), 132 wooded acres. Rocky beach, not ideal for swimming; hiking trails, playgrounds; 8 rustic cabins. The boat launch is unavailable (county page, read 2026-10-25). --Claude

name: Pinconning County Park
note: Bay County park on Saginaw Bay (3041 E Pinconning Rd): wooded or sunny sites, 12 with concrete pads; six heated log cabins rented year-round; boat launch and channel, small beach (no lifeguard), fishing dock, observation towers, boardwalks and trails in a 206-acre nature preserve. The shoreline is coastal wetland, and Lake Huron's water level decides how good the swimming and boating are. --Claude

booking.note: Reserve by phone or by the online request form (a ranger calls back; the form does not guarantee a site), held by credit card or advance payment, for the current calendar year only. Reservations are recommended May-September, when the campground is typically full every weekend; October-April they are not needed. Late arrivals pay at the office door's overnight payment slot before setting up. Long-term sites (1 week to 1 year) are limited to specific sites and currently have a waiting list. Cancel at least 7 days ahead. Renters must be 21. Check-in 3 p.m., check-out 2 p.m.

name: Thurston Park Campground
note: Village of Central Lake park at the northwest end of Intermediate Lake (Antrim County Chain of Lakes), 7854 Bradford St. Boat launch, public docks, gazebo, playground, fish-cleaning station; easy walk to downtown. --Claude

hookups.note: Full hookups at bluff sites 27-32 and upper sites 36-40 (most of them held by seasonal campers); water and electric at 33-35; electric with water for tank fill only at the waterfront sites 1-7, 9, 10 and standard sites 11-26.

season.note: The first Friday in May to the first Sunday in October.

booking.note: Booked on the village's Firefly page; the campground manager (Char & Ron Snay, 231-676-8539, on site 7 days a week in season) handles reservations. The next year's sites open in January: the village page says the 2nd Tuesday at 8am (January 13, 2026), the guide says the second Monday. The waterfront sites (1-7, 9, 10) take 4 nights on weekends and 14 nights at most. Seasonal sites by the village clerk's waiting list. Check-in 3-10 pm; late arrivals must call the manager. Check-out noon.

name: St. James Township Campground (Beaver Island)
note: St. James Township campground on a bluff overlooking Lake Michigan and Garden, Squaw and Whiskey Islands, just off Donegal Bay Rd about a mile from the St. James ferry dock at the end of the bike path; a short walk to town and the Donegal Bay swimming beach. Beaver Island is reached only by the Beaver Island Boat Co. car ferry from Charlevoix: only the Emerald Isle carries vehicles (limits 13'6" tall, 46 ft long, 50 tons, so a motorhome fits), and the vehicle space must be reserved by phone. 2026 fare for a vehicle over 7'6" tall and 10 ft long: from $110.41 each way (call with dimensions for the exact price), plus $33.50 per adult each way. Dark-sky viewing area; take care near the bluff. --Claude

sites.note: 12 non-electric sites (1-12) and 5 electric (14-18; there is no site 13). Sites 1-4 and 7 are tent-only (7 is walk-in); RV-capable sites per the booking page: 5, 6, 9, 10 up to 20 ft, 8, 11, 12 and electric 14-16 up to 25 ft, ADA electric sites 17-18 (concrete pads) up to 28 ft. Four people per site (single families or youth groups may be larger).

facilities.note: Hand pump near the rustic sites and a cold-water spigot by the showers; two pit toilets plus portable toilets (one ADA); four enclosed outdoor hot showers, free to campers. Campground host on site; some firewood on hand (bringing firewood to the island is unlawful).

booking.note: Booked online on the township's Firefly Reservations page, or through the campground host at 231-497-4477. Full refund of site fees for cancellations two weeks or more before arrival (by email to the host). A vehicle needs its own Beaver Island Boat Co. ferry reservation, which the township says to secure first.

note: Bergland Township park on Bergland Bay of Lake Gogebic (local government; RV Life mislabels as city). Lower campground on mostly level gravel spurs; upper campground heavily wooded, some sites hard to reach or unlevel. Sand beach, playground; DNR dock and boat launch a short walk south. Generators prohibited. Distinct from the county-run Ontonagon County Park to the south. --Claude

name: Ojibwa Campground (Sand Point)

note: Marquette County park on the N shore of Lake Independence in Big Bay (Powell Twp), ~22 mi N of Marquette on CR-550. Registered campers may ride ATVs/ORVs on park roads between the campsite and the entrance. --Claude

Check-in 3 p.m., check-out 11 a.m. Cancellations only by phone or voicemail to the park office.

note: City of Houghton municipal RV park on the Portage Waterway at 1100 W Lakeshore Drive, paved sites. Self-contained units only: no pop-ups or tents, as there is no bathroom or shower building; no generators. Next to Ray Kestner Waterfront Park (beach, fishing piers, boat launch), at the west end of the four-mile waterfront trail to downtown. GPS may misroute: follow the highway signs and don't turn onto Houghton Canal Road. --Claude

name: Lake Carmi State Park
note: Vermont's largest state-park campground, on the south-east shore of Lake Carmi in two areas: Area A by the lake's east shore, and Area B on a knoll reached by a road across the park's black spruce-tamarack bog (a State Natural Area). Prime sites along the shore in both areas look at the lake through a belt of trees; each area has a swimming beach. Many interior sites list only 15-20 ft, so site choice matters for a 23-ft rig. Registered campers get a PIN for the security gate. --Claude

sites.note: 138 tent/RV sites (132 take an RV, 6 are tent-only), 35 lean-tos and 2 cabins in Area A, Area B and an 8-site C Loop. RV sites list 15-40 ft; 87 of the 132 list 25 ft or more, 36 list 15-20 ft and 9 give no length.

season.note: Third weekend in May through the second weekend in September (2026: May 15 - Sep 13; 2027: May 21 - Sep 12, last night Sep 11). The 2026 Map & Guide says Memorial Day weekend to Indigenous Peoples' Day instead.

name: Winhall Brook Camping Area
note: Corps of Engineers campground of the Ball Mountain Lake flood-control project, in the valley where Winhall Brook meets the West River, seven miles above the lake; the West River Trail runs past it. A narrow one-lane bridge (16-ton limit) leads to the south side. Sites near the river sit behind a brushy, wooded bank, and water held back by the dam can close parts of the campground. Cash and checks are not accepted. --Claude

Spring-fed swimming pool on Moose Brook, and a link to the Presidential Rail Trail. Limited cell service. --Claude

name: Jericho Mountain State Park
note: Campground in a state park built around 75 miles of ATV, UTV and trail-bike trails a few miles northwest of Berlin, with a beach and boat launch on Jericho Lake (no gas motors). Riders reach the trails from their sites on the campground roads, so expect ATV traffic and engine noise through the campground in season. The newer full-hookup RV loop is tents-free with no facilities of its own; the bathhouse is about 0.4 mile away. --Claude

The lake's boat-in remote sites and cabins are not part of this entry. --Claude

name: Mollidgewock State Park
note: Primitive campground along the Androscoggin River in the Thirteen Mile Woods Scenic Area, ~3 mi south of Errol on NH-16. Mostly tent and pop-up sites plus 2 lean-tos and 2 remote canoe-to sites; only the 2 'standard' drive-in sites take a 23-ft rig: 018, a back-in on the open lawn by the river, and 029, a pull-through set back from the water. A new office and camp store are open; the new showers and flush toilets were still delayed by construction when the park page was read (2026-11-23). Wood, ice and canoe/kayak rentals at the office. Every camper registers at the office (self-registration when closed); payment at the park is cash or traveler's check only. --Claude

name: Charlestown Breachway Campground
note: RIDEM camping area in a gravel lot on the east side of the Charlestown Breachway, between Ninigret Pond and Block Island Sound and a walk from the state beach. Fully self-contained units only (manufacturer-installed holding tanks; no tents, pop-ups, hybrids or canvas tops); one extra vehicle a site. Campers may use the dump and water fill at Burlingame or Fishermen's Memorial once at no charge. No open fires (propane stoves allowed) and no pets. Sites 58-75 back onto the breachway channel. --Claude

sites.note: All 75 are back-in gravel sites in one lot, 30-44 ft (ReserveAmerica Max Vehicle Length: 6 at 30 ft, the rest 32-44 ft).

season.note: Opened Friday April 10 in 2026 (DEM). No closing date was posted when read 2026-11-11; October 31 is from the earlier note.

booking.note: Fully self-contained RVs only. ReserveAmerica, up to 12 months ahead and for the same day. As of October 2026, 2027 reservations are on hold while RIDEM picks a new reservation provider, so the channel and rules may change. Unreserved sites are let first come at the parks. STAY LIMIT: 7 nights in any 21 days in peak season (the Thursday before Memorial Day through Labor Day weekend), then 14 nights away; 21 nights in 28 the rest of the year. RIDEM's full policy also sets peak-season minimum stays, not recorded here. Check-in 1-10 p.m. (no later, reserved or not), check-out 11 a.m.; the permit holder is 18 and stays on the site; one family, or six people, a site; two vehicles. The site must be occupied the first night or it is resold with no refund. CANCELLING: 8 days or more before arrival, everything back but the reservation fee and an $8.75 cancellation fee; 2 to 7 days, one night is kept as well; under 2 days, no refund. No refunds for weather or leaving early.

name: Raven Rock State Park
note: Moccasin Branch Campground (opened ~2023), at 814 Moccasin Branch Road just before the park's main entrance. --Claude

facilities.note: Bathhouse with toilets and hot showers; water spigots around the loop; firewood sold at the campground (cash only).

booking.note: 'Reservations are required for all types of camping at Raven Rock - no walk-ups permitted.' Up to 6 months ahead and for the same day; 14 consecutive nights in any 30 days. Holiday weekends (Memorial Day, July 4th, Labor Day) need 2 nights, cut to 1 when booking within 14 days. Go straight to the site; staff come round to check in. $6/night cancellation fee.

name: Standing Indian Campground
note: USFS Nantahala NF (Nantahala Ranger District) at the headwaters of the Nantahala River, ringed by 5,000-ft peaks and crossed by trout streams; trailheads to the Appalachian Trail. 20 minutes from Franklin, the last 1.7 miles on paved FR 67. Campground store sells firewood and delivers it to the site. Horses are not allowed; Hurricane Creek horse camp is 2 miles up FR 67. --Claude

sites.note: recreation.gov catalog: 78 standard non-electric sites (32 reservable, 46 first-come), all back-in with a 50-ft maximum vehicle length, plus 3 group sites (Kimsey Creek). Double sites: 10/11, 17/18, 36/37, 44/45, 55/56, 62/63.

season.note: First-come loops: April 1 to the Sunday after Thanksgiving. Reservation-only sites (Loop 5 and the Kimsey Creek group sites): April 1 - October 30.

booking.note: Loop 5 and the group sites are reservation-only on recreation.gov (booking closes 3 days before arrival; 2-night weekend and 3-night holiday-weekend minimums); the other loops are first-come, and reservable sites may also be taken first-come outside the reservation season. Cash or check only at the campground. Check-in 2 pm, check-out 1 pm.

name: Cheoah Point Campground
note: USFS Nantahala NF (Cheoah RD) on a peninsula of Lake Santeetlah. Only the six electric sites take RVs; the first-come sites are tent sites. Boat ramp and Cheoah Point Beach (no dogs on the beach). --Claude

sites.note: Six reservable RV sites (18-23), all electric, back-in, to 40 ft; 17 first-come non-electric sites are tent sites (vehicle to 22 ft). Steep terrain; many sites overlook the lake.

season.note: The boat launch is open year-round.

booking.note: Run by the Forest Service's Cheoah Ranger District (not a concession). The six RV sites are reservable; the 17 tent sites are first-come. Check-in after 2 p.m., check-out by 2 p.m.; 2 vehicles and 8 people per site; generators 3 hours total between 10 a.m. and 10 p.m.

name: Jackrabbit Mountain Campground
note: USFS Nantahala NF (Tusquitee RD) on a peninsula of Lake Chatuge near Hayesville. Wooded loops, most sites with lake views; the RV-sized sites are in Loops A and B. Swim beach, boat ramp, fishing pier, 15-mile mountain-bike trail system. --Claude

Sites typed RV have no tent pads.

booking.note: 'All sites (Loop A, Loop B, and Loop C) must be reserved through recreation.gov. There are no first come first serve sites available ... Reservations can be made up to the day of arrival.' 14 nights in a rolling 30 days. Check-in 4 pm, check-out noon.

name: Tsali Campground
note: USFS Nantahala NF (Cheoah Ranger District) off NC-28 on an arm of Fontana Lake, with a boat launch. Many sites fit small/mid RVs; a sharp interior curve hampers big rigs. Mountain-bike and horse trail hub (bikes and horses ride the loops on alternating days; per-person trail fee). --Claude

booking.note: All 42 sites first-come; campers pay at the campground fee station. Forest-wide order: no more than 14 days camping within any 30-day period.

name: Van Hook Glade Campground
note: USFS Nantahala NF (Nantahala Ranger District) on US-64 in the Cullasaja Gorge, 4.5 miles west of Highlands; shady, wooded sites. A sharp curve inside the loop makes maneuvering an RV difficult. A short trail leads to Cliffside Lake (swimming, trout fishing, no boating). --Claude

booking.note: Concession-run by FIND Outdoors (the Cradle of Forestry in America Interpretive Association); hosts on site. Reservations on recreation.gov close 4 days before arrival; holiday weekends need 3 nights. Two vehicles and two tents per site; 8 people.

name: North Mills River Campground
note: USFS Pisgah NF (Pisgah RD), concession-run by Naventure; two loops on opposite sides of the North Mills River, mostly shaded. Bear-country food storage rules enforced. --Claude

sites.note: Catalog: 20 standard non-electric, 1 RV electric (014, 28 ft) and 3 tent-only family sites plus a group tent area and 4 management sites. All back-ins; most RV sites take only 18-20 ft, seven take 30-35 ft. Sites 14-26 close in winter.

facilities.note: Bathhouse with hot showers and flush toilets March 20 - November 15; in winter no running water or electricity, pit toilets only. Firewood sold on site ($10).

season.note: Winter 2026-27: open November 16 to March 20 for walk-up, one-night stays only. The Upper Loop, showers and flush toilets are closed; no running water or electricity, pit toilets only.

booking.note: Reserve on recreation.gov up to 6 months ahead, March 20 - November 15; winter sites are walk-up only and cannot be reserved. 14 nights in a rolling 30 days. Check in with the campground host before setting up. Concession-run by Naventure.

booking.note: All nine sites are reservable on recreation.gov; 'Availability is extremely limited during weekends and holidays.' Run by the concessionaire Naventure. Check-in after 2 pm, check-out by noon; 2 tents and 2 vehicles per site, a third vehicle $5 paid on site.

name: Cedar Point Campground
note: USFS Croatan NF at the junction of the White Oak River and Bogue Sound, beside Swansboro Inlet; salt marsh, shallow-draft boat launch. Within a mile of shopping. --Claude

sites.note: 36 campsites, all electric (32 reservable, 4 first-come). recreation.gov's catalog lists max vehicle lengths of 50-75 ft (most 52-70 ft); one pull-through (site 20), the rest back-in.

facilities.note: Bath house with private hot showers; dump station with a potable-water connection. Small-craft boat ramp and fishing pier; Tideland Trail.

season.note: Hurricanes and tropical storms (usually July-September) sometimes close it temporarily.

booking.note: Run by the Forest Service's Croatan Ranger District (not a concession). Reservations up to 180 days ahead and no later than 3 days before arrival; 4 sites are first-come (see the host before paying; Scan & Pay only for those). Holiday weekends need 3 nights. 14 nights in any 30 days, then 16 days away.

name: Tanglewood Park RV Campground
note: Forsyth County-operated RV campground in 1,100-acre Tanglewood Park along the Yadkin River near Clemmons, secluded from the park's sports areas; golf, trails, horseback riding and the Festival of Lights in the park. RVs only: no tents or canopies. --Claude

Up to 14 nights in any 30 days, then 14 days away before returning; 'not a long-term stay facility'. Check-in 1-8 p.m., check-out 11 a.m. Must be 21 to reserve. Cancel within 14 days of arrival: one night's charge.

name: Okefenokee State Park
note: GA state park inside the Okefenokee National Wildlife Refuge near Fargo, a main entrance to the swamp; boat tours and canoe/kayak rentals, certified dark-sky park. Renovated campground reopened Aug 2025. Formerly Stephen C. Foster State Park (renamed 2026). --Claude

sites.note: Two loops, every site with 50/30-amp electric and water. The RV loop (29-52, 24 sites) takes a 23-ft rig at every site: 30-50 ft, 18 full-hookup pull-throughs. The other loop (2-28, 26 sites) runs 15-35 ft; only seven of its sites (2, 4, 11, 14, 15 and pull-throughs 23 and 26) take a 23-ft rig. 31 sites in all fit.

booking.note: Park gates lock at 10 pm (inside the national wildlife refuge); the park is open 7 am - 10 pm.

name: Lake Conasauga Campground
note: USFS Chattahoochee NF, Conasauga RD; Georgia's highest lake in the Cohuttas. Two loops a short way apart off one entrance: the Lower Loop within view of the lake, the Upper Loop in forest above it. Access is 15+ mi of steep, narrow, winding, rough gravel mountain road from either Chatsworth or Ellijay; Forest Road 68 is the recommended route for trailers. Swimming dock and picnic shelter across the lake; electric boat motors only.  TIGHT FIT: recreation.gov lists motorhomes only to 21 ft and the Forest Service 24 ft; campsite photos on recreation.gov look closer to 24 ft, so a 23-ft rig should fit some sites but with little room - pick a site carefully (2026-10-30). --Claude

sites.note: Recreation.gov permits an RV (motorhome) only up to 21 ft, on 20 of the 29 sites (2, 3, 6, 8-12, 16-24, 26, 28, 29); trailers to 25 ft on 18 of them; sites 1, 5 and 27 are tent/pop-up/van only and 4, 7, 13-15, 25 take 8-ft trailers. The FS page says 'RV maximum length 24 feet'; rec.gov: 'Tents, pop-up campers, and travel trailers under 25 feet are recommended ... due to access and campsite size limitations.' AWH 2026-10-30, from rec.gov's campsite photos: the FS 24 ft is closer to reality than rec.gov's 21 ft.

booking.note: Check-in 3 pm, check-out 2 pm. Site must be occupied the first night; 5 people and 2 vehicles per site.

name: Lake Conasauga Overflow Campground
note: USFS Chattahoochee NF, Conasauga Ranger District: overflow campground about a mile past the reservation-only main Lake Conasauga Campground, across the road from the Songbird Management Area's beaver pond. Access is a 15+ mile drive on steep, narrow, winding gravel roads; Forest Road 68 is the recommended route with a trailer. No gas or store within 15 miles; cell service very limited. --Claude

sites.note: Six non-electric drive-in sites with parking spurs; four list RV and trailer, one RV and pop-up but not trailer, one car/van/pickup camper only. No site lengths are published; the 25 ft is recreation.gov's access advisory: 'Travel Trailers over 25 feet are not recommended.'

booking.note: First-come, first-served only; pay on site by scanning the QR code in the Recreation.gov app (works offline) or with cash/check in the fee box. Unstaffed; 14-day limit.

name: Lake Rabun Beach Recreation Area
note: USFS Chattahoochee NF (Chattooga River RD), run by FIND Outdoors. Two loops in the hills above Lake Rabun, across the road from the lake's beach. When towing, rec.gov's directions advise the route via US 76, Charlie Mountain Rd, Bridge Creek Rd and Burton Dam Rd. --Claude

facilities.note: Hot showers, boat ramp, firewood sold, camp hosts. The lake's swim beach and boating are across the road.

booking.note: 39 RV sites bookable on recreation.gov up to 2 days ahead; the other 33 are first-come, first-served. Holiday weekends need 3 nights. 14 nights within 30 days.

name: Lake Russell Recreation Area Campground
note: USFS Chattahoochee NF on 100-acre Lake Russell; no gas motors on the lake. Two paved loops. Firsthand reports: sites are uneven, bring leveling blocks. --Claude

facilities.note: Swim beach, boat launch (electric, wind or paddle only) and fishing dock. The restroom across from site 25 is decommissioned.

booking.note: Reservation only, no first-come sites. 14 nights in any 30, then off the national forest for 30 days. Check-in 2 pm, check-out noon.

note: USFS Chattahoochee NF (Blue Ridge RD), run by concessionaire FIND Outdoors; on 18-acre Lake Winfield Scott near Suches (electric motors only, swimming beach). South Loop holds the hookup and longer sites; North Loop stays open in winter. CLOSED from Sep 1, 2026 for construction and renovation, no reopening date (checked 2026-10-30). --Claude

South Loop sites 1, 5 and 11 are limited to 20 ft; North Loop sites 21-37 to 15 ft.

booking.note: Reservations through recreation.gov or 877-444-6777, not at the campground office; same-day booking allowed. North Loop sites 22-37 are first-come. Check-in 2 pm, check-out 12 pm.

name: Low Gap Campground

The road is narrow, curving and steep. The vault toilet is across the bridge at the back of the campground. Generators up to 4 hours a day, 6 am-10 pm. --Claude

sites.note: Recreation.gov lists no site for an RV/motorhome: equipment is tents, pickup campers, camper vans and trailers, with trailers to 24 ft at sites 2, 3, 4 and 8 and 26 ft at site 5 (14-21 ft elsewhere; 11 and 12 tent/vehicle only). The Forest Service says 'Due to narrow, curving, and steep roads to and from this area, the recommended size of a RV is 28 ft.'

booking.note: Reservation only - no first-come sites. Check-in from 2 pm, check-out 12:01 pm.

name: Pocket Campground
note: USFS Chattahoochee NF, in a limestone valley between Horn and Mill mountains in NW Georgia; Spring Branch creek runs through the adjacent picnic area. Paved access road. Cell service very limited; nearest store and gas 8 miles away in Villanow. Alcohol prohibited in the whole recreation area. --Claude

The next season goes on sale as a block, not on a rolling 6-month window.

name: Rocky Mountain Recreation Area
note: Georgia DNR Wildlife Resources Public Fishing Area campground NW of Rome (4054 Big Texas Valley Rd) on Antioch Lake, part of the Rocky Mountain Project lakes. The land is owned by Oglethorpe Power; Wildlife Resources runs the area and books the campground. Beach, boat ramps (idle-only lakes), lakeside primitive tent sites. Heath Lake is open to fishing only the 1st-10th of each month. --Claude

sites.note: 36 electric RV sites on the booking site (2-37; 8 and 37 are doubles for two rigs), 40-60 ft except site 21 ('Short Site 18 Feet'), so 35 take a 23-ft rig; plus 9 primitive tent sites (A-I) and a group camp. The area's page says '37 RV campsites (2 sites are double campsites) and 9 tent campsites'. Campground road is one-way, counter-clockwise; site 37 must be backed in.

booking.note: Every site is booked through Go Outdoors Georgia (Georgia DNR's licensing and reservation site), online or at 1-800-366-2661. 14 consecutive nights, then 7 nights away. No monthly camping. Campground gate closes at 10 pm (no re-entry); check-out noon. Alcohol is prohibited anywhere on the area.

name: Myakka River State Park
note: Big Flats campground sits near the Upper Myakka Lake, the Myakka Outpost and Wi-Fi; Old Prairie and Palmetto Ridge are near the SR 72 entrance and the river, and only Palmetto Ridge has sewer. Drinking water has been unavailable park-wide since Oct. 28, 2025 - bring your own; bottled water is free at the ranger station (park page, read 2026-10-21). --Claude

sites.note: 90 campsites in three campgrounds (Big Flats, Old Prairie, Palmetto Ridge). Reserve Florida lists 80 'RV or Tent' sites: Big Flats 21 (20-35 ft) plus 6 tent-only, Old Prairie 21 (20-35 ft), Palmetto Ridge 38 (40-45 ft, 10 pull-throughs). Hammock camping is allowed on sites 7, 8, 11, 15, 23, 27, 33 and 48.

name: Dinner Island Ranch WMA - Hammock Camp
note: FWC Wildlife Management Area. Hammock Camp: primitive sites under an oak hammock; no amenities beyond a vault toilet. Gravel access road off CR 833 (short, washboardy, can get muddy after heavy rain). Best dry season Nov-Apr.

sites.note: Hammock Camp: 17 primitive sites, 7 tent-only and 10 for tents, campers or small RVs (one an ADA RV site). One RV and one tent per RV site, two vehicles per site; no generators at sites 1-6. FWC gives no length limit.

booking.note: Every camper needs a free FWC permit/site reservation, made online (WebReserv) or by calling the South Regional Office at 561-625-5122 (Mon-Fri 8-5), up to 14 days ahead; no camping outside the designated camps. 14 consecutive days in a month, then 14 days must pass; a site left empty 48 hours may be cancelled.

name: Dinner Island Ranch WMA - Kowechobe Camp
note: FWC Wildlife Management Area. Kowechobe Camp: open-field sites (40x50 ft each) for tents, campers or RVs; primitive, no amenities. Easy trailer access in dry season (Nov-Apr); may flood and require 4x4 in summer.

booking.note: Free camping permit = site reservation, online (FWC's WebReserv page) or by phone to the South Regional Office, Mon-Fri 8-5 only. Permits up to 14 days ahead; at most 14 consecutive days in a month, then 14 days before a new permit. Display the permit by placing a copy in the brochure box at the Hammock Campground. A site left unoccupied 48 hours may be cancelled. One RV and one tent per RV site.

name: Mack Landing Campground (Apalachicola National Forest)
note: USFS campground about 10 miles NW of Sopchoppy on a ridge above the Ochlockonee River; picnic tables, fire rings and a concrete boat ramp, camp host October-March. Serves as a hunt camp during general gun season (camping still open to non-hunters). --Claude

facilities.note: Drinking water per recreation.gov ('Potable water is available') and the Forest Service amenity list, though the Forest Service page's boilerplate further down says 'Potable water is not available at this site.' Boat ramp, picnic tables, campfire rings; host on site October-March.

booking.note: No advance reservations: a recreation.gov 'Scan & Pay' site (rule 'S&P Only'), paid on arrival with the recreation.gov app using the QR code on the site kiosk; cell service may be missing, so download the app first. The usual 14-day limit is lifted during general gun season, when the campground serves as a hunt camp.

name: Ocean Pond Campground (Osceola National Forest)
note: USFS campground on the north shore of Ocean Pond near Olustee; boat ramp, picnic pavilion and a swim beach that is for campers only.

sites.note: Recreation.gov says 64 campsites (its catalog lists 65 public sites: 23 Electric, 22 Water, 20 Primitive); the Forest Service page says 67 (19 electric/water, 28 water, 20 primitive). Electric and Water sites are paved spurs; the forest gives them a 50-foot capacity, the rec.gov catalog 60 ft; every site is back-in. Primitive sites: tents, pop-ups, truck campers and camper vans only. Two vehicles per site, five people.

booking.note: All sites book on Recreation.gov; 54 of the 65 also carry Scan & Pay, so an unreserved site can be taken on arrival and paid in the Recreation.gov app. No more than 14 days in any 30 anywhere on Osceola National Forest. No minimum stay on the site rules.

name: Bear Island Campground (Big Cypress National Preserve)
note: Big Cypress backcountry-unit campground at the end of ~20 mi of graded crushed-limestone Turner River Rd (passable by a normal vehicle/camper, no 4WD; washboard/dusty when dry). Gravel or grass pads; cash not accepted and little or no cell coverage, so pay online before arriving. ORV trails and hunting nearby (ORV permit required). --Claude

booking.note: All 40 sites reservable on recreation.gov (or 877-444-6777); 'Any sites not reserved in advance are available on a first come first serve basis', but cash is not accepted and cell coverage is limited, so advance reservations are 'highly recommended'. The 180-night limit is the preserve's 180 days in any 12 months.

name: Lake Eaton Campground
note: USFS Ocala NF campground in the Big Scrub on 308-acre Lake Eaton, with a boat ramp, accessible fishing pier and interpretive trail. Access via FR 44 is unimproved/rutted with dips, but firsthand reports note 30+ ft rigs camp here.

sites.note: 14 primitive tent & RV sites (13 reservable on recreation.gov); rec.gov driveway lengths 34-62 ft.

booking.note: Reserve on Recreation.gov or at (877) 444-6777. 14 consecutive days in any 30-day period across all Ocala NF campgrounds. Main entrance gate open 8 a.m. to 8 p.m.; check-in 3 p.m., check-out 11 a.m. Weekends fill. A rented RV may not be delivered; the reservation holder must drive it in.

name: Fisheating Creek Outpost
note: Concessionaire-run (Cape Leisure) campground in Fisheating Creek WMA at Palmdale, run for the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission; drive-in RV and tent sites, canoe/kayak outfitter on Fisheating Creek. Office hours vary with water levels.

booking.note: Online through the operator's Staylist page; a one-night non-refundable deposit by credit card. The camping page states a 2-night minimum on waterfront sites in peak season and 3 nights on holiday and special-event weekends for all sites; the booking engine also refused one-night stays on ordinary weekdays (Tue 2026-11-10, Tue 2027-01-12: 'You must book more than 1 night to continue'). Group sites by phone. Check-in 3 pm, check-out 1 pm.

name: Hart Springs Park & Campground
note: Gilchrist County park at Hart Springs on the Suwannee River; full-hookup sites under oak canopy, a spring-fed swimming area, boardwalk, pool and splash pad. Pets (2 max) are allowed in the RV campground but not in the springs park, pool or buildings; no alcohol anywhere on the grounds. --Claude

sites.note: Sites 1-71 on the park's site map; ReserveAmerica sells 67 of them as Standard Full Hookup, all back-in, 41 taking 50 ft and the rest 28-45 ft. Up to 8 people and two vehicles per site; one RV per site.

facilities.note: RV park bathhouse with hot showers, restrooms and washers/dryers; pool for registered campers. Wi-Fi is limited, 'best suited for checking emails'. No generators; EV charging prohibited.

booking.note: 'All reservations must be made at least one day in advance'; for short notice the park office is (352) 463-3444. Monthly rate needs 30 consecutive nights on one site.

name: Jacksonville Equestrian Center RV Park
note: City of Jacksonville equestrian center at 13611 Normandy Blvd, run since 2014 by the non-profit Northeast Florida Equestrian Society. RV site rental does not include use of the equestrian center, and no horses are allowed in the RV lots; the outside restroom by the main arena is open around the clock; swimming and fishing are prohibited on the property. --Claude

Firsthand report: sites 35-70 ft deep, Site #17 a pull-through double, RVs welcome. No pets in the park or campground (ADA service animals only); outside park hours the common areas and waterfront close and campers must stay in the campground. --Claude

name: Otter Springs Park & Campground
note: Gilchrist County land leased to the nonprofit ForVets, Inc. concessionaire (still local); 636 acres near the Suwannee River with 100+ full-hookup sites (30/50A, max 60 ft), tent sites, 4 cabins. Reopened after a multi-year wastewater closure (operator booking site live as of mid-2026). Reservable via operator site/phone up to 1 yr out; not on rec.gov. RV Life $$, 4 stars. Recommend a phone confirmation that it is currently open. --Claude

name: John Prince Park Campground
note: Palm Beach County Parks & Rec campground on Lake Osborne, inside 726-acre John Prince Park in Lake Worth; boat ramp in the campground, no swimming. Gated (code given at check-in); manager lives on site. --Claude

sites.note: 301 RV sites on 48 acres, 51 of them on Lake Osborne; tent camping too (limited to 3 days in a 60-day period).

booking.note: By phone only, 7 am-9 pm daily (561-582-7992, toll free 877-992-9925); no online booking and no same-day reservations; card payment at booking, no cash. Palm Beach County residents may book the 14-day short-term area 120 days ahead. Camping is limited to 155 days in any 12-month period, and the lakefront sites to 14 days in a 28-day period. Full refund up to a week before arrival; one night's charge after that, two on the day of arrival. Check-in 1 pm, check-out 11 am. Motorhomes must be able to move under their own power, and the RV's RVIA certification number is asked for at check-in.

name: Turtle Beach Campground
note: Sarasota County beachfront campground on Siesta Key (8862 Midnight Pass Rd). Crushed-shell pads, cable TV. Direct Turtle Beach (Gulf) access; kayak launch on Blackburn Bay side. No pets (service animals only), no campfires, up to six guests per site. Free trolley to Siesta Beach, Siesta Village and downtown Sarasota. --Claude

facilities.note: Portable restrooms and shower trailers. Free Wi-Fi and cable TV, 'not guaranteed'. Camp host on site.

booking.note: Booked online through Sarasota County's WebTrac up to one year ahead (a separate link for a start date exactly 365 days out). Holiday and event weekends (Fall Fest, Veterans Day, Thanksgiving, Christmas, New Year) book by phone only. Closed for maintenance Sept 14-17, 2026 and Sept 12-16, 2027. Arriving after 1 p.m. the day after your arrival date without notice is a no-show.

note: Broward County Parks campground in Easterlin Regional Park, a heavily wooded inland park (a Designated Urban Wilderness Area with 250-year-old cypress) in Oakland Park. Paved sites; tight loop turns for big rigs. --Claude

sites.note: 45 full-hookup RV sites and 10 additional sites; Easterlin also accepts tent camping. One camping unit and one vehicle per reservation, plus one more vehicle, motorcycle or trailer per site; up to eight people.

facilities.note: Restroom complexes with hot showers, laundry room, Wi-Fi (ask the park office where), after-hours security, campground host.

note: SFWMD gated campground in the Kissimmee River Public Use Area, on the Istokpoga Canal near Lorida, next to the Hickory Hammock trailhead. ~12 lightly-graveled drive-in sites plus ~6 spots in the treeline; tents or any size RV (Big Rig Friendly). name: Fenske Lake Campground
note: Superior National Forest (Kawishiwi district) campground on 130-acre Fenske Lake, about 10 miles north of Ely on the Echo Trail. Widely spaced sites on one large loop under tall pines; some overlook the lake through the trees. Grassy swimming beach, boat ramp, accessible fishing pier, log picnic shelter and a 1-mile nature trail; the lake is on a canoe circle route near Boundary Waters entry points. The group site sits apart on a rock ledge above the lake. No ATVs. --Claude

name: Chester Woods Park
note: Olmsted County park east of Rochester; the campground sits in woods on a rise above Chester Lake, with a swimming beach, watercraft rental and a dog play area in the park. --Claude

Season-long use prohibited: 10 consecutive days, then 24 hours out of the campground. Refunds only more than seven days out; the booking fee is not refunded.

name: Lake Byllesby Regional Park Campground
note: Dakota County regional park campground on Lake Byllesby Reservoir in the Cannon River Valley, near the Cannon Valley Trail; swimming beach, boat launches and a paved lakeside trail. The west sites (1-17) back onto open grass and the paved lakeside trail, about 30 m from the water; the central row (18-46) has the campground road on its lake side. Use Harry Avenue: Gerlach Way (from 295th Street) is not a through road and has no clearance for RVs and trailers. --Claude

sites.note: 83 sites: west 1-17 and central 18-46 water/electric, east 47-83 electric only. Every site has a 60-ft paved parking pad; the RV plus any towed vehicle must fit on the pad. Sites 1-8 and 18-46 take no tents. Pull-through sites are one-way.

season.note: Approximate: Open May to October.

booking.note: Reserve online (Dakota County WebTrac); 2027 reservations open Thursday, March 11 at 9 a.m. All campers need a reservation and check in at the campground office on arrival. Three-night minimum on Memorial Day and Labor Day weekends; 14 nights at most in any 30 days. Check-in after 2 p.m., check-out noon.

name: Rothenburg Campground
note: City of Springfield campground in a wooded bend of the Big Cottonwood River beside Riverside Park, two blocks from downtown; the park's pool, playgrounds, courts and canoe landing are next door, and paved trails run to the golf club. Some sewer sites need an extended hose. One vehicle per site; no parking on the grass. --Claude

name: Lewis and Clark Recreation Area
note: GFP recreation area on the north shore of Lewis and Clark Lake just above Gavins Point Dam, 5 miles west of Yankton. Three campgrounds strung about 4 km along the shore (Gavins Point, Midway, Yankton), mostly in shade trees; a paved shore trail and riprap separate even the front-row sites from the water. Gavins Point Horse Camp (8 sites with corrals) is its own loop at the west end. The marina, motel and restaurant are run by a private resort. --Claude

name: Custer State Park - Center Lake Campground
note: Custer State Park campground on Playhouse Road off SD-87, in ponderosa pine above Center Lake (swim beach and boat dock). GFP describes it as for smaller RVs and tents: 26 of its 51 RV sites are listed at 20 ft, so a 23-ft rig needs one of the 22 sites listed at 25-50 ft. Dump station elsewhere in the park. --Claude

booking.note: Custer State Park takes reservations ONE YEAR ahead, not the 90 days the rest of South Dakota gets, and check-in and check-out are noon rather than 4 p.m. SAME-DAY ONLY: Center Lake is one of the two campgrounds in the state on the same-day system - sites open at 7 a.m. CT / 6 a.m. MT on the day of arrival, not a year ahead like the rest of Custer, and the unit must be on the site by 10 p.m. or the rest of the reservation is forfeited.

name: Sheridan Lake South Shore Campground (Black Hills National Forest)
note: Black Hills NF campground on the forested south shore of Sheridan Lake, off US-385 via Calumet Road about 5 mi NE of Hill City, run by a concessionaire in summer. Five loops in ponderosa pine; the Wood/Woodsy loop on the peninsula has sites looking through scattered pines to the lake. Boat ramp and the Flume Trail trailhead in the campground; swim beaches and a marina nearby. Generators 6 a.m.-10 p.m. --Claude

The 33-acre lake allows only paddle craft and electric motors; a boat ramp, swim beach, picnic shelters, archery range and playground are in the recreation area. Drinking water in season only. --Claude

name: Roubaix Lake Campground
note: Black Hills NF campground in ponderosa pine beside small Roubaix Lake, about 13 mi S of Deadwood off US-385 (FR-255), run by a concessionaire in summer. Four loops; the sites at the meadow edge east of Loop D (50-53 on the FS map) look across the meadow to the lake. Swim beach, fishing and non-motorized boating at the adjoining day-use area, free to campers; a 1-mile multi-use trail open to off-road vehicles links to the forest trail network. Generators 6 a.m.-10 p.m. --Claude

Run by the South Dakota State Fair, not GFP, so none of the state-park policy applies - no park entrance licence, no 90-day window, no 4 p.m. check-in, and the $16/$23 GFP rates are not these rates, which is why this entry declines the registry. During the fair the only nightly camping is Lot J, self-contained, no hookups, about 40 sites: 'Sites are first come-first serve... No reservations are taken for nightly camping.' You pay at the Gate 13 gate house on arrival. The hookup sites are sold as a fair-week package only (6 nights plus 4 gate passes), booked by phone with the Fair Administration Office, and renewals from previous years are offered before new reservations open on June 1. Outside the fair and Wheel Jam (Coyote Corner only) no reservations are taken: pay at the campground kiosks or the fair office (Mon-Fri 8-5); phone payment no more than a week before arrival.

Three RV loops among pine shelterbelts on a bench above the shore; swim area and day-use beach on the east shore by the cabins. Marina (when the lake is above 1830 ft), four-lane boat ramp, fish-cleaning station, and canoe, kayak, paddleboard, fat-tire bike and snowshoe rentals. --Claude

name: Rough Rider State Park
note: Renamed from Sully Creek State Park; on the Little Missouri River about 2 mi south of Medora, with a Maah Daah Hey Trail trailhead and canoe/kayak access at the park. One of the state's designated horse parks: the equestrian sites and corrals fill the north end of Wrangler Loop, apart from the no-horse Rancher and Rustler loops. --Claude

sites.note: Rancher Loop (no horses): 19 modern and 4 two-unit modern group sites. Wrangler Loop: modern sites 28-34 at its south end and 20 equestrian sites (35-54, corrals) at its north end. Rustler Loop (no horses): 14 primitive gravel sites, 3 of them marked tent sites on the park map. Modern pads post 31-168 ft; every primitive pad posts 24 ft (one 40), a uniform value that may be a placeholder.

The modern sites sit in two shaded loops on the slope above the river; the primitive sites are walk-in tent sites in the river bottom. Camping cabins, full-service cabins open all year, and groomed cross-country ski trails in winter. --Claude

name: Lake Sakakawea State Park
note: On a prairie point on the south shore of Lake Sakakawea, beside Garrison Dam near Pick City. Three modern loops among shelterbelts, the open grass Far Loop on the southeast point, and Fishing Point's grass sites on the west bluff edge. Full-service marina with a store and gas dock, two boat ramps, fish-cleaning station, swim beach and pontoon rentals; the North Country Trail's western end starts in the park. Only Fishing Point sites 241, 242 and 244 are on the water (20-40 m over open grass); the other loops sit back from the shore. --Claude

Swim beach, boat ramp and paddle-craft rentals; the Pioneer Heritage Center and the Gunlogson Nature Preserve trails are in the park. Three camping cabins. --Claude

name: Beaver Creek Recreation Area
note: Corps of Engineers campground on the north side of Beaver Bay, Lake Oahe, 16 mi W of Linton off ND 1804. Three-lane boat ramp and docks, a second ramp on the bay's SE side, fish cleaning station, playgrounds and a nature trail. --Claude

note: Corps of Engineers campground on the west shore of Lake Audubon, the only campground on the lake, beside the Audubon Wildlife Management Area. The outer row of the electric loop (016-030) sits on open grass just above the rocky shore; the inner sites look over them to the lake. Boat ramp, fish cleaning station and shoreline access area. --Claude

booking.note: All 40 sites are reservable, up to the day of arrival; no cash or checks on site. 14 nights in any 30. Weekend and holiday minimums are recreation.gov booking rules and may be relaxed for same-day bookings.

name: Summit Campground
note: USFS campground in the Little Missouri National Grassland (Dakota Prairie Grasslands), ~19 mi S of Watford City off US-85 via gravel Summit Rd (McKenzie Ranger District). Three pull-off sites along the gravel road with picnic tables and fire rings, and trailhead parking; the two entrances carry only a small National Grasslands picnic-area sign. Pack in, pack out. The Summit Trail is closed past its first ridge (erosion, 2026); the short open stretch has wide Badlands views. --Claude

name: Hankinson Hills Campground
note: USFS campground in the Hankinson Hills area of the Sheyenne National Grassland: oak woods and grassed sand dunes. Two loops, one for campers with horses; large picnic shelter. Pack in, pack out. Connects to the 8-mile non-motorized Hankinson Hills Trail. --Claude

sites.note: Non-equestrian loop: sites 1-9 (gravel; 4 and 5 are 60-ft RV pull-throughs, 6 and 7 are 30 ft, the rest 40-60 ft). Equestrian loop: sites 10-15 (30-60 ft, three pull-throughs); campers without horses may use it when 1-9 are full.

booking.note: No reservations; pay on site. The site must be occupied the first night and not left unattended over 24 hours; 28 nights a year.

name: Bennett Campground
note: USFS campground on the Little Missouri National Grassland (Dakota Prairie Grasslands, McKenzie Ranger District), ~27 mi S of Watford City: 19 mi S on US-85, 4 mi W on 6th St NW, then 1 mi S on gravel. name: Jamestown Campground
note: Private RV park on 25 wooded acres at the southeast edge of Jamestown, a mile down a gravel frontage road west of I-94 exit 256 (some GPS units misroute; the operator's directions follow the south frontage road). Mature trees shade most sites; interstate noise reaches the park. Dog park, walking path and canopy walk. --Claude

sites.note: 41 RV sites, every one a pull-through (posted 55-86 ft on the home page, 60-85 ft on the sites page), and 6 primitive tent sites in a wooded area; two rustic cabins as well.

season.note: Also open in April and October as the weather allows (call for those dates); water to the sites from May 1.

booking.note: 2027 online reservations open January 1, by phone March 1; April and October stays by phone.

name: North Park Campground
note: Year-round private RV park on the north edge of Dickinson (2320 Buckskin Dr; the operator gives 547 Chestnut Lane as the GPS address). Gravel pull-through and back-in sites in long rows beside farmland, away from train and highway noise. Tent sites for overnight travelers and touring cyclists. --Claude

name: Lake Tschida - Rimrock Campground (Grant County)
note: Main developed campground on Lake Tschida (Heart Butte Reservoir), a Bureau of Reclamation lake run under a co-op with the Tri-Cities JJDA; the office and welcome center are on ND 49 by the dam. Five loops sit above the swim beach, fishing pier and boat ramp. The lake's other camping areas (Crappie Creek, Downstream, Koehlers Point, Schatz's Point, Sled Creek, and Southside with Hawabesi and Gilligan's Hilltop) have their own entries. --Claude

booking.note: Online booking closes 7 days out; inside a week, book by phone with the office. Friday or Saturday arrivals must take two nights between Memorial Day and Labor Day weekends. Loops D and E are booked online only as whole 8-site group loops. Unreserved sites are first come, first served with envelopes at the self-registration kiosks (cash or check).

No-wake reservoir with a boat ramp at the south park, canoe/kayak launches and a fishing pier. --Claude

name: Clausen Springs Recreation Area
note: Barnes County Park Board campground in the 545-acre Clausen Springs Wildlife Management Area, 4.5 mi west and 1.5 mi south of Kathryn off ND-1, around Clausen Springs Lake. The electric sites sit in wooded loops along the spring creek near the camp host; the more secluded non-electric sites, marked for small campers and tents, are scattered across the grassland. Swim area (no lifeguard), fishing dock with kayak launch, boat ramp, playground and a 2-mile lake loop; the North Country Trail follows the park's north edge. Game and Fish rules apply: no ATVs, snowmobiles or metal detecting, no fireworks, and the WMA is open to hunting in season. --Claude

booking.note: Every site must be reserved online through RoverPass and paid in full; reservations are not moved to other dates. The 2026 system opened April 15. Check-out 1 PM.

name: Dead Colt Creek Recreation Area
note: Ransom County recreation area about 5 miles SE of Lisbon on the Dead Colt Creek reservoir, run by the county water resource district. Two RV loops on the north shore: the West campground by the office and swim beach, and the East campground by the ballfields and boat ramp. Swim beach, fishing, playground, ballfields. No ATVs or dirt bikes in the park; UTVs and golf carts on roads only, licensed drivers. --Claude

booking.note: Reservations with prepayment are required; a camper arriving without one checks availability with staff or on RoverPass first. The 14-night limit is on the short-term-only sites (1, 9-14, 30-35, 45-48), the south-side camping and the tent sites; the other RV sites also take long-term campers under an agreement. Check-in 1 PM, check-out noon; more than 24 hours' notice to cancel.

name: Lewis & Clark Caverns State Park

facilities.note: Dump station and water faucets during peak season, weather permitting; 23 vault toilets; fish cleaning station. The marina store at Campers Point sells firewood, ice, groceries, bait, gasoline and boat rentals.

booking.note: Reservations only for peak season (third Friday of May to third Sunday of September), up to 3 months ahead and at least 1 day before arrival; 69 non-electric sites are always first-come, and every site is first-come off season.

name: White Sandy Campground
note: BLM campground on the west shore of Hauser Lake at the mouth of Prickly Pear Creek, ~15 mi NE of Helena via the Lincoln Rd exit off I-15. Open shrub-steppe with little shade; every site has a lake and mountain view. Concrete boat launch with courtesy dock, beach, fish cleaning station; small general store across from the entrance. Dump station at Black Sandy SP 1/4 mi up the road. --Claude

Reserved sites must be occupied every night; no changing sites or loops.

name: Holter Lake Campground (Holter Lake Recreation Site)
note: BLM Butte Field Office campground on Holter Lake (Missouri River) near Wolf Creek, every site with a view of the lake and the Sleeping Giant; swimming beach, boat ramp and docks. Part of the Holter Lake/Log Gulch/Departure Point complex. --Claude

Stay limit 7 consecutive days and 14 days in 28; up to 2 sites held at once. Check-in 2 p.m., check-out 11 a.m.

name: Fish Creek State Park
note: Fish Creek State Park (largest state park in western MT), up Fish Creek Rd off I-90 Exit 66 near Alberton. Developed camping is at the Big Pine FWP fishing-access site within the park (site of the area's largest known ponderosa pine), with fire rings and tables (state conservation stamp required); additional drive-in dispersed sites along Fish Creek Rd, a few fitting larger rigs. Big rigs should follow the signed route, not GPS over the mountain. --Claude

name: Painted Rocks State Park
note: Montana State Park on Painted Rocks Reservoir (West Fork Bitterroot River), Bitterroot Mountains SW of Darby, in a remote pine-forest setting. The reservoir is drawn down: FWP, as of October 1, 2026, 'Due to dropping levels in Painted Rocks Reservoir, access to the water from Painted Rocks State Park is unavailable.' --Claude

note: BLM (Butte Field Office) campground on the Big Hole River, 7 mi west of Wise River on MT Hwy 43 (BLM: from I-15 exit 102, 19.4 mi on MT-43, then left on Bryant Creek Rd). name: Canoe Launch Campground (Chouteau County Fairgrounds)
note: Chouteau County Fair-operated campground in Fort Benton beside the Missouri River canoe launch (river mile 0 of the Upper Missouri Breaks); a separate site from the fair's ChoCoFair Campground at the fairgrounds. Free day-use parking by the launch ramp for boaters and floaters; the launch is a popular summer tubing spot. --Claude

name: Shambo (Beaver Creek Park)
note: Hill County's Beaver Creek Park in the Bears Paw Mountains south of Havre: the first-come sites in the trees along Beaver Creek east of MT-234, from Shambo Loop south past Taylor Road to Pine Coulee, about 1.5 km south of the park office at Camp Kiwanis. The park map names Shambo, Doney and Hagener here; Dean Hanson, Rotary (on Rotary Pond), J.C. Park and H.F.D. among them are reservable group sites. Cattle graze the park after Labor Day. --Claude

facilities.note: No dump or water in this part of the park: the park's RV dump is about 3 km north near mile marker 18 and the potable water fill stations are in front of the park office at Camp Kiwanis, about 1.5 km north. Picnic table, fire pit or ring and trash cans at sites; an outhouse within walking distance of most.

booking.note: The 100+ individual sites are not reservable: 'self-filled on a first come-first served basis' with a valid park permit. Only the large group campgrounds (pink with an asterisk on the park map) can be reserved, by the whole weekend, online or through the park office. Campers may stay 14 days on a site in any 30-day period.
