name: Parkside Campground
note: USFS Custer Gallatin National Forest (Beartooth Ranger District) campground on the banks of the Main Fork of Rock Creek, ~12 mi south of Red Lodge at the base of the Beartooth Highway (US-212) switchbacks, 0.4 mi up Main Fork Rock Creek Rd (FR 2421). season.note: Forest Service: 'Open year-round. Fees charged Memorial Day - Labor Day.' A reserved site is held 24 hours past check-in. 16-day maximum in all Beartooth Ranger District campgrounds.

name: St. Mary Campground
note: Glacier NP's largest east-side campground, half a mile inside the St. Mary entrance near the foot of St. Mary Lake and the east end of Going-to-the-Sun Road; sparse shade among aspens, mountain views. Generators only in Loops B and C. Vehicles over 21 ft long or 8 ft wide are barred from Going-to-the-Sun Road between Rising Sun and Avalanche, so a 23-ft rig cannot cross Logan Pass. --Claude

Reservations required for every site April 18 - October 31, 2026, on recreation.gov up to 6 months ahead; from August 17 to September 11 the campground switches to a day-of window (book on the day of arrival only). No reservations in winter (first-come, free). 14-night maximum; up to 8 people, 2 vehicles and 2 tents per site.

name: Pine Creek Campground
note: Custer Gallatin NF (Yellowstone RD) campground in Paradise Valley ~13 mi S of Livingston, under mature Douglas fir and spruce at the foot of the Absarokas, beside the Pine Creek trailhead (Pine Creek Falls 1 mi, Pine Creek Lake 5 mi). Few pull-throughs and hairpin curves on the access road; reviewers advise nothing much over ~28 ft. No horses in the campground. --Claude

facilities.note: Trash collection and recycling; accessible fishing dock and a half-mile accessible Creekside Trail in the campground. On-site host.

booking.note: Every unit is reservable on recreation.gov (the Forest Service page links 'Make Reservations Here'); reservations close 3 days before arrival and reserved sites are held until check-out time the day after arrival. Concessionaire-run (ExplorUS).

name: West End Tent and Trailer Campground
note: USACE Fort Peck Project campground on a hill on the north shore of Fort Peck Lake, near the town of Fort Peck; most sites have at least a partial lake view. Quieter than the main (Downstream) campground, with two boat ramps within 2 mi. --Claude

booking.note: Same-day only: 'Reservations are only allowed on the day of arrival' - the former first-come campground now has you claim a site online on arrival day, for up to 14 nights. Not staffed by gate attendants; check in with the camp host or by text. Sites must be occupied the day of arrival and every night. 14 nights in any rolling 30 days.

name: Woodbine Campground
note: Custer Gallatin NF (Beartooth RD), on the banks of the Stillwater River at the end of Stillwater River Road #2400, adjacent to the Absaroka-Beartooth Wilderness; 7 mi south of Nye, 57 mi west of Red Lodge. Wooded and shady. The 1.5-mile round-trip Woodbine Falls Trail starts in the campground; the Stillwater Trail (#24) reaches Sioux Charley Lake in 3 miles. Very popular on summer weekends and holidays. --Claude

sites.note: Fully paved with paved spurs. recreation.gov lists 43 sites (two group sites, #1 and #44); most single sites take 24-56 ft, and pull-through site 036 is listed at 90 ft, matching the Forest Service's 'Max Trailer Length: 90ft'.

facilities.note: Accessible vault toilets and drinking water; bear-resistant dumpster and some bear-resistant food lockers. Camp host on site sells firewood.

booking.note: 8 sites are first-come, first-served (booked in person on site only; don't call); the rest are by reservation only on recreation.gov, up to 6 months ahead. The Forest Service says reservations close 24 hours before the stay; recreation.gov's rule is a 2-day cutoff. Outside the reserved season (in 2026, May 1-21 and September 11-30) recreation.gov's rate table lists first-come, first-served seasons. Late arrivals are held 24 hours. Concessionaire-run (recreation.gov contact camping@rrmofa.com).

name: Crystal Lake Campground
note: Helena-Lewis and Clark NF (Snowy Mountain Range) campground at 5,700 ft below Mt. Harlow in the Big Snowy Mountains, reached by ~22 mi of Crystal Lake Road from US-87 west of Lewistown; the road narrows to single lane in places and only the last 5.7 mi are paved. Hazard-tree removal left open mountain views. Trails to the Crystal Lake Loop and the ice caves; the lake is stocked with rainbow trout, good for canoeing, and may dry up by late July in drought years. --Claude

name: Lake Alva Campground
note: Lolo National Forest on the north shore of Lake Alva, ~11 mi north of Seeley Lake off MT-83 (larger main campground, distinct from the small Lakeside CG at the north end). Swimming beach, boat ramp and day-use area; no-wake lake with nesting loons. --Claude

sites.note: 39 individual RV/tent sites: 19 in Loop 1 (reservable in summer; catalog vehicle lengths 46-64 ft) and 20 first-come sites in Loop 2 (no catalog lengths), plus group sites #42 and #43. Each has a paved parking stall; vehicles that don't fit the spur pay $5 and park in the day-use area.

facilities.note: Drinking water from a hand pump, peak season only (rec.gov amenity 'Drinking Water (peak season)'). Campground hosts on site; swimming beach, concrete boat ramp and day-use area.

booking.note: Loop 1's 19 sites are reservable on recreation.gov from the Friday before Memorial Day to the Tuesday after Labor Day and first-come outside those dates; Loop 2's 20 sites are always first-come, paid on site by QR code in the Recreation.gov app. 16 consecutive nights, 32 nights a year. Check-in 3 p.m., check-out 1 p.m. Run by the Forest Service (Seeley Lake Ranger District).

name: Lid Creek Campground

name: Peter's Creek Campground
note: USFS (Flathead NF, Spotted Bear RD) campground beside Hungry Horse Reservoir, 42 mi south of Hungry Horse on the gravel East Side Reservoir Road #38 (pavement ends 2 mi past Martin City). Sites are set back from the road in second-growth trees, less than 100 ft from the reservoir; a low-use site that usually has open campsites. Remote: no cell service; nearest phone 13 mi south at Spotted Bear Ranger Station; gas and food back in Hungry Horse. The Forest Service maintains it May 15 - September 30, and it is used for the late-season hunt in October and November; Road #38 between mileposts 37 and 53 has a winter wildlife closure Dec 1 - May 14. --Claude

facilities.note: Accessible vault toilet; tables and metal fire rings at every site. No potable water (reservoir water must be treated). No garbage service: pack it in, pack it out. Stock not allowed.

name: Trout Creek Campground
note: Lolo NF (Superior Ranger District) campground beside Trout Creek, about 7 mi east of Superior: I-90 exit 47, then Diamond Road about 5 mi (paved) and Trout Creek Road #250 for 2 mi (improved gravel). Forested, cool and shady, with graveled roads and spacious, well-screened sites, several creekside. Gas and groceries within 7 miles. --Claude

name: Monture Creek Campground

From Clearwater Junction, 12.5 mi east on Hwy 200, then 7.5 mi north on good gravel Monture Rd #89; 8 mi to groceries and gas. RV space is limited: Hipcamp says only one site suits an RV; the Forest Service gives no length or site count. --Claude

name: North Dickey Lake Campground
note: USFS campground on a hillside next to 800-acre Dickey Lake (Kootenai NF, Rexford/Fortine RD), just off US-93 a little over a mile south of Fortine, in larch and fir. Boating, fishing (kokanee, kamloops, rainbow trout), swimming and water skiing; the grassy swimming beach is at South Dickey Day Use Area across the lake. The accessible half-mile Dickey Lake Overlook Trail and a trail to Mt. Marston start nearby. Nearest dump station: just north of Eureka on US-93, behind a gas station. --Claude

sites.note: 23 tent/RV sites plus a camp-host site (recreation.gov lists 24). Per-site max vehicle lengths on recreation.gov: 40 ft at 20 sites, 50 ft at 2, 30 ft at 2. Gravel parking surfaces.

name: Sage Creek Campground
note: Custer Gallatin NF (Beartooth RD), the only campground in the Pryor Mountains, along Sage Creek. Access: the direct route from Bridger (Pryor Mountain Rd, then FR 2500 Powerline Rd, rocky single track) 'is not advised for campers or horse trailers' and the Forest Service recommends high clearance for it; for campers and trailers it recommends coming from the south via Warren, Quarry/Helt/Gyp Springs Rds, Crooked Creek Rd and FR 2308 (~2.5 hrs from Bridger). Pryor Mountain roads become impassable when wet. --Claude

name: Spire Rock Campground
note: Along Storm Castle Creek (a Gallatin River tributary), Custer Gallatin NF (Bozeman RD), 23 mi south of Bozeman on US-191 then 2-3 mi east on gravel Storm Castle Creek Rd; most sites along the creek under spruce and fir. Storm Castle and Garnet Mountain Lookout trails nearby. Bears (grizzly and black) in the canyon. --Claude

sites.note: The Forest Service page says 17 campsites; the recreation.gov catalog lists 20 (18 reservable single sites, a host site, an unreservable site and group site 12). No per-site lengths published; average RV parking spur 25 x 50 ft.

facilities.note: No drinking water: bring your own. Trash pickup, recycling, food storage lockers, host; firewood sold on site. Gravel roads and parking spurs.

booking.note: Reserve on recreation.gov; reserved sites are held until check-out time on the day after the scheduled arrival. Run by the concessionaire Rocky Mountain Recreation Company (ExplorUS).

name: Steel Creek Campground
note: In lodgepole pine and Douglas fir with Steel Creek flowing through, ~9 mi up Steel Creek Road north of Wisdom in the Big Hole, Beaverhead-Deerlodge NF (Wisdom RD), a gateway toward the Anaconda-Pintler Wilderness; fishing access. A 22-ft trailer limit fits a 23-ft motorhome; larger rigs tight. --Claude

facilities.note: ADA-accessible vault toilets; no garbage service (pack it out). Horses/pack animals allowed.

season.note: Forest Service Seasons of Use: 'June through September'.

note: The only campground in the Highwood Mountains, Helena-Lewis & Clark NF, east of Great Falls: US-89 6 mi, MT-228 13 mi, County Road 121 16 mi, then FR 8840 2 mi, the last on dirt and gravel. Windy Mountain 6-mi loop trail nearby; Highwoods trails close Sept 1 or Oct 15. --Claude

facilities.note: Drinking water: Current Conditions (May 2026) says 'no water.'; the amenity list says potable water is available, and the forest's standard text says 'during the warmer months'. Horses not allowed; OHVs must stay on the campground road.

sites.note: 16 single sites plus 2 group sites. Average trailer/RV parking spur 12 x 40 ft; the campground road is not suitable for vehicles longer than 40 ft.

facilities.note: No trash pickup and no firewood. Accessible toilets, tables and parking.

name: Avalanche Campground
note: Glacier NP campground on Going-to-the-Sun Road in the Avalanche Creek/McDonald Creek forest. Vehicles over 21 ft long or 8 ft wide (mirrors included) are prohibited on the road between Sun Point and Avalanche, so approach from West Glacier. --Claude

sites.note: Only 50 of the 87 sites take an RV or truck-and-trailer up to 26 ft; 4 are walk-to.

facilities.note: Flush toilets and potable water are seasonal. Bear-proof food lockers; no cell service. Generators only 8-10 a.m., noon-2 p.m. and 5-7 p.m.

booking.note: Reservation only, all 87 sites ('Advanced reservations are required for all sites'). Most sites open 6 months ahead on a rolling basis; 'a certain number of sites will be reservable up to 4 days before the desired date.' Up to 8 people, 2 vehicles and 2 tents per site.

name: Barry's Landing Campground
note: NPS campground in Bighorn Canyon National Recreation Area (MT side, ~27 mi north of Lovell WY via Hwy 37 and the signed Barry's Landing turn), on a point of Bighorn Lake at the Barry's Landing boat ramp. --Claude

name: Basin Campground
note: Custer Gallatin NF (Beartooth RD) campground on the banks of the West Fork of Rock Creek, ~7 mi W of Red Lodge on paved Forest Road 2071 (distinct from adjacent Cascade CG). Burned in the 2008 Cascade Fire, so the setting is open and full of wildflowers; Basin Lakes trailhead across the road, Wild Bill Lake nearby. --Claude

sites.note: Forest Service: 30 sites, max trailer length 40 ft. recreation.gov lists 29 units with max vehicle lengths of 24-45 ft (most 27-36). Back-in spurs are medium length; 3 accessible sites.

facilities.note: Drinking water from hand pumps. Bear-resistant dumpster and food-storage lockers; on-site host sells firewood.

booking.note: 25 of 29 recreation.gov units reservable; the rest are first-come and must be booked in person on site. Reservations close 2 days before arrival; a late arrival is not a no-show until 24 hours after check-in time. 16-day maximum stay in all Beartooth Ranger District campgrounds. Concessionaire-run (Recreation Resource Management of America).

name: Hilltop Campground
note: Beaverhead-Deerlodge NF (Madison RD), atop a hill in old-growth Douglas fir midway between Cliff and Wade Lakes, ~37 mi south of Ennis (US 287, then FR 241 west 5 mi). Quiet, shaded sites away from the lakeshore crowds; fishing, swimming and small-boat boating at Cliff Lake (~1.25 mi) and Wade Lake (~1.75 mi, trail from camp). Reached by a steep, winding 3/4-mi drive; tight for anything near the 22-ft trailer limit. --Claude

sites.note: 22 ft is the recommended maximum trailer length; the campground is reached by a steep, winding 3/4-mile drive from Cliff Lake Road.

facilities.note: Drinking water from three hydrants (recreation.gov: peak season). Garbage service May 15 - September 15. The Forest Service says bear-resistant food storage boxes are not available (recreation.gov lists a food storage locker). No cell service.

booking.note: First-come, first-served; pay at the self-pay station or with recreation.gov Scan & Pay (the forest page's 'Make Reservations Here' link leads to this Scan & Pay listing, which has no reservable sites). The Forest Service gives a 16-day stay limit; recreation.gov's Scan & Pay rule caps one purchase at 7 consecutive nights. Sites must be attended the first night and not left unattended more than 24 hours.

name: Logging Creek Campground (Little Belts)

No cell service; access road narrow/potholed in spots. Distinct from Glacier NP's Logging Creek. --Claude

name: Limber Pine Campground
note: Custer Gallatin NF (Beartooth Ranger District), ~11 mi S of Red Lodge on US-212 then 0.9 mi W on Main Fork Rd (FR 2421), near the base of the Beartooth Highway switchbacks. On the banks of the Main Fork of Rock Creek in aspen and pine; Greenough Lake 0.5 mi away. Grizzly country: food storage rules apply. --Claude

booking.note: Run by concessionaire Recreation Resource Management of America (RRMA). Most sites book on recreation.gov; 2 sites (1 standard, 1 tent) are not reservable, and recreation.gov sells a first-come walk-in season after the reservable one. 'FIRST COME FIRST SERVE sites must be booked in person.' Extra vehicles are paid to the host on arrival.

name: Sinks Canyon State Park (Popo Agie Campground)
note: Popo Agie is the larger of Sinks Canyon State Park's two campgrounds, on the Middle Fork Popo Agie River SW of Lander. Pads 03-05 in the cul-de-sac at the west end sit closest to the river. The park calls room for large trailers very limited. A separate USFS Sinks Canyon campground lies farther up-canyon. --Claude

name: Seminoe State Park (North Red Hills Campground)
note: North Red Hills is the campground on a peninsula on the northwest side of Seminoe Reservoir, about 34 mi north of Sinclair via County Road 351, among red rock bluffs with no shade. The pads on the north side of the loop sit on open ground a short walk above the high-water line. Boat ramp at the campground. South Red Hills and Sunshine Beach are the park's other campgrounds. --Claude

sites.note: Plus one group site (NR18, 50-amp). Every unit lists the same 40-ft parking size.

name: Medicine Lodge State Archaeological Site
note: Wyoming State Parks archaeological site NE of Hyattville in the Medicine Lodge Creek canyon, with petroglyph cliffs and an interpretive cabin. Its three small campgrounds are strung about 800 m along the park road among cottonwoods; a creek beach is used for fishing and wading. --Claude

booking.note: The booking site sells nights only in the summer season (in season mid-May, out of season mid-April and mid-October 2027); the rest of the year the campground is first-come.

name: Soda Lake (WHMA) Campground
note: Wyoming Game & Fish wildlife habitat management area (an elk feedground) about 5 mi N of Pinedale on Willow Lake Rd (CR 119). Camping at the marked campground areas around the lake; motor vehicles only on roads marked with white arrows; no fireworks, no firewood cutting, certified weed-free hay required. --Claude

note: Primitive campground on Bureau of Reclamation land at the foot of Gray Reef Dam on the North Platte, run by Natrona County, about 27 miles southwest of Casper via WY-220 and County Road 412. name: Five Springs Falls Campground
note: BLM Cody Field Office campground on Five Springs Creek in the Bighorn foothills, reached by a steep, narrow 2-mile access road off US-14A, 22 miles east of Lovell. RVs belong in the upper loop: the lower loop by the creek is for tents and picnicking. A short trail leads from the lower parking area to a Five Springs Falls overlook; the upper loop has trails into the Bighorn National Forest and wide views over the Bighorn Basin. --Claude

Roads narrow in spots; larger interior sites fit big rigs while shoreline sites suit smaller trailers/vans. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Townsite Campground
note: At the south end of Waterton townsite beside Upper Waterton Lake, a large, mostly open campground. The 110 full-hookup sites (loops A and B) are drive-through; the 75 electric-only sites (C, D, G; 15/30 amp) are back-in, and loops D and G face the lake across Waterton Avenue. Loops E and H are tents only. No fire pits at the sites: wood fires only in the shared kitchen shelters. The full-hookup B loop closes in late September. Outside the operating season, electric and unserviced sites stay open first-come by self-registration with no washrooms, but the campground is not cleared of snow. --Claude

booking.note: Booked through the Parks Canada Reservation Service (online or 1-877-737-3783); every site is reservable. First-come at the kiosk May 1-8 (no washrooms or showers) and September 22 to October 12 (some washrooms and serviced sites). Check-in after 2 pm, check-out before 11 am. One wheeled camping unit per site, six people. Generators 7-9 am, 11 am-1 pm and 5-7 pm.

note: South of Lake Louise village on the east bank of the Bow River, alongside the Canadian Pacific rail line. Hard-sided units only: anything with soft sides or pop-outs must use the separate soft-sided section across the river, which is the part inside the electric fence. Sites are shared double-length pads; some have no firepit. --Claude

name: Silverhorn Creek Campground
note: Parks Canada campground on the Icefields Parkway (Hwy 93N), 56 km north of the Highway 1/93N junction in Banff National Park, set around small ponds by Silverhorn Creek. Solar-treated drinking water and greywater sinks, but no RV fill: fill at Waterfowl Lakes Campground, 6 km north, in season. Nearest sani-dump at Waterfowl Lakes or Lake Louise. No cell coverage. --Claude

name: Bow Valley Provincial Park — Bow Valley Campground
note: Large Alberta Parks campground in spruce forest along the Bow River, off Hwy 1X about 30 km east of Canmore, run by Cedar & Spruce Campgrounds. Loops C and E line the river; loop A is unserviced. Some power posts share a breaker with the neighbouring site. Water (taps, showers, flush toilets) runs mid-May to season's end; showers for a fee. The dump station is at the adjacent Willow Rock campground. Amphitheatre with interpretive programs, playground. --Claude

name: Peter Lougheed Provincial Park - Interlakes Campground
note: Well-treed sites in a long string along the east shore of Lower Kananaskis Lake in Peter Lougheed Provincial Park; the sites on the lake side of the road sit at the top of the beach. note: Large prairie campground shaded by cottonwoods on the north side of Travers Reservoir, south of Vulcan off Hwy 529: Loops B and C fan across the hillside, Loop A runs down toward the boat basin. name: Etherington Creek Provincial Recreation Area
note: Alberta Parks campground in the Highwood Valley, 45 km southwest of Longview on Hwy 541 and 7 km south on the Forestry Trunk Road (Hwy 940), run by Kananaskis Campground Services. name: Little Bow Reservoir Provincial Recreation Area
note: Alberta Parks prairie campground on Little Bow Reservoir, south and east of Vulcan via Hwys 23, 529 and 845, run by MIM Management Group: two open loops whose outer rows back onto the reservoir (Loop N sites 4-14 and Loop S sites 4-17 are tagged Near Water), shade from scattered trees, a boat launch and a day-use area. name: Lynx Creek Campground (Castle Provincial Park)

name: Payne Lake Provincial Recreation Area
note: On the southeast shore of Payne Lake, 25 km west of Cardston on Hwy 5 (18 km east of Waterton Lakes National Park). Some sites are right on the water with views to the mountains, others in mixed forest a short walk back. Two camping loops, A and B, about 450 m apart: an open loop on the shore by the dam (the pin) and a larger wooded area by the boat launch. Boat launch and pier; no towing on the lake. Firewood is sold in summer. --Claude

name: Lake McGregor Provincial Recreation Area
note: Prairie recreation-area campground on the west side of the Lake McGregor reservoir, just west of the Village of Milo: about 100 sites scattered along two lanes running 1 km down the shore, many with lake views. name: Dinosaur Provincial Park Campground
note: Alberta Parks campground in two loops (N and S) in the Red Deer River badlands valley, 48 km northeast of Brooks, shaded by cottonwoods; many sites back onto a creek. Lower rates in the off-season. Seven furnished comfort-camping wall tents (May-September). The service centre has the campground booth, store, food service, showers and laundry; the visitor centre, guided tours and fossil displays are nearby. Water, showers and laundry shut off from about October until early May; the sani-dump stays open but without rinse water. --Claude

booking.note: Reservable year-round (bookings ran to Dec 31, 2026 when read); seven Loop N/S sites are first-come. Site numbers changed for 2025/2026 - check the shop map before booking.

name: Crimson Lake Provincial Park — Crimson Lake Campground
note: Alberta Parks campground in six loops (A-F), 14 km west of Rocky Mountain House, a short walk from Crimson Lake's beach, boat launch and day use. Driveways run 20-51 ft; about a third of the sites are under 23 ft. Winter camping in Loop A: 11 sites are ploughed and powered (A-1, A-3, A-18 to A-21, A-23, A-25, A-31 to A-33); vault toilets only, no water or showers October-May, firewood cash or cheque. Ski, snowshoe and fat-bike trails and a skating rink in winter. --Claude

booking.note: Peak season is reservation-only; from Sep 21 to the spring opening, first-come winter camping in Loop A only. Bookings for the season open February 12. Peak season 2027 opens May 19.

note: Alberta Parks campground on Fish (Shunda) Lake, 6 km west of Nordegg on Hwy 11 and 2 km south on a gravel access road, run by a contracted operator. note: Alberta Parks provincial park 65 km south of Nordegg on the Forestry Trunk Road (Hwy 734); the gravel road to the campground can be rough, steep and winding in places (agency wording). note: Alberta Parks campground on the north side of Gleniffer Reservoir (Dickson Dam), about 20 km W of Innisfail south of Hwy 54. name: Rock Lake Provincial Park
note: Alberta Parks campground at Rock Lake, 35 km west of Hwy 40 on a gravel road north-west of Hinton, run by West Fraser Mills and the Fox Creek Development Association. The 54-site Green Mountain Loop sits in forest south-east of the lake; smaller Moose Landing loops are on the north shore, with walk-in tent sites, equestrian camps with corrals, and a Willmore Wilderness staging area. name: Lesser Slave Lake Provincial Park - Marten River Campground
note: Marten River campground in Lesser Slave Lake Provincial Park, about 32 km north of Slave Lake on Hwy 88: treed, well-spaced sites a short walk (by stairs) from the lake beach. Loops A and B suit RVs better; C and D have smaller sites better suited to tents. Coin-operated showers. No boat launch at the campground (the nearest is the Slave Lake municipal launch, 30 km south); a hand-launch path runs from the day-use area. The stairs from Loop A (between A-28 and A-29) and the southern stairs from Loop B (between B-23 and B-24) are closed for structural problems (Alberta Parks, Sep 18, 2026, until further notice). Freighter Lakeshore Trail access. --Claude

name: Pembina River Provincial Park
note: Alberta Parks campground in a bend of the Pembina River at Entwistle, in six loops of treed and open grass sites; some sites are close to the river. name: Moose Lake Provincial Park
note: Alberta Parks campground in jack pine forest on Moose Lake, about 13 km NW of Bonnyville (Hwy 41, Hwy 660, then 1 km south). Two loops set back from the lake; a sandy beach, boat launch, pier, fish cleaning and playground nearby. The taps are not drinkable: bring water, or fill tanks at Franchere Bay PRA. Blue-green algae and fecal-bacteria advisories were posted for the lake in August 2026. --Claude

name: Lakeland Provincial Recreation Area - Pinehurst Lake Campground
note: Alberta Parks recreation area campground on Pinehurst Lake, 48 km southeast of Lac La Biche: two wooded loops of drive-in sites set back from the lake, with a playground between them, a camp store (check-in, groceries, firewood), a beach day-use area joined by trail to the boat launch, and fish-cleaning stations. Hand-pump water is potable, but Alberta Parks recommends bringing drinking water; there is no fill station. A new RV dump station is under construction from Sep 8, 2026 to Apr 30, 2027; until then the nearest dump is at the Rich Lake fire hall. Gravel access road (can rut after heavy rain). Loops A and B close after the September long weekend; the Group Use A area then takes first-come campers (cash or cheque, bring water). --Claude

note: Small M.D. of Bonnyville-run Alberta Parks recreation area on the southeast shore of Cold Lake, 1 km south of Kinosoo Ridge Resort, in two loops about 600 m apart: the Lower East loop (sites 1-4) by the swimming area and day-use beach, and the Upper West loop (sites 5-10) by the boat launch, dock and fish-cleaning stand (launch use depends on lake level). name: Vegreville Municipal Campground (Pysanka Park)
note: Town of Vegreville campground at Pysanka Park (World's Largest Pysanka) on Hwy 16A at the east end of town: two loops either side of the CN rail line inside a bend of the creek, with check-in at the on-site Visitor Information Centre. note: Fully serviced campground in the woods a short walk from the Waskesiu townsite in Prince Albert National Park, built for large RVs and trailers. Check in at the campground kiosk (mid-June to Labour Day); in spring and fall check in at Beaver Glen or the Visitor Centre. Open fires are not permitted; propane fire pits are. --Claude

name: Sandy Lake Campground
note: Campground on the east shore of Sandy (Halkett) Lake near Prince Albert National Park's South Gate on Highway 263, in spruce, fir and aspen woods. Sand beach with a buoyed swim area, camp kitchen and picnic area by the lake, fish-cleaning station and boat launch. The drive-in sites are raised gravel back-ins; six more are walk-in tent sites. The nearest dump and potable-water fill is the Meridian station 3 km south on Highway 263. --Claude

name: Brightsand Lake Regional Park
note: Saskatchewan regional park (Brightsand Lake Regional Park Authority) at the north end of Brightsand Lake, about 27 km NE of St. Walburg. Non-electric sites 21-23 and 32, beside the boat launch, sit on open ground at the shore; the electric sites called beachfront (13-19) are across the main beach road in the trees. 52 of its 125 sites are seasonal. 9-hole golf course, concession, two rental cabins and registered ATV trails. --Claude

name: Buffalo Pound Provincial Park - Maple Vale, Shady Lane and Trails End Campgrounds
note: Provincial-park campgrounds at the north-west end of the park on Buffalo Pound Lake, a reservoir in the Qu'Appelle Valley about 20 minutes northeast of Moose Jaw: Maple Vale up the valley side by the store, Shady Lane and Trails End on open slopes down to the shore. Shady Lane B's S40 and S42 and Trails End's T13 sit on open grass close to the water; the other shore sites look at the lake through shrubs or trees or are seasonal (44 Shady Lane and Trails End sites are). Most Shady Lane A sites are posted for units of 18 ft or less. No dump station in these loops; the park's is by Elmview. Elmview, Lakeside and Valley by the beach about 2.8 km southeast, and Lower Chalet, have their own entries. --Claude

name: Makwa Lake Provincial Park - Stabler Point Campground
note: Provincial-park campground on Stabler Point, a wooded peninsula in Jumbo Lake near Loon Lake village, with a beach, boat launch and ski docks; the full-service sites sit in their own pod at the south end. Mewasin, about 3 km south on the Exner Lake road, and Jumbo Beach, about 1 km northeast by the village, have their own entries. 62 sites are sold by the season, and 9 nightly sites take units of 18 ft or less. --Claude

name: Meadow Lake Provincial Park - Sandy Beach Campground
note: On the south shore of Pierce Lake in Meadow Lake Provincial Park, off Hwy 919, in spruce and aspen woods behind a sand beach. The B loop's lake row (S34-S44) sits 30-45 m from the water with a line of spruce on the bank; a concession at the campground sells basic groceries and rents canoes and kayaks. --Claude

name: Narrow Hills Provincial Park - Zeden Lake Campground

name: Pike Lake Provincial Park
note: Provincial-park campground in aspen, ash and birch woods beside Pike Lake, an oxbow of the South Saskatchewan River about 20 minutes south of Saskatoon; three loops (A, B, C), with 24 seasonal sites in C. Heated outdoor pool, waterslide and beach. --Claude

name: Saskatchewan Landing Provincial Park - Bearpaw and Sagebrush Campgrounds
note: Provincial-park campgrounds at the west end of Lake Diefenbaker, at the historic South Saskatchewan River crossing about 50 km north of Swift Current on Hwy 4: Bearpaw's two loops in woods east of the bridge and Sagebrush in scattered trees beside it, both off one access road from Hwy 261. Bearpaw is set back in the trees from the shore; Sagebrush's south-east sites look at the lake through trees. Showers, laundry and groceries are in Bearpaw. Riverside and Nighthawk about 2 km east and Bison Hollow about 5 km west have their own entries; a separate equestrian campground on the south shore has non-electric horse sites. --Claude

note: Regional park about 20 km north of Gull Lake, run by the Antelope Lake Regional Park Authority, beside a man-made swimming pond with a sand beach; 9-hole sand-green golf course, concession and a group tenting area. name: Attons Lake Regional Park
note: Regional park on the south shore of Atton's Lake, about 20 km NE of Cut Knife off Hwy 40. Private cabins stand between the RV loops and the beach. Seasonal sites are let by contract, and overflow non-serviced sites take 40-ft rigs. 9-hole golf course, concession, sand beach, boat launch. ATVs are banned in the park in June, July and August, and motorboats on summer weekends. --Claude

note: Mostly seasonal: about 54 of its 224 sites are sold by the night; the shore rows (The Point, Lakeside, Darlings' west row) are seasonal. Regional park strung along the east shore of spring-fed Lac Pelletier, about 50 km by road from Swift Current, with beaches, a boat launch, a nine-hole grass-greens golf course, a store and restaurant, and micro-chalets. Among the nightly sites only the Glade's back row (T12, T15, T16) looks across open lawn to the lake. --Claude

name: Martins Lake Regional Park
note: Mostly seasonal: about 68 of its 146 sites are sold by the night. Near Leask, with a sandy beach, boat launch, fish-cleaning station and a 9-hole golf course. Daily sites are grass and gravel among mature trees; power posts can be far from the pad (the park suggests a 25-ft extension cord). The gate is locked 9 pm to 7 am and there is no entry overnight. Campsites rent only to those 19 and older unless with a parent or guardian. --Claude

note: Regional park on the west shore of Moosomin Lake in the Pipestone Valley, 14 km southwest of Moosomin (Hwy 8, Grid 709, then Lake Road); cabin lots line much of the shore, with a sand beach, boardwalk, marina, boat launches and a store-restaurant. name: Nickle Lake Regional Park
note: Regional park on the shores of Nickle Lake and the Souris River near Weyburn, where tall poplars line the road in and each area has a playground; there are shelters and benches along the shoreline, a groomed sandy beach and roped-off swimming area (no lifeguard), an 18-hole mini golf course and a canteen.  Mostly seasonal: about 70 of its 342 sites are sold by the night (River View, Circle Drive, Dorsch Bay and a few at Crescent Point); seasonal sites are long-term leases.  Two boat launches and a floating dock serve the lake, which holds walleye, perch and pike and has a fish-cleaning area.  An 18-hole golf course is 3 miles away. --Claude

name: Nipawin Regional Park
note: Regional park on the Saskatchewan River (the river section of Tobin Lake) 2 km from Nipawin, with forested loops of birch, pine and tamarack, a fish pond, dual boat launch and marina, mini golf, spray park and a barnyard zoo. About half the sites are seasonal. ATVs, dirt bikes and golf carts are not allowed in the park. --Claude

name: Palliser Regional Park
note: Regional park about 8 km southwest of Riverhurst on the east shore of Lake Diefenbaker, with two campgrounds about 3 km apart: the main park (north campground, beside the swimming beach, pool and golf course) and Rusty's Coulee Marina (south campground, larger full-hookup sites by the marina). Mostly seasonal: about 81 of its roughly 300 sites are sold by the night, about 14 of them at the marina. Electric sites have 220-volt plug-ins; a 110 plug needs an adaptor. --Claude

season.note: May long weekend to September 30 (the long weekend starts Friday May 21 in 2027; it was May 15 in 2026).

booking.note: Bookings for a season open in March in stages: 60-night-plus stays first, then 30-night-plus, then all lengths a week later (March 9, 16 and 23 for 2026). Group sites by phone.

name: Redberry Lake Regional Park
note: Regional park on Redberry Lake ~10 km NE of Hafford, run by a local park authority. Mostly seasonal: about 64 of its 145 sites are sold by the night. A treed lakeside row looks out on the lake through a line of trees; sandy beach with a buoyed swim area, nine-hole sand-green golf course, stocked trout pond. --Claude

booking.note: Online booking opens March 1. Cancelling costs $20; full refund less the fee more than 7 days out, half at 7 to 2 days, nothing inside 48 hours.

note: Town of Redvers campground on Hwy 13 behind the log-cabin tourist booth and the Red Coat Mountie statue, beside the rec centre's pool and ball diamonds. name: Rockin Beach Regional Park
note: Regional park on the south shore of Fife Lake, 9 km east of Rockglen on Highway 18 and 1 km north, with a sand beach and swimming area (no lifeguard), a concrete boat launch and dock, disc golf, ball diamonds, two playgrounds and an event quonset. A motocross track adjoins the campground, and the July long weekend brings mud-bog races and a beach cabaret. The lakeside row sits behind a dense shelterbelt above the beach. note: Regional park on Suffern Lake in the Manitou Sand Hills near Senlac. Beach with a playground and an outdoor shower, a store selling ice cream, firewood and ice, a free nine-hole artificial-green golf course, and a hall for rent. Some sites need up to 40 ft of cord and hose to reach the hookups, and site 37 is very small. No jet skis or ATVs in the park. --Claude

name: Wynyard Regional Park
note: Regional park at Wynyard's west entrance, 2.5 km south of the Yellowhead Highway on Grid 640, quiet and well treed; its reservoir, behind the old CPR dam, is aerated and holds rainbow trout (canoes, kayaks and electric-powered boats are allowed; fishing needs a provincial licence).  Campers have barbecues and free firewood; drinking water is at a coin-operated station at the Town Shop in Wynyard.  There is no full-time attendant: the facilities are cleaned and restocked once a day.  The trails stay open all year. --Claude

season.note: From the Victoria Day long weekend (May 16 in 2026) to the end of September.

name: Ice Springs Campground
note: Small primitive Boise NF (Mountain Home RD) campground on Fall Creek ~5 mi north of Fall Creek Resort (Anderson Ranch Reservoir area), reached via gravel/dirt Forest Rds 120/123/134. 3 developed drive-in sites plus several primitive sites (some right on Fall Creek); each developed site has campfire ring, grill, picnic table and shares a vault toilet; no potable water. Best for smaller rigs; the road onward to higher elevations gets rough but the campground itself is gravel-road accessible. --Claude

Strike Dam, about 24 miles south of Mountain Home: 10 acres with 33 RV sites (shared water, no power), 3 turf tent sites, fire rings, a waterfront walking path, a seasonal dump station, a boat ramp and a reservable picnic shelter. name: Nine Mile Ranch
note: Working cattle ranch of Ben Mead and his daughter Carla in Nine Mile Canyon, 24 paved miles up Nine Mile Canyon Road from Wellington and a gateway to the canyon's petroglyphs; its campgrounds are the only camping allowed in the canyon.  Its campgrounds sit beside Nine Mile Creek with plenty of shade and green grass; every site has a picnic table and a fire pit or ring, and every campground a spring-water faucet.  Kokopelli is best for RVs, trailers and vans, Cottonwood Hollow is mostly for tents, small vans and truck campers, and the Turnouts are pull-throughs.  Showers ($3) are at the main ranch, and generators are off from 10 p.m. to 7 a.m. (9 p.m. in fall).  The ranch also rents settler cabins rebuilt on the property and bed-and-breakfast rooms.  There is no cell service in the 50-mile canyon, and Wi-Fi only around the main house. --Claude

name: Fish House Inn & RV Park
note: Country inn and RV park in Dayville, in a craftsman house built in 1908 for the mill owner Walt Greenwell and converted into an inn in 1991, nine miles from the Sheep Rock Unit of the John Day Fossil Beds and the Thomas Condon Paleontology Center.  The seven full-hookup spaces behind the inn are each 60 ft long on level gravel, separated by grass and trees, and the five power-only sites are on the lawn and have picnic tables.  Guests share a community fire pit with a bar and grill, barbecue grills and horseshoe pits; the John Day River, the town park and playground, the Dayville Cafe, the Mercantile and the South Fork Mini Market & Gas are within walking distance, and there are swimming holes nearby.  EV charging costs $10 an hour or $30 a day, and an RV check-in before 2 p.m. costs $10; monthly winter rates, November through April, are by phone.  The inn also has rooms and an Airstream Bambi for glamping. --Claude

fees.note: BLM LTVA, two fee seasons (BLM page read 2026-11-07). Sep 15-Apr 15: an LTVA permit is required, $40 short-visit permit for any 14 consecutive days (renewable without limit) or $180 long-term permit for the whole season or any part of it. Apr 16-Sep 14: $15 per vehicle per night or $75 a year per vehicle, up to 5 people per vehicle, $1 each person over 5 ($10 per vehicle for day use); maximum stay 14 days in a 28-day period. nightly_low is the Apr 16-Sep 14 night, nightly_high the cheapest in-season night (a $40 short-visit permit); the schema has no seasonal price, so the season rides in the permit names. A 2024 Yuma Field Office draft business plan proposed $600 long-term / $200 short-term (30 days); BLM's own pages still post $180/$40 as of 2026-11-07.

fees.note: BLM LTVA, two fee seasons (BLM page read 2026-11-07). Sep 15-Apr 15: an LTVA permit is required, $40 short-visit permit for any 14 consecutive days (renewable without limit) or $180 long-term permit for the whole season or any part of it. Apr 16-Sep 14: $15 per vehicle per night or $75 a year per vehicle, up to 5 people per vehicle, $1 each person over 5 ($10 per vehicle for day use); maximum stay 14 days in a 28-day period. nightly_low is the Apr 16-Sep 14 night, nightly_high the cheapest in-season night (a $40 short-visit permit); the schema has no seasonal price, so the season rides in the permit names. A 2024 Yuma Field Office draft business plan proposed $600 long-term / $200 short-term (30 days); BLM's own pages still post $180/$40 as of 2026-11-07.

name: Rancho Seco Recreational Area
note: SMUD's 400-acre park around a 160-acre lake fed by the Folsom South Canal, 25 miles from downtown Sacramento, with 21 RV and 32 tent sites and a designated swimming beach.  Weekend stays take two nights, Friday and Saturday together; stays are limited to 14 days, and campers with reservations cannot enter after 10 p.m.  Boat trailers have been banned since March 14, 2025 to keep out the invasive golden mussel, and hand-launched craft are inspected on entry; boats are rented on weekends and holidays from Memorial Day to Labor Day.  The lake holds bass (catch and release only), bluegill, redear sunfish and crappie, and rainbow trout are stocked from November through March.  The Howard Ranch Trail is an easy seven-mile round trip across a working cattle ranch, so dogs stay home.  The park also rents Jupes, and outside firewood is not allowed. --Claude

name: Amazing Rocky Park Campground
note: Daiva RV Resorts park beside 2,500 ft of the Rocky Saugeen River, on more than 25 acres, over 19 of them left natural with walking trails.  The river drops 30 ft over a hydro-electric dam: upstream is deep enough for swimming, diving, boating and fishing, and downstream suits nature hikes and fly-fishing.  Below the dam a creek leaves the river and runs through the lower loop of sites.  It has a heated pool, a playground and a comfort station, horseshoe pits, shuffleboard courts and badminton and volleyball nets, and planned activities such as Christmas in July, movie nights, children's crafts, horseshoe and euchre tournaments and dances.  It also has seasonal sites and a cabin. --Claude

name: Bayview Lodge Resort
note: Resort on 50 acres of White Lake lakefront, about 60 km west of Ottawa between Calabogie and Arnprior.  Each RV site is individually metered and has a fire pit, and sites range from full sun to full shade.  No tents; the campground page asks for trailers with washrooms.  It has a marina with gas at the docks, boat slips, boat rentals and boat storage, a saltwater pool, a recreation and games hall, a coffee shop, a fish-cleaning station and firewood.  White Lake hosts several bass tournaments a year and holds largemouth and smallmouth bass, northern pike, walleye, rock bass, yellow perch, pumpkinseed, brown bullhead and bluegill.  Cottages and chalets are also rented. --Claude

name: Bear Lake Experience
note: Small family-owned campground on 42 acres of mostly natural forest in the Village of Warwick, Lambton County, with over 2 km of trails and a new dog park.  The camping area sits beside a 2-acre spring-fed pond, with five shady sites along its bank; motorized boats are not allowed, fishing is catch-and-release and there is no lifeguard.  Besides its powered sites it has off-grid sites, and each site takes one family with at most 2 adults and 2 pets.  Bottled drinking water and firewood are sold.  The name comes from the creek through the property, not from bears. --Claude

note: Daiva RV Resorts park in woodland beside the Grand River, amid hundreds of acres of farmland, where mature cedars and maples surround each site and the shallow river is good for floating. name: Stoney Lake - Daiva RV Resorts (formerly Harmony Resorts)
note: Daiva RV Resorts park among Precambrian rock and windswept pines on the shores of Stoney Lake in the Kawarthas, with pinery and lakeside sites.  It has a private sandy beach, boat docks and a launch, and canoe and kayak rentals for exploring the lake's hundreds of islands; the lake holds bass, walleye and muskie.  Petroglyphs Provincial Park, across the street, is a sacred Indigenous site holding the largest known concentration of rock carvings in Canada, along with hiking trails and McGinnis Lake, one of the few meromictic lakes in North America.  It also has seasonal sites and boat slips. --Claude

name: Alder Bay Resort
note: Private RV park and marina near Port McNeill on northern Vancouver Island, on 30 acres of private land with abundant walk-on waterfront, run by the McGrady and Brockway families.  Its more than 80 sites run from tent sites to big rigs: fully serviced pull-throughs, full-service 15- or 30-amp sites (some with an ocean view), rustic oceanfront tent sites and The Mecca's four non-serviced group sites.  There is a two-lane launch ramp usable at all tides, a 43-slip marina for boats up to 26 ft, an easy kayak launch and a fish-cleaning station, plus a Level 2 car charger and propane fills up to 100 lb, and Roxy's Diner, a licensed food truck with an ocean-view patio, serves burgers and local lingcod fish and chips.  Partner operators run fishing, bear-viewing and whale-watching tours.  Generators may run from 9 to 11 a.m. and 6 to 8 p.m.  The resort also has long-term RV sites, park-model cottages and two RV trailer rentals, and a residential phase, Orca Views, is coming. --Claude

name: Halcyon Heights RV Campground
note: Campground overlooking Upper Arrow Lake in the heart of the Kootenays, 25 minutes from Nakusp and an hour from Revelstoke; Halcyon Resort's hot-spring pools, spa and dining are 1 km away.  Every site has a lake view except site 4, which looks onto the forest, and sites 23 and 24 are creekside.  Water is at every site, and drinking water and ice are sold at the camp store. name: Kimberley Riverside Campground
note: Campground beside the St. Mary's River, an 8-minute drive south-west of Kimberley's town centre, the Platzl, with over 150 campsites.  Full-service sites 26-67 and 91-140, in the Mountain View and Pine Meadows areas, take 15- to 50-amp power and rigs of 25 to 45 ft, and the riverview sites 68-79 take 30 or 50 amps and 25 to 35 ft; sites 26, 27, 28, 39, 41, 43, 45, 47, 49, 53-57 and 110-140 are pull-throughs.  The power-and-water back-ins, 1 to 25B (15 or 30 amps, 25 to 40 ft), are closest to the pool and mini-golf, and the non-service sites NS1 to NS9 (20 to 25 ft) are first come, first served.  A free heated pool is open from mid-May to the September long weekend and an 18-hole putting course from early May to late September, and there is a timber picnic shelter, a playground, bocce, horseshoes and sand volleyball.  The Adventure Centre rents e-bikes, stand-up paddleboards and inflatable kayaks and sells Kootenay Rafting Company tours.  Cell service is spotty.  In winter the bathrooms behind the office stay open with running water and hot showers, tanks are filled there from a hose, and the sani-dump is at site 26.  Winter storage costs C$250 from October 1 to April 20.  The campground also rents trailers and trapper's tents and has walk-in tent sites. --Claude

season.note: Full services from April 15 to October 15.  From October 15 to April 15, select sites at the top of the campground stay open, by reservation, with 15- and 30-amp power but no water or sewer hookups.

name: The Lodge at Panther River
note: Remote private lodge campground on the Panther River west of Sundre (about 40-45 minutes from town), reached by ~30 km of gravel road; cell service is limited in the valley and there are no stores nearby. Three loops: A semi-serviced (15-amp power, potable water for tank fill-up and dump access, no sewer at the site; air conditioners will not run on 15 amp), B fully serviced along the river, and C, the newest, with larger premium sites. Gravel pads only, each with picnic table and fire ring; shared gazebo with BBQ, equestrian sites, and a lodge with meals in peak season, cabins and canvas tents. Only the front row of about five sites is right on the river; the rest sit 30-80 m or more back. --Claude

booking.note: Booked online through the lodge's Cloudbeds engine (Campground A sites 1-17, Campground B sites 1-25, Campground C). The FAQ says 'During peak weekends or special events, we may have a 2-night minimum.' Check-in 3 pm, check-out 10 am (engine). Seasonal sites are sold separately.

name: Camping Plage Gagnon Beach
note: Campground 19 km (12 miles) east of Shediac off Highway 133, at the border of Cap-Pelé and Grand-Barachois, beside Gagnon Beach, with its sunsets, sandbars for miles and what the campground calls the warmest waters north of Virginia.  Every site is 2 to 5 minutes' walk from the sand.  There is an animal-friendly area, a playground with a bouncy pillow, a basketball court, a recreation hall for pool, ping-pong and other indoor games, a new family inground pool and a large field.  Sites run from unserviced field camping to 2-service sites in the main area (20 amps) or the open field (20 or 30 amps) and 3-service sites (30 amps), mostly drive-through.  Wi-Fi costs extra, C$7 a day per device.  The campground also rents trailers and a studio cottage, and seasonal sites have a waitlist.  Max Michaud, Pat Jacob and Fred Jacob have owned it since August 2024; it is over 40 years old.  A beach day pass or visitor pass costs C$10 a carload. --Claude

name: Hyclass Ocean Campground
note: Campground at Havre Boucher with ocean-view RV sites and, in the E section, primitive sites out on the point.  Swimming is off the dock, in what the campground calls the warmest waters north of the Carolinas; there is no sandy beach, so water shoes are recommended, and there are canoes, kayaks and pedal boats.  There is beach-side volleyball, washer toss, a playground, a small walking trail, birdwatching (more than 30 kinds seen) and a book exchange.  Two cabins and a fifth-wheel trailer are rented, there are seasonal sites, and cyclists get a special rate for one tent.  Quiet hours run from 11 p.m. to 7 a.m. --Claude

name: Old Shipyard Beach Campground
note: Campground at Spencer's Island on the Bay of Fundy, where every site has a front-row seat to the bay.  The land was a shipyard with a lighthouse, then a lumber yard; Bob and Noreen ran the campground from 1999, and Bill and Joanne have since 2023.  Lobster season runs to the end of July, a public boat ramp is right next to the campground, and there is a book exchange.  From June 27 to August 29 the cottages rent by the week only, Saturday to Saturday.  Check Cumberland County's burn restrictions before lighting a fire. --Claude

sites.note: 94 full-hookup sites (30/50 amp) for overnight and monthly stays plus 22 tent and pop-up sites (20-amp electric and water, most on the river). Seasonal sites are sold too.

facilities.note: In-ground pool, bathhouse, arcade, basketball and volleyball. No outside firewood.

Holiday rentals require a 3-night non-refundable deposit and 7 days' cancellation notice; other stays a 1-night deposit and 3 days' notice. River sites: 6 people, 2 tents, 2 vehicles, no visitors. name: Graves Mountain Farm Campground
note: Primitive open-meadow camping on the 1,800-acre Graves Mountain Farm & Lodges property in the Rose River valley, at the edge of Shenandoah National Park. Operator's campground page: 'RV - any size' welcome, pick-your-own spot across roughly 7 acres of meadow that expands to about 55 acres for holidays and festival weekends; water spigots at the front of the campground, porta and pit toilets, showers at the farm's bathhouse behind the packing shed. The operator's campground-map PDF shows numbered water/electric and water/electric/sewer drive-in pads (sites 1-105) on two long loops off the access road, plus primitive tent sites, heated bathhouses with private showers, honey-wagon service and a rentable pavilion. 2026 nightly rates $35 primitive, cabins $58-128. Direct access to the state ATV and snowmobile trail systems (ATV trails Memorial Day weekend to the last full weekend in September). --Claude

note: Year-round 33-site campground at 125 Walmar Manor off Franklin Church Rd near US 15 in Dillsburg, run by Walmar MHC, LLC as its own loop beside the company's Walmar Manor manufactured-home community - satellite shows the two as clearly separate: an RV loop with a swimming pool and open grass sites to the north, a grid of permanent manufactured homes to the south. name: Riverfront Campground and Fishing Camp
note: Wooded fishing camp on the Susquehanna at the mouth of the Juniata, just north of Duncannon and a short walk from the Appalachian Trail (the owners run an AT hiker shuttle). Operator's rates page lists full-hookup sites, water-and-electric sites, and no-hookup tent sites plus a separate off-river tent area. Operator's camping page: "Most of our sites are wooded, and over half are located along one of our two rivers," and the season is April 1 to December 1, "river permitting" - it sits on the floodplain, so late-season and high-water closures happen. Sites and interior lanes are wooded and unpaved off a grade crossing of the Norfolk Southern line, fine for a 23-ft rig but no big-rig suitability is claimed. Rates are not published online ("Please Call" on every line) and there is no online booking - reserve by phone or email; check-in 5 PM, check-out 4 PM. A Hipcamp listing exists but is still marked "coming soon," so it is not a live booking channel. Boat, canoe and kayak rental plus a bait shop on site. RV Life ~$27/night. --Claude

name: Woodland's Campground on Pine Creek
note: Listed by RV Life as "Pine Creek Campground" at 3686 US-6; the operating name on its own Facebook page and in directory listings is Woodland's Campground on Pine Creek, 9 Woodlands Ln, Wellsboro (the Watrous hamlet between Gaines and Ansonia, Tioga County). About 35 sites on mowed grass loops between US-6 and Pine Creek, with full hookups including 50-amp, pull-through and back-in sites, restrooms; tents accepted, no cabins. Walking distance to Pine Creek and the Pine Creek Rail Trail, and about 15 minutes from Colton Point / Leonard Harrison and the PA Grand Canyon. Satellite shows sheds or decks beside many of the trailers, so a good share of the pads are seasonal campers - call ahead for a transient site. No online booking channel found; reserve by phone. name: Wilsonville Recreation Area
note: Largest of the Lake Wallenpaupack recreation areas, on a wooded point off US 6 at 113 Ammon Dr; the lake and its recreation areas are owned and run by utility operator Brookfield Renewable (formerly PPL), so it is a utility park rather than a government one. 160 tent and trailer sites with dump station, playground, marina with rental slips, gas dock and boat ramps. The operator's colour site map classes sites as seasonal, 7-night-minimum, or 2-night-minimum (3 nights on holidays), so a large transient block is bookable; seasonal sites are currently full. Electric and water reach at least part of the loop (a dated firsthand review reports 30A and water at site 41). No pets permitted, and swimming is not allowed within the recreation area. The older wilsonvillecampground.com domain now serves an expired certificate; wilsonvillecampground1.com is the live site. --Claude

name: Ponderosa Pines Family Campground
note: 31 Ponderosa Dr, in the Bethany area northeast of Honesdale; under new ownership since 2020. The operator's site map shows roughly 85 numbered drive-in sites in four areas - Hillside H01-H27, Lakeside L01-L41, Kossack Court/Sabol Circle T01-T08 and Kasey Trail/Laurel Dr P01-P07 - plus seven cabins and two rustic tent sites, colour-coded seasonal versus non-seasonal with a solid block of non-seasonal sites in each loop. Its Firefly Reservations engine books nightly and asks for RV length, offering Lake Area, Lakefront, Deluxe Sewer and Rustic RV/Tent site classes; hookups run 15/20/30 amp with water, and sewer on the deluxe sites (no 50 amp advertised). Salt-water pool, mini golf, boat rentals on the campground's own Lake Ponderosa and rec hall. Seasonal rentals are sold too but must be paid by check rather than online. Open season is roughly mid-April to late October per directory listings; the operator's own pages do not publish the dates. RV Life ~$40/night. --Claude

name: Firehouse RV Campground
note: Small no-frills RV park behind the Jefferson Volunteer Fire Company hall at 1483 Jefferson Rd in Greene County, run by the fire company as a fundraiser (reviewers deal with 'Chief Joe' and the volunteer staff). Roughly 30-37 gravel full-hookup sites on a single loop - 30/50 amp, water and sewer, around 20 pull-thru, some with concrete patios, sites about 35 ft wide by 60 ft deep - open year round with long-term rates. Transient nightly stays are genuinely taken. The resident mix skews long-term, though, so call ahead rather than assuming a nightly opening. Little shade and no amenities beyond the hookups. The fire company has no campground website and no online booking - reservations are by phone. Camper-reported rate: $18 a night (Campendium, June 2025; $21 in 2021). --Claude

name: Beaver Run Campground
note: Small independent campground at 461 Mount Morris Road just off I-79 exit 1 in Greene County. Operator's own site publishes nightly lot fees - full hookup (electric/water/sewer), electric+water with a dump station, electric only, $35 tent - with weekly and monthly rates and only a limited number of seasonal and yearly lots, so transient camping is the main business ('come relax with us for a night, a weekend or even longer'). 6-person maximum; check-in 3pm, check-out 11am; restrooms and laundry included for all paid guests; two pets per site; firewood sold on site; city water. Reservations are by phone or email only and payment is CASH ONLY at present - no online booking. Site count and maximum rig length are not published; the operator describes shady sites. Caveat: the campground appears to be recently built - the current Esri imagery of the address (Sep 2025) predates it and shows no pads, so the pin is the street address confirmed by both the Census and Nominatim geocoders rather than a satellite-verified loop; the RV Life coordinate sits ~350 m northwest on an unrelated stockpile yard. --Claude

name: Eagle's Nest Campground
note: Family-owned since 2011 on Patterson Creek Village Pike, about 9 mi from Cumberland MD. Seasonal packages are sold alongside the nightly sites (weekends-only Thu-Sun $450/month, full-time resident $850/month, May 1-Oct 10 season, a whole row $1800), so expect a mixed transient/seasonal park; cabins and a pavilion are separate products. On-site Fireside Inn restaurant and lounge, camp store (ice, firewood, beer, propane), live music Fridays and karaoke Thursdays, playground and yard games, creek swimming and fishing, weekend community float trips. Late check-in by phone. RV Life counts 80 sites; the operator does not publish a site count or a max RV length. Note the operator's own warning that GPS mis-routes to the address - they direct drivers to Patterson Creek Village Pike off WV-28. --Claude

name: Sleepy Hollow Campground
note: Small campground in the Appalachian Mountains of Garrett County, family-owned since 1964, 2 miles from New Germany State Park.  Its rustic, shady sites are mostly back-ins on gravel and may need levelling; an RV water-filling station and a wash sink stand outside the renovated, heated bathhouse.  The sewer disposal area doesn't accommodate modern RVs but takes a rolling portable tank, and New Germany State Park's dump station is less than 5 miles away.  The small Glamp Store is open around the clock, fiber Wi-Fi arrived in summer 2026, and cell service is limited.  A-frame and other cabins are rented, a new pavilion is coming, and political flags aren't allowed.  CAVEAT on the pin: three sources disagree by up to 1.7 km on where this sits (a US Census rooftop match on the operator's published address, RV Life's pin 680 m west and Campspot's coordinates 1.7 km west), and Esri imagery is unbroken canopy at all three, so the coordinate here is the address match rather than a confirmed loop.  Not to be confused with New Germany State Park Campground, the separate state-run campground nearby. --Claude

note: Primitive GFP lakeside use area on a wooded peninsula in the 235-acre Amsden Lake, east of Groton off US 12: one loop of back-in sites, boat ramp and dock, fishing pier, swim beach and year-round vault toilets. No drinking water at the park. Sites 1 and 2 face the main lake across small open clearings; 9-12 sit above a cove behind a fringe of shore trees; the rest are in the woods. Pads are posted at 25 ft, a snug fit for a 23-ft rig. The lake is known for muskie over a flooded gravel pit that drops to 27 ft, and gave up the state record at 40 lb in 1991. --Claude

Three boat ramps, the Gore Canyon Whitewater Playpark and foot trails up and down the river. Seasonal drinking water may run May-October but is not reliable and is not for filling RV tanks; no cell service without a booster. Supplies in Kremmling, ~15 miles east. --Claude

note: Primitive, reservable campsites scattered through the Delta National Forest, the only all-bottomland-hardwood national forest, between Rolling Fork and Yazoo City off MS-16. Not one campground: 56 sites sit in small groups along Forest Service roads 703, 707, 710, 715, 720 and 721, Dummyline Road, the Green Ash and Dowling Bayou greentree reservoirs, MS-16, and the Blue Lake and Little Sunflower River recreation areas (this pin is Blue Lake, 3 sites). note: Five drive-in sites on the lowest stretch of the river, about 5 km west of Oscoda near the Whirlpool Angler Access; 100D and 101D are pull-throughs, and 098D (18 ft) is too short for a 23-ft rig. Part of the AuSable River Dispersed Camping system: 102 designated sites along 55 miles of the lower AuSable in the Huron NF, booked as one recreation.gov facility. Dirt or gravel parking aprons; the sites sit on bluffs 5-300 ft above the river and access to the water can be steep. Equipment within 25 ft of the site post; two vehicles and two camping units per site. --Claude

sites.note: Five drive-in sites 098D-102D for tent, RV or trailer: 100D (pull-through, to 40 ft), 101D (pull-through, 26 ft), 099D and 102D (back-in, 26 ft), and 098D (back-in, 18 ft).

facilities.note: No drinking water, toilets or trash removal at any site: bring water, a portable toilet and garbage bags; pack it in, pack it out.

booking.note: Run directly by the Forest Service (Huron Shores Ranger District), not a concessionaire. Every site is reserved by number on recreation.gov April 15 - November 30; December 1 - April 14 no permit or reservation is required. Occupy the site within 24 hours of the reservation's start or it is forfeit unless the Forest Service approves a late arrival. 14 nights in any 30 days.

Site length not published, but every site lists fifth wheels as permitted. Lakefront only at sites 7, 8, 18, 19, 21 and 22 on the east shore; the point sites sit on a 5-6 m bank above the water. --Claude

name: Hopewell Lake Campground (Carson NF)

note: BLM campground on small Duncan Reservoir in the sagebrush west of Silver Lake's dry lakebed: 5 miles east of Silver Lake on OR-31, then 5 miles south on gravel County Road 4-14 (sometimes rough, with washouts that reviewers drove around). Four single sites along the west shore, three of them pull-throughs at the water, plus a group site below the dam; boat ramp, covered picnic area, no food or gas nearby. name: Wolcott Campground (Eagle River, BLM)
note: BLM campground and boat ramp on the Eagle River just east of Red Canyon, off I-70 Exit 157 at Wolcott: north from the exit, left on the frontage road (Old Highway 6) at the stop sign, 2 miles past the bridge and the Wolcott Yacht Club, then right at Wolcott Recreation Area and downhill to the campground. name: Jack Lake Campground
note: Langlade County campground on Jack Lake northeast of Antigo, in mature maple, birch, oak and pine beside Veterans Memorial Park (beach, playground, disc golf). Direct access to the Ice Age Trail, mountain-bike and ski trails, and the county ATV/UTV and snowmobile trails. Sites 7-15 back onto the wooded shore with the lake seen through the trees; 51-57 sit on a clearing behind a belt of trees on the south shore, with a footpath to the water. 49-57 (the former South Shore area) take one camping unit and no tents. Three sleeping cabins. --Claude

sites.note: 48 electric sites and 9 non-electric (49-57, one camping unit each, no tents). Posted site dimensions run 30 x 30 to 70 x 32 ft; all wooded and shaded on gravel.

booking.note: All campsites must be reserved online through the county's site; each year's bookings open on the first business day of January at 8:30 am. Check-in 3 pm, check-out 11 am.

note: Vernon County's oldest park, in a Driftless valley on the North Fork Bad Axe River between Westby and Coon Valley. Hookup sites line the park road beside a stocked trout pond; the rustic sites spread across an open meadow along the river. Hiking trails and a picnic shelter, with a nine-hole golf course next door. --Claude

name: Paris Park
note: Mecosta County park on the Muskegon River at the old Paris fish hatchery (1881-1964; hatchery building with a pictorial history, trout ponds), north of Big Rapids beside the White Pine Trail. Canoe/kayak/tube launch; the park runs tube rentals and shuttles upriver Thursday-Sunday in season. --Claude

booking.note: Reserve online (an account is needed to check out); 2-night minimum on all campsite reservations, 3 nights on holiday and event weekends. Payment in full when booking.

name: Trailway Campground
note: City of Montague campground on Business 31 between Montague and Whitehall, across the street from White Lake and beside the White River, the World's Largest Weathervane and the paved Hart-Montague bike trail; an easy walk to both downtowns. No boats or boat trailers overnight in the campground (paid parking in the adjacent city lot, arranged with the manager). --Claude

sites.note: No tent sites (small tents in the rustic area as space allows). The 2024 campground map marks pull-through and back-in sites and about 30 seasonal sites. One RV and one vehicle per site; sites are assigned by management.

facilities.note: Dump station free to campers ($20 to non-campers). Wireless internet at the sites for registered campers. Communal fire pit and pavilion with wood provided; no campfires at sites (portable propane fire pits allowed).

note: Village of Marion park on M-66 southeast of Cadillac, on the Middle Branch River Walk (the Middle Branch is a designated trout stream). Grassy sites; playground, basketball court, pavilions, ball fields and a disc golf course; grocery store, gas stations and restaurants within walking distance. No alcohol, ORVs or dirt bikes in the park. --Claude

name: Empire Township Campground
note: Rustic Empire Township campground in the woods at 264 W Osborn Rd, 5 miles from the Village of Empire and the Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore headquarters. Fills on holidays. --Claude

sites.note: 60 sites in two wooded sections (Hardwoods and Pine Tree): 9 with electricity, RV dry sites, tent sites and 3 group sites. One tent/camper and one vehicle per site.

facilities.note: Coin-operated showers, one flush toilet beside the drinking-water station, outhouses and drinking water throughout, dump station, ice. No generators or chainsaws allowed.

booking.note: Reserve by emailing empiretownshipcampground@gmail.com with dates, party size, rig type and size; full payment for stays of 5 nights or less, a one-night deposit per week otherwise. Register at the office before setting up. Cancelling 5+ business days out costs one night (per week reserved); inside 4 business days the whole stay.

note: Dubuque County Conservation park on Mud Lake, a Mississippi backwater of Pool 11, six miles north of Dubuque off Hwy 52. 42 camper sites with electric and water (1-26 at 30 A, 27-42 at 50 A in a gravel pull-through herringbone), three tent sites, accessible showers and dump station in the middle of the campground. Sites 7-10 are grass and posted not recommended for Class A motorhomes. Boat ramp, fishing pier, marina and grill next door; ranger in residence year-round. Water and showers are shut off roughly Nov 1 to May 1. --Claude

booking.note: About 30% of sites (camper sites 7-10, 23-25, 29-32, 39-42 and tent site 44) book online on mycountyparks at least 4 days ahead; the rest are first come, first served, and unbooked reservable sites go first come too. Reserved sites carry a yellow tag. Online bookings are non-refundable; cancel or reschedule by calling the county office 14 business days ahead. Check-in after 3 pm, check-out by 2 pm.

A ranger lives on site year-round. --Claude

name: Saulsbury Bridge Recreation Area
note: Muscatine County Conservation recreation area on the Cedar River about eight miles northwest of Muscatine, named for the old bridge whose last two spans now carry foot traffic. The Main Campground sits in the woods near the lodge with a campground host and playground; the River Campground is a separate loop on the river bank about 500 m west. Boat ramps on the Cedar River and Chicken Creek, canoe and kayak rental, hiking and equestrian trails. --Claude

booking.note: Main Campground sites 1-24 book online on mycountyparks.com ('reservable online 3-days in advance'); an unreserved site is taken first come, first served by paying through the QR code or mycountyparks.com. River Campground sites are first come, first served at the self-pay kiosk. Cancel 30+ days out for a coupon less the $4 fee; 15-29 days, less $10 a night; no refund under 15 days. Check-in 3 pm, check-out noon.

name: Cedar Bridge Park
note: Mitchell County Conservation park just west of Osage on Hwy 9, at the Cedar River Greenbelt Trail and the Milton R. Owen Nature Center. One gravel loop on open mowed ground with a playground and shelter; the Cedar River runs past the east side behind a belt of woods, with access for fishing and paddling. --Claude

No more than 14 days in any 21-day period. Check-in after 3 pm, check-out before 2 pm. The county map marks sites 15, 16 and 18 as seasonal campsites.

name: Camp Comfort Recreation Area
note: Butler County Conservation area on the Shell Rock River at the fieldstone dam, 23525 Camp Comfort Rd north of C-23. 38 electric sites (30/50 amp; most grass pads, pairs sharing a pedestal) on a lane along the river, plus tent space; water hydrants, shower house, boat ramps and canoe access above and below the dam, open shelter, playground. --Claude

No online reservations in the off-season. Reservations non-refundable. After 14 nights campers must leave for 3 nights.

Boat ramp, fishing pier, kayak launch, beach, trails and a 9-hole par-3 course. Construction continues through 2026: the lower camping area and the north beach stay closed. --Claude

In 2026 online booking opened May 18 for May 21 - November 1 (the county normally opens its parks' booking the first Monday in March). Check-in 3 PM, check-out 2 PM; check-in by emailed link or the QR sign. Up to four sites per reservation. Five sites are leased for the season by lottery ($1,900, May 29 - Oct 1, 2026).

name: Estes Park Campground at Mary's Lake
note: Estes Valley Recreation and Park District campground on the south edge of Estes Park, a few miles from Rocky Mountain NP's south entrance; mostly open and sunny, view to the Twin Sisters. Mary's Lake is across Mary's Lake Road (shore fishing only - no boating or swimming). --Claude

sites.note: EVRPD says 128 sites; ReserveAmerica's overview says 120 and its catalog lists 117: 82 RV-only (24 full-hookup back-in, 24-32 ft; 23 full-hookup pull-through, 35-56 ft; 24 water & electric, sixteen 25 ft and eight 20 ft; 11 no-hookup, one 25 ft and ten 15-20 ft) and 35 tent-only. About 64 RV sites take a 23-ft rig. Lengths are strictly enforced (measured hitch to bumper).

facilities.note: Coin-op hot showers (quarters), heated swimming pool, propane filling, playground; picnic table, fire ring and bear locker at every site. No Wi-Fi; cell coverage good.

booking.note: ReserveAmerica online or (800) 964-7806, up to 180 days ahead and up to the arrival date. Two nights on weekends; three on Memorial Day, Independence Day and Labor Day; none Monday-Thursday. Any unreserved site is first-come at the office (no walk-ins after the store closes at 8 pm). 14 days in 28; no monthly stays. Check-in 2 pm, out 11 am.

name: Casey Jones RV Hideaway (Elizabeth)
note: Elizabeth Park & Recreation District campground in the ponderosa pines of 103-acre Casey Jones Park, 4189 Hwy 86 just east of Elizabeth; the campground entrance is separate from the park's, just east of it off Hwy 86. The park also has ballfields, an equestrian arena with overnight corrals (fee; no livestock in the campground), a dog park and a 1.4-mi trail; Evans Park next door has a fishing pond and trails to Main Street. Camp host near the entrance. No wood or charcoal fires; propane only. --Claude

name: Lost Creek Campground (WY-70, Encampment)
note: Medicine Bow-Routt NF campground on the Battle Highway (WY-70) 18 miles west of Encampment, at about 8,800 ft. Small sites among conifers and meadow; the FS says trailers under 22 ft, at the edge for a 23-ft rig, though the driveways run 25-99 ft. No trash service. The Baby Lakes Trail into the Huston Park Wilderness starts across the highway; ATV riding on Forest Road 811 nearby. --Claude

name: Rio Grande Campground (Creede)
note: Small Rio Grande NF campground in a grassy meadow beside the Rio Grande, 8.5 miles west of Creede off CO 149, then ~0.5 mile on FSR 529 (signed Rio Grande Fisherman's Area). The sites sit below the highway on the river bottom, so there is little road noise. The FS does not recommend it for large RVs or long or wide trailers because the access road down to the site is narrow and steep. No trash service: pack out all garbage. Fishing access (Colorado license required) and a summer raft put-in/take-out; the river is close enough to be a hazard to unsupervised children. --Claude

booking.note: First-come only; pay with the recreation.gov app's Scan & Pay at the site (works with or without service), or cash/check. Check-in after 2 p.m., check-out before 11 a.m.

name: Cathedral Campground (Embargo Creek, Del Norte)
note: Rio Grande NF (Divide RD) campground on Embargo Creek northwest of Del Norte. Reached by county roads 18, 15 and 65, then 7.6 mi on FR 640, which the Forest Service describes as dirt, single lane with no turnouts. Two loops: the left one around a meadow with a few open sites, the right in dense aspen and spruce; view of Cathedral Rock to the north. Fremont's 1848 winter camp is nearby. --Claude

sites.note: 22 sites in two loops: 17 dead-end spurs and 5 pull-throughs, 35-45 ft long. 'Not all sites will fit vehicles of this length' (45 ft).

booking.note: First-come only; pay on site by cash/check or with recreation.gov Scan to Pay (QR code in the Recreation.gov app).

name: Turtle Rock Campground (Buena Vista, BLM)
note: BLM campground 3.5 miles north of Buena Vista in the Fourmile Recreation Area, in pinyon-juniper at the base of the Turtle Rock granite (popular with climbers), with views of the Collegiate Peaks. Many sites are short, so pick one listed at 23 ft or more. Hiking, mountain-bike and OHV trails from camp. From Buena Vista: E Arkansas St, CR 371 2.2 mi, CR 375 0.8 mi. --Claude

sites.note: Small sites, most built for tents or vans; RVs and trailers over 35 ft not allowed. Sites 7-12 are tent-only/walk-to and 8 is the group site. Per-site maximums of 23 ft or more: 2-6, 13-16, 18, 19 and 21-24 (35 ft at 4, 5, 6, 14 and 19); sites 1, 17 and 20 are 20-22 ft. Pull-throughs at 14 (35 ft) and 20 (20 ft).

facilities.note: One double vault toilet. No drinking water or trash service: bring water, pack out trash, bring firewood.

booking.note: Sites 5-21 reservable on recreation.gov 3 months ahead; an unreserved one can be taken first come for one night at the pay station. Sites 1-4 and 22-24 are first come, first served (pay at the station on arrival).

name: Aspen Grove Campground (Blackfoot River, Lincoln)
note: Helena-Lewis and Clark NF (Lincoln RD) campground on the upper Blackfoot River, 6.5 miles east of Lincoln off MT-200 then 1/2 mile of gravel. Blackfoot River fishing (cutthroat, rainbow, brown trout, whitefish). Near Continental Divide Trail access at Rogers and Flesher passes; Indian Meadows trailhead into the Scapegoat Wilderness is 10 mi up Copper Creek Road. A separate group-use campground shares the site. --Claude

sites.note: 24 sites in 2 loops. recreation.gov gives max vehicle lengths only for the 10 reservable sites: 20-60 ft (three at 45, one each at 50 and 60).

facilities.note: 3 vault toilets, several potable-water spigots, 2 dumpsters; food storage lockers. Grizzly country: the food storage order is enforced.

booking.note: One loop is reservable on recreation.gov (10 sites; 'The reservable loop is to the east of the Host Site'); the other 13 sites are walk-in. 16 nights in a rolling 30 days. Check-in after 2 pm, check-out before 2 pm.

Gravel back-in sites in two loops: the electric sites on the north loop and along its east side, non-electric at the north end and on a small south loop; the wooded east side runs along the river. Group shelter, basketball and sand volleyball; beside the Elk River Hiking Trail and the mountain-bike trails. --Claude
