name: Lyman Lake Campsites (Hiawatha NF)
note: Ten primitive campsites lining 67-acre Lyman Lake, Hiawatha NF (Rapid River/Manistique district), off Forest Roads 2218 and 2880 (site 1 off FR 2218; site 10 is isolated on its own access road). For a 23-ft motorhome the best bets are site 5 (75x50 ft, good road access) and site 8 (level, on a hill over the lake); site 3 is a big open area but listed for tents and trailers; sites 4 and 9 have little turn-around room, 6 slopes and 7 is tents-recommended. Back-in boat access with parking between sites 6 and 7; best swimming at sites 3 and 5. Bluegill, pumpkinseed, rock bass, largemouth bass and northern pike. --Claude

sites.note: 10 primitive lakeshore sites. Catalog max vehicle lengths: 003 and 005 40 ft, 004 and 008 30 ft, 001/006/007/009/010 24 ft, 002 20 ft; 001-003 list tents and trailers only, the rest RVs too. The catalog types every site 'Pull-Through', but recreation.gov calls turn-around space 'very limited' at 4 and 9 and turning radius 'very limited' at 6, so pull_through is left unset.

facilities.note: Pack in, pack out. Dead and down firewood may be gathered around the campsite; no outside firewood. Toilets: recreation.gov says primitive toilets at sites 3, 4, 5, 8 and 9; the Forest Service page says 'Restrooms are not available at this site'.

booking.note: Reservation only from May 15 through Columbus Day: 'Walk ins are not allowed' (recreation.gov or 877-444-6777); same-day booking allowed. The site must be occupied the first night and may not be left unattended more than 24 hours. Check-in 2 p.m., check-out 11 a.m. The recreation.gov peak season runs May 15 - October 15 (2026, 2027). Run by the Forest Service, not a concession.

name: White Ranch Conservation Area
note: MDC forest area south of West Plains. Twelve designated camping spots are scattered along the area's gravel roads: each is a small cleared pull-off in the oak woods beside the road, with no pad, table, toilet or water, and most fit one rig. The pinned spot is at the crossroads 300 m east of the White Ranch Lake road; the lake (a few acres, with a picnic area and gravel ramp) is 450 m off and not in view from any spot. name: Painted Rock Conservation Area
note: Forested Osage River bluff country. The camping spot a rig can use is the gravel parking lot with a privy above Clubhouse Lake, at the end of about a mile of unimproved gravel road that drops some 200 ft from Highway 133; the designated spots themselves are small clearings in the woods beside it, on the lake's dam and along the road, suited to tents. The small lake is about 60 m away through the trees and not in view from the lot. Other spots are mapped at the Osage Bluff Scenic Trail lot off Highway 133 and along a grown-in track in the middle of the area. Lot and spot sizes are not published. --Claude

name: Rudolf Bennitt Conservation Area
note: 27 numbered primitive sites in six small camps spread over the area, each with a fire ring and lantern post and nothing else. This pin is sites 25-27 on the open point at 48-acre Bennitt Lake, the only camp closed to horses, with a privy, boat ramp and fishing dock close by. Sites 1-24 are shared with horse campers and have hitching posts; the largest group, sites 6-16, is a gravel loop off County Road 2920 on the west side. Camping along roads and in parking lots is allowed only in firearms deer season. --Claude

name: Ranacker Conservation Area
note: Six primitive camping spots, each at a small gravel lot. Four are along the improved gravel road in from Route RA at the north end: a gravel turnaround loop in an open bottom on the bank of Peno Creek, just before the road's concrete bridge over the creek, the only one of the six by water (the pin, 10 to 15 m from the creek); two roadside lots in timber past the shooting range; and the lot with a privy where the road ends. Two more sit on their own on county roads at the east side and the south edge (the south one has a privy and a mown lawn). No pads, tables or water. --Claude

name: Riverbreaks Conservation Area
note: Six primitive camping spots in the loess hills above the Missouri River floodplain, each one a small gravel parking lot (lettered A to G on the area map) with room to camp beside it. Five are in the west tract: two at the foot of the bluff off Route T, both beside a busy railroad line, and three up on the ridge along gravel Quebec Road, where the lot at the road bend near the shooting range has open mown ground next to it. The sixth is the trailhead lot by a fishing pond in the east tract, off Route O; the multi-use trails that start there are open to horses. The river itself is miles off across the floodplain and not in view. No pads, tables or water; the only privy is at the shooting range. Bare gravel lots with no designated sites. --Claude

name: Pea Ridge Conservation Area
note: Six primitive spots are mapped, and only the Indian Creek camp (this pin) has a season longer than firearms deer season. It is in the main tract off Highway 185: about 1.5 km of gravel road to a gravel turnaround in open bottomland woods a short walk from the creek. The Hi Pointe spot, 10 km east on Pelican Ridge Road, is a short gravel spur with a turnaround in oak-pine woods. The other four are unmarked spots in the woods beside roadside parking lots in the main tract. No facilities, and spot length is not published. --Claude

name: Peck Ranch Conservation Area
note: Five small primitive camping areas strung along the last 2 km of the gravel entrance road west of the area headquarters, in oak-pine woods: Mill Creek (a gravel pull-off at a bend, the first reached), Long Hollow (a gravel loop), Pine Loop and Little Pine (in pine stands beside the road) and Possum Hollow (an open mown field with a gravel lot opposite the headquarters, beside the shooting range). Three have an accessible privy. The four on the north side of the road are outside the fenced elk refuge, whose gate is at the headquarters and opens in daylight only. About 7 miles of gravel from the end of Route H; the agency warns that Peck Ranch gravel roads may need good ground clearance and can be cut by high water at stream crossings. Spot length is not published. --Claude

Two primitive spots, both small gravel pull-offs in dense timber on the area's gravel road: one just inside the Route A entrance, the other about 900 m south near Strip Pit 4. The water-filled pits are 40-60 m away through the trees and not in view. No open fires. No facilities, and the lots are small; spot length is not published. --Claude

Reached by gravel road from the end of Route D at Brazeau; when the Chester river gauge reaches 32.5 ft the bridge into the area is impassable. --Claude

name: Schell-Osage Conservation Area
note: Two primitive campgrounds about 1 km apart on the same area road, each with a privy. The larger (this pin) is a gravel loop of eight or nine pull-in spurs on a wooded knoll above Schell Lake's south shore; the smaller, three or four spurs, is beside the Atkinson Lake boat ramp. No open fires. The area reopened in October 2026 after a wetland renovation, and Schell Lake is closed to fishing while the fishery rebuilds. Parts of the area, Atkinson Lake among them, are refuge closed to all public use Oct 15 to Mar 1. MDC does not say whether either campground lies inside the closed part, so call the area office before a trip in those months. --Claude

name: Yellow Creek Conservation Area
note: Bottomland forest along an unchannelized stretch of Yellow Creek, beside Swan Lake National Wildlife Refuge. Two designated camping areas on Hog Ridge Avenue, 400 m apart with the road's creek bridge between them. The northern one is a small gravel lot at the trailhead, a rig or two at most; the southern one is only a roadside pull-off under the trees. No pads, tables, toilets or water. Yellow Creek bends within 50 m of the northern lot behind timber. The bottoms flood; the suspension footbridge on the trail is out of service (flood damage). --Claude

name: William R. Logan Conservation Area
note: MDC area of wooded hills and small fishing lakes north of Silex. Two primitive camping areas, each with a privy and no pads, tables or water: one off County Road 226 on the west side, a small gravel lot and turnaround in the woods south of Lake 4; the other on Robey Road south of Route RA, a gravel loop about 50 m across around a grass island, across the road from the Lake 7 lot. note: Two primitive camping spots at Pin Oak Lake, in open prairie. name: Worthwine Island Conservation Area
note: Missouri River bottomland south-west of Amazonia, on the river side of the levee. Two designated camping areas, each a bare gravel lot with no pads, tables, toilets or water: one where County Road 396 crosses the levee, the other about 1.4 km north along the levee road, at the end of a short spur about 100 m from the river bank. The river is hidden by bottomland timber at both. Open fires only in the designated camping areas. The ground is river bottom that floods. --Claude

name: Marion Bottoms Conservation Area
note: Missouri Department of Conservation floodplain area of bottomland forest, wetlands and old fields on the Missouri River north of Marion, with six miles of river frontage reached by mowed paths and levees closed to vehicles. MDC's map marks one primitive camping area on open grass beside the entrance parking lot, just east of the railroad crossing on Moniteau Creek Road; no defined sites or amenities. The area has no flood protection: the road can close when the river floods or the surface is impassable, and there is only one way in and out. --Claude

name: Thomas Hill Reservoir Conservation Area
note: The Highway T campground, the only place camping is allowed on this power-plant cooling reservoir: a built campground on a point on the south side of Route T at the bridge, with concrete pads, a small shelter at each site and fire grates, in two loops. Only the west loop's three lake-side pads are on the water, about 40 m from it across mown grass; the east loop sits back by the road. Boat ramp, courtesy dock and jetty at the foot of the campground. One camping unit and six people per numbered site. The arm north of Route T is a waterfowl refuge. --Claude

name: Clark State Fishing Lake
note: KDWP state fishing lake: a 300-acre lake in the canyon country of Clark County, south of Kingsdown on K-94. Camping is allowed throughout the area, with four named primitive camping/day-use areas: South End (at the dam), East Shore (a gravel loop on a point and a gravel lane along the shore, off K-94), Bloom Cove (west shore, by county gravel road) and North End (upper end). No marked sites. Boats for fishing only. --Claude

booking.note: Free, first come; no reservations at Kansas state fishing lakes. Seven consecutive days at a state fishing lake, then five days away (K.A.R. 115-8-9(c), amended 2023); a longer stay needs a written KDWP permit.

name: Jewell State Fishing Lake
note: KDWP state fishing lake in grassland hills between Glen Elder and Lovewell reservoirs. Camping only at six designated sites around the lake (Cattail Cove, Panfish Flats, Willow's Weep, Catfish Cove, Plum Thicket Shores, Ash Creek); Trappers Hollow, Turtlehead Bend and Limestone Point are day use only, and no camping at the reservable group shelter. sites.note: 14 full-hookup sites (017-030) with 50-ft paved back-in driveways; 16 non-electric sites (001-016) with 20-ft back-in driveways, too short for a 23-ft rig. Five camper cabins in the same campground.

booking.note: Booking page: campsites (electric and non-electric) 'Reservations can be made for today and can be made up to 6 Month(s) in advance.' Holiday weekends (Memorial Day, July 4th, Labor Day) need 2 nights, cut to 1 night when booking within 14 days of arrival. The park gate is locked daily at posted closing hours (general park hours 7am-9pm); no vehicle access after closing except in an emergency.

name: Old Veteran's Lake Campground - Governor Earl Peshtigo River State Forest
note: Small rustic campground on the east shore of Old Veteran's Lake in the Governor Earl Peshtigo River State Forest, on Parkway Road about 3.5 miles north of County X near Crivitz, with a small swimming beach and the Old Vet's Lake hiking loop. Generators are not allowed. The longest rig reported here is 21 ft; larger rigs are unproven on the narrow forest road. --Claude

name: Bray Creek State Forest Campground
note: Secluded rustic Michigan DNR state forest campground on the Baldwin River at its confluence with Bray Creek, 2.3 miles northeast of Baldwin via M-37, Merriville Road and 40th Street. Trout fishing; hiking and mountain biking on the Pine Forest Pathway; ORV routes nearby (Little O/Big O 4 miles northwest). --Claude

facilities.note: Drinking water from a hand-pump well. Carry-in access to the Baldwin River down a short set of stairs beside the day-use parking area (room for 2-3 vehicles). ORVs may be ridden from a campsite to reach the area's routes; other ORV use in the campground is prohibited.

booking.note: No reservations or advance payment. Registration is online or by phone using the number or website posted at the campground, no earlier than 8 a.m. on the day of arrival; the site must then be set up and occupied. Clip the hang tag (site, due-out date, booking number) to the site post.

sites.note: Nine sites 'for tent and small trailer use' (the DNR's standard state forest wording). No length limit posted. One camping unit and six people per site.

name: Schecks Place State Forest Campground
note: Rustic state forest campground on the banks of the Boardman River (a Blue Ribbon trout stream and designated Natural River), 12 miles southwest of Williamsburg via Williamsburg, Supply and Brown Bridge roads, Grand Traverse County; a stop on the Shore-to-Shore Trail. Shaded sites, a fishing platform on the river and paddle-in access for canoe campers. ORVs and snowmobiles may ride between the campground and nearby trails (Grand Traverse Motorcycle Trail 1 mile south). The adjacent Schecks Place Trail Camp is a separate 200-person equestrian group camp, not this entry. --Claude

booking.note: First-come: register online or by phone (number and website posted at the campground) no earlier than 8 a.m. on the day of arrival, then set up and occupy the site and clip the hang tag to the site post. No advance payments or reservations.

sites.note: 30 sites 'for tent and small-to-medium trailer use' (no length posted). One camping unit and six people per site.

name: Traverse City State Park Campground
note: Keith J. Charters Traverse City State Park: an urban Michigan DNR campground 2 miles from downtown Traverse City, in three wooded loops (West, Central, East). The day-use area, directly across US-31 by a pedestrian crossing, has a quarter-mile sandy beach and buoyed swim area on the East Arm of Grand Traverse Bay. The paved TART Trail runs beside the park, linking to the Leelanau Trail. --Claude

sites.note: 336 campsites on the booking maps (the DNR page says 338): West Loop 63, Central 128, East 145, wooded with lots of tree cover. Allowed equipment is 25-50 ft at 294 sites and 20 ft or unlisted at 42; four pull-throughs (West 108, 201, 202; East 250). A 10-site bike-loop overflow area, two mini cabins and a rustic group camp are separate.

facilities.note: Sanitation station with potable water and two lanes (expanded in the 2026 rebuild); the toilet/shower buildings are open for the whole reservable season. Recycling in the campground.

booking.note: Reserve online on MiDNRReservations or at 800-447-2757; group-site reservations by calling the park at 231-922-5270. The DNR rates table gives no reservation season for these loops.

name: Jordanelle State Park - Hailstone Campground
note: Hailstone, the main recreation area of Jordanelle State Park, on the west shore of Jordanelle Reservoir off US-40 exit 8, a few miles from Park City and above the Heber Valley. About 120 RV sites in several open loops - most with water and 30 or 30/50-amp electric, 21 full hookup - many long enough for big rigs, plus tent sites, cabins, marina, swim beach, dump station and a designated International Dark Sky Park. Little shade. Construction outside the park boundary was audible in 2026. Rock Cliff (east end, walk-in tent) and Ross Creek are separate areas. Reservable on Utah State Parks' ReserveAmerica site. --Claude

name: Beavers Bend State Park - Lower Mountain Fork Campgrounds (Acorn, Buckeye, Cypress, Fern, Pine Ridge)
note: The main RV campgrounds of Beavers Bend State Park, strung along the trout-stocked lower Mountain Fork River below Broken Bow Lake dam, north of Broken Bow. About 110 RV sites in four loops: Buckeye (28 long full-hookup 50-amp pull-throughs) and Pine Ridge (11 full hookup) take big rigs; Cypress (51, 30-amp) and Acorn (22, 30/50-amp) are water/electric under tall pines. The park's Hochatown-area loops on Broken Bow Lake are a separate entry. Reservable on Oklahoma State Parks' ReserveAmerica site; busy on summer and fall weekends. Fern loop (11 RV sites, 30-amp, 30-35 ft) sits in the same River Area by the miniature train and stables. --Claude

note: Rustic Michigan DNR state forest campground on Ski-kwe zaag'igan Lake (the lake and campground were renamed in 2023; formerly Squaw Lake), 15 miles southwest of Republic via M-95, Marquette County; managed from Bewabic State Park. name: Dutch Treat Camping & Recreation
note: Family campground opened in August 1969 in a gravel pit dug for the highway, and run by three generations of the Riemersma family.  It has a fishing pond with boat rentals, a pool (added in 1975), a rec room, an activity field, a playground and PumpkinFest, and rents cabins.  Rustic pop-up sites take stays of a week at most, and clubs are welcome. --Claude

name: Beaver Trail Campground
note: Country campground in Ogemaw County beside a big pond stocked for catch-and-release fishing, with a swimming beach and kayaks, a canoe and paddle boats.  There is volleyball, a playground, a sharing library, basketball hoops and a community area by the pond.  Campers can ride from the campground to the ORV and snowmobile trails, and DNR ORV licences are sold.  It rents tents, sleeping bags, a 2019 VLite camper and cabins.  Clear Lake's public boat launch is a mile away, Ogemaw Nature Park just over 2 miles, and the Rifle River Recreation Area is nearby.  Storage costs $35 a month; electric-only sites can have their fresh-water tanks filled, or their holding tanks emptied by the honey wagon, for a fee, and propane is sold.  A site may have two dogs at most. --Claude

name: Trails End Campground
note: Rustic wooded campground around a small lake 1/2 mile west of Copper Harbor on M-26, with camper cabins. Operator: 'most sites accommodate a small pop up camper and some sites accommodate larger RVs' ('several sites that offer a deep, level parking surface to facilitate boondocking with your big rig') - pick a larger site for a 23-ft rig. Spigots are not threaded for a hose: fill tanks before arriving. Not on Lake Superior (bike trail to Hunter's Point). Winter camping allowed, no plowing. --Claude

name: Mecosta Pines Campground
note: Campground beside the Little Muskegon River near Morley, with something going on every weekend: kids' crafts, games, theme weekends, cornhole, dance parties and karaoke.  A swimming pool opens from Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day weekend, and there is a jump pad, mini-golf, a basketball court, a game room and rec room, and a large picnic area by the river.  It has an LP fill station and delivers firewood and ice to the site, and bikers on the White Pine Bike Trail get special rustic rates Sunday to Thursday.  Cabins and park models are rented. --Claude

sites.note: The operator's site map shows about 122 numbered RV sites: about 75 seasonal full-hookup sites, about 30 water/electric and 17 full-hookup transient sites, and 3 park-model rentals, plus 10 primitive tent sites (A-J) by the Little Muskegon River. Campspot sells 48 RV sites: 30-amp W/E (20), 50-amp W/E (10), full-hookup back-in (11) and full-hookup pull-through (7), lengths to 45-50 ft.

booking.note: The 2-night weekend minimum runs Memorial Day to Labor Day; holiday weekends take 3 nights including Friday and Saturday. Campspot refused Saturday arrivals and departures in June 2027. Deposit one night; $20 cancellation fee, 7 days' notice (14 for holidays). Check-in 1-8pm, check-out 11am.

note: Campground in natural woods along Duke Creek, an official trout stream (fishing needs a license), 18 miles north of Grand Rapids in Cedar Springs.  Every weekend brings arts and crafts, an activity, a penny dive and a wagon ride, and there are hiking trails and a pool with no lifeguard on duty.  Sites have a fire ring and a picnic table but no grill.  Aggressive dog breeds aren't allowed, nor is outside firewood.  Cabins and park models are also rented. --Claude

note: Family-owned camp on 140 wooded acres along the east shore of Long Lake south of Harrison (6651 N Eberhart Ave), with half a mile of lakefront, three beaches, docks, canoes, kayaks and paddle boats and a private island; also cabins, a lodge and weddings/events. RV sites are rustic back-in sites, rustic waterfront (bluff) sites and newly built 30/50-amp electric sites; arrive with a full fresh-water tank. Not on RV Life; Campspot 4.7 over 31 verified reviews; Good Sam lists it unrated. --Claude

note: Large RV campground run by Covenant Hills Camp & Retreat, a Christian youth/family camp near Otisville, open to the public by the night alongside the camp's own programs. There are two heated pools (no lifeguard), volleyball, tetherball, ping-pong, hiking, disc golf and a fish-cleaning station, and mobile pump-outs come on Mondays and Fridays.  Log cabins sleep five, and golf carts, ATVs and UTVs aren't allowed in the campground. --Claude

name: Heart of the Forest RV Park
note: RV park in the Manistee National Forest at Wellston, with the Whitetail Party Mart at its entrance, Fawn Crest Golf Course a short walk away, Tippy Dam 3 miles off and Lake Michigan 17 miles west on M-55. The person booking must be 21, seasonal campers go through a background check, and quiet hours run from 10 p.m. to 7 a.m. --Claude

name: Brush Creek Campground
note: Campground, family-owned since 1977, on over 50 wooded acres beside Brush Creek in Lawrence, just south of I-94 at Exit 52.  There are hiking trails, a playground and fishing; firewood costs $7 a bundle and visitors $5 each.  Generators, fireworks and chainsaws aren't allowed, golf carts, ATVs and UTVs need permission, and quiet hours run from 11 p.m. to 8 a.m. --Claude

name: Poppy's Family Campground
note: Family campground five miles southwest of downtown Gaylord, near Otsego Lake and thousands of acres of state forest.  It has an indoor pool and spa, an outdoor waterslide, a playground, a stocked trout lake for fishing and an 18-hole mini golf course, plus basketball, horseshoes, kayak rentals and an arcade; a fitness center is being developed.  There are picnic areas and fire pits, cabins and campers are rented, and there is an event venue. --Claude

name: Wooded Acres Family Campground
note: Campground near Houghton Lake, Michigan's largest inland lake by surface area, with large wooded sites.  There is a pool (no lifeguard), a fishing pond, basketball, volleyball, horseshoes, a large open playground and a dog run; propane is sold, firewood is delivered to the site, and ORV trails are nearby.  Cabins and a bunk house are rented, there are seasonal sites, and monthly camping is offered after Labor Day.  Outside firewood isn't allowed, and quiet hours run from 10 p.m. to 7 a.m. --Claude

sites.note: Back-in electric-only sites on the outer edges (10 with 30-amp, 4 with 30/50-amp), water/electric and full-hookup back-ins, and 30/50-amp full-hookup pull-throughs. Campspot's longest RV site is 45 ft (premium pull-through); the plain water + 30-amp sites run to 34 ft. Seasonal sites are 30-amp only or 30-amp with water.

name: Spirit Springs Campground
note: Campground in rolling hills near Marcellus, with fishing, hiking and walking trails, a pool and a playground.  RV sites have full hookups on gravel, or water, electric and greywater, with the black tank dumped at the end of the stay; power is a 110-volt plug on a 30-amp breaker, so adapters may be needed.  The Olive Branch camper and the Mustard Seed cabin are rented, and there is a primitive tent site. --Claude

name: Winding Creek Camp
note: Christian non-profit camp near Hastings that rents campsites and cabins by the day or week alongside its camps and retreats for youth, adults and families.  It has an outdoor pool (Memorial Day to Labor Day), gaga ball pits, basketball, volleyball, tetherball, a playground, a 9-hole frisbee golf course and a nature trail; firewood is $5 a bundle, and seasonal sites cost $1,200 a year.  Tobacco, alcohol and illegal drugs aren't allowed, campers are expected to dress modestly, and quiet hours run from 10 p.m. to 8 a.m. --Claude

name: Sharp Park Campground
note: Family campground on Turner Lake, a natural 18-acre lake with a sandy beach (no lifeguard), bordered by state land and close to Deep Lake, Gun Lake and the Yankee Springs Recreation Area.  Some sites are lakeside.  Kayaks, canoes, rowboats and paddleboards rent for $5 an hour on site or $20 an hour off site, and paddleboats for $10 for the first hour and $5 for each hour after; there are hiking trails and a fenced dog park.  Annual events include bingo, crafts, a kayak race, cornhole and fishing tournaments and live music; ice costs $4 a bag and firewood $6 a bundle, which can be delivered to the site.  Golf carts are allowed with a licensed driver 16 or older and insurance, and cabins are rented. --Claude

booking.note: Book on Campspot ('Book Now') or by phone; full payment at booking. 2027 season reservations open now. Refund in full 28+ days out, 75% at 15-27 days, 50% at 8-14, none within 7. Seasonal sites by phone; waitlist for 2026.

name: War Hill Park Campground
note: Dawson County park on a Lake Lanier peninsula off GA-53 east of Dawsonville, with a swimming beach, pier and four boat ramps; fishing tournaments launch from the ramps early in the morning. Alcohol prohibited. --Claude

sites.note: 14 sites, each with its own posted camper length: 30 ft (sites 1 and 10), 40 ft (2, 3, 4, 9, 11, 13), 45 ft (5, 7, 8), 50 ft (12, 14); site 6's back-in driveway runs up to 80 ft but is slightly elevated. name: Lake Capote Recreation Area
note: Southern Ute Indian Tribe recreation area on CO-151 south of Pagosa Springs, run by the tribe's Division of Wildlife around a stocked fishing lake; no Colorado fishing license needed, but a daily lake permit is. Tribal rangers patrol; no alcohol or firearms. --Claude

facilities.note: Bathhouse with toilets, sinks and showers; dump station on the road west of the bathhouse. The bait shop sells food, snacks, drinks and fishing supplies and has a fish-cleaning station and an emergency phone (limited cell reception).

season.note: 2026 schedule: March 5-29 open Thursday to Sunday only (campers stay Thursday to Saturday nights and leave by Sunday afternoon); March 30 - October 27 open daily; closed for the season October 28. No water in the campground in March or October.

name: North Cove Campground (South Republican SWA)
note: Colorado Parks and Wildlife campground at the South Republican State Wildlife Area, the former Bonny Lake State Park: the reservoir was partly drained and the park became a wildlife area in October 2011, and North Cove is one of two campgrounds left open (East Beach is the other) with limited amenities. Dry dirt-pad sites among scattered trees on a bench above the old lake bed. --Claude

entrance.name: State Wildlife Area pass
entrance.waived_by: an annual Colorado fishing, small-game, big-game or turkey license

fees.note: Two people, one night: $40. There is no camping fee; the cost is Colorado Parks and Wildlife's State Wildlife Area pass, which everyone 16 or older needs on the property. 2 people x 2 one-day passes x $10 = $40: a one-day pass is valid only on the date printed on it, and a night spans the arrival and departure dates. Nobody holding an annual Colorado fishing, small-game, big-game or turkey license needs the pass, and neither do under-16s. An annual SWA pass is $43.87 (March 1 to March 31 of the next year; youth/senior $11.96). The pass is per person, not per vehicle; buy it online or in the My CPW app, up to 60 days ahead. (AWH 2026-10-11: price as two people, one night.)

Full-hookup sites sit back in the trees, partial-hookup sites on the hillside above Cherry Creek, and primitive tent-or-RV spaces along the lake and creek. --Claude

Gravel back-in sites with picnic table and fire pit; portable restroom; community fire pit at 'The Point'; river access by a ramp and a sandbar beach. Dump station at Love's on Hwy 2 (~1 mi, $10 or less). Daily, weekly and monthly rates. --Claude

booking.note: Book online (Firefly), by email or by phone. Cancel at least 24 hours ahead or pay one night; no refunds after check-in.

The RV sites sit back from the water; the creek-side sites are tent sites on tent island, between the creek and the spring and reached by footbridge. name: Mountain Creek Family Resort
note: Family float resort on the Niangua River near Eldridge: canoe, kayak and raft trips, a waterslide, playgrounds, cabins and a store. The RV sites are on an open field well back from the river, with woods and the primitive tent area between; several electric + water sites come with a gazebo. Water at sites 21-38 is on a well put in in July 2024 (the operator recommends a pressure regulator). Coolers over 48 quarts, styrofoam and glass are not allowed. Primitive tent camping is priced per person. --Claude

name: Little Sinkin Creek RV Resort & Campground
note: Ozark RV park in the Sinkin Creek valley in Mark Twain National Forest country west of Bunker (1960 County Road 5630), reached by 2 miles of well-maintained gravel off Highway A; the operator warns that GPS routes via County Road 565 / Logger's Lake Road are not RV friendly. It markets itself to UTV/SxS riders, who ride out on forest and county roads; also floating, hiking and a fishing pond. Self check-in; sites are chosen on arrival. name: Sinking Creek Ranch
note: Ozarks ranch campground near Bunker, with the Mark Twain National Forest on three sides: one row of 20 long gravel back-in pads along spring-fed Sinking Creek, facing open pasture, plus glamping tents and creekside tent sites. Private dirt-bike and side-by-side trails start at the pads and riders are common. Horses by arrangement. Little cell service. The operator warns trailers off Highway A: come in on Highway 72 or 19. --Claude

name: Colossal Cave Mountain Park
note: Pima County-owned park (concession-run) on Old Spanish Trail east of Vail. RV/car camping at about 30 individual sites in Posta Quemada canyon (CCC-built picnic areas El Bosquecito and La Selvilla, with tables and grills; water and restrooms there). Check in and pay at the Cave Shop first; park hours 8am-4pm and the front gates are locked at night. Pin is the cave parking lot; the camping areas are in the canyon below it and could not be located precisely. --Claude

name: Heritage Campsite & RV Park
note: Campground and RV park at 3961 Hwy 97, Monte Lake (between Westwold and Falkland, 30 minutes from Kamloops), on a pine slope across the highway from the lake: up to 40 sites with 30A power, water and sewer, big rigs and pull-throughs; showers, toilets, laundry, Wi-Fi, tipi rentals; no wood fires. Posted (May 2026): full hookup C$270 weekly, C$850 monthly, plus taxes; tenting C$20. Book by phone or e-mail. Open year-round. Caveat (2026-10-09): long-stay residents share the park - about 25 units sit on the pads in mid-April imagery, as many as in June - so perhaps 15 sites turn over to travellers. --Claude

name: Crazy Creek Hot Pools Resort
note: Hot-pools resort at 6162 Trans-Canada Hwy, Malakwa, in the Eagle River valley between Sicamous and Revelstoke: 97 RV and tent sites among cabins - 22 forest full-hookup (about 35 ft, up to 50A, full service year-round), 23 premium full-hookup (about 50 ft, 30A), 14 XL pull-throughs (about 60 ft), 16 budget 30A/15A power-and-water sites (about 25 ft) and 22 unserviced small-RV/tent sites; sani-dump, playgrounds, bike track, dog park; three hot pools and a cold plunge (separate admission). 15A power-and-water standard site (trailers to 26 ft, motorhomes to 32 ft). Booked online (WebRez - its search sits behind a human check, so a normal browser is needed). Open 365 days; water May long weekend to Thanksgiving except the forest sites. An active CP rail line runs along the property's south side. --Claude

name: Bald Eagle State Forest Campsites 064 Tower Road, 065 Swift Run Road, 066 Swift Run Road (Hickernell)
note: Three separate sites strung along about 0.8 mile of forest road, one camping unit each: 064 on Tower Road north of the Swift Run Road and Locust Ridge intersections (toward the fire tower), 065 on Swift Run Road east of Locust Ridge Road, and 066 on Swift Run Road west of Pine Ridge Trail. All are gravel back-ins in the woods; 065 is the levellest, 064's pad and 066's pad and 290-ft driveway are graded moderate. DCNR describes all three as large enough for horse trailers. Fire rings and picnic tables, nothing else. From PA 235 by Water Company Road and Timber Road, about 6 miles. State forest roads are not plowed in winter, and some Bald Eagle roads need 4WD and high clearance: check the route. --Claude

name: Buchanan State Forest Campsite BV002 Two Mile (Bear Valley)
note: A gravel parking lot beside Bear Valley Road at the Two Mile Trail junction, in plain view of the road; DCNR rates it for one camper trailer or two vehicles with tents. Gravel forest road all the way in: about 4.8 miles from Upper Strasburg Road (OpenStreetMap labels the last 2 miles Broad Run Road). A stream runs about 300 ft away. No toilet; pack out trash. State forest roads get no winter maintenance and are not plowed. --Claude

State forest roads get no winter maintenance and are not plowed. --Claude

name: Buchanan State Forest Campsite BV019 Broad Mountain Landing 2 (Bear Valley)
note: Site BV019 (Broad Mountain Landing 2) on Broad Mountain Road, 0.1 mile north of Lookout Trail: an old log landing, a bare clearing about 40 m by 15 m at the end of a 325-ft track off the road, that DCNR says holds one camper trailer or two vehicles with tents. Easy access and somewhat secluded; no fire ring or picnic table is listed. About 3 miles of Broad Mountain Road along the ridge from Shearer Road above Upper Strasburg. State forest roads are not plowed in winter. --Claude

name: Buchanan State Forest Campsite CV017 Lawhead (Chaneysville)
note: A grass opening about 50 m long and 15 m wide at the junction of Robinson Road and Lawhead Trail, somewhat secluded; the agency says it holds one camper trailer. Pack out trash. State forest roads are not plowed in winter. --Claude

name: Buchanan State Forest Campsite SH002 Bark Road A (Sideling Hill)
note: A grass pull-in off Bark Road, 0.14 mile from Betsey Road and in sight of the road; the agency says it holds 'one small camper trailer or one vehicle with tents', and lists the site as 50 by 40 ft. It lies under hardwood canopy and no clearing shows on imagery, so the size of the pad is not confirmed. Grass, so soft after rain. Bark Road is a forest road off Betsey Road, about 2 miles from Pleasant Valley Road near the US 30 / I-70 junction east of Breezewood. Pack out trash. State forest roads are not plowed in winter. --Claude

name: Buchanan State Forest Campsite SH007 Mitchell Trail (Sideling Hill)
note: A grass clearing in the woods, about 40 m by 15 m on imagery, just past the fork of Mitchell Trail and about 0.2 mile off Bark Road; secluded, with a stone fire ring. The last stretch is the trail itself, a two-track that DCNR calls 'a little rough', and the site is grass, so it may be soft when wet. Back-in. Bark Road is gravel, about 1.2 miles from US 30 on top of Sideling Hill to Mitchell Trail. No toilet; pack out trash. State forest roads get no winter maintenance and are not plowed. --Claude

name: Buchanan State Forest Campsite SH008 Culvert Field (Sideling Hill)
note: A mown grass field, about 150 m by 110 m on imagery, at the end of Fire Tower Road and booked as a single site: open, with almost no shade, and well away from traffic. A gate at the entrance has to be opened and closed behind each vehicle. The whole field is grass with no hardened pad, so pick ground with care after rain. Gravel all the way in: about 0.3 mile of Bark Road from US 30 on top of Sideling Hill, then 0.3 mile of Fire Tower Road. No toilet; pack out trash. State forest roads get no winter maintenance and are not plowed. --Claude

name: Buchanan State Forest Campsite SH017 Jerry Road (Sideling Hill)
note: A small gravel-and-grass pull-off on the south side of Jerry Road, right at the road edge and in plain view of passing traffic; imagery shows an apron about 25 m wide and 15 m deep. DCNR sizes it for 'one small camper trailer' and grades the site moderate: the ground climbs away from the road at roughly 8 percent, so leveling takes some work, and the grass part may be soft when wet. Back-in. Jerry Road is gravel, 1 mile from US 30. An intermittent stream runs about 150 ft away across the road. No toilet; pack out trash. State forest roads get no winter maintenance and are not plowed. --Claude

name: Buchanan State Forest Campsite SH023 Oregon Ball Field (Sideling Hill)
note: A grass field about 80 m by 60 m, the old Oregon ball field, beside the abandoned Pennsylvania Turnpike underpass on Oregon Road about 1.2 miles from PA 915. One booking takes the whole field; there is no pad, parking is on the grass, and the agency warns 'be cautious with parking when wet, especially with trailers'. It is popular with horse campers and is offered for group camping and events. A small stream runs about 60 m away in the woods. Pack out trash. State forest roads are not plowed in winter. --Claude

name: Buchanan State Forest Campsites BV004 Pipeline East, BV005 Pipeline West, BV007 Broad Mountain West, BV008 Clarks Knob (Bear Valley)
note: Four separate sites strung along 1.3 km of Broad Mountain Road, an unpaved ridge-top forest road reached from Upper Strasburg Road by Bear Valley Road; all are in full sun and in sight of the road. BV004 Pipeline East and BV005 Pipeline West are mown strips of a pipeline right-of-way on either side of the road, 100 m apart: BV004 has a loop track to pull through, BV005 is a parallel pull-off. BV007 Broad Mountain West is an open grass-and-gravel lot about 40 m across, 280 m farther north-east, also parallel. BV008 Clarks Knob is a grass triangle in the fork of Broad Mountain Road and Clarks Knob Road, 0.9 km beyond BV007, pull-through. BV008 is closed for evaluation and maintenance: as of 2026-11-10 none of its nights can be booked through 2026-12-31, while nights from 2027-01-01 are on sale. Pack out trash. State forest roads are not plowed in winter. --Claude

name: Buchanan State Forest Campsites SH012 Akersville E, SH013 Akersville D, SH014 Akersville C (Sideling Hill)
note: Three separate grass landings off Akersville Road, 0.8 (C), 1.05 (D) and 1.3 (E) miles from US 30; the pin is on D. Each sits back in the woods at the end of its own grass two-track: about 70 to 80 m for D and E, about 40 m for C, with wheel ruts showing on D's track in imagery. DCNR sizes D and E for two camper trailers and C for one, and says of all three 'Access road is a little rough, but site is secluded from road'. Nothing is hardened, so the driveways and landings will be soft after rain. Back-in. Akersville Road is gravel. No toilet; pack out trash. State forest roads get no winter maintenance and are not plowed. ReserveAmerica lists all three as walk-up only, with nothing bookable online, and DCNR does not say how a walk-up permit is issued: call the Buchanan district office before going. --Claude

name: Buchanan State Forest Campsites SH027 Summit Road A, SH028 Summit Road B, SH029 Summit Road C (Sideling Hill)
note: Three sites off Summit Road, the forest road along the top of Sideling Hill, spread over 0.8 mile and each set 150 to 200 ft back from the road. Summit Road C is an open grass-and-gravel clearing about 40 m across, reached by a gravel track that drops about 4.5 m from the road (about 7%). Summit Road B is a smaller clearing the agency calls somewhat secluded. Summit Road A is a small grass pull-in in sight of the road, listed at 30 ft and described as holding one vehicle with tents. Grass at A and B is soft after rain. Summit Road leaves State Route 4006 off North Valley Road, north of US 30 at Harrisonville; the sites are about 1.8, 2.3 and 2.6 miles along it. Pack out trash. State forest roads are not plowed in winter. --Claude

name: Cornplanter State Forest Campsite 001 Cornplanter (Hunter Run)
note: A gravel pull-through beside Jamison Run Road in the Hunter Run tract, under conifers, with a picnic table and fire ring; the pad is listed at 13 ft wide. Reach it only from the north: PA 36, Neilltown Road about 2.1 miles, then Jamison Run Road about 1.4 miles (GPS units may call it Depot Street). PennDOT has closed the rest of Jamison Run/Dawson Run Road for erosion (advisory read November 2026), and the agency says it may be necessary to drive past 'Road Closure' signs to reach the site. Oil-field traffic uses the roads in this part of the forest. Pack out trash. --Claude

name: Delaware State Forest Campsite E007 Middle Branch (Edgemere)
note: A gravel back-in beside Hay Road, where a side track leaves it, with a picnic table and fire ring. From PA 402 take Pine Flats Road about 2.2 miles, Pine Flats Colony Road for a few hundred feet, then Hay Road 0.2 mile. The agency lists a potable water source on Pine Flats Road. Pack out trash. State forest roads are not plowed in winter. --Claude

name: Delaware State Forest Campsite E012 Flat Ridge (Edgemere)
note: A small gravel pad in open hardwoods at the end of its own narrow gravel spur, about 55 m off Flat Ridge Road, with a picnic table and a fire ring with grill. DCNR's Edgemere map classes it 'Small Trailer, RV, Tent', the smaller of its two classes, and the listed pad is only 45 ft by 35 ft: a rig has to back the length of the single-lane spur or turn on the pad, and overhead clearance is posted at 15 ft. The ground is level. Flat Ridge Road is an unpaved forest road, 1.1 miles north from Bushkill Falls Road (3 miles south from Silver Lake Road). No toilet; pack out trash. State forest roads get no winter maintenance and are not plowed. --Claude

name: Delaware State Forest Campsite E013 CCC Camp (Edgemere)
note: A narrow gravel pull-in, listed at 12 ft wide, at the end of a 280-ft drive off the south side of Silver Lake Road, shaded, with a picnic table and fire ring. The booking page calls the driveway grade moderate; the site sits about 9 m above the road. Silver Lake Road is paved and runs between PA 402 (about 5 miles) and PA 739 (about 6.7 miles). Pack out trash. State forest roads are not plowed in winter. --Claude

name: Delaware State Forest Campsites O018 Rest Stop 1, O019 Rest Stop 2 (Owego)
note: Two sites on a shared gravel track that leaves the south side of US 6 about 2.4 miles east of PA 402. Rest Stop 1 is about 75 m from the highway, in earshot of it; Rest Stop 2 is about 160 m farther in and about 13 m higher. Open woodland with no cleared pad and no rest-area building; each site is listed at 10 ft wide, with a picnic table and fire ring, and the agency also offers the pair for group camping. Pack out trash. State forest roads are not plowed in winter. --Claude

name: Delaware State Forest Campsites O020 Dimmick Meadow, O021 Yellow Pine (Owego)

note: Two open clearings off Laurel Run Road, about 0.3 mile apart, in full sun, each with a picnic table and fire ring. name: Elk State Forest Campsite 017 Middle (West Hicks)
note: A single site on the hillside above West Hicks Run Road, 5.0 miles past the East/West Hicks fork (7.2 miles from PA 555 at Hicks Run); the booking page calls it full sun. The driveway is dirt, about 300 ft long and listed as a moderate grade: elevation data puts the pad some 9 to 10 m above the road, about 10% on average, so it is a dry-weather driveway and worth walking first. The agency's campsite map layer marks the site as having no trailer access, while the booking page sells it as an RV and trailer site. The road in is a gentle valley-bottom forest road (no more than 3% over any 1.2 km), dirt or gravel. No toilet. Pack out trash. --Claude

name: Elk State Forest Campsite 050 Tangle Snake (Ridge Road North)
note: A grass-and-gravel clearing about 25 m wide and 70 m long on the ridge top, at the end of a level 270-ft gravel driveway on the west side of Ridge Road, 0.7 mile south of the Crooked Run Road junction; open to the sky. The agency's campsite map layer marks it as having no trailer access, while the booking page sells it as an RV and trailer site with a 40-ft maximum. Reaching the ridge means a long forest-road climb: from PA 155 by Cowley Hill Road the steepest stretch measures about 8.5% for 850 m (7.4% over 1.2 km), then 7 miles of rolling ridge road, dirt or gravel; dry weather is the time for it. No toilet. Pack out trash. --Claude

name: Elk State Forest Campsite 052 Gaswell (Ridge Road South)
note: A grass opening about 60 m across among conifers on the ridge, reached by a level gravel track of some 200 to 300 ft on the east side of Ridge Road, 3.6 miles south of Stillhouse Road. Not the Gaswell equestrian camping area on Bell Draft Road near Benezette, which shares the name; horses are not allowed here. Stillhouse Road climbs from PA 120 at no more than about 7% over any 1.2 km, then the ridge road is rolling; both are dirt or gravel forest roads. The other way up, Grove Hill Road from PA 120 near Driftwood, holds about 9% for over two miles. No toilet. Pack out trash. --Claude

name: Elk State Forest Campsite 060 Bronson (Montour)
note: A small site (45 by 35 ft, full sun on the booking page) up a dirt driveway of about 260 ft on the west side of Montour Road, 7.6 miles from PA 120. The driveway rises 5 to 7 m from the road, about 7 to 8% on dirt, so it is for dry weather. The agency's campsite map layer marks the site as having no trailer access, while the booking page sells it as an RV and trailer site. Montour Road from PA 120 is a severe climb: about 10% held for 2.6 miles (411 m of rise). The gentler way is from PA 872 by Elk Lick Run Road and Trout Run Road, whose one hard pitch is about 10.5% for 0.8 mile, followed by 10 miles of ridge road. All of it is dirt or gravel forest road. No toilet. Pack out trash. --Claude

name: Elk State Forest Campsite 061 Bubbling Springs (Montour)
note: A grass opening in the woods at the end of a level dirt driveway of about 170 ft on the west side of Montour Road, 13.6 miles from PA 120; soft after rain. The agency's campsite map layer marks the site as having no trailer access, while the booking page sells it as an RV and trailer site with a 40-ft maximum. Montour Road from PA 120 is a severe climb: about 10% held for 2.6 miles. The better way is from PA 872 by Elk Lick Run Road and Trout Run Road, whose one hard pitch is about 10.5% for 0.8 mile, then 4.6 miles south on Montour Road; Swank Road from First Fork Road holds about 9% for nearly 2 miles. All dirt or gravel forest road, for dry weather. No toilet. Pack out trash. --Claude

name: Hicks Run Campground (Elk State Forest)
note: The forest's one rustic campground: a gravel loop under tall conifers just up West Hicks Run Road from the East/West Hicks fork, 2.2 miles from PA 555. Each motorized site has a gravel back-in pad and a picnic table, and there is a pit or vault latrine within 300 ft. The branches of Hicks Run are 55 to 75 m off through the trees, out of sight. Hicks Run Road is a level valley road. Horses are not allowed. Bring water. Pack out trash. --Claude

name: Jakersville CCC Camp (Loyalsock State Forest)
note: Five sites on the grounds of a former CCC camp beside Loyalsock Creek, strung along a shared gravel lane (Sand Stone Lane) off Rock Run Road: one in an open meadow, the rest in a conifer plantation. The creek is 75 to 120 m away across the meadow and a line of trees. The Iron Bridge on Rock Run Road next to the camp has been closed to vehicles since September 2026 (replacement expected in 2029), so the way in is from the PA 87 end of Rock Run Road, about 4.6 miles of forest road over a hill with pitches of about 8% for up to 0.6 mile; the agency also names Loyalsock Road from PA 154 below Worlds End State Park. The agency says the sites were not designed for RVs: check each site's dimensions, and several have 15 ft of overhead clearance. No toilet. Pack out trash. --Claude

note: A small open pad right beside Bear Wallow Road, about 0.6 mile from Dry Run Road and next to the gated Browns Road (do not block the gate). The agency says the site was not designed for RVs, though its campsite map layer calls it suitable for a large trailer or RV; the pad is listed as 39 by 20 ft. Pack out trash. --Claude

name: Loyalsock State Forest Campsite 924 (Loyalsock Road)
note: A gravel pull-off on the west edge of Loyalsock Road, parked parallel to the road. The agency's campsite map layer calls it a tent-only site with no trailer access, while the booking page sells it as an RV and trailer site and adds that it was not designed for RVs; the pad is listed as only 30 by 10 ft, with 15 ft of overhead clearance. The Iron Bridge on Rock Run Road has been closed to vehicles since September 2026 (replacement expected in 2029), so the site cannot be reached from the PA 154 side of Rock Run Road: the agency says to come by Loyalsock Road off PA 154 below Worlds End State Park, or from the PA 87 side of Rock Run Road, and warns that some map apps show Loyalsock Road wrongly. No toilet. Pack out trash. --Claude

name: Masten CCC Camp (Loyalsock State Forest, sites 024, 025)
note: Two shaded grass back-in sites in the small state forest campground at the old Masten CCC camp, with a latrine within 300 ft and a picnic table at each. The agency says the sites were not designed for RVs and its campsite map layer calls them tent or small trailer/RV sites; the pads are listed as 27 by 19 ft and 29 by 23 ft, with 20 ft of overhead clearance. It also warns that map apps and GPS units misread the roads here: come from PA 14 by Masten Road (formerly Pleasant Stream Road), from Ellenton Mountain Road by Masten Road, or from Hoppestown Road by Cabbage Hollow, Cascade and Mill Creek Roads. A temporary above-ground waterline being installed in the area may bring periods of increased activity, expected at least through summer 2027. Unlike the rest of this forest's campsites, these are not rested for half the year. Pack out trash. --Claude

note: Six grass sites in the open clearing of the old Sand Spring CCC camp, off Sand Spring Road half a mile from Little Bear Creek Road (about 5 miles up from PA 87 north of Montoursville). 122 stands apart at the north end, a large full-sun back-in (100 by 70 ft); the other five sit close together along one lane, back-in or parallel, with 124 and 125 sharing a driveway and pads from 36 by 24 ft to 70 by 36 ft under 25 to 30 ft of overhead clearance. name: Peggy's Hill Parking Area (Michaux State Forest)
note: Two signed sections of the Peggy's Hill trailhead parking lot, a T-shaped gravel lot about 25 m off Old Forge Road: 'Campsites will be delineated with signs in the parking area. Please use only your defined section.' The lot is in full sun and close enough to the road for traffic noise. It is the trailhead for the forest's equestrian trails, so campers share it with day-use parking and horse trailers; each site has a hitching post and a stone fire ring. Old Forge Road is paved to the entrance. One of the four Michaux areas kept open through the winter camping season (third Sunday after Thanksgiving to April 1); forest roads get no winter maintenance. No toilet; pack out trash. --Claude

name: Sproul State Forest Campsite 025 Oxbow (Left Hand Branch Young Womans Creek)
note: A shaded streamside site near Oxbow Hollow on the Left Branch of Young Womans Creek, a pull-in at the end of a shared dirt driveway about 525 ft long, with camps nearby. Sold for trailers and RVs only, no tents, and a self-contained toilet is required. The booking page gives a 25-ft maximum vehicle length but also an equipment length of 15 ft and a 20-ft spur, on a 35 by 35 ft site with 20 ft of overhead clearance: ask the district before bringing a 23-ft rig. The agency has closed the south end of Left Branch Young Womans Creek Road indefinitely: it is gated and locked at the state forest boundary about a mile north of North Bend, where it crosses private land, and can be reached only from the north, so the booking page's directions from North Bend no longer work. As of November 2026 the site could not be booked for any night before 2 July 2027. Pack out trash. --Claude

name: Sproul State Forest Campsite HY040 (Carrier Road)
note: A single small pull-in dirt site in full sun on Carrier Road just north of King Hollow Trail, about 5.1 miles north of the Hazard Road junction in Farrandsville or 9.7 miles from PA 44. The booking page sells it as an RV, tent and trailer site, while the agency's campsite map layer records no trailer access. The booking page gives a 25-ft maximum vehicle length but only a 15-ft driveway and a 10-ft spur on a 30 by 40 ft site, so ask the district office whether a 23-ft rig fits before booking. The agency's route from Renovo follows PA 144 south 13.4 miles, turns sharp right onto Jews Run Road and reaches the site on the left in about two miles. The agency cautions that it is reached by remote dirt or gravel forest roads that may not suit low-clearance vehicles or large RVs. No table, toilet or water. Pack out trash. --Claude

name: Sproul State Forest Campsites 023, 024 Shingle Branch (Left Hand Branch Young Womans Creek)
note: Two streamside sites about 310 m apart on Left Branch Young Womans Creek Road near Shingle Branch: site 023 is the first after the Shingle Branch bridge and site 024 the second, on the right. The booking calendar read 2026-11-10 offers neither site before 2 July 2027 and gives no reason. DCNR has closed the road indefinitely from its junction with Young Womans Creek Road, gated and locked at the state forest boundary, because its southern part crosses private land; the forest beyond can be reached only from the north, so the booking pages' directions from North Bend no longer work. Campers must bring a self-contained toilet. The agency cautions that it is reached by remote dirt or gravel forest roads that may not suit low-clearance vehicles or large RVs. No table or water. Pack out trash. --Claude

note: A single shaded back-in dirt site for up to ten people on Butternut Hollow Road. name: Tuscarora State Forest Campsites 081, 082, 084 (South Block)
note: Three separate sites spread over about a mile of Laurel Run Road and Ant Hill Trail, reached over several miles of gravel forest road. Site 082 is an old log landing about 20 m by 15 m on a 200-ft gravel driveway off Laurel Run Road. Site 081 is a larger old log landing (about 35 m by 25 m) on Ant Hill Trail, at the end of a 425-ft gravel driveway the booking page grades 'Moderate'. Site 084 is a grass pull-off beside Laurel Run Road, 75 ft by 30 ft, in full sun, with no built pad. The agency's own campsite layer marks 081 as trailer-accessible and 082 and 084 as not, though the booking pages list all three for trailers up to 25 ft. A picnic table and fire ring at each. No toilet; pack out trash. State forest roads get no winter maintenance and are not plowed. --Claude

name: Lake Five Resort
note: Resort on the south shore of Lake Five near West Glacier, homesteaded in 1915 and built in the 1920s; full-service RV sites, water/electric 'Lake Sites', shaded water/electric campsites, cabins and dock slips, with a private beach and swimming docks. Trains run on the far side of the lake. Towing: come in by the paved Lake Five Road; the owners advise against Belton Stage from US-2. --Claude

booking.note: Booked online through the operator's ResNexus page. The policies page says 'We have a three night minimum for advance reservations. For less than three nights, we are first come, first served, day of arrival', but ResNexus offered a two-night midweek July 2027 stay ('Enjoy for 2 nights or More'). Reservations recommended June 20 - August 20. 50% deposit; half of it refunded with 30+ days' notice, none after. Check-in 3-7:30 p.m., check-out 11 a.m. Rates include two people (extra adult $10.10/day, child $7.50, dog $10.10).

Wi-Fi (Starlink) only from the office toward the stage, not at the campsites. Firewood and bug repellent sold in the office. Private beach with swimming docks, 16 dock slips.

name: Blueway RV Park
note: Cove Communities park of about 375 RV sites around a stormwater pond, sold by the night, week, season and year, with a handful of cottages and rental trailers; nightly sites sell out in the winter. The booking engine tags it 55+ while the operator's page calls it an all-age RV park. --Claude

name: Linger Lodge RV Park

name: Sun-n-Shade RV Resort
note: Winter-season Riverstone park with 6-month and annual residents and a park-model section alongside its nightly RV sites; online booking covers stays outside November 1 - April 1, and winter stays are booked by phone. --Claude

fees.source: https://online.rezexpert.com/book?business_code=301012 read 2026-10-21: Class C Motorhome 23 ft, 2 persons, Tue 10/27/2026 x1 night, '30 Amp (1 Days(s)@53.00)' subtotal $53.00 + 7% sales tax $3.71 = $56.71, no other fees; 50 Amp quoted the same. Feb 2027 dates refused online ('Winter Booking Restriction 2026-2027 ... Reservations for November 1 through April 1 can be made by calling'), so no winter rate was readable.

name: Boulder Woods Campground
note: Mostly seasonal: about 37 of its roughly 190 numbered sites are kept for nightly RV campers on the operator's 2025 map, the rest leased by the season. Reservations go through a request form or a phone call, with no instant online booking. --Claude

fees.source: https://boulderwoods.com/boulder-woods-camping-rates (WP-modified 2025-10-13, read 2026-10-21): RV Sites (Electric & Water) Daily $55.00, Weekly $330.00; Holiday Weekend RV sites 2 Day $130.00 / 3 Day $195.00; site fee covers one unit, 2 adults and their children; no resort or grounds fee (visitor $5-$12 and 'Check in prior to noon $10' are optional). Rates 'subject to change'; not a booking-engine quote.

booking.source: https://boulderwoods.com/boulder-woods-camping-rates (read 2026-10-21): holiday weekends (Memorial Day, July 4th, Labor Day, two Halloween weekends) are sold only as 2- or 3-day RV packages; the ordinary RV rate is per day with no minimum stated, unlike the tent rows' '2 Day (Min)'.

name: Brandywine Creek Campground
note: Mostly seasonal: the operator's site map marks 32 of its 55 numbered RV sites as occupied by seasonal campers, and the rest sell by the night, week or month; no tents. Open April 1 to November 1, reservations by phone or email (no online booking). --Claude

fees.source: https://www.brandywinecreekcampground.com/rates.php (read 2026-10-21): '2026 Rates ... based on 2 adults and 2 children', RV Site (water, electric, sewer, cable) Nightly $55.00, Weekly $350.00, Monthly $750 (Jun-Aug: $900) plus electric, Seasonal call for price; extra adult $10/night and extra child $5/night beyond 2+2 only; no resort or grounds fee. One site type, so $55 is the base weeknight rate.

name: Hidden Acres Campground
note: Mostly seasonal: roughly half or more of its ~200 wooded sites hold seasonal campers' trailers, with nightly sites mixed in; RV-only (no tents), open April 15 - October 15, reservations by phone only. --Claude

fees.source: https://www.hiddenacrespa.com/rates (2026 season rates, valid Apr 15-Oct 15 2026, read 2026-10-21): 30 AMP W/E $52/day, 30A W/E/S $56; 50 AMP W/E $56, 50A W/E/S $65; covers family of 4 (1-2 adults + 2 children), extra adult $9/night; no mandatory resort fee; same per-day rate any day of week

booking.source: https://www.hiddenacrespa.com/rates (read 2026-10-21): 'Holiday weekends require a 3-night minimum stay'; one-night deposit on all reservations; no other minimum stated

name: Little Red Barn Campground
note: Family-run wooded campground open mid-April through October, with a large seasonal contingent: about half the pads held trailers in Feb 2020 off-season imagery. Reservations by request form, confirmed by the office. --Claude

booking.note: Memorial Day, July 4th and Labor Day weekends need 3 nights, paid in full; holiday sites still open a week out are sold for shorter stays. The October Halloween weekends need 2 nights.

fees.source: https://littleredbarncampground.com/rates/camping-rates/ (page modified 2026-03-02, read 2026-10-21): RV Campsites W/E 30 amp $60.00 standard / $67.00 holiday weekends; W/E 50 amp $65.00 / $72.00; 7-night $408/$443; monthly $953/$1010. Basic no-hookup sites are listed only in the tent table ($47). Additional adults $10, children $5; no resort or grounds fee. Not quoted through an engine: reservations are by request form only.

booking.source: https://littleredbarncampground.com/rates/reservation-request/ (read 2026-10-21): 'Holiday weekends include: Memorial Day, July 4th, Labor Day - 3 night minimum ... Any sites not reserved 1 week prior to holiday will be made available for less than 3 night stay'; 'Two-night minimum for these Halloween weekends'. Events calendar (home page, 2026) repeats the 3-night holiday and 2-night Halloween minimums.

name: Paradise Bay Park Family Campground
note: Mostly seasonal: the park map marks about 22 of its roughly 100 sites for nightly campers, and the lakeshore rows are seasonal-only; reservations by phone with a one-night deposit. --Claude

fees.source: https://www.paradisebaypark.com/rentals.html (current Weebly site, built Aug 2026; read 2026-10-21): 'Campsite: Day: $50, Week: $300' (week = 6 nights), one sleeping unit per site, $25 extra for an added tent; no hookup or date tiers given. Matches RV Life review Jul 2026 'Nightly Rate: $50 USD'.

name: Quakerwoods Campground
note: Part seasonal: seasonal and monthly sites share the wooded loops with nightly campers (roughly half the pads held stored trailers in a February 2020 leaf-off capture); open April 1 - October 31, reservations by phone only. --Claude

fees.source: https://quakerwoods.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/rates-2026-3.jpg (2026 rate table on quakerwoods.com/rates/, read 2026-10-21): Water & Electric (30 Amp) $54/day, Full Hookup (30 Amp) $60/day for 2 adults + 2 children; 50 Amp / pull-through +$5/day optional; holiday weekends flat 3-day rates; no mandatory resort fee ($2 card convenience fee avoidable with debit)

name: Sara's Campground
note: RVs camp on the wooded bay-side sites east of Peninsula Drive, at the Presque Isle State Park entrance; the Lake Erie beach side across the road is tent-only and first come, first served. Reservations by phone or email only, no online booking. --Claude

booking.note: 5-night minimum on reservations May 15 - Sep 15; shorter stays by checking with the office, availability limited.

fees.source: https://www.sarascampground.com/ '2026 Rates' (read 2026-10-21): Motorhomes and Trailers $58.00 per night, $348 per week; additional adults beyond the party $10/person/night (not a per-site fee). RV Life reviews Sep-Oct 2026 paid $58 for numbered sites; 'BF' sites reported at $74-85 are not on the operator's table.

booking.source: https://www.sarascampground.com/ Reservation Information (read 2026-10-21): 'We require a 5 NIGHT MINIMUM STAY for reservations from May 15th through September 15th. If you do not meet the 5 night reservation requirement, you can check with the office for availability but availability is limited.'

name: Tohickon Family Campground
note: Part seasonal: a seasonal community and year-round monthly sites fill much of the wooded loops (winter-stored trailers on 2020 leaf-off imagery), with the nightly sites in the creek-side rows; open year-round. Approach by Richlandtown Road, since Google routes over a covered bridge with a 12-ft clearance. --Claude

fees.source: https://www.tohickoncampground.com/stay-with-us/rates-and-reservations (2026 season, read 2026-10-21): Standard Full Hookup Sun-Thu $58, Fri-Sat $68, holidays $78; Premium Full Hookup Sun-Thu $68, Fri-Sat $78, holidays $88; 'service fee of $4 per reservation' (per stay, not per night). Campspot quote Tue 2026-10-27, 1 night, 2 adults: Standard $65.00 total and Creekside $75.00 total = site charge + $4 park service fee + Campspot's $3 booking fee. No resort/grounds fee.

booking.source: https://www.tohickoncampground.com/stay-with-us/rates-and-reservations (read 2026-10-21): 'Weekend reservations must include both Friday and Saturday nights'; Memorial Day, 4th of July and Labor Day weekends 'requiring a three (3) night minimum'; Christmas in July and Halloween weekends 2 nights. Campground rules page says reservations are 'accepted for stays of 2 or more nights', but Campspot sold a single Tuesday night (2026-10-27), so no standing minimum.

name: YMCA Camp Sherwin Family Campground & Outdoor Center
note: YMCA of Greater Erie camp on the Lake Erie bluff (stairs down to the beach), open to the public; mostly seasonal: about 57 of its ~85 RV sites are seasonal on the 2026 camp map, alongside cabins, a pool and day-pass guests. --Claude

booking.note: Holiday reservations require a three-night minimum (operator general-info page and rate sheet). For summer 2026, full-hookup sites (and cabins) were booked only as 5-night Friday-Wednesday stays until April, when shorter stays opened; water/electric sites were not under that rule.

fees.source: https://reclique-core-erie.s3.amazonaws.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/23084136/RATE-SHEET-2026-Updated.pdf (read 2026-10-21; family rate for 5 people): summer (Memorial Day-Labor Day) daily RV water+electric $50, concrete-pad W/E $55, full hookup $65, lake-view full-hookup pull-through $80; spring/fall daily $40/$50/$55/$75; weekly = 6 nights. booking.source: https://www.ymcaerie.org/camp/general-info/ and https://www.ymcaerie.org/camp/camping/ (read 2026-10-21)

name: Family Affair Campground
note: Mostly seasonal: overnight campers get the N (full hookup) and C (water/electric) sections and a primitive field, roughly 50 of some 300 numbered sites on the operator's map; the rest are leased seasonal sites with decks and sheds. --Claude

booking.note: Memorial Day (Fri-Mon), July 4th (Thu-Sun) and Labor Day (Fri-Mon) sold only as whole 3-night packages paid in full at booking; the late-July Jamboree weekend sold as a Fri+Sat pair. Reservations by phone, one-night nonrefundable deposit.

fees.source: https://www.familyaffaircampground.com/_files/ugd/031509_860eccf2cd964b14a569ac6f0c2c0da4.pdf ('Overnight Schedule fee' download on /overnight-camping; '2026 Overnight Rate Schedule', PDF dated 2026-01-17, read 2026-10-21): standard nightly rate for 2 adults + dependent children: electric & water $70, electric/water/sewer $75, primitive (no hookups) $50; week $420-450, month $1,568-1,680; visitors $5/day, $7 overnight (not mandatory for a family of two). Holiday packages: Memorial Day / July 4th / Labor Day 3-night minimum ($260-280 hookups), Jamboree Fri+Sat $170-185.

booking.source: 2026 Overnight Rate Schedule PDF (URL in fees_source), read 2026-10-21

name: Philadelphia / West Chester KOA Holiday
note: KOA Holiday in the Brandywine Valley on the West Branch of Brandywine Creek, with a canoe launch and creekside tent sites; RV sites sit on wooded hillside loops above the creek. --Claude

name: Presque Isle Passage RV Park & Cabin Rentals
note: Mostly seasonal and monthly: 39 of its ~99 RV sites (the pull-throughs by the pool and the 100s row) are sold by the night, the rest are seasonal or monthly on the operator's 2025 site map; also ~30 rental cabins, park models and yurts. --Claude

Optional 4- and 6-week 'leave your RV on site, stay any 3 nights each week' weekend packages are sold separately.

name: Virginia's Beach Lakefront Cabins & Camping
note: Mostly seasonal: about 26 of its ~115 RV sites are sold by the night (a lakefront row, a lake-view row and wooded water/electric sites), alongside lakefront cottages and cabins. Reservations by phone with a credit-card deposit or an email request form, no online booking; 21+ to reserve. --Claude

booking.note: Three-night minimum on holiday weekends. Reservations from Feb 1 by phone (100% deposit) or email request form; walk-ins taken if a site is free.

fees.source: https://virginiasbeach.com/campingrates.html read 2026-10-21: 2026 prime season (Jun 5-Sep 7) Sun-Thu $60 for 30-amp W/E sites T4/T5 (25-ft max trailer) and T12-18; Lake View FHU $68/$70, Lake Front FHU $70 Sun-Thu / $75 Fri-Sat; holidays $80; early/late season $2-4 less; rates for 2 adults, children 12 and under free, no resort fee; units 35 ft and up +$5/night.

name: Springs Campground (Beaver Creek Park)
note: Hill County's Beaver Creek Park near its south end, about 21 miles south of Havre on MT-234: the first-come sites in the trees along Beaver Creek from below Alkali Springs Road south past Brough Coulee to Black Coulee. The park map names Springs Campground and Hidden Hollows here; Lions A and B, R.R.P.A. and H.P.P.A. among them are reservable group sites. The Bear Paw Nature Trail runs along the canyon's west side above them. Cattle graze the park after Labor Day. --Claude

facilities.note: No dump or water at this end of the park: the RV dump is near mile marker 18, about 7.5 km north, and the potable water fill stations are at the park office (Camp Kiwanis), about 6 km north. Picnic table, fire pit or ring and trash cans at sites; an outhouse within walking distance of most.

booking.note: The 100+ individual sites are not reservable: 'self-filled on a first come-first served basis' with a valid park permit. Only the large group campgrounds (pink with an asterisk on the park map) can be reserved, by the whole weekend, online or through the park office. Campers may stay 14 days on a site in any 30-day period.

note: The larger of Petoskey State Park's two campgrounds, at the park's south end about 1 km south of the Dunes Campground at the end of its own spur of the park road. Wooded loops behind a low foredune on Little Traverse Bay, with boardwalks from the loop ends to the beach; the bike trail to Petoskey leaves from the south end. --Claude

name: Lupine Campground
note: Sierra National Forest (Bass Lake Ranger District) campground on the south shore of Bass Lake, about 6 miles in on Road 222 from Highway 41 and adjacent to Cedar Bluff Campground; concessionaire-run (California Land Management). Sites under big ponderosa pines on the point inside the Road 222 loop; the RV-length sites are 63-87, while 100-113 take 20 ft and 88-99 are hike-in tent sites. --Claude

name: Robinson Creek North Campground
note: Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest (Bridgeport Ranger District) campground on Robinson Creek, 9.3 miles up Twin Lakes Road from US-395 in Bridgeport, the upstream loop beside Robinson Creek South; concessionaire-run (Westrek). Jeffrey and lodgepole pine; most sites are first-come, a few reservable in summer. Bears frequent the area. --Claude

name: Lake Pueblo State Park (Juniper Breaks)
note: North-shore campground of Lake Pueblo State Park, reached by its own road (Juniper Road) about 1.5 km east of the Northern Plains loops; the loops string along a juniper bench above Pueblo Reservoir's north shore and coves. --Claude

sites.note: 84 basic sites (100-183, 157HD ADA), no electricity; cpwshop lists vehicles to 30-65 ft (40 or 45 ft at most), one site with no length.

facilities.note: Central water hydrants and vault toilets; the dump stations are in the Northern Plains and Arkansas Point campgrounds.

season.note: CPW: camping is available year-round and only the Northern Plains campgrounds close for winter; limited sites and amenities in winter.

booking.note: A reservation is required: cpwshop.com, 1-800-244-5613, or at the park office, up to six months ahead. 14 days within a 28-day period; six people, two motorized vehicles and one camping unit per site. Check-in 1 p.m., check-out noon. Display a vehicle pass.

name: Navajo State Park (Tiffany)
note: Navajo State Park's basic-site campground on its own spur road just southwest of Carracas: a north loop of RV sites and a south loop with the park's three cabins and walk-in tent sites, on a bench above Navajo Reservoir. --Claude

sites.note: 25 RV sites: 24 basic plus full-hookup site 100 (30 ft). cpwshop vehicle lengths: ten at 55 ft (mostly pull-throughs), two 45, one 35, two 30, six 25, four 20 (102, 114, 127, 129, too short for 23 ft). Six walk-in tent sites (119-124) and three cabins not counted.

facilities.note: Restroom and shower house (push-button showers); camper services and restroom buildings close September 16 to April 14, when the park has vault toilets only. The dump station is in Carracas next door.

booking.note: A reservation is required: cpwshop.com or 1-800-244-5613, up to six months ahead; reservations cannot be made at the park. 14 days within a 28-day period; six people, two motorized vehicles and one camping unit per site. Check-in 1 p.m., check-out noon. Display a vehicle pass.

name: Trinidad Lake State Park (South Shore)
note: Trinidad Lake State Park's second campground, on the south shore about 1.7 km across the lake from Carpios Ridge and reached by its own gravel road along the south shore from the dam end rather than through the Carpios Ridge entrance. The sites, each with a picnic shelter, sit on open grass at the foot of a pinon-juniper hill looking north over the lake. --Claude

sites.note: 10 basic sites (101-110, 108HA accessible): 6 back-ins listed for vehicles to 30 ft and 4 pull-throughs (101 and 110 at 100 ft, 105 and 106 at 80 ft), so all 10 take a 23-ft rig.

facilities.note: A community water hydrant and vault toilets; the showers, laundry and flush toilets are in the camper-services building at Carpios Ridge, and the dump station is near the Carpios Ridge entrance.

season.note: CPW's camping page gives May 1 - October 15, and elsewhere on the same page says the campground is closed between mid-October and mid-May.

booking.note: A reservation is required: cpwshop.com or 1-800-244-5613, up to six months ahead. 14 days within a 28-day period; six people and one camper/RV plus one tent per site. Check-in 1 p.m., check-out noon. Display a vehicle pass.

name: Vega State Park (Island)
note: Vega State Park's smallest campground: two RV sites and a tent site on the Island, a low peninsula on the reservoir's north shore beside the Island day-use area and boat ramp, reached by a gravel park road off County Road 64.6 about 2 km by water from Early Settlers. The RV sites are gravel pull-ins on the edge of a large gravel lot, partly shaded by oak brush, with the lake on three sides. --Claude

sites.note: Two Basic sites (403, 404) with 60-ft gravel driveways, both listed for vehicles to 60 ft; site 402 is a tent-only site and is not counted.

facilities.note: The park's dump station is near Early Settlers (closes about Oct 31). CPW states nothing about toilets or water at Island; the camper services building with showers and flush toilets is in Early Settlers.

name: Carter Lake - North Pines Campground
note: Larimer County campground on the north end of Carter Lake, west of Loveland, reached by its own entrance off County Road 31 on the road down to the North Pines boat ramp. The sites sit in pines at the end of a short spur on the cove; N04 is at the shore. Restrooms and a water spigot by N01; the boat ramp, day-use area and parking lots are just down the road. --Claude

sites.note: 4 drive-in gravel non-electric sites (N01-N04): N01 back-in 24 ft on an incline the county says is best for tents, N02 back-in 35 ft, N03 pull-through listed for vehicles to 45 ft (80-ft driveway), N04 back-in 25 ft. N02-N04 take a 23-ft motorhome. The booking site files all four under tent and trailer sites, not RV sites.

facilities.note: Restrooms and a water spigot beside N01 (spigots off September-April except the frost-free ones). The RV dump station is at the south entrance on County Road 8E, about 4 miles ($15 a use); the token shower house is at Eagle Campground.

min_stay.season: April through September

booking.note: Reserve same-day to 180 days ahead online or at 1-800-397-7795; a reservation and a park entrance permit are required before setting up. Two nights required on weekends April-September; 14 days in any 30 across the county system. Check-in noon, check-out 11 am; one wheeled camping unit per site.

name: Carter Lake - Carter Knolls Campground
note: Larimer County campground on the east side of Carter Lake, west of Loveland, with its own entrance off County Road 31: a gravel loop on an open, rocky overlook above the lake, very windy at times. Drinking water from the spigots at the other Carter Lake campgrounds; restrooms on the loop and picnic shelters at C02 and C06. --Claude

sites.note: C05 is the one site a 23-ft motorhome fits: a gravel pull-through listed for vehicles to 40 ft (65-ft driveway). The other four drive-in sites (C02, C03, C04, C06) are 20-ft pull-throughs, and C08 and C09 are walk-to tent-only sites (120 and 150 ft from parking).

facilities.note: No water spigot at Carter Knolls; the county points campers to the spigots at its other Carter Lake campgrounds (frost-free ones only September-March). Restrooms on the loop, picnic shelters at C02 and C06. The RV dump station is at the south entrance on County Road 8E, about 3 miles ($15 a use); the token shower house is at Eagle Campground.

min_stay.season: April through September

booking.note: Reserve same-day to 180 days ahead online or at 1-800-397-7795; a reservation and a park entrance permit are required before setting up. Two nights required on weekends April-September; 14 days in any 30 across the county system. Check-in noon, check-out 11 am; one wheeled camping unit per site.

name: Anthracite Campground (Paonia State Park)
note: The electric loop of Paonia State Park, on Kebler Pass Road (County Road 12) beside Anthracite Creek, about 5 km south of the park's Hawsapple and Spruce campgrounds at the head of Paonia Reservoir. No office; the Crawford State Park visitor center serves Paonia. --Claude

sites.note: Seven back-in electric sites, 017-023; 017 is listed for 22 ft, the rest 25-70 ft. 018 and 019 are accessible. Sites 020-022 are along the creek.

facilities.note: No drinking water in the park; bring your own. Vault toilets, fire rings and picnic tables.

season.note: Paonia State Park is closed October 1 to May 1.

booking.note: A reservation is required: cpwshop.com or 1-800-244-5613, up to six months ahead. 14 days within a 28-day period. Display a vehicle pass.

fees.note: $36 a night ($252 a week), plus tax, CPW's reservation fee, and a daily vehicle pass ($10-$15) or an annual state parks pass.
