name: High Falls State Park River Campground
note: The larger of High Falls State Park's two camping areas: four wooded loops along the Towaliga River downstream of the dam and falls, reached by its own gated road south of High Falls Road, with a campers' playground in Loop C. The Lakeside Campground, 1.4 km north on High Falls Lake, is a separate entry. --Claude

facilities.note: Restrooms, showers and laundry in Loops A, B/C and D; dump station on the exit road by Loop A.

name: Key Largo Kampground & Marina
note: Condominium kampground: owners hold all 171 lots, about 38 of which the association rents by the night (2026 park map), and reviewers describe the rest as mostly full-timers and seasonal owners. The pool was closed for repairs (operator site, 2026-10-30). --Claude

booking.note: 3-night minimum over MLK Day, Easter, Memorial Day, July 4th, Labor Day, Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Year's Eve, and over lobster mini season. Check-in guest must be 25+ (the Campspot terms say 21). Walk-ins 6-10 pm through the security guard, subject to availability.

fees.source: campspot.com/book/keylargokampground site pages read 2026-10-30, 2 adults, no pets, 1 night Tue 2026-12-08: RV Non Water Front Back-in $120.00 x 1 night, Pull Through $125.00, RV Waterfront Full Hookup $156.00, before tax ($15.00 tax on $120). The engine's per-night average for these types is the same on Jan, Feb, Mar, May and Jul 2027 weeknights ($128.17 / $133.51 / $166.62 including fees), so $120 is the year-round base. Holiday weeks cost more: back-in $144 on 2026-11-10 (Veterans Day) and 2026-12-29. The only per-night 'Campground Fees' are pets ($20/night in the engine; $10 a pet per stay on the operator's policy page) and a 3.7% credit-card fee. There is no resort or grounds fee, and Campspot adds its own booking fee (~3.6%).

name: Keys Palms Luxury RV Resort
note: Small gated resort with 30 sites; it books by phone only, since the website's reservation form is just an information request. No tents or pop-ups, and travel trailers and fifth wheels go only on the pull-through and back-in sites. --Claude

name: Grassy Key RV Park & Resort
note: Small resort of about 36 RV sites with a boat basin. It books a site type, not a site number, by phone or email (there is no online booking), it takes no arrivals after 4:30 pm, and every RV must carry the RVIA seal. --Claude

booking.note: 3-night minimum on holidays and special events, which are also charged at winter rates.

note: A small RV-only park on Stock Island: about 48 back-in sites on a mangrove lagoon, plus a few rental campers and apartments. There is no bathhouse, so RVs must be self-contained. --Claude

name: Mohican State Park Class B Campground
note: Primitive campground in the Clear Fork gorge, about five road miles from the main campground. RV sites are B-10 to B-23, gravel spurs along a dead-end park road with the river across it; B-1 to B-9 are tent sites. --Claude

sites.note: 14 RV sites, B-10 to B-23, all back-in, no length posted by the agency. The other nine sites (B-1 to B-9), about 550 m west, are not RV sites. Up to two pets per site.

facilities.note: Pit toilets. Campers may use the Class A campground's showers and pool. No dump station is listed here; the park's is at Class A.

name: Jesse Owens State Park - Hook Lake Campground
note: A no-fee area at the east end of the park, off SR 83, around two ponds; the youth-only (15 and under) fishing ponds give it its name, with an archery range at the far end of the gravel road. name: Greene-Sullivan State Forest - Reservoir 26 Campground
note: A loop off W 25 N with its own two driveways, in the south-central forest, behind the levee on the east side of Reservoir 26. Fishing pier and a trail around the reservoir. The agency gives no length; 2020 Dyrt reviewers disagree, one calling it open and flat and good for larger RVs, another warning most sites here and at Wampler don't suit larger campers. --Claude

name: Bond Falls East Campground
note: Upper Peninsula Power Company's dispersed sites strung along the northeast shore of the Bond Falls Flowage, on the far side from the West loop. On Bond Falls Rd, about 3.5 km east of the falls, turn south at the Calderwood Rd junction; a dirt road follows the shore for about a kilometre, with spurs to the sites. Pick an open site; a host comes round about 11am with the required permit. A 2025 reviewer checked for open sites on the clipboard at the small building near the Outpost. UPPCO posts no length limit and no reviewer gives a rig length here; a motorhome used E14 in Jul 2025. Spurs under canopy are unmeasured. --Claude

name: Prairie Ridge A Loop (Rathbun Lake)
note: USACE Rathbun Lake campground on a high prairie ridge between Buck Creek and Honey Creek, SW of Moravia; the last 2.5 miles in are gravel (200th Avenue). Woodland draws and timbered hillsides, a modern playground, and a boat ramp sheltered on three sides with a courtesy dock and fish-cleaning station. An 8-mile trail links to Honey Creek Resort. Unstaffed. --Claude

sites.note: A loop on the lakeshore at the south end of the ridge; the B area is a separate entry, about 2 km north. Gravel pads, every site takes a 42 ft rig or more.

name: Lake Ogallala State Recreation Area - West Campground
note: Lake Ogallala SRA's West Campground, on the west shore of Lake Ogallala just below Kingsley Dam, with its own West Entrance off the Keystone road; across the lake from the East Campground. Basic grass sites off dirt and gravel lanes, spread about 2.3 km along the shore: a peninsula loop, a shore strip and a south loop; several RV sites sit right on the bank. Water at the fish-cleaning station, playground and south boat ramp. Pad lengths are not posted anywhere (2026-11-05); RVs are seen on the loops on imagery. Park entry permit required. --Claude

sites.note: 68 RV-or-tent basic grass sites (plus 32 tent-only), all drive-in; no lengths posted.

booking.note: All camping at Lake McConaughy and Lake Ogallala is by advance reservation only.

fees.note: Basic $15 Sunday-Wednesday, $20 Thursday-Saturday (May 21 - September 12), $10 the rest of the year. Plus tax.

name: Sutherland Reservoir State Recreation Area - Inlet Campground
note: Sutherland Reservoir SRA's Inlet and Westshore camping on the south-west shore, ~4.3 km across the lake from the Outlet Area by a separate road off Hwy 25: primitive clearings on packed sand under trees along a maintained track, some tent sites on the sandy beach. NGPC doesn't say whether any of the SRA's 22 Electric Plus sites are here. Drought can leave the lake low. --Claude

booking.note: Self-register at the iron ranger; envelopes take cash or checks only.

name: Merritt Reservoir SRA - Willow Cove Campground
note: Campground on the east shore of Merritt Reservoir SRA, ~1 km south of the dam on its own spur off the dam road; the pads and loop road are packed sand. Vault toilets and a hydrant here; the park's shower building is at Cedar Bay. Park entry permit required. --Claude

fees.note: In season: basic $15, electric plus $30 a night; $5 less mid-October through April. Plus tax, the $8.50 reservation fee when booked online, and a park entry permit ($7 a day for a Nebraska vehicle, $14 otherwise; $35 / $70 a year). Nebraska Game and Parks' camping rates grid ('These rates are consistent across all parks').

name: Calamus Reservoir SRA - Valley View Flat Campground
note: Small campground near the upper (northwest) end of Calamus Reservoir, on its own road off the highway: one paved loop of electric pads under mature trees, set back from the boat ramp and parking lots; tent sites and designated parking-lot spots alongside. The park's dump station is at Little York Point. Park entry permit required. --Claude

name: Liberty Cove Recreation Area
note: Little Blue NRD recreation area on a 37-acre spring-fed no-wake lake in Webster County, 2 mi west and 2 mi south of Lawrence on graded gravel county roads. The electric pads are angled back-ins off a short spur south of the park road, behind the shelters and day-use lawn; tents only in the area behind the dam. Two restrooms, well water, swim beach, boat ramp and dock, playground, arboretum, hiking and horse trails; archery deer/turkey hunting in season. --Claude

note: Little Blue NRD recreation area on a 36-acre flood-control lake on Thirty-Two Mile Creek (trolling motors only, no boat launch), south of Prairie Lake Rd 3 mi S and 1 mi E of Juniata. name: Cedar Point Park
note: USACE Harlan County Lake park on the south shore at the south end of the dam, off the road to Patterson Harbor: a swim beach with a paved lot and vault toilet, and a primitive camping field on the grassy point around a gravel loop with a second vault toilet. Camping is undesignated: the Corps says to pick a spot with a fire ring and picnic table and pay at the self-pay vault, but a 2021 Dyrt reviewer found no camping sign or fire rings, called the gravel roads narrow and rough, and thought it best for small trailers, vans and pop-ups; call the Corps office to confirm where to camp. Vehicles also drive onto the sand beach below the bluff. --Claude

name: Wilson State Park - Otoe Area
note: Wilson State Park's Otoe Area on the south shore of Wilson Reservoir, northeast of Hell Creek across a cove and reached by its own road (Shoreline Drive off KS-232): water/electric loops Yarrow and Goldenrod on open grassland, all back-in, plus primitive loops along the shore and four Elm cabins. Yarrow's water may be off in winter (Goldenrod has it year round). --Claude

min_stay.season: Memorial Day, Independence Day and Labor Day weekends (2027 rule)

booking.note: Sites reserve site-specific on Kansas's ReserveAmerica site (campitks.gov); unreserved sites allow self-registration on arrival. 2027 holiday minimum: 3 nights over Memorial Day, July 4th and Labor Day weekends. Up to 14 consecutive nights in one campground, then move to another campground in the park.

fees.note: KDWP's statewide schedule from November 1, 2026: a daily camping permit of $17.75 a night per camping unit, plus utilities at $11 a night for one (electric), $13 for two (water and electric) or and $2 a night more for a designated prime site April-September. A $2.75 processing fee per stay and a vehicle permit ($7 a day) are charged on top. The add-ons listed are the kinds of site the Otoe Area has (no sewer), per KDWP's park page; water and electric shows as electric +$11 plus water +$2. Read 2026-10-15.

name: El Dorado State Park (Shady Creek)
note: Shady Creek area of El Dorado State Park (KDWP), on the south shore of El Dorado Lake off NE Shady Creek Access Road: primitive gravel sites in Sunset Cove, Veterans Point and Patriot Lane, plus 19 walk-in tent sites in Shady Creek Outback. The booking site files every site as a tent site, but the gravel pads list 30-ft vehicles and 29 are pull-throughs, and the imagery shows an RV parked on a Veterans Point pad (2026-11-06). Bluestem Point, across the cove, is its own entry. --Claude

Read 2026-10-15.

name: Tuttle Creek State Park - South Randolph Area
note: South Randolph campground of Tuttle Creek State Park (KDWP), on a wooded rise above the east shore at the lake's north end, entered by Randolph Park Road off K-16 just east of the Randolph Bridge: two small gravel loops of electric sites, plus about 50 unreserved primitive sites. It is the park's horse-camping base (horse pens, wash racks, the Randolph equestrian trail) but sells ordinary RV and tent sites; water is from community hydrants, not at the sites. --Claude

name: Walnut Park (Arkansas City)
note: City of Arkansas City river park on the west bank of the Walnut River off E. Madison Ave just east of US-77, with a boat ramp: a gravel loop with no marked sites. MDC marks three primitive camping spots here, each beside a small gravel parking lot: this pin by Route D at the lake entrance, the others off County Roads 182 and 217. None is at the lake itself. The river-tract camps are their own entry. --Claude

Camping is only in the mapped campgrounds, with at most two camping units per site. --Claude

name: Poosey Conservation Area (south camping)
note: Rolling oak-hickory hills and small lakes northwest of Chillicothe. This entry is the south camping loop, a gravel loop with pull-ins and a privy in the woods above 192-acre Indian Creek Community Lake, about 150 m from the water with no view through the timber. Reached from its own county road, about two miles from the central loop, which is its own entry. The brochure speaks of camping in self-contained units and says drinking water is not provided. Spot length is not published. --Claude

Creekside on site 10 (and likely 12), on an open lawn at the river bank; the other sites sit behind trees. --Claude

name: Wilson Dam
note: Dickey County park on the south-west shore of Wilson Dam reservoir, about 7.5 miles west of Monango: camping is on a mown lawn inside two tree rows beside the picnic shelter, with no gravel pads seen on imagery and the number of electric sites unpublished. Pay by check to Dickey County Park at the lockbox on either utility pole (park board at extension 3). --Claude

name: Big Coulee Dam Campground
note: City of Bisbee campground on the east shore of the Big Coulee Dam (Bisbee Dam) reservoir, about 1 mile east of town on Dam Rd; camping is on mown lawn between shelterbelt rows near a shelter, playground, swim beach and fishing pier, with no pads seen on imagery. No fees, hookups, season or booking method are published and no phone was found; confirm with Bisbee city hall (302 Main St) before going. --Claude

name: Eagles Campground - Beulah
note: Beulah Park District campground on the west side of ND 49 opposite Riverside Park: one row of pads on a gravel loop between the highway and the Knife River, entered from the cross street at the ND 49 junction. The Park District mentions no restrooms or showers. --Claude

fees.note: $25 a night, $140 a week, $420 a month, paid in full when booked. Beulah Park District, read 2026-11-12.

sites.note: Ten electric sites in one row (Sites 1-10; the online list shows nine, without Site 7). Back-in only unless the office approves otherwise.

season.note: May through October, dates depending on the weather.

booking.note: Booked online through the Park District and paid in full. Check-in 3 p.m., check-out noon; arrivals after 8 p.m. must arrange check-in ahead (701-870-0602).

name: Perch Lake Campground
note: Rusk County Parks campground in the Rusk County Forest, on a wooded rise beside the man-made Perch Lake about 12 mi NW of Bruce and half a mile from Audie Lake Campground: one one-way gravel loop with a log pavilion. Unlike the county's other campgrounds, ATVs and UTVs may be ridden in the campground, and an ATV trail leaves from the loop. Sites 7 and 8 look at the lake through the trees. --Claude

sites.note: 15 back-in sites with 50/30/20-amp electric and water. Posted pads run 46-86 ft by 14 ft (site 3 has no published page), so every listed site takes a 23-ft rig.

facilities.note: Water at the sites is off from about the second week of October to late April. Nearest dump: the Cenex in Weyerhaeuser or Rice Lake.

season.note: Open year-round; water off in winter and sites are not plowed.

booking.note: Rusk County's own reservation site (Konect Parks), or the forestry office by phone. Reservations close 7 days before arrival; any site not reserved is first-come for that date. Only the current calendar year can be booked; next year's dates open January 1. Paid in full when booked, no refunds.

name: Sidie Hollow County Park, Boat Landing Campground
note: The full-hookup campground of Vernon County's Sidie Hollow park near Viroqua, at the east end of the 38-acre lake by the boat launch, on its own road about 1.3 km from the park's Main area. The camp hosts stay here (site #9 on the county page) and sell ice and firewood. --Claude

name: Buffalo Pound Provincial Park - Elmview, Lakeside and Valley Campgrounds
note: Provincial-park campgrounds by the beach, outdoor pool and boat launch on Buffalo Pound Lake, a reservoir in the Qu'Appelle Valley about 20 minutes northeast of Moose Jaw: Lakeside's seven sites behind a strip of shoreline trees, Valley's full-service sites in the woods behind the boat launch, and Elmview south of the park road. Every Elmview site, the winter-camping ones included, books only for a unit up to 18 ft or a tent or van, so a 23-ft rig fits Lakeside and Valley only (Valley V12F is posted at 20 ft). Showers are at the beach building. 6 Valley sites are seasonal. Maple Vale, Shady Lane and Trails End about 2.8 km northwest and Lower Chalet about 2.4 km southeast have their own entries. --Claude

season.note: 2026-27 dates. Full services May 14 to September 30; October nights booked through the park; winter camping in Elmview November 1 to March 14 with power, firewood and pit or portable toilets, but no water, showers or dump station.

fees.note: $4 a night less from October 1, with reduced services.

name: Buffalo Pound Provincial Park - Lower Chalet Campground
note: Two non-electric loops off the main park road by the Lower Chalet visitor centre at Buffalo Pound Lake, a reservoir in the Qu'Appelle Valley about 20 minutes northeast of Moose Jaw, set beside the city's water treatment plant. Sites are on grass with no gravel pads; no showers in the loops (the nearest are at the beach, about 2 km northwest). LCA-8 to LCA-14 and LCB-16 and LCB-17 book only for a tent or van camper. The Elmview, Lakeside and Valley campgrounds about 2.4 km northwest and Maple Vale, Shady Lane and Trails End beyond have their own entries. --Claude

name: Duck Mountain Provincial Park - Fern Campground
note: The park's small lakeshore loop by the park village on Highway 57, about 2 km southwest of the Pickerel Point campground (own entry). Wooded sites: only F1 and F2 have power; online booking takes a unit of 19-25 ft on eight more, 18 ft or less on five, and a tent only on F4, F5 and F12. Two Camp-Easy yurts. --Claude

season.note: 2026-27 dates. Summer season May 14 to September 30; winter camping November 1 to March 14 with power at site 2 only, firewood and outhouses, no water, showers or dump station. October nights are booked through the park office.

name: Makwa Lake Provincial Park - Mewasin Campground
note: The park's southern campground, at Mewasin Beach on the south bay of Jumbo Lake, about 3 km south of Stabler Point (own entry) on the road to Exner Lake. Wooded sites in two parts either side of the beach; the lake shows through the trees from a few west-arm sites (M13, M15, M21). 11 sites are sold by the season. --Claude

name: Saskatchewan Landing Provincial Park - Riverside and Nighthawk Campgrounds
note: Provincial-park campgrounds at the west end of Lake Diefenbaker, about 2 km east of the Hwy 4 bridge off Hwy 261: Riverside in a single row along the shore woods, Nighthawk across the highway from it. Riverside's lake-side sites R28-R41 look at the water through a belt of trees, R28 and R29 the most openly. Showers, laundry and groceries are at Bearpaw. Bearpaw and Sagebrush (the park's main campgrounds) and Bison Hollow have their own entries. --Claude

name: Saskatchewan Landing Provincial Park - Bison Hollow Campground
note: Provincial-park campground on the north shore of Lake Diefenbaker west of the Hwy 4 bridge, a single loop in scattered trees above the shore; a few sites see the lake past the trees. Showers, laundry and groceries are at Bearpaw, about 12 km by road. Four Prairie Meadow group areas sit beside it. Bearpaw and Sagebrush (the park's main campgrounds) and Riverside/Nighthawk have their own entries. --Claude

name: Sandy Beach Regional Park
note: Regional park on Highway 17 about 15 minutes north of Lloydminster, with a nine-hole golf course, a swim beach on a small lake and a cabin area. The nightly serviced and tent sites sit inland of a row of seasonal sites along the shore; the seasonal sites are fully booked with a waitlist. The park is gated, so after-hours arrivals must call ahead to have gate access set up. --Claude

fees.note: Serviced (30 A, water, sewer) sites C$40 a night; tent-only non-serviced sites C$24; weekly C$245. Park entry C$10 per vehicle a day, C$25 for a Friday-Sunday weekend pass or C$60 for the season.

sites.note: 25 nightly serviced RV sites (1-25, most taking 40 ft; site 4 50 ft, site 19 36 ft), 11 tent-only sites (A-K) and 26 seasonal sites.

season.note: Camping season; the park itself stays open to about October 9 (2026) and reopens May 1, 2027.

booking.note: Daily and weekly bookings open March 1 and stays over 30 days January 15; one site per online booking, and the booker must be 19 or older.

name: Rolling Green Fairways RV Park
note: RV park set inside the back nine of an 18-hole golf course on the western edge of Lloydminster, with a restaurant at the clubhouse. Besides nightly stays it sells weekly, monthly and May-October seasonal sites and courts contract workers; how much of the park goes by the night is not published. --Claude

fees.note: Daily: partial hook-up (30 A + water) C$37, full hook-up 30 A C$42, full hook-up 50 A C$48, plus GST. Weekly C$270-300 and monthly C$980-1,100; May 1-October 1 seasonal from C$4,250; RV-and-golf 'Stay & Play' packages.

booking.note: Reserve through the booking request form on the RV park page, by phone or by email; sites are assigned by availability and rig size, and every stay is paid in advance at the office.

name: Woodlawn Regional Park - Boundary Dam
note: Woodlawn Regional Park's second campground, on a point in Boundary Dam Reservoir 8 km south and 2 km west of Estevan, beside the park's beach and boat launch. Mostly seasonal: about 45 of its 144 RV sites are short-term sites, 31 of them sold online by the night. No grad parties on the May long weekend. --Claude

booking.note: Bookings for long weekends and for July and August are non-refundable; at other times a cancellation 48 hours ahead is refunded less C$15.

name: Big River Regional Park, Cowan Lake Campground
note: Big River Regional Park's lakeside campground on Cowan Lake at the end of Main Street, with a fish-filleting shack, a camp kitchen and gazebo, and the town dock and free boat launch beside it. The park's dump station and coin showers are at its Community Centre Campground on the north side of town, about 1.2 km away. --Claude

fees.note: 30-amp full service C$35 a night (C$240 a week, C$770 a month), 50-amp C$40 (C$245 / C$840), non-serviced C$22; park entry C$10 a day or a seasonal park pass. Taxes included.

booking.note: Off season (mid September to May 15) by e-mail or message and the park calls back; from May 15 by the office phone. Cancellations 14+ days out are refunded in full, under 14 days 50%, under 7 days nothing; date changes C$20; no refunds on long-weekend bookings.

note: Hudson Bay Regional Park's small campground at Ruby Lake, a former provincial recreation site 15 km north of Hudson Bay: a wooded loop at the south end of the park's beach, boat-launch and ball-diamond grounds, beside a cottage subdivision. name: Bronson Forest Recreation Site - Peck Lake Campground

name: Buffalo Bill State Park (Lake Shore Campground)
note: Lake Shore Campground (formerly North Shore Bay), about 9 mi W of Cody on US-14/16/20 between the highway and Buffalo Bill Reservoir: three small paved loops on sagebrush points above the north shore, a short walk down to the water. --Claude

fees.note: $10 a night for Wyoming residents, $18 for others, +$10 at an electric site, plus the day-use fee, $7 a vehicle for residents and $12 for others, plus sales and lodging tax. The booking site shows 'Fees Range From $33-50 (Per Night, Per 1 Vehicle)' on the electric sites and '$23-40' on the non-electric ones.

booking.note: All 36 sites are bookable online from May 1; the campground stays open in winter (water off), outside the booking season.

name: Shadow Mountain Designated Camping Area
note: Bridger-Teton NF designated undeveloped sites on Shadow Mountain, reached from US 26/89 by Antelope Flats Road on the east edge of Grand Teton NP; camping only at the marked, numbered sites. The base sites by the toilet are the easiest; the rest line the summit loop road, which the Forest Service calls rough in places and campers report muddy after rain. Larger rigs are best kept to the base sites; call the Jackson Ranger District about road conditions before setting out. --Claude

booking.note: 5-night limit May 1 through Labor Day (Order 04-03-24-204, all of Jackson RD); 14 nights in 30 the rest of the year. Camping only at the marked, designated sites.

name: Buffalo Valley Designated Camping Area
note: Bridger-Teton NF designated undeveloped sites strung along the paved Buffalo Valley Road from US 26/287 east of Moran to Turpin Meadow; camping only at the marked, numbered sites. A few open straight off the paved road (site 1 is a large gravel pullout above the Buffalo Fork); most lie down short dirt spurs the Forest Service rates for high-clearance vehicles, and in 2024 a camper found one spur blocked partway in. Call the Blackrock Ranger District about conditions before setting out. --Claude

booking.note: Camping only at the marked, designated sites; 14-day limit year-round (Buffalo Valley is in the Blackrock Ranger District, outside the Jackson RD 5-day summer order).

name: Elk Fork Campground
note: Shoshone NF, Wapiti Ranger District: a small campground strung along a gravel road beside Elk Fork creek just south of US-14/16/20, about 28 mi W of Cody, at the Elk Fork Trailhead into the Washakie Wilderness. The horse corrals and trailer lots belong to the trailhead beyond the back of the campground, not to the sites; the sites themselves are small with little room to manoeuvre, and the big lot at the back is the place to turn around. --Claude

fees.note: Single unit. Fee season not posted; earlier FS and press sources had no fee charged in the off-season (roughly October-April).

season.note: Fees, host and trash service run in summer; the campground stays open without services the rest of the year.

name: Seminoe State Park (South Red Hills Campground)
note: South Red Hills is the campground just south of North Red Hills on the northwest side of Seminoe Reservoir, about 34 mi north of Sinclair via County Road 351: two clusters of gravel sites, several with shade shelters, on open sage slopes above the water beside the South Red Hills boat ramp. No trees. The park's dump station is at North Red Hills. --Claude

season.note: Off season (Sep 16 - May 14) the sites are walk-up, paid at the entrance fee kiosks.

booking.note: Reservations required May 15 - Sep 15; off season the sites are walk-up.

name: Seminoe State Park (Sunshine Beach Campground)
note: Sunshine Beach is the park's southernmost campground, just southeast of South Red Hills on Seminoe Reservoir, about 35 mi north of Sinclair via County Road 351 and a mile of gravel road: gravel sites, a few with shade shelters, in loops on two low points and along the road between, on open sage ground above the sandy shore the park calls its most popular swimming area. No trees. Drinking water is at North and South Red Hills in summer, the dump station at North Red Hills. --Claude

name: Glendo State Park (Cottonwood Campground)
note: Cottonwood is a small campground in a cottonwood grove on the northeast shore of Glendo Reservoir, reached by a half-mile gravel road that turns north just before the Sandy Beach fee booth. Four of the five pads are natural sand ground under the trees, on a short spur off the gravel road, and may be soft going for a heavy rig; the paved pull-through (CW04) is the sure one. The lake rises into the grove at high water in late spring and early summer, then drops away. --Claude

name: Glendo State Park (Elkhorn Campground)
note: Elkhorn is the northernmost campground on Glendo Reservoir's west shore, off WY 319 about 5 miles north of Glendo and nearest the North Platte inlet. Its grass pads line a gravel spur at the edge of a belt of cottonwoods and willows; the lake reaches the trees in late spring and early summer, but by fall the water can be a half-mile walk away. The one vault toilet is at the boat ramp lot, up to a quarter mile from the farthest sites. --Claude

name: Glendo State Park (Indian Point Campground)
note: Indian Point sits on a peninsula on the east side of Glendo Reservoir, two miles out a gravel road that turns right just before the Sandy Beach fee booth. Its undeveloped sites lie in three areas off two-track dirt lanes, which the park says suit medium-sized units or tents: IP01-IP12 along the edge of a cottonwood stand (the first six without shade), a group site by the boat ramp, and IP17-IP20 a short way up the dirt road toward Broken Arrow, a road the park says has sandy stretches that heavy rain can make impassable. The lake reaches the edge of the campground only at high water (late spring to early summer); as the reservoir drops the shore recedes across bare flats. --Claude

name: Glendo State Park (Mule Hill Campground)
note: Mule Hill is a small campground on the west shore of a bay of Glendo Reservoir, entered from Glendo Park Road about a quarter mile southeast of the main fee booth. name: Glendo State Park (Red Hills Campground)
note: Red Hills spreads over a series of pine-dotted hills below red rock cliffs, on a peninsula on the west side of Glendo Reservoir just north of Reno Cove. The park recommends four-wheel or all-wheel drive for sites 12-15, reached by a steep, undeveloped track, and calls site 1's steep, narrow access road best for smaller units; RH08 and RH09 have 20-ft parking, too short for a 23-ft rig; sites 18-22 sit down at the high-water line among scattered cottonwoods and can be affected by high water, and as the reservoir draws down later in summer the shore recedes across bare flats. --Claude

name: Glendo State Park (Whiskey Gulch Campground)
note: Whiskey Gulch is a large campground strung along about half a mile of Glendo Reservoir's south shore, entered directly off Glendo Park Road, with the park's Whiskey Gulch high- and low-water boat ramps. Most sites lie among or behind the cottonwoods and willows that line the shore and flood at high water; sites 13 and 14, on an open point, come closest to the lake, and as the reservoir draws down later in summer the water recedes across bare flats. --Claude

fees.note: Wyoming's statewide schedule: each night's camping fee is the base rate plus that day's day-use fee plus sales & lodging tax, per vehicle.

sites.note: Plus two group sites (G23 up to three camping units, G24 up to two).

facilities.note: Seasonal drinking water, shut off in winter.

season.note: Off season (Sep 16 - May 14) the campsites are walk-up.

booking.note: Reservations May 15 - Sep 15; off season the sites are walk-up.

name: Sinks Canyon State Park (Sawmill Campground)
note: Sawmill is the first campground up Sinks Canyon from Lander, a small loop that is mostly a day-use area with a large picnic shelter; its campsites sit on the shoulder of the loop above the Middle Fork Popo Agie's cascade. Site 27 (24 ft) and the two parallel roadside sites 28 and 29 take a 23-ft rig; 28 and 29 will not take slide-outs, and site 26 is 20 ft. --Claude

facilities.note: A hand pump, shut off in the off season.

season.note: Off season (Oct 1 - Apr 30) access depends on the weather.

booking.note: Reservations May 1 - Sep 30; first-come the rest of the year.

fees.note: Wyoming's statewide schedule: the base camping rate plus sales & lodging tax per vehicle; Sinks Canyon charges no day-use fee.

name: Blackrock Meadows RV Camping Area
note: Bridger-Teton NF RV and camper-van area: a large open gravel lot on the north side of US 26/287 about 15 miles east of Moran Junction, half a mile west of Togwotee Mountain Lodge, entered straight off the highway. A summer camping area: in winter the lot is the Togwotee Snowmobile Trailhead. No campfires; self-contained rigs only. --Claude

booking.note: 14 nights within any 30-day period (forest-wide Order 04-03-328); Blackrock Meadows is not among the Blackrock RD areas under the 5-day summer limit of Order 04-03-24-204.

name: Big Eau Pleine County Park, South Campground
note: The wooded campground of Marathon County's Big Eau Pleine park, on a peninsula in the Big Eau Pleine Reservoir west of Mosinee: one shaded loop near the south shore with a boat launch, picnic area and firewood sales close by, and a shoreline walking trail. The West campground, about 1.4 km away on its own road beside the beach and disc golf, has its own entry. --Claude

facilities.note: Water from pressurized-well pumps; the park dump station is open 8 am - 8 pm ($8).

season.note: October is first-come only: reservations cover May 1 - September 30.

booking.note: Five sites are first-come only. Online reservations close 3 days before arrival; an unreserved site may be self-registered on site for up to 3 nights (cash or check), and in October every site is first-come. Check-in 3 pm.

name: Maxwell Park Campground
note: City of Arlington in-town campground in Maxwell Park, the block between Elm St (US 14) and the railroad at N Main St downtown, with a free grass tent area; the city's other campground, Nordland Park, is about 0.45 km SE. No season or booking method is published (a 2020 camper review says to pay at the city office, 202 W Elm St, with an after-hours drop box): call the city to confirm. --Claude

name: Dakota Sunsets Campground
note: Each site is reached by an assigned color-coded entry and exit path shown on the operator's site guides, and the operator asks rigs to follow it because the turns are tight. --Claude

season.note: Open all year; Oct 16 - Mar 31 sites are sold electric only, with no water, restrooms or laundry.

Winter: 1-night 30A W/E quotes 2027-01-19 ($45 less an automatic 'No Water, Restrooms, Laundry = ELECTRIC ONLY' discount of $18 = $27) and 2026-11-24 ($42.50 - $17 = $25.50); winter list averages (fee included) on 2027-01-19..03-31 and 10-16..11-16: primitive $24, 30A W/E $30, 30A FHU $33, 50A $36/$39, so primitive $21 and 50A-over-40ft $36 net of the $3 fee (derived from the list average, not a full quote). Season boundary from list prices: 2027-03-31 winter, 04-01 full; 10-15 full, 10-16 winter. Tent sites ($40 in season) not counted.

name: Royal River Casino RV Park
note: Flandreau Santee Sioux Tribe casino's RV lot: a separate paved lot of angled back-in sites on a central median across the road south of the casino; check in and collect keys at the hotel front desk, and RV guests use the hotel's showers, laundry and pool. 28-day maximum stay. --Claude

name: Menno City Park Campground
note: City of Menno camper pads at the north end of the City Park on S Park St, with the park restroom just north of them; the city dump station is at the football field at the south end of Park St. No season is published (the city shut the site water off for winter on 2026-11-12); pay at the Finance Office, its drop box or online through paygov.us. --Claude

name: American Creek Campground
note: City of Chamberlain campground on the Lake Francis Case (Missouri River) shore at the north edge of downtown, with a boat ramp, fishing pier and swim beach beside the day-use area. Pad lengths are not published; imagery shows travel trailers of roughly 28-35 ft on the pads, and a 2026 camper found one site a little short for a truck and trailer. --Claude

fees.note: Electric + water site; tent sites $35. 9% tax extra; posted prices are card prices with a 3.5% cash discount built in.

booking.note: Reservations by phone only; reservations not required. Weekend minimum covers Friday and Saturday. One night's site fee is charged on any cancellation; no reservations taken November-March.

name: Roy Lake State Park (West Unit)
note: Roy Lake State Park's West Unit campground, on a peninsula at the park's main entrance SW of Lake City, beside the modern cabins, suites, store, swim beach and the floating bridge to the Roy Island trail. The East Unit campground, about 3 km across the lake, is a separate entry. Shore sites 20E-29E look at the lake through a fringe of trees. --Claude

sites.note: Plus tent-only sites T1-T5, electric tent site 8E and camping cabins C3, C10 and C11.

season.note: October 1 to April 30 the showers, flush toilets and water may be off; vault toilets stay open.

name: Angostura Recreation Area (Cascade Campground)
note: Angostura Recreation Area's Cascade campground, on its own loop road off the park road about 2 km south of the north entrance, with a swim beach at its north end. The west row (26E-44E) is in a belt of shore trees; when the reservoir is down a wide sand flat lies between the trees and the water. Cheyenne to the north, and Hat Creek with Horsehead to the south, are separate entries. --Claude

name: Angostura Recreation Area (Hat Creek and Horsehead Campgrounds)
note: Angostura Recreation Area's two south campgrounds, Hat Creek (90E-112E) and Horsehead (113E-163E), each on its own spur off the park road from the south entrance, with a day-use area between them (boat ramp, fishing pier, fish cleaning station, picnic shelter). Horsehead's sites look at the lake through trees. Cheyenne and Cascade to the north are separate entries. --Claude

name: Oahe Downstream Recreation Area (Campground 3)
note: Campground 3 of Oahe Downstream Recreation Area, on the south bank of the Missouri River channel below Oahe Dam's stilling basin, 5 mi N of Fort Pierre, reached by its own road from SD-1806 at the south end of the river bridge (the park's dump station is at that turn). Campgrounds 1 and 2, across the channel, are a separate entry. Sites 194E-197E, 204E and 205E sit on open lawn at the river's edge; camping cabins C1-C8 line the bank to the south-east. --Claude

sites.note: Plus camping cabins C1-C8 along the river.

name: Palisades State Park (Queen Campground)
note: Palisades State Park's original Queen Campground, in the trees above Split Rock Creek at the north end of the park, reached by the park road from the 256th St entrance past the day-use area and the historic bridge. Camping cabins and the park's group lodge are close by; the park's dump station is on the entrance road by King Campground, about 1.2 km south-west, which is a separate entry. --Claude

sites.note: Sites 98E-102E are 25-ft pull-offs along the loop road. Plus tent-only sites 78-84, 90, 91, 94, 96 and 97 and camping cabins C5-C10.

season.note: October 1 to April 30 the showers, flush toilets and water may be off; vault toilets stay open.

fees.note: GFP publishes this park's own rate: non-electric $16, electric $30 a night (the statewide $7 electrical fee is already in the electric figure). Residents and non-residents pay the same to camp; the entrance licence and the $10 non-resident reservation fee are what differ.

name: Pickerel Lake Recreation Area (East Campground)
note: Pickerel Lake Recreation Area's East Campground, on the wooded east shore of Pickerel Lake N of Waubay, with its own entrance, boat ramp, fishing pier, fish-cleaning station, swim beach and camping cabins. The West Campground, about 2.4 km away on the north shore, is a separate entry. Shore-side sites 48E-58E look at the lake through the trees. 2026 reviews on the booking site warn of branches overhanging the roads that can scrape rooftop units. --Claude

name: Sheps Canyon Recreation Area (Sheps South Campground)
note: Sheps Canyon Recreation Area's non-electric campground on a peninsula of Angostura Reservoir's west arm, about 2.5 km down its own park road south of the main Sheps Canyon loop: one gravel road with sites on both sides, lakefront at the east-side shore row (clearest at 35, 37, 39, 41 and 56), facing the reservoir across open grass and beach; the west-side row is inland. When the reservoir is down the water is 45-60 m off. Showers and the dump station are at the main loop; the horse camp sits between the two. --Claude

fees.note: No electric sites, so the statewide $7 electrical fee never applies. Residents and non-residents pay the same to camp; the entrance licence and the $10 non-resident reservation fee are what differ.

name: Jacobs Brook Campground
note: About half seasonal: the operator's site map marks 27 of its roughly 60 numbered sites 'All Season', and the rest are sold by the night (5 also by the month) or are tent sites. The operator asks RVs to skip the 3-ton Archertown Road bridge and follow the truck detour by Dublin Road. Jacobs Brook's swimming holes are a trail walk from the RV loops. --Claude

fees.note: Water + electric $48; water, electric + sewer $53; 50-A full hookup $60. Tent sites $30 (water only) and $38 (water + electric, 20-A max); group tent area $35 per site. Rate covers 2 adults and 3 children; additional persons charged.

booking.note: Reservations by phone or the operator's web form/email; replies within 48 hours. The 3-night minimum covers the Memorial Day, Independence Day and Labor Day weeks.
